Senate Menu Home Meet Abdul Priorities Money Out of Politics Money in Your Pocket Medicare for All How to Vote Endorsements Events Events with Abdul Events for Volunteers Volunteer News Store Donate Policy Agenda Terms of Engagement for Data Centers January 8, 2026 Our Communities, Our Terms Throughout the last year, Michiganders have watched as at least 15 data center projects have been proposed in communities across our state.
And we demand transparency.
Michiganders want to understand the impact this could have on our electricity rates, grid reliability, water sources, and jobs.
Utilities companies like DTE and Consumer’s Energy, with a long history of hiking rates without improvements in reliability, are pushing to greenlight projects without any accountability.
All while state and local government regulators are being steamrolled by corporations.
The people deserve to know their rights when a data center comes into our communities.

Abdul outlines the following rights for Michiganders as we navigate the inception of data centers here Michigan and across the country: No rate hikes Data centers must pay for their own energy demand — costs cannot be passed onto ratepayers.
Community transparency Communities must have a meaningful say in project approvals and community benefits packages.
Energy reliability guarantees Energy reliability cannot worsen because of data center projects.
Projects must include enforceable commitments from utilities to improve energy reliability, funded by data center revenues.
Jobs guarantee Data centers must create the local jobs they promise, or face penalties, and must be built by Michigan contractors with DOL registered apprenticeship programs.
Water protection Data centers must commit to closed-loop cooling systems to avoid stressing or polluting local water resources.

Community benefits agreements Projects should include binding agreements that deliver real benefits, including local infrastructure investments, improvements to the electrical grid, burying power lines, and upgrading water treatment facilities and piping.
No clean-energy loopholes Utilities cannot use data center projects to weaken or sidestep clean energy laws.
Enforceability All agreements must be enforceable through actionable penalties.

Senate Menu Home Meet Abdul Priorities Money Out of Politics Money in Your Pocket Medicare for All How to Vote Endorsements Events Events with Abdul Events for Volunteers Volunteer News Store Donate Policy Agenda Labor Policy Agenda January 27, 2026 The constitutional right to organize, bargain collectively, and be treated with dignity on the job sits at the foundation of a fair economy.
Yet for decades, pro-corporate, anti-worker policies have systematically undermined these rights—tilting the balance of power away from workers and toward corporations and billionaires.
Abdul is a second-generation union member, raised with a deep respect for collective bargaining and solidarity.
As Michigan’s U.S.

Senator, Abdul will prioritize rebuilding our economic and political systems to empower working people, protecting them from intimidation and exploitation Every worker should have the right to join a union and support a family with one good job.
It’s critical that the Senate pass the PRO Act and oppose any and all “Right to Work” legislation .
We must protect and expand prevailing wage protections and champion worker-centered trade policies , including strategic tariffs to grow good union jobs.
Abdul is committed to building a government that works for people – not billionaires – and to unlock what we can achieve together.

Abdul will introduce or support the following legislation: Demanding strong antitrust enforcement and empowering the Federal Trade Commission to stop harmful consolidation to protect wages, working conditions, and union contracts.
Pass worker-forward antitrust reform to structurally support workers over corporate interests.
Strengthen and broaden the FTC’s merger review authorities to give clear powers to block consolidation that hurts workers.
Banning corporate stock buybacks by repealing SEC Rule 10b-18, ensuring corporations invest in workers rather than executive bonuses.
Eliminate the loopholes that shield stock buybacks from market-manipulation enforcement.
Mandating employee-elected board representation for publicly-traded companies Shift power inside companies by mandating worker’s voices be heard through a seat at the board table.
Protecting retirement security , especially multi-employer pensions, by defending the Butch Lewis Act and supporting the Protecting Employees and Retirees in Business Bankruptcies Act.
Congress must resist efforts to repeal, weaken, or defund the Butch Lewis Act implemented under the American Rescue Plan and instead codify it as a permanent pillar of federal retirement policy.
Guaranteeing healthcare for every American through Medicare for All, freeing unions and their members to choose between bargaining for higher wages or add-on health insurance.
Empowering unions and their members to choose between the guaranteed public health insurance or private options while ensuring public coverage for every union member.

Senate Menu Home Meet Abdul Priorities Money Out of Politics Money in Your Pocket Medicare for All How to Vote Endorsements Events Events with Abdul Events for Volunteers Volunteer News Store Donate Policy Agenda Investing in Small Business: An Economic Agenda for Main Street, not Wall Street March 16, 2026 Small businesses are the backbone of our economy, representing 99.9% of all U.S. businesses and employing nearly half of American workers.
Small businesses drive innovation and build communities.

But corporate monopolies are using their market power and government lobbying to undercut competition, squeeze suppliers, dominate entire industries, and extract tax breaks that squeeze out smaller competitors.
Concentrated corporate power threatens the entrepreneurial spirit that built America’s middle class.
One billionaire holds the wealth of at least a thousand millionaires.
Abdul wants to create an economy where billionaires don’t stop small businesses from creating lasting wealth in local communities.

That’s why he supports the following set of policies to empower hardworking Michiganders to put more money in their pockets: Strong Antitrust Enforcement Create an Office of the Small Business Advocate at the Department of Justice to bring complaints on behalf of small businesses.
Codify and strengthen the FTC’s power to block mergers that harm small business competitors, suppliers, and buyers–not just those that raise consumer prices.
Regulate the practice of dominant platforms and large corporations acquiring competitors before they can grow into meaningful rivals.
Extend antitrust scrutiny to markets where a few large buyers dominate a market, which can devastate small suppliers, farmers, and manufacturers.
Challenge exclusive dealing arrangements and loyalty discounts that lock small businesses out of distribution channels, shelf space, or supply networks.

Prohibit Big Tech platforms from giving preference to their own products over third-party small businesses in search results, marketplaces, or app stores; and allow small business customers to port their data and require technical interoperability.
Enforce the Robinson-Patman Act, which prohibits large buyers from extracting preferential pricing that disadvantages small competitors and suppliers.
Regulate coercive terms in franchise agreements and large-buyer supplier contracts.
Authorize the FTC to reopen merger approvals where competition has suffered, and require corporations to demonstrate that deals will not harm competition ahead of any mergers taking place.

Banning Corporate PAC Contributions in Politics Large corporations use their vast financial resources to influence elections and buy access to policymakers, rigging the rules in their favor through tax loopholes, regulatory or legislative carve-outs, and subsidies that small businesses never see.

Investment in Small Business Revolving Capital Expand the Small Business Association’s (SBA) Manufacturers’ Access to Revolving Credit Loan (MARC) Program and the bipartisan INVEST Act to create a national Small Business Revolving Loan Fund.
Fund this expansion via taxes on billionaire wealth.
Reductions in Small Business Taxes Pass the Mom and Pop Tax Relief Act to allow small businesses to deduct the first $25,000 of qualifying business income annually.
Allow freelancers and small businesses to deduct healthcare from FICA obligations, matching treatment of other business entities.
Increase the employer childcare credit to 40% and provide enhanced deductions for employee training programs.
Reduce the employer payroll tax and replace it with an automation capital levy that excludes businesses with less than 50 employees or annual revenue under $5 million.

Investment in Healthcare for Business Owners and Employees Reinstate and expand enhanced premium tax credits that expired in 2025, which left millions facing significant increases in healthcare costs.
Increase the Small Business Health Care Tax Credit from 50% to 75% of premium costs and create purchasing pools to improve negotiating power against insurers.
Pass Medicare for All to liberate small businesses from the crushing burden of providing health insurance, an essential step to empower the small business sector long term.

Tax Incentives for Worker Cooperatives Follow Colorado’s HB25-1021 model by creating federal capital gains exclusions for owners selling to employees and enhanced deductions for cooperative formation costs.
Establish a dedicated Office of Cooperative Development within the SBA to provide technical assistance for businesses transitioning to worker ownership.

Addressing Equity in Small Business Policy Mandate equity in lending practices with transparent reporting by race, gender, and geography, holding financial institutions accountable for discriminatory patterns.

Senate Menu Home Meet Abdul Priorities Money Out of Politics Money in Your Pocket Medicare for All How to Vote Endorsements Events Events with Abdul Events for Volunteers Volunteer News Store Donate Policy Agenda Ban the Middleman Act May 6, 2026 Pharmacy Benefit Managers or “PBMs” don’t manufacture prescription drugs.
They don’t dispense prescription drugs.
They just extract profit by operating as middlemen in the space between drug manufacturers and patients.
Every single reform attempt has taught them a new way to game the system.
The only solution is elimination, not regulation.

Consider the Ohio problem: PBMs have historically used a tactic known as “spread pricing” where they charge employers and insurers more for prescription drugs than they pay pharmacies to distribute the drugs, keeping the difference as profit.
Ohio banned this corrupt practice in Medicaid in 2018 after PBMs overcharged the state by $225M in a single year.
PBMs simply pivoted.
They pay pharmacies above contract, then claw back the difference.
Net savings: zero.
Nobody needs PBMs.
Every function PBMs perform either already exists or can be replaced by a public entity at lower cost, with no conflict of interest.
The VA and Medicaid negotiate drug prices directly without PBMs, and they get the same or better pricing.
Claims processing is just an IT function.
Independent pharmacies design formularies.
CMS already negotiates some prescription drug prices under the Inflation Reduction Act, passed by Democrats in 2022.
PBMs offer zero additional value.
They exist to line their own pockets at the expense of Americans struggling to afford prescription medication.
As Michigan’s next U.S.
Senator, Dr.
Abdul El-Sayed will introduce legislation to: Abolish the PBM middleman business model entirely.
That includes rebate aggregators, Group Purchasing Organizations, and utilization management entities, sunsetting them over a three year transition period.
He will ban the rebate system entirely, requiring drug discounts to be upfront and visible to patients at the point of sale.

Bar PBMs or other entities from blocking or delaying access to lower-cost generic drugs and biosimilars through prior authorization requirements, step-therapy mandates, or other administrative hurdles, ensuring these medications are automatically placed on more affordable tiers than their brand-name counterparts.
This guarantees patients can access affordable medication without interference from middlemen protecting their own profits.
Expand CMS drug price negotiation under the Inflation Reduction Act Medicare drug negotiation authority to cover all federally regulated plans.
This will allow for direct manufacturer-to-payer negotiation under public transparency rules for commercial markets, using CMS-published reference prices as a floor.
Create a public pharmacy benefit administrator through a CMS-run claims processor and benefit administrator available to employers, self-insured plans, and small insurers at cost.
That means no profit motive, no manufacturer contracts, no affiliated pharmacies, and therefore no extra costs passed on to consumers.

Require decisions regarding drug coverage and pricing to be made by independent medical experts–not insurance or drug-industry insiders–by establishing transparent committees free from pharmaceutical industry influence, similar to the systems used by the VA and state Medicaid programs.
Drug placement would be based on clinical evidence and cost-effectiveness, not rebate size.
Make sure any pharmacy meeting defined safety and dispensing standards is automatically in-network.
Reimbursement floors will be set by a public rate-setting authority to protect independent pharmacies from the below-cost reimbursements that have shuttered them.

Establish an independent pharmacy transition fund financed by repayments from PBMs found to have engaged in anticompetitive pricing to support independent pharmacies harmed by decades of PBM self-dealing, with priority for rural and underserved communities.

Senate Menu Home Meet Abdul Priorities Money Out of Politics Money in Your Pocket Medicare for All How to Vote Endorsements Events Events with Abdul Events for Volunteers Volunteer News Store Donate Policy Agenda First, Do No Harm: AI Under Democracy June 29, 2026 As robots take on human abilities, they must be governed by human means.
Big Tech is teaching machines to write, reason, diagnose, create, and decide.
That means that a handful of billionaire-backed labs are shaping the future of work, of democracy, of our own safety.
And they’re doing it all behind closed doors, accountable to no one but their billionaire investors.
One AI CEO, Anthropic’s Dario Amodei, put it plainly : he was “deeply uncomfortable with these decisions being made by a few companies, by a few people.” We agree.
Which is why we need a plan to fix it.
We created the internet.
The American people funded the research that built it through public universities and federal grants.
Humanity created the data that populated it.
And without it, AI would not exist.
AI was built off us.
It should work for us, not against us.
Americans deserve clarity, control, and a say in how this transformative technology will shape our world.
In January, we released a Data Center Terms of Engagement platform because communities have the right to know and control what’s being built, who benefits, and what they get in return.

Now, we’re putting forward a plan to bring AI Under Democracy – guardrails and a roadmap for AI development with one goal in mind: to bring the most powerful technology in human history under human democratic control.
This will ensure that innovation serves all of us who made it possible, not just the few who can profit from it.
AI Should be Governed Under Democracy It’s not a coincidence that Google holds a major stake in Anthropic.
Or that Microsoft is embedded in OpenAI.
And Amazon holds billions in both.
This is a deliberate strategy to control the next platform before it threatens the last one.
We have to break up Big Tech’s hold on AI to ensure the public’s best interest is served.
This is not unprecedented.
Norway holds board seats in Equinor—it’s massive energy conglomerate—not just stock.
American public utility commissions hold veto power over major utility decisions.
The Federal Reserve requires public-interest directors who operate independently from the banks.
We’ve done this before.
Here’s how we do it again: Mandatory Public Benefit Charters: All frontier AI labs must be chartered as public benefit corporations, legally bound to balance public interest against profit.
“First, Do No Harm” Governance : Charters must enshrine this as an operating standard.
Profit cannot come at the cost of public safety, civil rights, or democratic integrity.
Democratic Board Control: 50%+1 of board seats at frontier AI companies must be publicly appointed or democratically elected, not chosen by shareholders.
Mandatory Divestiture: Companies developing frontier AI must operate independently of major platform tech companies.
Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and Meta must divest controlling interests within a defined transition period.
No Revolving Doors: Public board members cannot return to employment at any major tech company after their service.
Public Ownership, Public Dividend, Public Investments AI was built on our data and our labor; we should own a piece of it.
Senator Bernie Sanders’s American AI Sovereign Wealth Fund Act would transfer 50% equity from the largest AI companies into public hands.
I support that effort and propose to take it one step further because Americans deserve a seat at the table.
Warning signs are coming from industry leaders themselves.
Geoffrey Hinton, the Nobel Laureate godfather of modern AI, compared this moment to the Industrial Revolution: robots replaced our bodies then, and they’re coming to replace our brains now.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei predicted that 50% of entry-level white-collar jobs could vanish within five years.
Michigan knows what it’s like to have our jobs and industries ripped from under us, like when profit-driven automation devastated the auto industry in the #s.
Michiganders can’t afford to go down this road again.
This is what public ownership could look like: We Own Half : Consistent with Sanders’s proposal, with returns flowing to the American people.
Annual AI Dividend : Proceeds fund a direct annual dividend to every American.

Automation Levy : A per-worker-equivalent tax on AI-driven automation, reinvested in workers to do the following: Education Investment : Education should be free, particular for early and mid-career workers through community college partnerships, guaranteed apprenticeships, and entrepreneurship training.
Expanded Unemployment Benefits and Wage Insurance : Longer duration, higher wage replacement, and a federal bridge that makes up the gap between old and new wages during transition.
Small Business Revolving Loans: Publicly capitalized loans so local businesses can build and thrive.
AI Shouldn’t Be Able to Hurt Us AI is the single most consequential technology humanity has ever created.
It has the opportunity to address some of our most pressing challenges, from cancer to climate change.
But it also carries the ability to destroy us economically, socially, politically, and physically.
And we can’t just sit back and ignore the risks.
We don’t let pharmaceutical companies test their own drugs.
We shouldn’t let AI companies test their own models.
We have needed guardrails to protect humans from these risks.
Here’s what that should look like: Mandatory Interpretability Standards : It’s not enough to know what the AI said if we can’t understand why it said it.
We need mandatory interpretability standards that clarify AI decisionmaking.
Mandatory Behavioral Red-Teaming : Independent adversarial testing for deception, manipulation, and coercion before deployment.
Independent Safety Testing Agency: We need an FDA-style agency that evaluates frontier models before deployment.
Biosecurity Requirements : Mandatory biosecurity red-teaming, coordinated with the CDC, NIH, and FEMA, with restrictions on models that meaningfully assist bioweapons development.
Domestic authoritarianism prohibition: No mass political surveillance, protected-characteristic predictive policing, or AI targeting of dissent.
Self-acceleration Guardrails : AI used to build or improve other AI must face the same safety review as the models it produces.
And limits must be placed on the capacity for agents to produce other agents.
Mandatory Incident Reporting : There must be a clear mechanism for reporting AI harms to regulators the way pharmaceutical adverse events are reported.

Democracy Protections : We need a federal ban on deceptive AI-generated political media, mandatory disclosure of AI-generated political ads, and a federal task force on algorithmic disinformation with real enforcement power.
Compute Controls and “Know Your Customer” Requirements: We don’t sell nuclear centrifuges without knowing the buyer.
Similarly, chip access must be regulated and traceable on national and international markets.
AI No-Gos: AI may not deny medical care, autonomously fire weapons, conduct warrantless surveillance, replace human oversight in life-or-death decisions, or make hiring or firing decisions.

International Cooperation : We must re-engage the Bletchley framework and global AI Safety Institute network to advocate for a binding compute-threshold treaty with Authority to pause dangerous development A binding ban on lethal autonomous weapons Barring AI any role in nuclear command and control Pursuit of a broad multilateral safety dialogue on catastrophic risk, modeled on Cold War nuclear verification cooperation.

Senate Menu Home Meet Abdul Priorities Money Out of Politics Money in Your Pocket Medicare for All How to Vote Endorsements Events Events with Abdul Events for Volunteers Volunteer News Store Donate Policy Agenda The AAA Plan for Seniors: Aging Affordably in America June 3, 2026 Michigan’s seniors worked, paid in, and played by the rules.
They deserve Medicare that actually covers all their health needs, Social Security they can live on, and a home they can afford to stay in.
The Aging Affordably in America platform delivers all three — and pays for it by making the wealthy pay their fair share.
Medicare that covers ALL of you.
Medicare was designed as a comprehensive guarantee.

Through decades of cost-sharing requirements, benefit exclusions, and privatization, it’s become a patchwork that forces seniors into thousands of dollars of out-of-pocket expenses before meaningful coverage kicks in, and into a supplemental insurance market that exists only because Medicare itself has been purposely kept inadequate.
End all cost-sharing .
Premiums, deductibles, and co-pays are eliminated for Medicare beneficiaries.
The program provides first-dollar coverage.
No senior should be rationing medication or avoiding care because of a deductible.

Expand Medicare drug price negotiation powers: Expand CMS drug price negotiation authority under the Inflation Reduction Act to cover all drugs paid for by Medicare, rather than the limited number currently permitted.
Close the gap .
The supplemental insurance market for Medicare forces seniors to pay an additional $2,000 per year in premiums.
It’s a direct consequence of Medicare’s coverage gaps.
Comprehensive coverage makes it unnecessary.
Eliminating it removes an entire cost burden from seniors on fixed incomes.
Expand coverage for vision, dental, and hearing .
These are not secondary benefits.
Untreated hearing loss is among the leading risk factors for dementia.
Dental disease can cause cardiovascular disease.
Vision loss is the leading cause of preventable falls.
No logical healthcare system arbitrarily decides these items are not part of essential coverage.
Covering all three is not generosity, it’s good healthcare policy that saves seniors and saves money.
Ban AI-based prior authorization .
Automated denial systems are overriding physician judgment at scale, delaying or denying healthcare your doctor said you need.
No algorithm should be able to deny care that a licensed physician has determined is necessary.
Prior authorization decisions must be made by a licensed physician with full access to the patient’s record and subject to binding physician-to-physician review on appeal.
Securing Social Security.
Social Security is not a benefit, it’s a return on a lifetime of investment.
Two structural flaws undermine that return for millions of workers, and a third ensures the wealthiest Americans contribute less than their fair share.
Repeal the Windfall Elimination Provision and Government Pension Offset .
WEP and GPO reduce or eliminate Social Security benefits for public employees.
That includes folks like teachers, firefighters, police officers, nurses who spent careers serving their communities under pension systems that operated outside Social Security.
These workers paid into their pensions instead of Social Security, often by statutory requirement, not by choice.
WEP penalizes them for it by cutting their earned Social Security benefits.
GPO goes further, eliminating spousal and survivor benefits for public-sector retirees.
Both provisions are punitive, both disproportionately harm women, and both should be repealed in full.
Lift the payroll tax cap .
The Social Security payroll tax currently cuts off at $176,100 in earned income.
A billionaire and a warehouse worker pay identical dollar amounts above that threshold on every additional dollar earned.
Eliminating that cap more than extends Social Security solvency through the century.
Ending the tax on Social Security benefits .
Seniors earned their social security benefit.
They should keep all of it.
Social security benefits should be excluded from gross income.
Age in Place with Grace.
Rising home valuations have created a paradox: the home a senior paid off over thirty years has become an annual financial burden that grows regardless of their income.
A retired autoworker whose home has tripled in assessed value pays taxes on a paper gain they can never realize without selling the house they live in.
Additionally, for many seniors, the difference between aging in place and entering a facility comes down to a few hours of help each day—assistance with bathing, meals, medication, or mobility.

Yet Medicaid home and community-based services are chronically underfunded, leaving hundreds of thousands of eligible seniors on waiting lists while institutional care remains the default option the system is built to pay for.
We must fix this.
Federal framework for state-level property tax freezes.
For homeowners 65 and older, property tax assessments are frozen at their value at age 65 or the date of enactment, whichever is lower.
The federal government provides fiscal incentives and funding to cover municipal revenue shortfalls.
Income-targeted priority.

Relief is structured to prioritize seniors at or below 200% of the federal poverty level — those most at risk of displacement — while remaining available to all senior homeowners to avoid means-testing complexity at the point of administration.
Freeze follows the senior, not the property.
The assessment freeze does not transfer on sale or death.
When the home changes hands, it reassesses at market value.
This preserves local tax base integrity over time while ensuring the relief serves its intended purpose: allowing seniors to remain in their homes on fixed incomes.
Federal investment in home and community-based services (HCBS).

Increase the federal Medicaid matching rate for home health and personal care services, incentivizing states to expand eligibility, reduce waiting lists, and improve caregiver wages — addressing both access and the workforce shortage that limits capacity.
End the institutional bias in long-term care financing.
Current Medicaid rules make it easier to fund a nursing home bed than a home health aide.

This platform directs CMS to revise reimbursement structures so that home and community-based care is funded on equal footing with institutional alternatives, giving seniors and their families a genuine choice.
Support family caregivers who are already doing the work.
Millions of family members provide unpaid care that delays or prevents costlier interventions.

A federal caregiver tax credit and access to respite care services recognizes that contribution and helps sustain it—keeping seniors at home longer without burning out the people who make it possible.

Senate Menu Home Meet Abdul Priorities Money Out of Politics Money in Your Pocket Medicare for All How to Vote Endorsements Events Events with Abdul Events for Volunteers Volunteer News Store Donate Policy Agenda THRIVE: Transforming Housing, Resources, Infrastructure, Value & Economic Opportunities September 15, 2026 Investment That Reaches Our Communities – On Our Terms Black communities across Michigan have too often been an afterthought in federal policy with promised investment that arrives late, falls short, or comes with no way to measure whether it actually made a difference.
Abdul’s THRIVE Agenda sets a different standard: real accountability and measurable results.

Access to Capital & Minority Business Growth Close the lending and contracting gap – Expand Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI) Funds and Small Business Administration (SBA) lending to minority-owned businesses, with a goal of doubling the share of SBA-backed loans reaching Black- and Latino-owned firms within five years, and hold federal agencies accountable to disadvantaged-business contracting targets with real penalties for missing them.

Transparency and technical assistance – Require federal lending data to be published by census tract and race on a public dashboard, and fund Minority Business Development Agency centers and CDFI technical-assistance grants so entrepreneurs get real help with applications and compliance.

Affordable Housing & Homeownership Increase supply – Expand Low-Income Housing Tax Credit allocations paired with state gap financing, and tie federal incentives like HUD’s PRO Housing grants to local zoning reform, which will allow for supply-increasing changes like by-right multifamily and accessory dwelling units, reduced parking minimums, and firm permit review timelines, so red tape doesn’t block new units.

Make ownership and affordability real – Fix HUD’s Area Median Income calculations to use local, not regional, income data; expand first-generation down-payment assistance and FHA/USDA loan access in majority-Black and majority-Latino neighborhoods; tie federal investment to tenant protections and right-to-counsel so revitalization doesn’t price out longtime residents.

90-Day Housing Access for Veterans & Families A binding timeline – Require HUD-VASH and Housing Choice Voucher applicants to reach lease-up within 90 days of application, with public reporting by housing authority, and cut wait times by digitizing applications and allowing self-certification or virtual inspections for minor issues.

Accountability and veterans first – Tie a share of HUD administrative fee funding to housing authorities meeting the 90-day benchmark, paired with technical assistance rather than punishment for under-resourced agencies, and expand HUD-VASH voucher allocations with VA caseworkers embedded locally to fast-track veteran eligibility.
Improving Health & Access to Care Medicare for All – Fight to guarantee every single American cradle-to-grave health insurance without networks, premiums, co-pays, or deductibles.
End discrimination against patients based on their insurance.

Strengthen the safety net – Secure multi-year Community Health Center Fund reauthorization so Federally Qualified Health Centers can plan and hire beyond a year at a time, and establish Medicaid reimbursement parity for community health workers and patient navigators.
Adjust rules to enable cities and counties to build, better partner with, and administer Federally Qualified Health Centers.

Close food deserts and expand telehealth – Expand Healthy Food Financing Initiative grants to bring full-service grocery access into underserved neighborhoods, and make telehealth reimbursement permanent so care isn’t limited by transportation or provider shortages.

Healthy Mothers & Healthy Babies Make coverage and care permanent – Pass Medicare for All to guarantee every single mother and baby dignified healthcare without premiums, co-pays, and deductibles, and also include coverage for doulas and midwives.

At a minimum, lock in 12-month postpartum Medicaid coverage nationwide, expand Medicaid reimbursement for doulas and midwives, and fund community-based programs like Healthy Start and home-visiting services (MIECHV) nationwide.
National RxKids – Expand the RxKids program nationwide, providing unconditional cash assistance to expectant and new mothers to empower young families to invest in their children.

Support the whole family and track results – Strengthen and simplify WIC enrollment, pair maternal health investment with safe, stable housing support for pregnant and postpartum families, and direct Title V Maternal and Child Health Block Grant dollars specifically toward closing Black maternal mortality disparities, with public reporting by race and county.

Environmental Justice & Clean Water Infrastructure Fix the water – Enforce full lead service line replacement well ahead of the EPA’s 2037 backstop, with priority funding for communities that can’t cover local match requirements, and expand PFAS remediation dollars for affected municipal water systems with mandatory public disclosure of test results by zip code.

Guarantee 50 gallons of clean water per person per day (the basic minimum needed to drink, cook, and bathe) with water bills capped at 2% of household income and ironclad protections against shutoffs for families who can’t afford to pay.

Guarantee cumulative impact review for air quality – Require regulators to assess a community’s existing pollution burden–industrial emissions, diesel truck and rail traffic, and other combined sources–before allowing any new pollution sources nearby, guaranteeing air quality doesn’t get worse in Michigan neighborhoods already experiencing the highest levels of pollution.

Education & Workforce Pipeline Fund Underfunded School Infrastructure – Assure that every child goes to a school that is modern, clean, warm, and dry by updating funding formulas that deprive schools in urban communities from the infrastructure funding they need.
Debt-free and Tuition-free Higher Education –Build a pathway to universal debt-free and tuition-free higher education for every learner.
Invest in pathways – Expand Title III funding for HBCUs and community colleges, and grow DOL-registered apprenticeships.

Modernize CTE and ease debt – Increase Perkins V funding for career and technical education in majority-Black and majority-Latino school districts, and expand loan forgiveness for graduates who return to work in high-need public service fields in the communities they came from.

Voting Rights Restore and modernize voting protections – Support passage of the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act to restore preclearance-style review in jurisdictions with a history of discrimination, and establish a federal automatic voter registration standard tied to DMV and public benefits enrollment.

Count everyone and protect access – Increase outreach funding for accurate census counts in hard-to-count communities, since census data directly determines how much federal formula funding reaches these neighborhoods, and support same-day registration and secure drop-box access as a federal minimum standard.

Senate Menu Home Meet Abdul Priorities Money Out of Politics Money in Your Pocket Medicare for All How to Vote Endorsements Events Events with Abdul Events for Volunteers Volunteer News Store Donate Policy Agenda Farmers Over Billionaires October 9, 2026 At every turn, the Trump administration and MAGA Republicans have catered to billionaire and corporate donors while Michiganders fall further and further behind.
Family farmers are bearing the brunt.
With the illegal war in Iran and the needless tariff war with Canada spiking costs, their policies are sending the price of diesel through the roof right at the start of harvest season.
The Trump Administration might as well be waging an all-out war against Michigan farmers.
Mike Rogers backs every single one of Trump’s price hikes.
His policies would further devastate Michigan farmers.
But family farmers are the lifeblood of our state, and they deserve better than the Rogers-Trump’ anti-worker, anti-farmer agenda.
That’s why I’m launching my Farmers Over Billionaires policy agenda.
Our broken politics has put the interests of corporations, monopolies, and billionaires over the interests of our rural communities for far too long.
That ends when I get to the United States Senate.
Michigan farmers will always have their U.S.
Senator in their corner as we fight together for better opportunities and lower costs.
Pass Right to Repair Law: Michigan farmers should be able to fix their own equipment.
Instead, manufacturers like John Deere force them to wait for expensive dealer service, sometimes weeks, in the middle of planting or harvest seasons.

Abdul will champion a federal right-to-repair law, building on the bipartisan-minded Freedom for Agricultural Repair and Maintenance (FARM) Act , requiring manufacturers to sell the manuals, parts, software, and tools needed to diagnose and repair equipment to farmers and independent repair shops at fair prices.
Break Up Ag Monopolies That Are Pricing Out Family Farmers: Four companies (Tyson, Cargill, JBS, and National Beef) control about 85 percent of U.S. beef processing.
When so few buyers control the market, ranchers get squeezed on what they’re paid, and families pay more at the grocery store.

Abdul will work in the US Senate to enforce antitrust laws and break up monopolies across the agriculture industry—including meatpacking—that are pricing out family farmers and driving up costs for Michigan families.

Abdul supports passage of the bipartisan Meat and Poultry Special Investigator Act , which would create a team at USDA with subpoena power to investigate anticompetitive meatpacking practices and coordinate with the DOJ and the FTC.
Cut Red Tape So Farmers Can Get the Help They Need Farmers shouldn’t need a lawyer or have to spend a weekend doing paperwork to get a loan or sign up for a program.

Abdul will fight to simplify USDA applications, cut duplicative paperwork, provide plain-language guidance, and make it easy to apply online, so farmers spend their time farming and not filling out forms.

He will support the bipartisan USDA Express Loan Act , which would create a simplified short-form application and faster decisions on guaranteed farm ownership and operating loans, getting farmers answers when they need to buy seed, equipment, or land.

Protect Farmers From Trump’s Illegal, Devastating Tariffs Abdul will fight back against Donald Trump’s illegal trade wars and work to refund farmers for the costs his devastating tariffs have inflicted on farms across the state.

He will support the Tariff Free Farming Act , which would cap tariffs on seed, fertilizer, feed, fuel, machinery, and other farm inputs at their January 2025 levels, even under emergency trade powers.

Expand Market Access for Farms, Strengthen Local Food Systems, And Invest In Sustainable Aviation Fuel: Abdul will invest in local and regional food systems to open up new market opportunities for farmers and expand access to healthy food, including boosting value-added processing, promoting farm-to-school, and expanding independent meat processing infrastructure.

He will support the bipartisan Local Farmers Feeding our Communities Act , which would restore funding to connect local farmers with community food programs like food banks—giving Michigan growers a dependable local buyer and families fresh food grown by their neighbors.

Abdul will fight for federal incentives to invest in biofuels, including sustainable aviation fuels, to give Michigan family farmers more domestic markets for their products in the face of Donald Trump’s trade wars that have eliminated export markets.
Protect Michigan Farms from PFAS and Safeguard Our Water Michigan farmers shouldn’t pay the price for environmental contamination they didn’t cause.
Abdul will fight for federal funding to test affected farms, compensate farmers for lost income, and hold polluters responsible.
He will expand conservation programs that help farmers protect the Great Lakes, reduce runoff, and build resilience to extreme weather.
Create Opportunities For Young Farmers To Get Started For every farmer under 35, there are four who are 65 or older.
Abdul will pass the bipartisan Increasing Land Access, Security, and Opportunities Act to permanently fund help with down payments, succession planning, and clear land titles for beginning farmers.
He will invest in agricultural education, from high school career programs to community colleges and MSU Extension.
He will expand low-interest USDA loans and down payment assistance for new farmers, and fight to keep large corporate and investor buyers from outbidding families for farmland.

added: Kevin Abel has called North Fulton home since 1990.
He built a local business, chaired the Georgia Department of Transportation Board and knows firsthand how quickly a health crisis can become a financial crisis for families.
He's ready to deliver for us on day one.
Now he needs your vote.
Find where to vote → Fulton County Early Voting Information and Locations → Ready to help?
Fund our effort to reach every voter.
Three Ways to Vote for Kevin VOTE EARLY, IN PERSON October 13 to 30 at any Fulton County early voting site.
Weekdays 7am to 7pm, with Saturday and Sunday hours.
Skip the Election Day lines.
VOTE BY MAIL Request your absentee ballot by Friday, October 23.
Return it to a drop box by October 30, or mail it so it arrives by 7pm on November 3.
VOTE ON ELECTION DAY Tuesday, November 3, 7am to 7pm at your assigned polling place.
Bring a valid photo ID, such as a Georgia driver's license or free Georgia voter ID card.
Look for Kevin Abel, Democrat, under State Senate District 14 on your ballot.
And vote all the way down the ballot: every race counts.

Check my registration and polling place Find Early voting locations Ready to Deliver for North Fulton Kevin and his wife, Cindy, built a North Fulton technology company that created jobs and provided good benefits.
He chaired the Georgia Department of Transportation Board and founded Mobility Atlanta.
And as a stage-four cancer survivor, he knows what it means to face a serious illness while worrying about insurance.

In the State Senate, Kevin will: Make housing affordable for the teachers, first responders and nurses who serve our communities Expand access to affordable healthcare, so Georgians can see a doctor when they need one Overturn Georgia's abortion ban and keep medical decisions between women and their doctors Fully fund public schools and raise teacher pay Fight for North Fulton's fair share of transportation funding to cut traffic See Kevin's Full Platform Stand with Kevin Every dollar helps us reach North Fulton voters before Election Day on November 3.
Donate $25 Donate $50 Donate $100 Donate $250 Donate $500 Donate $1000 Donate $2500 Donate $3300 Donate OTHER Help Get Out the Vote!
The race will be won in the final weeks.
Knock doors, make calls, send texts, write postcards, deliver yard signs or greet voters at the polls on Election Day.
Every shift helps a North Fulton neighbor get to the polls.

Volunteer Today Georgia Senate District 14 Georgia Senate District 14 is located in northern Metro Atlanta, entirely within Fulton County, covering parts of Alpharetta, Johns Creek, Roswell, Sandy Springs, and northeast Atlanta.

added: Home Meet Alex Endorsements Contribute More Home Meet Alex Endorsements Contribute Home Meet Alex Endorsements Contribute active in our community A little bit about Alex Alex Dallman is currently serving in his third term as your State Representative and has been appointed to serve on the powerful budget writing Committee on Joint Finance.
Alex began his career by serving our local communities in the office of our local Republican Congressman.
He is a member and volunteer in the Green Lake County Republican Party, previously serving as the role of Chairman.
He also enjoys golfing, hunting, fundraising for the Markesan Food Pantry, and continuing to be a member of both the Green Lake County Farm Bureau and Manchester Rod & Gun Club.
removed: Home Meet Alex Endorsements Contribute More Home Meet Alex Endorsements Contribute Home Meet Alex Endorsements Contribute A little bit about Alex Alex Dallman is currently serving in his third term as your State Representative and has been appointed to serve on the powerful budget writing Committee on Joint Finance.

He began his career in constituent services for the Office of Congressman Glenn Grothman, which serves Wisconsin’s 6th Congressional District and encompasses the majority of the 39th State Assembly District.
Through his work on behalf of the Congressman, Alex specialized in assisting constituents in the areas of veterans affairs and tax issues.
Alex also served as Outreach Representative for the Office of Congressman Glenn Grothman.
He is a member and volunteer in the Green Lake County Republican Party, most recently serving as its Chairman since 2018.

He also enjoys officiating youth basketball, golfing, hunting, fundraising for the Markesan Food Pantry, and continuing to be a member of both the Green Lake County Farm Bureau and Manchester Rod & Gun Club.

added: Skip to content Home About Alexi’s Priorities News In the News Contact Volunteer Contribute Home About Alexi’s Priorities News In the News Contact Volunteer Contribute Home About Alexi’s Priorities News In the News Contact Home About Alexi’s Priorities News In the News Contact Contribute June 6, 2023 Secretary of State Giannoulias Charges Coinbase in Groundbreaking Suit Illinois is among 10 states initiating legal actions against crypto exchange for violating securities laws Illinois Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias and other state regulators have taken legal action against crypto exchange platform Coinbase Global, Inc. and Coinbase, Inc. for violations of securities laws.
“This action will protect consumers and investors to ensure they can make informed and safe decisions in Illinois and across the nation,” Giannoulias said.

“Illinoisans who invest their money in Coinbase or any other digital asset trading business deserve both security and transparency and my office intends to hold crypto companies to the highest standards.” The Illinois Secretary of State’s Securities Department is a member of a task force alongside nine other state securities regulators charging Coinbase for its violation of securities laws in connection with the company’s staking offerings.
Staking is the process of holding a certain number of digital assets on a blockchain to facilitate processing transactions and to earn a return on the investment.

Coinbase operated staking offerings where small to mid-sized investors could turn over their assets to Coinbase, which in turn would manage the process of staking and then takes a cut of the profits before sharing them with investors.
This action alleges Coinbase failed to register its staking offerings with the Securities Department.

Registration would have given Illinoisans considering investing their money with Coinbase the opportunity to evaluate the risks involved and compare Coinbase’s staking offerings with other investments.
Registering an offer or sale of securities ensures investors receive all material information needed to evaluate the risks of participating in an investment, including in staking offerings.
The Secretary of State Securities Department determined Coinbase offered its staking offerings to Illinois residents without registering those securities.
Of Coinbase’s nearly 3.5 million accounts holding staking offerings, over 140,000 were issued to Illinois investors.
Additionally, Coinbase is not a member of the FDIC or SIPC, which means investors are not protected from Coinbase’s losses.
A copy of the Illinois Secretary of State Securities Department’s Notice of Hearing can be reviewed here .
Other states on this task force include California, Kentucky, Maryland, New Jersey, Alabama, South Carolina, Vermont, Washington, and Wisconsin.
Investors of Coinbase with complaints about their staking offerings may file a complaint with the Securities Department here.
Investors should also reach out to the Securities Department at 1-800-628-7937 to check the registration status of a firm before investing their money in staking offerings.
The Securities Department licenses and regulates financial services, including investment advisers, loan brokers, and business brokers.

[image: IT’S TIME FOR A BREAKUP. 24 YEARS IS LONG ENOUGH! The first step toward restoring public safety in New York is fixing our broken bail reform laws. As a candidate for State Senate, I fully support this mission, and as a state legislator, I will fight to make these long-overdue changes. @sarithaforny , candidate for Attorney General, and I share the same commitment to public safety. This election gives New Yorkers an opportunity to replace longtime incumbents like Liz Krueger and Letitia James with leaders who will put the safety of innocent people first. According to the NYPD, the number of individuals arrested three or more times for felony assault has increased by 205.6% since 2018. In May, 76-year-old retired teacher Ross Falzone died after being pushed down subway stairs. The man charged with his murder had four prior arrests that year and had been released from psychiatric evaluation just hours earlier. This is just one of numerous tragedies raising serious concerns about repeat violent offenders. Not every victim dies. Many survive brutal assaults, stabbings and other violent crimes, carrying physical and emotional trauma for the rest of their lives. How many more innocent New Yorkers must suffer before we change the dangerous laws that have failed to protect them? A retired Army combat veteran, a healthcare worker, a mother and grandmother, and a tireless advocate for veterans, families, and reproductive rights, she has spent her life in service to others.
Maryland is lucky she chose to call it home.
When it matters most, Alleria shows up and that is exactly who we need making decisions in Annapolis.
I am proud to support her campaign for State Delegate." - - Congresswoman April McLain-Delaney “I am proud to endorse Alleria Stanley for the Maryland House of Delegates.
Alleria is a dedicated leader whose record of service reflects both her deep commitment to public good and her readiness to lead.

She will fight tirelessly for the people she represents, and I look forward to seeing all she will accomplish in the legislature.” — Sarah McBride, US Representative, Delaware “I am proud to endorse Alleria Stanley for Maryland House of Delegates for District 4.
Frederick families are being priced out of their own neighborhoods, and Alleria has built a housing platform that meets that reality head on.
She backs reforming the transfer tax to lower closing costs for first time buyers, and social housing models that use public land to build mixed income communities..
She backs zoning reform for missing middle housing, statewide Just Cause eviction protection and the elimination of predatory rental fees.
Her work on tenant protection mirrors work I am pursuing in The City of Frederick.
Alleria's healthcare agenda draws directly from her twenty years as a military medical leader.
She wants to treat healthcare delivery as community infrastructure, expanding regional clinic networks, funding mobile health units, and protecting Maryland's community health centers.
She has committed to defending the for school based mental health programs and to funding youth psychiatric care.
She wants real teeth behind Maryland's Prescription Drug Affordability Board and a transparent Medicaid model that cuts out predatory pharmacy benefit managers.
Alleria understands that healthcare access and financial stability are the same fight.
District 4 needs a delegate who is willing to fight for the real issues that impact our communities.
Alleria will be that delegate.” — César Díaz, City Council President of Frederick Newsletter Block This newsletter signup form needs a storage option.

removed: Johnson, II Endorses Amanda Hollowell for Congress SAVANNAH, GA (April 22, 2026) — Today, Mayor Van R.
Johnson, II of Savannah endorsed Democrat Amanda Hollowell’s campaign for Congress.

Since launching her campaign in August 2025, Hollowell has met with community members across the district to hear their concerns and share her vision to put power, policy, and progress back in the hands of the people.

Read More Hannah Vega 3/3/26 Hannah Vega 3/3/26 State and Local Leaders Endorse Amanda Hollowell for Congress SAVANNAH, GA (March 3, 2026) — Today, leaders from Georgia’s First Congressional District and across the state endorsed Democrat Amanda Hollowell’s campaign for Congress.
Since launching her campaign in August 2025, Hollowell has met with community members from Chatham, Liberty.
Glynn, Ware, Wayne, Camden, Appling counties and more to hear their concerns and share her vision to put power, policy, and progress back in the hands of the people.
Today’s endorsements are a clear demonstration of the support Hollowell has earned and the coalition she is forming to win the open seat in November.

added: Press Room Events & Appearances Healthcare Plan Core Priorities Volunteer Contribute RALPH AMBROSIO FOR CONGRESS (NY-20) Healthcare Policy Brief: Restoring Market Discipline, Patient Power, and Lowering Costs Executive Overview America’s healthcare crisis is not the result of free-market failure; it is the direct consequence of federal distortions that have systematically destroyed price transparency and consumer choice.
In the 20th Congressional District, working families are struggling under high insurance premiums, ballooning deductibles, and opaque medical bills.
To lower the cost of living and deliver real economic relief, Ralph Ambrosio advocates for fundamental, market-based reforms.

By addressing the core structural flaw of American healthcare—the severance of the direct financial relationship between patient and provider—we can introduce living, breathing incentives for affordability, quality, and competition.
The Core Problem: The Third-Party Payer Trap The healthcare market is crippled by a single structural issue: the person receiving care is almost never the person paying for it.
Loss of Consumer Discipline: Roughly 90 cents of every healthcare dollar in the United States is paid by a third party—either a private insurer or the government.
Elimination of Price Competition: Because patients do not directly spend their own money, they are prevented from shopping around, comparing costs, or questioning inflated service fees.
Distorted Tax Incentives: This system was artificially created by the tax code's exclusion of employer-sponsored health insurance from taxable income.
Originating from World War II wage controls and codified in 1954, this tax break suppresses direct cash wages, chains workers to their employers, and crowds out direct consumer direct care.
Strategic Solutions & Legislative Action Plan 1.
Universal Expansion of Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) The single most effective step toward restoring consumer power is expanding Health Savings Accounts.
When individuals control their own pre-tax medical dollars, direct price discipline returns to the marketplace.
Remove Plan Eligibility Restrictions: Uncouple HSA eligibility from rigid high-deductible health plan requirements.
Follow the Consumer: Allow HSAs to follow the individual across all plan types, including short-term limited-duration insurance, health-sharing arrangements, and direct primary care models.
Expand Contribution Limits & Usage: Build upon contribution expansions to ensure pre-tax dollars can be saved continuously throughout a worker's lifetime to cover routine direct medical expenses.
Restoring Direct Patient-Provider Relationships By encouraging direct direct purchasing, we eliminate bureaucratic insurance middlemen for routine care and drive down baseline costs.
Support Direct Primary Care (DPC): Clarify tax rules to ensure DPC memberships and direct direct payments to local clinics are fully qualified medical expenses under HSAs.
Mandate Real Price Transparency: Require hospitals and medical networks to publish upfront, cash-choice pricing so patients can evaluate value before receiving treatment.
Equalizing Tax Incentives for Working Families Workplace-based insurance should not hold a monopoly on tax advantages.
Ralph Ambrosio supports tax fairness that puts individual purchasing power on equal footing with corporate spending, returning control to employees and increasing wage growth potential.
Policy Contrast Matrix Policy Area Ralph Ambrosio’s Market Vision Paul Tonko’s Status Quo Record Core Philosophy Patient-driven, market choice, and price discipline.
Top-down bureaucratic regulation and expanded subsidies.
Cost Control Expanding HSAs, direct purchasing, and price transparency.
Government spending programs that mask true prices and fuel inflation.
Consumer Flexibility Unchaining care from employers; universal HSA access.
Restrictive plan mandates that limit patient choices.
Impact on Wages Reducing employer tax distortions to unlock higher cash wages.
High compliance overhead suppressing wage growth for workers.
Conclusion Restoring healthcare affordability requires replacing government-created opacity with direct direct consumer choice.

By expanding HSAs and opening the market to real competition, Ralph Ambrosio will deliver a practical policy shift that lowers costs, improves care quality, and protects the direct financial sovereignty of families across New York’s 20th District.

References https://www.cato.org/commentary/why-healthcare-so-expensive-america-what-do-about-it https://freedomcaucus.org/put-patients-back-in-charge-of-their-healthcare/ Ralph Ambrosio for Congress Powered by CampaignPartner.com - Political Websites Press Room Events & Appearances Healthcare Plan Core Priorities Volunteer Contribute Close Menu

Join Dawn Richardson & Amelia Rabroker, two educators and candidates for the Texas House, for a meet & greet and candid conversation about women’s rights, the freedom to read, public education, and the decisions being made in the Texas Legislature.
We’ll look at Texas legislation impacting women and families—including SB 8 and HB 1280—along with laws affecting books and materials in Texas schools, such as HB 900 and SB 13.
Come learn what these laws do, ask questions, hear where the candidates stand, and understand why the people we elect to the Texas Legislature matter.
Get informed.
Ask questions.
Make your voice heard at the ballot box.

added: 0 Skip to Content News About Platform Endorsements Volunteer Events Join us Merch Donate Open Menu Close Menu News About Platform Endorsements Volunteer Events Join us Merch Donate Open Menu Close Menu News About Platform Endorsements Folder: Volunteer Back Events Join us Merch Donate Campaign Statement ICE agents shot a Bronx father in front of his son.
Abolish ICE Now.

October 9, 2026 Bronx, NY — On October 9, a day after Oscar Belgal was shot by an ICE agent in the Bronx, NY-15 candidate Andre Easton released the following statement: “Yesterday, I picked up my three boys from school.
That same afternoon, an ICE agent shot another Bronx father, Oscar Belgal, in the neck while his five-year-old son sat in the car.
This injustice sickens me.
I can’t stop picturing my own children in that seat, and the trauma they would carry for the rest of their lives if this happened to them.
“ICE agents fired seven shots into Oscar’s car, putting in danger every parent picking up their child from school and every worker returning home.
We cannot have masked men brandishing AR-15s running around our communities with a license to shoot whomever they deem a threat.
That the killers of Renee Nicole Good and Alex Pretti still have not been charged has sent a signal to ICE agents everywhere that they are above the law.
For the protection of our neighbors, we must abolish ICE and kick every ICE agent out of our communities.
“This injustice reflects the betrayal of both establishment parties.
Time and again, Democrats have failed to deliver meaningful immigration reform, leaving millions of workers vulnerable.
Now Trump and his team of billionaire bigots feel empowered to unleash state-sanctioned violence on immigrant communities, threatening the rights and safety of us all.
“New York City calls itself a sanctuary city.
In practice, our neighbors are still terrified to go to work, to buy groceries for their families, to pick up their children from school.
ICE agents lurk in parking lots across the city, ready to round up immigrant workers, including the lot at 40 West 225th St., blocks from where agents fired seven rounds into Oscar’s car.
“We cannot accept a world where armed, rogue agents terrorize families and violently round up working people for deportation.
We need immediate action to defund, abolish, and expel ICE from our cities.
“Ritchie Torres, who currently represents New York’s 15th Congressional District in the Bronx, has voted for pro-ICE legislation.
This includes Trump’s draconian Laken Riley Act.
Now, with this injustice unfolding in his own borough, he has exposed his cowardice by refusing to call for ICE’s abolition.
Instead, he is asking for an “investigation” and for ICE to release footage of the shooting.
“To call these demands inadequate is an understatement.
They are a betrayal of the Bronx.
“By bringing up Oscar’s past interactions with law enforcement, none of which justify shooting him and endangering his child, NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch helped demonize him.
Tisch and the NYPD are effectively running cover for the Trump administration, which works overtime to paint all immigrant workers as criminals.
“Jessica Tisch must be fired.
But she is not the only one responsible for the city’s collaboration with ICE.
The real onus is on the mayor, who was elected with the backing and support of the immigrant rights movement and must be held accountable.
It is good the mayor has called to abolish ICE, but now he must fully enforce his own Executive Order 13 and kick every ICE agent out of our city.
They shouldn’t be able to use any public parking lots as staging grounds.
They shouldn’t be at Rikers.
A lot more can be done to obstruct Trump’s rampaging paramilitaries.
“We won’t end ICE terror by relying on the same politicians who built the deportation machine and keep funding it.
We need a mass movement powerful enough to dismantle it and win full, equal, and permanent rights for all immigrants.
“Immigrant workers keep this country running, not billionaires.
The same billionaire class that has made super-profits from their exploitation is now turning around to intimidate and scapegoat them for the country’s problems.
The tens of billions of dollars going to ICE need to be redirected to good jobs, our schools, our housing, and our healthcare.
Full rights for all immigrants, now.” info@andreforthebronx.nyc PAID FOR BY ANDRE EASTON FOR CONGRESS 2026

Proposed Marine Tariff Increase 10/08/2025 12:06 PM The Office of Senator Angel L.

Bolques Jr., Senator At Large, is conducting this survey to ensure that any proposed rate adjustments by V.I.P.A. reflect transparency, fairness, and the economic realities of Virgin Islanders—especially those on St.
John, where higher import costs already affect daily living.
Your input will help guide legislative oversight, promote accountability, and protect residents and small businesses from unreasonable financial burdens.

This survey seeks feedback from residents, business owners, and community stakeholders across the Virgin Islands regarding the Virgin Islands Port Authority’s (V.I.P.A.) proposed increases and new fees under its marine tariff structure.
Read More 02 Oct Senator Bolques Stands Firm Against New Fees That Punish St.
John Residents 10/02/2025 12:54 PM St.
John, U.S.
Virgin Islands — Senator At Large, Angel L.
Bolques Jr. is strongly opposing the Virgin Islands Port Authority’s (VIPA) proposed marine and parking fees, calling them regressive and unfair to the people of St.
John—an island already carrying the highest cost of living and the least access to public services in the territory.
The proposed fees include: An Additional Passenger Fee for Non-Drivers at the Red Hook Barge Ramp.
A Cargo Overflow Staging Fee and A Paid Parking System at the Victor Sewer Marine Facility lot (across from the Cruz Bay Post Office).
Unlike St.
Thomas and St.
Croix, St.
John lacks full-service public infrastructure, including a fully operational fire station, a Human Services office, a Youth and Recreation Center, and medical facilities, among others.
Many government departments do not maintain full local offices on St.
John, and those that do often operate with limited hours, reduced staff, or restricted services.
As a result, residents are often forced to travel to St.
Thomas at their own expense for essential services, appointments, and basic necessities.

Read More 01 Oct Senator Bolques Honors Fireburn Queens on Contract Day 10/01/2025 01:01 PM Read More 23 Sep BOLQUES BULLETIN - SEPTEMBER TO OCTOBER 2025 EDITION 09/23/2025 04:36 PM Dear Virgin Islanders,Since the last edition of the Bolques Bulletin, I’ve remained fully engaged—immersed and focused in legislative hearings, meetings, site visits, and community events that reflect the pulse of our people.
Many of these moments are too numerous to list, but each one strengthens my resolve to serve you with purpose, humility, and unmatched dedication.
Whether advancing healthcare, preserving culture, or supporting economic growth, my work on your behalf continues—with consistency and conviction.
I believe leadership means showing up, listening, and taking action—and that’s exactly what I’ve been doing.
Here are just a few recent highlights: Attended the Ribbon Cutting Ceremony for the VI Diabetes Center of Excellence, expanding healthcare access for our residents.
Toured Cruzan Rum, a cornerstone of our economy, to advocate for the strength of the Rum Cover-Over Program.
Connected with the CDRA Board and attended the Cash Days Racing preview events, and met with and lobbied for support for the organization through VIPA and DSPR.
Visited the Early Head Start facility with Lutheran Social Services to address pressing challenges and assisted them with WAPA issues.
Licensing issues, and lobbied for appropriation.
I remain right here with you, doing the work every day.

With gratitude, integrity, and purpose, Sincerely,Angel Bolques Jr., Senator-At-Large Read More 11 Sep Senator At Large Angel Bolques Jr. to Present Major Road Protection Bill 36-0110 - After 56 Years, the Virgin Islands is Finally Regulating our Public Road Excavation—For Real 09/11/2025 01:47 PM Senator At Large Angel Bolques Jr. to Present Major Road Protection Bill 36-0110 After 56 Years, the Virgin Islands is Finally Regulating our Public Road Excavation—For Real Read More 05 Jun Senator At Large Angel Bolques Jr.

100 Day Report - 2025 06/05/2025 07:49 PM To the People of the Virgin Islands, It is an honor and my duty to share this 100-day Report with you, highlighting the progress we have made together in the first months of2025.
As your Senator-At-Large, I remain fully committed to building a Virgin Islands that is safer, stronger, and more inclusive for everyone.

From passing meaningful legislation to advancing infrastructure projects, engaging with our communities, and strengthening regionalities, my focus has been on delivering results that benefit every resident of our beautiful Virgin Islands.

Virgin Islands – Senator Angel L.
Bolques, Jr. is proud to join the Virgin Islands in celebrating the U.S.
Department of Agriculture's approval of a waiver request that will unlock critical funding for the restoration of water infrastructure at the historic Estate Bethlehem site.
This waiver paves the way for the St.
Croix Farmers in Action (FIA) to rehabilitate a million-gallon cistern, bolstering sustainable agriculture and water security for the island's farming community.

Read More 04 May Disappointment in Taxicab Commission Executive Director 05/04/2023 08:40 AM Senator-At-Large Angel Bolques, Jr. expressed his dissatisfaction with the lack of service and communication from the Virgin Islands Taxicab Commission.

His office has been inundated with calls over the past two weeks regarding the commission being closed for at least the last few months due to what is being stated as "unsafe work conditions." Though Senator Bolques does not advocate working in an unsafe environment, Senator Bolques does not understand why the commission's Executive Director has not taken any actions to continue the commission's work via e-government protocols or collaborating with other government departments, agencies, boards, or commissions to work out of another location to curtail the lapse of services.
"Based on several discussions with Taxi-Men and Taxi-Women, I am being told that employees are working from home and are unreachable or cannot provide the required service," Bolques stated.

"Even in this hybrid and remote work era, leadership in those roles must still be held accountable for executing and completing their tasks and responsibilities." It was also brought to the Senator's attention that there is no online service option during this closure, further complicating the situation and impeding those needing plates, medallions, renewals, etc.

"The fact that drivers cannot work legally because they cannot access services is completely unacceptable." Senator Bolques continued, "This is the livelihood and main or only source of income for these people, and the entire commission is responsible for this lapse in management, execution, customer service, and overall interest in assisting them; I have tried on numerous occasions to contact the office myself with no avail" Bolques concluded.

Congratulates USVI Track Star Michelle Smith on Her No.
1 Ranking In the Under 18 Category at Millrose Games in New York City 02/14/2023 07:48 PM St.
Croix- On February 11, Michelle Mycah Leonie Smith achieved a winning time of 1:29:52 in the 600-meter race at the Millrose Games in New York, and in so doing, propelled herself to become No.
1 in the world for the under 18 category.

As a member of the Virgin Islands Track and Field Team and native Crucian, Michelle Smith has recast the spotlight on our beloved territory, where world-class athletes from multiple sports disciplines are raised and trained.
“It cannot be overstated how significant Ms.
Smith’s achievement is to become the 9th fastest high school girl in history in the 600M,” Senator Angel L.
Bolques, Jr., stated.
On behalf of the Office of the Senator-At-Large, I am so proud of her and give thanks to her parents, who also were track stars, and her coaches who have groomed her,” Senator Bolques continued.

“Michelle Smith is another shining example in a long legacy of outstanding student-athletes from the Virgin Islands who demonstrate that unprecedented accomplishments are attainable even amidst formidable challenges,” Senator Bolques concluded.

Proposed Marine Tariff Increase 10/08/2025 12:06 PM The Office of Senator Angel L.

Bolques Jr., Senator At Large, is conducting this survey to ensure that any proposed rate adjustments by V.I.P.A. reflect transparency, fairness, and the economic realities of Virgin Islanders—especially those on St.
John, where higher import costs already affect daily living.
Your input will help guide legislative oversight, promote accountability, and protect residents and small businesses from unreasonable financial burdens.

This survey seeks feedback from residents, business owners, and community stakeholders across the Virgin Islands regarding the Virgin Islands Port Authority’s (V.I.P.A.) proposed increases and new fees under its marine tariff structure.
Read More 02 Oct Senator Bolques Stands Firm Against New Fees That Punish St.
John Residents 10/02/2025 12:54 PM St.
John, U.S.
Virgin Islands — Senator At Large, Angel L.
Bolques Jr. is strongly opposing the Virgin Islands Port Authority’s (VIPA) proposed marine and parking fees, calling them regressive and unfair to the people of St.
John—an island already carrying the highest cost of living and the least access to public services in the territory.
The proposed fees include: An Additional Passenger Fee for Non-Drivers at the Red Hook Barge Ramp.
A Cargo Overflow Staging Fee and A Paid Parking System at the Victor Sewer Marine Facility lot (across from the Cruz Bay Post Office).
Unlike St.
Thomas and St.
Croix, St.
John lacks full-service public infrastructure, including a fully operational fire station, a Human Services office, a Youth and Recreation Center, and medical facilities, among others.
Many government departments do not maintain full local offices on St.
John, and those that do often operate with limited hours, reduced staff, or restricted services.
As a result, residents are often forced to travel to St.
Thomas at their own expense for essential services, appointments, and basic necessities.

Read More 23 Sep BOLQUES BULLETIN - SEPTEMBER TO OCTOBER 2025 EDITION 09/23/2025 04:36 PM Dear Virgin Islanders,Since the last edition of the Bolques Bulletin, I’ve remained fully engaged—immersed and focused in legislative hearings, meetings, site visits, and community events that reflect the pulse of our people.
Many of these moments are too numerous to list, but each one strengthens my resolve to serve you with purpose, humility, and unmatched dedication.
Whether advancing healthcare, preserving culture, or supporting economic growth, my work on your behalf continues—with consistency and conviction.
I believe leadership means showing up, listening, and taking action—and that’s exactly what I’ve been doing.
Here are just a few recent highlights: Attended the Ribbon Cutting Ceremony for the VI Diabetes Center of Excellence, expanding healthcare access for our residents.
Toured Cruzan Rum, a cornerstone of our economy, to advocate for the strength of the Rum Cover-Over Program.
Connected with the CDRA Board and attended the Cash Days Racing preview events, and met with and lobbied for support for the organization through VIPA and DSPR.
Visited the Early Head Start facility with Lutheran Social Services to address pressing challenges and assisted them with WAPA issues.
Licensing issues, and lobbied for appropriation.
I remain right here with you, doing the work every day.

Donate Contact Gallery Home News and Updates The Bolques Bulletin (A bimestrial newsletter) The Bolques Bulletin (A bimestrial newsletter) 15 Mar 15 Mar Senator-At-Large Angel Bolques, Jr. is excited to announce the release of the inaugural edition of his bimestrial newsletter, the Bolques Bulletin.
This publication intends to keep his colleagues and the territorial public abreast of his team’s activities during this term.
This edition briefly overviews what has transpired since the beginning of his term in the 35th Legislature of the Virgin Islands.
The Bolques Bulletin will be released every two months with the latest information on constituent activity, legislation, and accomplishments from the office of the Senator-At-Large.
“Transparency, community engagement, and communication are vital in building good rapport and public trust,” stated Senator Bolques.
"My office and I look forward to sharing our efforts and work,” said Senator Bolques.

Donate Contact Gallery News and Updates #agricultural innovation USVI 23 Sep BOLQUES BULLETIN - SEPTEMBER TO OCTOBER 2025 EDITION 09/23/2025 04:36 PM Dear Virgin Islanders,Since the last edition of the Bolques Bulletin, I’ve remained fully engaged—immersed and focused in legislative hearings, meetings, site visits, and community events that reflect the pulse of our people.
Many of these moments are too numerous to list, but each one strengthens my resolve to serve you with purpose, humility, and unmatched dedication.
Whether advancing healthcare, preserving culture, or supporting economic growth, my work on your behalf continues—with consistency and conviction.
I believe leadership means showing up, listening, and taking action—and that’s exactly what I’ve been doing.
Here are just a few recent highlights: Attended the Ribbon Cutting Ceremony for the VI Diabetes Center of Excellence, expanding healthcare access for our residents.
Toured Cruzan Rum, a cornerstone of our economy, to advocate for the strength of the Rum Cover-Over Program.
Connected with the CDRA Board and attended the Cash Days Racing preview events, and met with and lobbied for support for the organization through VIPA and DSPR.
Visited the Early Head Start facility with Lutheran Social Services to address pressing challenges and assisted them with WAPA issues.
Licensing issues, and lobbied for appropriation.
I remain right here with you, doing the work every day.

With gratitude, integrity, and purpose, Sincerely,Angel Bolques Jr., Senator-At-Large Read More Home Greetings Objectives LEGISLATIVE WORK Legislative POLICY Agenda Bill Tracking Professional Experience News and Updates Your Support How will my Donation be used?

Read More 02 Oct Senator Bolques Stands Firm Against New Fees That Punish St.
John Residents 10/02/2025 12:54 PM St.
John, U.S.
Virgin Islands — Senator At Large, Angel L.
Bolques Jr. is strongly opposing the Virgin Islands Port Authority’s (VIPA) proposed marine and parking fees, calling them regressive and unfair to the people of St.
John—an island already carrying the highest cost of living and the least access to public services in the territory.
The proposed fees include: An Additional Passenger Fee for Non-Drivers at the Red Hook Barge Ramp.
A Cargo Overflow Staging Fee and A Paid Parking System at the Victor Sewer Marine Facility lot (across from the Cruz Bay Post Office).
Unlike St.
Thomas and St.
Croix, St.
John lacks full-service public infrastructure, including a fully operational fire station, a Human Services office, a Youth and Recreation Center, and medical facilities, among others.
Many government departments do not maintain full local offices on St.
John, and those that do often operate with limited hours, reduced staff, or restricted services.
As a result, residents are often forced to travel to St.
Thomas at their own expense for essential services, appointments, and basic necessities.

Many of these moments are too numerous to list, but each one strengthens my resolve to serve you with purpose, humility, and unmatched dedication.
