removed: Home About Teresa Mission Media DONATE Back to Media & News Campaign Update Sharon Trask Endorses Teresa Fox for Congress Sharon Trask, a Mason County Commissioner, has officially endorsed Teresa Fox for US Representative in Congressional District 6 July 4, 2026 Campaign Staff The Fox for Wa campaign is pleased to announce the personal endorsement by Sharon Trask, Mason County Commissioner, for Teresa Fox running as a Republican for US Representative in the 6th Congressional District in Washington State.
Mason County is one of six counties in the 6th Congressional District.
Sharon Trask has been a servant to the people of Mason County during her term as Commissioner.
Trask said of the endorsement: "Teresa brings real-world experience, strong leadership, and a commitment to serving the people of Washington's 6th Congressional District.

She understands the challenges facing working families, small businesses, and our rural coastal communities because she has spent her career working alongside them." The Fox for Wa campaign is powered by people instead of corporate or political associations.
With all six county Republican Parties endorsing Teresa Fox, we turn our eyes and motivations toward the Primary Election in August with a unified Republican Party backing Fox as a candidate.
Fox said of the endorsement: "Serving in elected office is a privilege to represent the people.
Sharon Trask is a brave woman who stepped forward as a citizen volunteer to lead in her county.
I am honored and humbled to have the endorsement of a successful woman in politics, and a knowledgeable elected official.

We must get the fringe activism out of political office, and return to a pragmatic stewardship of governance for all of 6th Congressional District." Back to all articles Show Your Support Get your official Fox for Congress yard sign and put it proudly on display.

title.before: Teresa Fox at Tacoma Northwest Detention Center

removed: Home About Teresa Mission Media DONATE Back to Media & News Campaign Update Teresa Fox Takes Her Case Directly to Northwest Detention Center Protesters Teresa Fox went directly to the Northwest Detention Center in Tacoma, engaging protesters face-to-face and drawing a sharp contrast with Rep.
Emily Randall over immigration, public safety and the role of a congressional representative.
August 14, 2026 Campaign Staff WA-06 challenger engages activists face-to-face as sharp contrast with Rep.

Emily Randall emerges over immigration, public safety and the role of a congressional representative TACOMA, Wash. — Teresa Fox, candidate for Congress in Washington’s 6th Congressional District, went directly to the Northwest Detention Center in Tacoma to do something increasingly rare in American politics: walk into a crowd that did not agree with her, ask questions, listen to the answers and explain exactly how she believes a member of Congress should make decisions.
The resulting exchange presents a striking contrast between Fox and incumbent Rep.
Emily Randall over immigration enforcement, political rhetoric and what it means to represent Washington’s 6th District.

Randall has made the Northwest Detention Center a recurring focus of her tenure in Congress, visiting the facility 9 times in her first term and publicly accusing the Trump administration of waging a “war on brown people” and calling ICE agents “masked murderers.” Fox arrived with a different question: What do the people gathered there actually want Congress to do?
“As your representative, it’s going to be my job to represent all of the voices in our district,” Fox says at the beginning of the video .

“I want to hear what they have to say, if they have any proposed legislation.” Fox also made clear that she wanted the conversation to include something she believes is too often missing from the national immigration debate: crime victims.
And the experience of families and communities whose loved ones have been victims of preventable crimes committed by criminals in the country illegally.
She then walked into the demonstration.
Rather than delivering remarks from a distance, Fox approached activists and introduced herself as a candidate for the United States House of Representatives.
“I’m running for Congress, and I want to hear what you have to say,” Fox told members of the group.
“What’s your objective?” When protesters described alleged conditions inside the detention facility, Fox did not end the conversation.
She asked them what they wanted their congressional representative to do.
“What kind of legislation would you propose?” Fox asked.
“What kind of changes would you like to actually see?
I was elected, what could I do in office?” That exchange quickly became more confrontational.
Fox stuck with it even as a man with plate armor marched confrontationally toward her team, and then circled her team menacingly.
Some demonstrators compared the detention facility to a concentration camp.
One participant invoked the Holocaust.
Others repeatedly pressed Fox to declare whether she personally believed the facility should exist and challenged her when she declined to answer the question on their terms.
Fox instead returned to the principle she says is a cornerstone of her campaign.
“Here’s the deal, and this is a cornerstone of my campaign,” Fox said.
“I’m going to represent the people.” She then described the standard she says will guide her in Congress: “Number one, I’m going to do what’s legal under the Constitution.
And number two, I’m going to represent the majority of the voices in our district.

That’s my job.” When activists continued pressing Fox for her personal opinion, she rejected the idea that the personal preferences of a member of Congress should override the people that member was elected to represent.
“My personal opinion is absolutely zero in this,” Fox said.
“I have no dog in the fight.

Because I’m supposed to represent the citizens of my district.” She repeated the point moments later: “What the majority of people in our district want to do is what I’m going to do.” The encounter underscores a fundamental difference emerging in the race for Washington’s 6th Congressional District.
Randall has repeatedly used her congressional office to obstruct federal immigration enforcement and scrutinize conditions at federal facilities across the country.
Randall recently stated she has been to the Tacoma facility nine times while she fanned the flames of violent political rhetoric.
Randall calls for the abolishment of ICE and accuses immigration authorities of targeting people based on the color of their skin.
Fox is presenting voters with a very different conception of the job.
Her message at the detention center was not that a member of Congress should arrive with all the answers already decided.
It was that a representative should ask questions, listen to competing voices, stay within the Constitution and ultimately represent the citizens of the District.
The differences were visible in real time.
Fox asked the activists where they were from.
All in the group were from Oregon.
One protestor described the demonstration as an expression of solidarity across the Pacific Northwest.
Fox continued the conversation anyway.
“I’m crossing the aisles,” Fox said during the encounter.
“My platform is people over politics.
I’m here to represent the citizens in my district.
And I want to hear the voices of everybody.” Even as the discussion became increasingly hostile, Fox continued answering questions and asking for specific policy proposals.
Near the end of the exchange, protesters again demanded that she take their position on the detention facility.
Fox gave them the same answer.
“As a representative in the federal Congress, I am going to do what’s legal under the Constitution, first and foremost.” That may be the clearest distinction in the race.
One candidate has characterized current immigration enforcement in sweeping terms involving race, fascism and a war against immigrant communities.

The other walked directly into a protest, asked what people wanted their government to do, listened while they challenged her and refused to substitute political pressure for the obligations she believes come with representative government.
For Fox, the contrast between the Fox for Washington Campaign for the People and the incumbent could not be more clear.
Law and order, with justice for victims or chaos on the streets.
The choice is yours in November.

removed: Home About Teresa Mission Media DONATE Back to Media & News Opinion The Tragedy on Our Streets Why It’s Time to End the 'Homeless Industrial Complex' and Restore Public Safety June 9, 2026 Campaign Staff The Tragedy on Our Streets: Why It’s Time to End the 'Homeless Industrial Complex' and Restore Public Safety I am running to represent Washington’s 6th Congressional District because, like many of you, I look at our communities today and barely recognize them.

Everywhere I go, from Bremerton to the furthest corners of our six-county district, the questions I hear most are centered on a singular, urgent crisis: public safety and the catastrophic state of homelessness on our streets.
For me, this crisis isn't abstract or merely political.
It is deeply personal.
I have friends whose children are dead—stolen away by an unchecked drug epidemic.
We are on the verge of losing an entire generation to narcotics and the crime that follows in their wake.
What we are witnessing is a human tragedy on a scale previously unknown in the United States.
While there are many pathways to homelessness, the horrific reality for those trapped on our streets is universal.
They are subjected to repeated rapes, robberies, and murders.
They are preyed upon by human traffickers, plagued by devastating health conditions from severe drug abuse, and shuffled from corner to corner with no stability.
It is clear to anyone paying attention: the current approach is not just failing—it is actively enabling a humanitarian disaster.
The Cost of a Broken Status Quo For years, our state's failed laws and lenient policies have directly fueled this crisis.
We have asked our law enforcement officers to do more with less, while tying their hands.
Meanwhile, our homeowners, families, and local businesses pay the price through damaged property, lost livelihoods, and a pervasive sense of insecurity.
We can no longer throw billions of taxpayer dollars at this problem without demanding quantifiable results.
For too long, we have funded a "homeless industrial complex"—a network of unaccountable programs and NGOs that profit off the continuation of the crisis rather than its cure.
We must stop enabling dependency and stop encouraging individuals to migrate to our district for limited resources.
It is time to keep more hard-earned money in your pockets and expect real solutions, not endless lip service from career politicians.
A Comprehensive, Accountable Way Forward As your representative in Congress, I will leverage federal avenues to address this public safety and humanitarian emergency.
However, federal intervention cannot be top-down or disconnected from local reality.
Since launching my campaign in February, I have spent my time on the ground, listening to citizens, business owners, and law enforcement personnel across all six counties.
My approach to legislation is built on three cornerstone principles: Inclusive Stakeholder Engagement: Effective policy cannot be written in a vacuum.
It must include the voices of all constituents—including law enforcement, medical professionals, and local business leaders.
Quantifiable Metrics: We must tie every federal dollar to measurable outcomes.
If a program isn't reducing homelessness, curbing addiction, or improving safety, it will lose its funding.
Restoring Law and Order: We must support our police and enforce the law to protect both the public and the vulnerable populations currently being victimized on our streets.
Finding Common Ground This is a complex crisis with no overnight fix, but the first step toward a solution is admitting that the status quo is broken for everyone.
We must approach this challenge with mutual respect for our varying perspectives, look past partisan divides, and find the common ground required to heal our communities.
Public safety is not a partisan issue; it is a fundamental human right.
I ask for your vote as your 6th Congressional Representative so that we can finally prioritize safety, accountability, and compassion for all of us.
To learn more about our platform, share your perspective, or find upcoming campaign events, please visit FOXFORWA.COM .

added: 0 Skip to Content Home About Issues Contact Donate Open Menu Close Menu Home About Issues Contact Donate Open Menu Close Menu Home About Issues Contact Donate TERMS OF SERVICE & Privacy Policy Last Updated: 10/07/2026 This document governs the website and mobile messaging program for Friends of Ian Chamberlin ("we," "us," or "our").
By visiting our website or opting into our messaging program, you agree to the following terms and practices.
TERMS OF SERVICE Mobile Terms of Service.
By providing your phone number and opting in, you consent to receive recurring automated promotional and personalized marketing text messages (e.g., SMS and MMS) from us.
Messages may include campaign updates, event information, volunteer opportunities, and requests for donation.
Consent to receive text messages is program-specific and does not constitute consent to receive calls or messages from other programs or third parties.
Consent to receive automated marketing text messages is not a condition of any purchase or donation.
You may cancel the SMS service at any time.
Text "STOP" to the number from which you received the message.
You will receive a single confirmation message.
After this, you will no longer receive SMS messages from that specific program.
For assistance, reply "HELP" to any message or contact ian@friendsofianchamberlin.com Message frequency varies based on activity and your level of engagement.
Standard message and data rates may apply.
Check with your mobile carrier for details.
Messages may solicit donations.
Consent to receive messages is not a condition of making any donation.
Mobile carriers, including T-Mobile, are not liable for delayed or undelivered messages.
PRIVACY POLICY ​ Information We Collect.
We collect personal information that you provide directly to us, as well as information collected automatically through your use of our website.
Use of Information.
We use the information we collect to: Communicate with you regarding the campaign and your involvement.
Process and report contributions in accordance with applicable law.
Optimize campaign strategy and website performance.
Comply with legal obligations and protect our rights.
Disclosure and Sharing of Information.
We do not sell your personal information.
We may share your information as follows: We share information with vendors, consultants, and other service providers who need access to such information to carry out work on our behalf.
These providers are prohibited from using your information for their own purposes.
We may disclose information if we believe disclosure is required by any applicable law, rule, or regulation, or to comply with law enforcement or legal process.
We may share information with your express consent.

We will not share text messaging originator opt-in data and consent, provided that the foregoing does not apply to sharing (1) with vendors, consultants and other service providers who need access to such information to carry out work on our behalf (and who will not use such information for their own purposes); (2) if we believe disclosure is required by any applicable law, rule, or regulation or to comply with law enforcement or legal process; and (3) if the user consents to our sharing of such information. ​ Third-Party Links.
Our website may contain links to third-party sites.
We are not responsible for the privacy practices of these third parties and encourage you to review their policies.
Security and Children’s Privacy.
We implement reasonable security measures to protect your data.
Our services are not directed to children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from children.
Amendments to this Terms of Service or Privacy Policy.
We might revise this Terms of Service and Privacy Policy occasionally to reflect changes in our methods or for other operational, legal, or regulatory purposes.
Any amendments will be immediately effective upon the updated Terms of Service and Privacy Policy's posting on our website.
We encourage you to check this page periodically to stay updated about our privacy practices.
Contact Information.
Friends of Ian Chamberlin Ian Chamberlin ian@friendsofianchamberlin.com Like many other websites and online services, We do not currently alter our practices when we receives Do Not Track signals.
To find out more about “Do Not Track,” you may wish to visit http://www.allaboutdnt.com .
Donations Contributors may not remain anonymous by request.
If a contributor does not want to be identified, the contribution should not be made.
Under Ohio law, individuals, political action committees, and certain organizations may contribute subject to applicable limits and reporting requirements ($16,615.57 per Individual/PAC).
Contributions from corporations and labor organizations are prohibited.
State law requires that Friends of Ian Chamberlin collect and report name, address, occupation, and employer of each contributor.
Contributions from foreign nationals are prohibited by law.
Donations are not deductible as charitable donations for federal or state income tax purposes.

Checkout Continue Shopping Accepted here Friends of Nancy Valdez Let's go HOME YOUR VOICE DONATION EVENTS CONTACT ME REGISTER TO VOTE GALLERY VOLUNTEER More MEET NANCY VALDEZ A New Voice for District 31 My name is Nancy Valdez, and I am running for State House Representative in District 31.
Like many local families who call Hawaiʻi home, I know firsthand how challenging it can be to make ends meet.
As a single mother of four wonderful boys, I worked a full-time job and two side jobs to provide for my family.
Trying to balance work, family responsibilities, and being there for every one of my sons’ school and sporting events was not easy.
But like so many parents, I did everything I could to support my children and give them the best opportunities possible.
Sadly, many local families are facing the same struggles today.
The high cost of living and limited opportunities have forced some of our loved ones to move to the mainland in search of more affordable living and a better future.
Two of my own sons have made that difficult decision.
No family should have to choose between staying in Hawaiʻi and being able to afford a decent life.
That is why I am running for office.
I want to fight for our working families, our kūpuna, and everyone who wants to continue calling Hawaiʻi home.
Our people work hard, yet the rising cost of housing, groceries, utilities, and taxes continues to put enormous pressure on household budgets.
I believe our residents deserve more than just getting by.
They deserve the opportunity to live, work, raise their families, and retire with dignity in the place they love.

As your State Representative for District 31, I will work to be a voice for the people, advocate for responsible government, and push for solutions that make Hawaiʻi more affordable for the generations who call these islands home.
Together, we can work toward a Hawaiʻi where our children can afford to stay, our families can thrive, and our kūpuna can enjoy the retirement they deserve.
GOVERNMENT ACCOUNTABILITY We need term limits for all elected officials to bring fresh perspectives, encourage new leadership, and give more citizens the opportunity to serve their communities.
Our government should represent the people, not allow political power to remain in the same hands indefinitely.
The people deserve transparency and accountability.

OUR KEIKI We need to provide healthier, more nutritious meals in our schools and teach financial literacy to help our children become financially responsible, informed, and productive citizens who are prepared for the future.
OUR KŪPUNA Our kūpuna deserve dignity, respect, and affordable living.
We must protect their well-being, support their needs, and ensure they can enjoy their golden years here in Hawaiʻi, surrounded by the families and communities they love.

In the ad, which will join the campaign’s seven-figure statewide rotation, Coach Buc calls out Abbott’s failed leadership, from property taxes going up #% to schools being forced to close their doors and move to four-day weeks while his corporate donors get rich off Texans’ backs.
WATCH THE FULL AD HERE.
From her time in the legislature fighting alongside MAGA moms to defeat vouchers in 2023 to now, Hinojosa has built a broad coalition by meeting Texans in their communities where they are.

Now, she’s leading Abbott in multiple independent polls – including winning over 9% of Republican voters – because Texans are ready for her to deliver on her plan to secure the American Dream by saving public schools and putting money in people’s pockets.
Transcript: Tim Buchanan: I’m Coach Buchanan.
As a football coach, I won eight state championships.
I know how to read a scoreboard.
Under Greg Abbott, the billionaires are up, and Texas is down.
Taxes are through the roof.
Parents stressed out.
That’s Abbott’s corruption, and it’s costing us everything.
I voted for Abbott three times, but I’m getting off the sidelines for Gina Hinojosa.
Gina’s running for governor to take on the billionaires and always put our kids first.

added: Skip to content Skip to main content Elect Ginny Ehrhart State Representative HD-36 Menu Home Meet Ginny Top Issues News Contact Facebook-f Instagram DONATE Meet Ginny I am honored to represent House District 36, which includes portions of western Cobb County, a community I have proudly called home for more than 45 years.
As the daughter of a U.S.
Army Lieutenant Colonel, I was raised on military bases across the country before my family eventually settled in Cobb County.
I attended Osborne High School and later graduated from Auburn University with a degree in International Trade.
Throughout my career, I have been blessed with a variety of opportunities that have shaped my perspective and strengthened my commitment to public service.
I taught high school economics and American government, homeschooled my children, and built a successful small business.
I also became a frequent speaker on regional and national television and radio, sharing my passion for Southern cuisine and hospitality.

As a television chef and home life consultant for FamilyNet Television, I authored two cookbooks, Sunday in the South and Seasons in the South, and hosted a popular weekly lifestyle radio show on Atlanta’s 920 AM.
My experiences as a hands-on small business owner, educator, entrepreneur, wife, and mother have deeply influenced my conservative principles and approach to governing.
I believe in supporting public safety, fostering a pro-business environment, and strengthening educational opportunities for our children.
I strive to bring a practical, common-sense, and solutions-oriented perspective to the Georgia General Assembly because I believe that is exactly what the people of our district deserve.

My husband, Earl, and I live in Powder Springs, where we enjoy spending time with our six grown children, four grandchildren, and our talented Australian Shepherd, Dixie. - Ginny Ehrhart Donate Your Support Today Will Make the Difference I’m running for reelection because our community deserves experienced conservative leadership that will continue fighting for our values and our future.

added: Skip to content About Delivered Promises Delivered Projects MN District 3 News Get Involved Contact About Delivered Promises Delivered Projects MN District 3 News Get Involved Contact Donate RELEASE: Hauschild Ad Draws Sharp Contrast Between his Opponent’s Tax-and-Slash Past and His Record of Delivering for the Northland The ad highlights Iron Range residents sharing their experiences with Hauschild and Zupancich FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE HERMANTOWN, MN. — On Thursday, Senator Grant Hauschild released the third tv ad of his 2026 reelection campaign, highlighting his work to support local law enforcement, strengthen rural emergency medical services, and deliver property tax relief for Northland families.
WATCH HERE.
The ad contrasts Hauschild’s legislative record of investments in public safety and tax relief with that of his opponent Andrea Zupancich.
As mayor of Babbitt, Zupancich raised property taxes by one of the highest in the state and still tried to cut funding for police and first responders.
Hauschild has made public safety, emergency medical services, and cutting the cost of living key priorities during his first term in the Minnesota Senate.
He championed legislation providing state funding for rural ambulance services, and this year delivered $125 million of property tax relief for Minnesota homeowners.
In addition, Senator Hauschild secured $515 in on-going property tax credits for every household in the Taconite Assistance Area which includes the community of Babbitt.
Transcript of ATM We all live on the Range … And we all support our state senator … Grant Hauschild.
Grant secured state funding for our police.
And championed rural ambulance aid.
While cutting property taxes for Northland families.
We also know mayor Andrea Zupancich.
She raised property taxes by 20 percent … And tried to cut police and first responders.
Now Andrea Zupancich wants to go to the State Senate?
She’d fit right in down there.
Grant Hauschild’s got our vote.
ABOUT GRANT HAUSCHILD Grant Hauschild represents Senate District 3 in the Minnesota Senate, which includes the Arrowhead, Iron Range, North Shore, and much of the Northland.

First elected to the Senate in 2022, Hauschild has focused on delivering results for rural communities, supporting working people, families and seniors, strengthening local economies, standing up to Big Tech, and making sure Northern Minnesota receives its fair share of state investment.
Hauschild has delivered on bringing down the cost of living and defending rural healthcare, investing in jobs, and preventing fraud.

He was instrumental in stabilizing rural emergency medical services by securing new funding and a Northern Minnesota Sprint medic pilot program, and delivered millions of dollars in public safety funding for local police and fire departments across the Northland.

Hauschild has also helped deliver historic tax relief, including the largest Social Security tax relief legislation in Minnesota history, ensuring that over 80% of Minnesota seniors no longer pay income tax on their benefits.
In 2026 he secured $125 million in property tax relief for Minnesota households.
Before serving in the Senate, Hauschild worked in rural economic development for the U.S.
Department of Agriculture, and as a labor policy aide for U.S.
Senator Heidi Heitkamp, before serving on the Hermantown City Council.
He and his wife Grace live in Hermantown with their two children.

removed: Skip to content About Delivered Promises Delivered Projects MN District 3 News Get Involved Contact About Delivered Promises Delivered Projects MN District 3 News Get Involved Contact Donate RELEASE: Northland Mayors Endorse Sen.

Hauschild For Second Term Mayors Across Northern Minnesota Back Grant Hauschild: “He Shows Up and Just Delivers” FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE [Pictured in left photo: International Falls Mayor Drake Dill, Cook Mayor Dan Manick, Senator Grant Hauschild, and Ely Mayor Heidi Omerza] [Pictured in right photo: Two Harbors Mayor Lew Connor, Rice Lake Mayor Jayme Heim, Senator Grant Hauschild, Proctor Mayor Chad Ward, and Duluth Mayor Roger Reinert] HERMANTOWN, MN. — State Senator Grant Hauschild hosted two ‘Mayors for Grant’ events today, beginning in Rice Lake and continuing on the Iron Range in Tower.
Mayors from across the largest and most rural district in the state, Senate District 3, joined Hauschild to discuss their work together and announce their support for his reelection.
“I served on City Council before becoming a State Senator, so I know how much local leaders are asked to do with limited resources,” Hauschild said.
“They know which road needs work, where an ambulance service is struggling, and what a big project could mean for local property taxes.

My job is to listen, work across party lines, and help them deliver.” Those partnerships have helped secure funding for water and utility projects in International Falls, Cook, Rice Lake, Ely, and Grand Marais; Highway 61 improvements in Two Harbors; support for rural ambulance services; and investments in schools and community facilities across the district.

Hauschild also worked to help keep the Boundary Waters Care Center open in Ely, bring state bonding dollars to Cook for the first time in the city’s history, and save coast guard services on the Northshore after the federal government pulled out.
“We have different political views and different local priorities, but we all want our communities to succeed,” Hauschild said.

“That’s why I’ll keep working with mayors in every corner of this district and putting the Northland First.” Mayors lending their support include : Chad Ward (Proctor), Drake Dill (International Falls), Tracy Benson (Grand Marais), Roger Reinert (Duluth), Jayme Heim (Rice Lake), Heidi Omerza (Ely), Dan Manick (Cook), Wayne Boucher (Hermantown), Lew Connor (as a private citizen – Two Harbors), Amy Phifer (Big Fork), Brennan Scott (Hoyt Lakes), and Dennis Wagner (Ranier).
International Falls Mayor Drake Dill “I support candidates on both sides of the aisle because what matters to me is whether someone delivers, and Grant delivers.

He helped secure bonding funds for our water project to ease the burden on residents’ utility bills and brought needed support to the International Falls ambulance service.” Duluth Mayor Roger Reinert “Duluth is fortunate to have Senator Hauschild in our delegation.
He understands that Duluth’s success is tied to the success of our entire region, and has taken that regional approach to the State Capitol.

We appreciate his hard work and proven success to secure critical Local Government Aid and state bonding investments for the Duluth community” Rice Lake Mayor Jayme Heim “Grant puts northern Minnesota ahead of party politics and works with leaders on both sides of the aisle.

That bipartisan approach helped Rice Lake secure state support for our road project and utility expansion, and it is why I am proud to support him.” Tower Mayor Dave Setterberg “Senator Hauschild has been highly engaged with the City of Tower and understands that our rural communities need strong partners and effective representation at the State Capitol.
In particular, he has worked across party lines to secure funding for critical infrastructure and help address a significant deficit facing our ambulance service.

I want to express my appreciation for Senator Hauschild’s engagement, commitment, and focus on delivering results that make a meaningful difference for our entire community.” Proctor Mayor Chad Ward “Grant understands the challenges facing local communities because he served in local government himself.

He worked across party lines to secure funding for Proctor’s Interstate 35 utility expansion and helped win approval for the sales tax supporting our Munger Trail connection with Hermantown and Duluth.” Two Harbors Mayor Lew Conner “Speaking solely as an individual citizen, I support Grant because he listens to local leaders and delivers results.

His work securing Highway 61 gap funding will shorten the disruption to our community, and he helped deliver needed funding for the elementary school renovation.” Bigfork Mayor Amy Phifer “Grant shows up in Bigfork, listens to our community, and works across party lines on the issues that matter here.

He helped deliver funding for our community center and school gym while remaining a strong advocate for rural hospitals like Bigfork’s.” Hermantown Mayor Wayne Boucher “I have seen Grant’s commitment to Hermantown since our time working together when he was on city council, and I am proud that our hometown has a senator fighting for us.

He understands local needs and helped secure major state support for the Hermantown Community Recreation Initiative.” Hoyt Lakes Mayor Brennan Scott “Grant listens to local leaders and works across party lines to deliver for communities like Hoyt Lakes.

Together, we have advanced funding for our arena renovations, ambulance service, the Ranger ATV Club, and the Mesabi Trail.” Cook Mayor Dan Manick “Grant worked alongside our community to secure the first state bonding investment in Cook’s history.

When devastating flooding hit, he also helped bring state assistance to affected businesses, proving that he shows up when northern Minnesota communities need him most.” Ely Mayor Heidi Omerza “Grant is consistently present in Ely and has made our community a real priority.

He helped save the Boundary Waters Care Center, secured gap funding for our school renovation, and delivered state support for critical water infrastructure.” ### Contact the Campaign Contact Us PO Box 1045 Duluth, MN 55810 Contribute $50 $75 $100 $250 $500 $1000 Other Amount Follow Us Facebook Twitter Flickr Vimeo @Grant_Hauschild @GrantforMN Privacy Policy Prepared and paid for by the Grant Hauschild for the Minnesota State Senate Committee PO Box 1045 Duluth, MN 55810

The event was held at the Lubbock Country Club.
Abbott, in his keynote speech, addressed what he called “the fight against an overreaching federal government.” Abbott told Republicans not to worry about the way the national election turned out.
He said the recent elections in Texas ended in a great victory for Republicans and that the Texas model for doing business is the right way to go.
Abbott said, “Texas is the leading state in the country for creating jobs for a reason.

It’s because we believe in limited government, and we’re going to fight to keep it that way.” Abbott said Republicans are facing challenges from the president’s administration and their “overreaching illegal actions.” He said he has filed more than 20 lawsuits to stop the administration from violating the constitution.

added: Find Your Early Voting Location: https://gregabbott.com/vote Menu Meet Greg Meet Cecilia Accomplishments Issues News Endorsements Download Abbott Impact Join Greg Today Contribute Contribute Online Contribute via Mail Contribute via Phone Contribute via Bitcoin Abbott Store Accident set Texas Attorney General Greg Abbott on a path toward politics Nov 26, 2010 Accident set Texas Attorney General Greg Abbott on a path toward politics By Theodore Kim Dallas Morning News AUSTIN – Greg Abbott was elected attorney general in 2002.
But his political trek began decades earlier – in agony.
At age 26, Abbott was partially paralyzed in a freak accident and bedridden for a month.
His dream to practice law withered.
But he tilled new ambitions, reading about politics during his recovery and internalizing a credo from his mother: Never say I can’t.
“That is one of the more guiding principals that got me through,” said Abbott, now 52.
“Just because this happened doesn’t mean I can’t do whatever it is I wanted to do.

It picked me up off of the hospital bed and got me going.” The accident – an oak tree fell and struck his back as he jogged by – kept him hospitalized and in rehabilitation for more than three months.
The recovery was often excruciating.
He has used a wheelchair ever since.
It also hardened his resolve and propelled him on a path toward politics.
He passed the bar exam a year after the accident, excelled as a Houston lawyer and eventually was elected a judge.
Abbott, a Republican, has won two terms as attorney general and is running again against retired Houston lawyer Barbara Ann Radnofsky, a Democrat.
He has used his tenure to combat child predators and human trafficking and to chime in on highly charged topics from climate change to health care.
Abbott disarms audiences with a folksy charm, but he casts a polarizing shadow.
Critics see him as an opportunistic publicity hound.
They, and his supporters, regard him as a future candidate for higher office, perhaps governor.

Transportation Announced a record $148 billion investment in Texas’s transportation infrastructure to improve safety, address congestion and connectivity, and preserve roadways for Texas drivers Texas Clear Lanes congestion-relief projects will see an increase in funding of $1.9 billion, supporting the $75.8 billion total investment for completed, under-construction, and planned non-tolled projects since 2015.

It also includes around a $17.3 billion investment in safety and an additional $1.7 billion in funding for rural corridors and key roadways in economic hubs Provided $106 million to complete eight airport projects that will improve aviation infrastructure and boost economic growth in local communities Dedicated $250 million towards rail-road grade separation projects, located at intersections of railroads and public pedestrian crossings, to increase public safety and reduce traffic Exempted counties from motor fuels taxes for essential public service vehicles used for road maintenance and emergency response Signed a Constitutional Amendment in 2015 to increase funding for public roadways by allocating a portion of the sales and use tax and the motor vehicle sales and rental taxes into the State Highway Fund (SHF).

As of November 2025, a total of $19.5 billion in Proposition 7 deposits have been made into the SHF. • Provided historic, first-time funding of $600 million through the Port Access Account Fund and the Ship Channel Improvement Revolving Fund (SCIRF) to develop port infrastructure projects, like deepening and widening ship channels. • Since 2015, Texas has invested $820 million in seaports to bolster the state’s thriving economy, provide a more robust supply chain, and maintain its global competitiveness.

added: Find Your Early Voting Location: https://gregabbott.com/vote Menu Meet Greg Meet Cecilia Accomplishments Issues News Endorsements Download Abbott Impact Join Greg Today Contribute Contribute Online Contribute via Mail Contribute via Phone Contribute via Bitcoin Abbott Store Attorney general pledges to continue to fight for Texas families Feb 19, 2013 Attorney general pledges to continue to fight for Texas families By Garner Roberts Abilene Reporter-News February 19, 2013 State Attorney General Greg Abbott said he didn’t invent the phrase “Don’t mess with Texas,” but “I’ve applied it more often than anyone else.” In a visit to Abilene Tuesday with other Republican officials — including U.S.
Rep.
Randy Neugebauer and Barry Smitherman, Texas Railroad Commission chairman — Abbott promised to continue “to maintain Texas in the conservative column” and “to fight for Texas families and our values.
“The greatness in this country lies in the hearts of each and every American,” he added, “not in the capital buildings in Washington, D.C., or in Austin.

What makes this nation great is not government but freedom.” He assailed Barack Obama and the president’s administration and repeated his well-publicized defense of Second Amendment rights to bear arms.
“We’re not about to allow liberals from Washington barge into Texas and strip our rights,” Abbott said.
He said he differs with people “who say Obama doesn’t know what he’s doing.” Obama knows what he’s doing, Abbott said.

The president “wants to grow government and raise taxes.” In his attack on Obama’s health care policies, Abbott noted that White House employees are exempt from “Obamacare.” “Every Texan should be exempt from ‘Obamacare,’” he added.
Abbott said he has sued the Obama administration 25 times and the U.S.
Environmental Protection Agency 12 times in the last four years.
“The good news is we’re winning these lawsuits,” he added.
“Lawsuits are the only language this administration seems to understand.” Abbott said he also will continue his campaign against voter fraud and his advocacy for the Texas economy.
“We stand as a model for the rest of the nation,” he said.
“We’re looking for more ways to keep government off your backs and out of your wallets.” Abbott sidestepped the issue of his political future.
Dallas television station WFAA has reported Abbott told campaign donors he will run for governor in 2014.
But in Abilene Tuesday after prepared remarks at a luncheon, he said decisions and announcements about his plans for 2014 will come after the current session of the Texas Legislature ends May 27.
“We are bogged down in the legislative session now,” he added.
Abbott was the guest speaker at the Lincoln Day Luncheon of the Taylor County Republican Party, held at Abilene Christian University.

In introducing Abbott, Neugebauer said, “Greg Abbott gets up every day and tries to ensure that people ‘don’t mess with Texas.’” Click here to read more… Facebook X Instagram Political Ad paid for by Texans for Greg Abbott, PO Box 308, Austin, TX 78767. © #.

added: Find Your Early Voting Location: https://gregabbott.com/vote Menu Meet Greg Meet Cecilia Accomplishments Issues News Endorsements Download Abbott Impact Join Greg Today Contribute Contribute Online Contribute via Mail Contribute via Phone Contribute via Bitcoin Abbott Store Governor Abbott Hosts Rural Affordability Roundtable in Texarkana Sep 24, 2026 TEXARKANA – Governor Greg Abbott today traveled to Texarkana to meet with rural Texans to discuss the Abbott Affordability Agenda and how his plan will lower costs for families and businesses.
The discussion took place at Miller Bowie Supply, a local business serving the agricultural community with the equipment and supplies farmers and ranchers rely on to keep their operations running.
Governor Abbott was joined by Senator Bryan Hughes and candidate for House District 1 Chris Spencer.
“Rural Texas is the backbone of our great state,” Governor Abbott said.
“Rural communities feed and fuel what is now the eighth largest economy in the world.
They are the very definition of what it means to be a Texan.

We must lower costs for Texans in every corner of our state, and with my affordability agenda we will help make Texas the most affordable state in America.” During the discussion, Governor Abbott spoke with Texarkana community members regarding water usage and affordability issues.
The Governor highlighted Texas’ generational water investment over 20 years to strengthen the state’s water infrastructure and ensure communities have reliable water supplies for generations.

He also discussed his Abbott Affordability Agenda, which will slash property taxes, and lower health, auto and home insurance, housing, and electricity costs, and make college more affordable and attainable for Texas families.
Click here to read more about the Abbott Affordability Agenda.
Additional photos of today’s events will be provided here when available.

added: Text JOIN to 55233 for alerts from Team Abbott Menu Meet Greg Meet Cecilia Accomplishments Issues News Endorsements Download Abbott Impact Join Greg Today Contribute Contribute Online Contribute via Mail Contribute via Phone Contribute via Bitcoin Abbott Store Governor Abbott Meets with Rural Texans to Discuss the Abbott Affordability Agenda in Wichita Falls Sep 24, 2026 WICHITA FALLS – Governor Greg Abbott today spoke with Wichita Falls residents at the Cattlemen’s Trailer and Ag Supply LLC, a local business that provides livestock equipment.
The Governor heard directly from rural Texans on the cost of living and how the Abbott Affordability Agenda directly address high costs.
Governor Abbott was joined by Representative James Frank.
“I was born in Wichita Falls.
Farming, ranching, and cattle raising is the way of life that founded the Texas we call home,” Governor Abbott said.
“Texans work hard for every dollar they earn, and they deserve to keep more of it.

With my affordability agenda, Texans will keep more money in their pockets. ” During the discussion, Governor Abbott heard from rural Texans, small business owners, firefighters, and local leaders about the affordability challenges facing families.

The Governor also discussed his plan to eliminate school district property taxes for homeowners, including how the state can use its strong fiscal position and other savings to provide lasting property tax relief.

Governor Abbott highlighted his proposal to lower the cost of summer courses at Texas colleges and universities and discussed the importance of supporting Sheppard Air Force Base and its continued role in the Wichita Falls community.
Click here to read more about the Abbott Affordability Agenda.
Additional photos of today’s events will be provided here when available.

added: Text JOIN to 55233 for alerts from Team Abbott Menu Meet Greg Meet Cecilia Accomplishments Issues News Endorsements Download Abbott Impact Join Greg Today Contribute Contribute Online Contribute via Mail Contribute via Phone Contribute via Bitcoin Abbott Store Governor Abbott Talks Affordability with Rural Texans in Sherman Sep 24, 2026 SHERMAN – Governor Greg Abbott today met with residents at MG’s Burger Restaurant, a longtime local diner in Sherman known for classic American fare and a welcoming community atmosphere, to discuss how lowering the cost of living can strengthen rural communities.
Governor Abbott was joined by Representative Shelley Luther.
“My goal is to empower Texans to keep more money in their pockets,” Governor Abbott said.
“That is why my affordability agenda will make Texas the most affordable state in the nation.

By cutting healthcare costs, property taxes, and insurance rates, we can save Texans thousands of dollars a year.” During the roundtable, Governor Abbott met with local leaders to address questions across various topics from affordability and property taxes to education and border security.

Regarding public school funding, the Governor highlighted his record $90 billion investment in Texas public schools, including $4 billion for teacher and staff pay raises and the Teacher Incentive Allotment, which rewards the best teachers with higher salaries.
Governor Abbott also spoke about the $7.5 billion federal reimbursement for Texas’ efforts to secure the southern border.
He also discussed his Texas Taxpayer Empowerment plan to cut property taxes in Grayson County and across the state.
Finally, the Governor discussed his Abbott Affordability Agenda and how it will make Texas the most affordable state in the country.
Click here to read more about the Abbott Affordability Agenda.

added: Text JOIN to 55233 for alerts from Team Abbott Menu Meet Greg Meet Cecilia Accomplishments Issues News Endorsements Download Abbott Impact Join Greg Today Contribute Contribute Online Contribute via Mail Contribute via Phone Contribute via Bitcoin Abbott Store Greg Abbott shares views with local Republicans Feb 19, 2013 Greg Abbott shares views with local Republicans Attorney general talks about his job, hot-button issues By Jennifer Rios San Angelo Standard-Times February 19, 2013 SAN ANGELO, Texas — Although Texas Attorney General Greg Abbott didn’t mention the upcoming gubernatorial race, local Republicans who came to see him speak were picturing him in that role Tuesday.
“I think he’s done a great job as attorney general,” local attorney Greg Gossett said.

“He’ll make an excellent governor.” Abbott’s speech touched on the future of the Republican Party and his fight against concerns such as voter fraud, the right to bear arms and President Barack Obama’s health care reform.
He said he’s asked what his job entails and explained it’s gotten simplified.

“I go into the office in the morning,” he said, “I sue Barack Obama, and then I go home.” “We’re taking care of business right now,” he said before the dinner at San Angelo Country Club, adding there was a lot of work to be done in the courts.
“We’ll let politics take care of itself later,” he said.
Instead, his speech included statistics on how Texas is leading the nation in job creation.
He cited that 50 percent of the jobs created nationwide in the past five years were created in Texas.
He talked about the party making strides in diversity by citing the election of the first Hispanic U.S. senator, Ted Cruz, and six Hispanics and three African-Americans elected as state legislators.
Abbott asked everyone in the audience to turn on their smartphones, log onto Twitter and start getting involved with the social media he said helped Obama win the election.
The five Republican justices of the 3rd Court of Appeals also took the microphone for quick words of thanks.

Party Chairman Jeff Betty gave introductions, joking that his hardest job was “estimating the size of the room.” About 150 people attended the Presidents Day celebration hosted by the Tom Green County Republican Party — more than double what they expected, Betty said.
At the end of the presentation, Betty said that money raised that evening was the beginning of a building fund for the party so it can host speakers.
He said 10 percent of its goal was reached Tuesday night.
Mike Boyd, president and CEO of First Financial Bank, said he believes Abbott stands for everything the local party does — that the state is strong and a leader in the nation in job creation.
He said that he also likes Abbott’s strong sense of conviction and that he practices it every day.
“He’s not afraid to give his opinion. … And he does his research,” Boyd said.

“Socialist Democrats like Gina Hinojosa want to hike your property taxes, make you pay a new state income tax, and even tax you after you die.
In 2025, Gina had a chance to stand for common sense and failed.
She and other Democrats voted against banning death and inheritance taxes in Texas.

added: Text JOIN to 55233 for alerts from Team Abbott Menu Meet Greg Meet Cecilia Accomplishments Issues News Endorsements Download Abbott Impact Join Greg Today Contribute Contribute Online Contribute via Mail Contribute via Phone Contribute via Bitcoin Abbott Store Perry, Abbott tell residents of other states that Texas is the place to be Feb 8, 2013 Perry, Abbott tell residents of other states that Texas is the place to be By Anna M.
Tinsley Fort Worth Star-Telegram February 8, 2013 They’ve been at war with Washington for years.
Now Texas Gov.
Rick Perry and Attorney General Greg Abbott have set their sights on other places as well.

The Republican leaders — both of whom aspire to higher office — are launching broadsides at leaders in states from California to New York, encouraging residents and businesses there to flee to the Lone Star State.
Democrats and residents of those states say Perry and Abbott are only embarrassing themselves and Texas with their antics.
But some political observers say the governor has typically benefited at home from attacks on outsiders.
Plus, they say, all’s fair in politics, and other states aren’t above bashing Texas.
“If you don’t think other states are doing it, too, reaching out to other states, you’re wrong,” said Bill Miller, an Austin-based political consultant.
“There’s an enormous amount of dissatisfaction with taxes there, and states with lower tax rates are a big draw.
“Political leaders in California don’t care about Texas, and Texans don’t care about them,” he said.

“This is about business … and it’s brilliant.” Some wonder whether the Texas leaders’ moves will create a backlash against a state that’s already the butt of occasional jokes on late-night talk shows.
But that won’t stop Perry.
On the heels of releasing ads in California, trying to lure residents to Texas, Perry is heading there in person.

“While much of the California and national media commentary has been negative, the message that Rick Perry’s Texas is ‘wide open for business’ has been received loud and clear by the three groups Perry cares most about: Texas voters, Republicans nationwide, and business owners in California and elsewhere,” said Mark P.
Jones, a political science professor at Rice University in Houston.
California This week, Perry poked at California, announcing that he’s running one week’s worth of radio ads there, encouraging businesses to move to the “best state” — Texas.
Perry said it’s tough to develop a business anywhere and even harder in California.
He touted Texas’ “low taxes, sensible regulations and fair legal system” as reasons why California businesses should head this way.

“I have a message for California businesses: Come check out Texas,” he said in the $24,000 radio ad buy, paid for by TexasOne, a public-private partnership that markets Texas throughout the world as a prime business destination.
California Gov.
Jerry Brown, a Democrat, dismissed Perry’s radio ads.
“It’s not a serious story, guys,” Brown told reporters.
“It’s not a burp.
It’s barely a fart.” But the ads come as California has faced economic difficulties and some residents are leaving.

“It is likely a ‘poke in the eye’ to what is perceived as a liberal state with economic difficulties while Texas and other states are doing relatively well,” said Allan Saxe, an associate political science professor at the University of Texas at Arlington.

Perry’s encroachment into California — which continues next week when he meets with business leaders in the high-tech, biotechnology, financial, insurance and film industries — sparked the Sacramento Bee to write the editorial “Pity Rick Perry; his big state has big needs.” The paper cited a “high dropout rate, lack of health insurance coverage and economic disparities” in saying that Texas isn’t exactly the nirvana that Perry might paint it to be.
The editorial said Perry’s ad campaign is more of a “cry for help.” “Perry can’t create jobs, he can only steal them from other states,” according to the editorial.
“His campaign for the Republican presidential nomination was a joke.
His beloved Dallas Cowboys haven’t been in the Super Bowl since 1996.” Perry will be in California from Sunday through Wednesday, a trip also paid for by TexasOne.

“The ads are likely to be more effective in bolstering Abbott and Perry’s standing as solid conservatives than they are in actually convincing California businesses and especially New York gun owners to move to Texas,” Jones said.
New York As recently as last month, Abbott urged gun owners in New York to leave their state — and restrictive gun laws — and move to Texas.
“Texans always like to talk about how great our state is,” Abbott told reporters after the ads aired.
“And what Gov.

Cuomo in New York did is to just give us another opportunity to distinguish Texas from New York and explain to the entire country why Texas is better than New York.” Abbott used campaign dollars to buy ads on news websites in New York City after Gov.
Andrew Cuomo signed broad gun control legislation.
Other than a few concerns about more New Yorkers moving to Texas, the response he received was mostly positive.

Abbott’s ads included one that read: “WANTED: Law abiding New York gun owners seeking lower taxes and greater opportunities.” One click on the ad took readers to a Facebook page about the Second Amendment that bragged about Texas’ virtues — including that the state has no income tax, so “you’ll be able to keep more of what you earn and use that extra money to buy more ammo.” One ad read: “Here in Texas, you will have the liberty and the opportunity to achieve your dreams.
On top of that, we have no income tax, yet still manage to have a multi-billion dollar budget surplus.
“We have right to work laws and a reasonable regulatory environment.
Texas has created more than 275,000 jobs in the last year alone!

And we’ll fight like hell to protect your rights.” Jones said, “In these ads, Abbott and Perry are once again contrasting distinct aspects of the Texas model — strong support for Second Amendment rights and a business-friendly environment — with the inferior conditions found in the decidedly more liberal states of New York and California.” Click here for more… Facebook X Instagram Political Ad paid for by Texans for Greg Abbott, PO Box 308, Austin, TX 78767. © #.

BRIGHTER TOMORROW.
GREG ABBOTT ON THE ISSUES MORE SAVINGS.
MORE OPPORTUNITY.
MORE FREEDOM.
EXPLORE THE ISSUES Governor Abbott is fighting for Texas families on the issues that matter most.
Explore his plans to make Texas more affordable and prosperous.

Property Tax Reform Texas needs comprehensive property tax reform so families aren't taxed out of their homes › Housing Costs Cutting red tape and expanding the housing supply will make housing more affordable for all Texans › Healthcare Costs Lowering out-of-pocket healthcare costs by capping co-pays and lowering insurance premiums › Insurance Costs Lowering the cost of home and auto insurance benefits all Texans › Energy Costs Saving customers and small businesses thousands per year by increasing competition in the energy market › Public Safety Four steps that will protect our communities and keep criminals behind bars › Higher Education Helping students save money on tuition and graduate sooner › Public Education Better Classrooms.

Brighter Futures. › Property Tax Reform OVERHAUL THE PROPERTY TAX SYSTEM ELIMINATE SCHOOL PROPERTY TAXES FOR HOMEOWNERS Despite record property tax relief provided by the state, local government tax increases have wiped out billions in savings for homeowners.
More must be done to rein in out-of-control property taxes.
School district property taxes are the largest portion of Texas homeowners' tax bills, and voters deserve the right to decide whether to abolish school district taxes.
Under Governor Abbott's plan, voters will have the right to decide - through a constitutional amendment - to eliminate school district property taxes on homeowners.
It is not your homestead's responsibility to pay for public schools.
That's the state's responsibility, and that's exactly what Governor Abbott's plan will do.
Removing school district taxes from your property tax bill will cut the average homestead's property taxes by half.
REFORM THE APPRIASAL PROCESS The current appraisal process is unnecessarily burdensome, and Texans should not be troubled with appraisal protests year after year.
It strains families and businesses and allows taxing entities to take more of your money while blaming rising values.
Governor Abbott's plan will require that all properties be appraised only once every five years .
That means fewer surprises, less red tape, and more peace of mind for Texas families and businesses.
Currently, Texas law limits appraisal value growth of homesteads to 10% per year.
While meant to provide relief to Texas homeowners, rising values and tax increases are still pricing people out of their homes, especially those on fixed incomes.
Governor Abbott's plan will lower the homestead appraisal cap from 10% to 3% , providing homeowners with the help they need.

Further, his plan will expand that cap to all properties, which will help renters and businesses - a major step to protect property owners, deliver more relief and predictability, and keep housing affordable.
EMPOWER VOTERS TO LOWER TAXES The State of Texas does not levy any property tax.
Local governments control your property taxes and they can raise them in multiple ways.
Unfortunately, there are limited options for taxpayers to lower their tax bills.

Under Governor Abbott's plan, if 15% of registered voters in a local area sign a petition, they can force a rollback election to lower rates, reducing taxes for all property owners and constraining the growth and spending of local governments.
CONTROL SPENDING AND TAX RATES REQUIRE COMMON SENSE LOCAL SPENDING LIMITS Texas families must live within their means, and local governments must too.
The State of Texas has five spending limits, but there are no standardized limits for cities, counties, and other local government entities.
Limiting local government spending to population + inflation or 3.5% (the lesser of the two) would ensure fiscally responsible governance.
Other safeguards like the state's debt limit and prohibition on deficit spending are common sense policies that should apply to all levels of government.
Governor Abbott's plan will protect taxpayer dollars and institute fiscally responsible policies that will keep Texas prosperous.
REQUIRE TWO-THIRDS VOTER APPROVAL FOR TAX INCREASES Right now, it is far too easy for local governments to impose higher taxes on Texans without their approval.
It must be harder, not easier, for local governments to take your hard-earned money.
In fact, certain laws regarding property taxes and spending require a two-thirds and, in some cases, a four-fifths vote.
Governor Abbott's plan will require a two-thirds voter approval on all local property tax increases before they can take effect.
This will empower voters and protect taxpayers, putting everyday Texans in control of proposed tax hikes.
Housing Costs LOWER HOUSING COSTS FAST-TRACK HOMEBUILDING: CUT RED TAPE, CUT COSTS Permitting and inspection delays extend homebuilding timelines and increase the cost of construction.
In fact, unnecessary regulations add thousands of dollars to the cost of a single-family home.

Governor Abbott’s plan will: (1) allow builders to use third-party inspections immediately (2) require local authorities to make an occupancy determination within 10 days (3) withhold sales tax if cities don’t follow the law.
Savings of up to $9,650 + 2 months on new home construction ACCELERATE APPROVAL PROCESS: EXPEDITE DESIGNS, INCREASE SUPPLY The building plan approval process can delay homebuilding.
Governor Abbott’s plan will accelerate the process by allowing developers to build pre-approved home designs.
Once a design has been approved by at least three cities, it would be pre-approved for building in similar areas.
Studies show that pre-approved building plans reduce overall development costs by up to $7,000 on a $350,000 single-family home.

INCREASE SUPPLY EXPAND HOUSING OPTIONS ON EXISTING PROPERTY: GIVING TEXANS ROOM TO GROW Property additions allow homeowners to make better use of their land by allowing them to build additional structures on their own property to meet household needs.

However, cities often hinder or outright prohibit their construction through excessive regulations Governor Abbott’s plan will remove these barriers by allowing property additions to be built by right, helping homeowners add value to their property and expand housing options across Texas.
PROTECT PRO-HOUSING REFORMS FOR TEXANS: STOP MANDATES, EXPAND SUPPLY Governor Abbott’s 2025 housing reforms are expanding housing supply for Texans.
However, some cities are undermining these reforms by requiring luxury amenities, design specifications, and other unnecessary mandates that prevent construction and raise housing costs.
Governor Abbott will lower costs for Texans by prohibiting rogue cities from setting such regulations and withhold local sales tax from cities that undermine the law.
Healthcare Costs CAP CO PAYS AT $25 AFFORDABLE LIFE-SAVING MEDICINE: CAP CO-PAYS, GREATER ACCESS Common life-saving medications can generate high, recurring out-of-pocket costs for families.
Texans shouldn’t have to choose between critical medicines and everyday household essentials.
Governor Abbott will ensure that life-saving medications remain accessible and affordable for all by capping monthly co-pays at $25 for inhalers and epinephrine .

Texans could save at least $120 annually on inhalers and at least $650 annually on epinephrine LOWER INSURANCE PREMIUMS AFFORDABLE HEALTH INSURANCE: LOWER PREMIUMS, MORE ACCESS Healthcare costs comprise a substantial portion of every family’s budget.
That’s because many health plans are weighed down by an excess of expensive health insurance mandates, which translate to higher premiums for hardworking Texans.
Governor Abbott’s Essential Benefits Health Insurance Plan will authorize the creation of a more affordable insurance plan for Texas employers covering the essential healthcare needs of Texans.
Under this new plan, premiums could fall by nearly 20%.

Texas families would save nearly $1,150 per year and small businesses would save up to $3,400 per employee per year Insurance Costs LOWERING CAR INSURANCE COSTS AFFORDABLE CAR INSURANCE: BETTER DRIVERS, BETTER RATES In Texas, most insurers cannot consider traffic violations when setting insurance rates.
Governor Abbott’s plan will allow all auto insurers to consider good driving habits when setting premiums.
The result: safe drivers will be rewarded with reduced insurance premiums.

Good drivers will save between 10 and 30% on their car insurance premiums LOWERING HOME INSURANCE COSTS AFFORDABLE HOME INSURANCE: STRONGER ROOFS, LOWER RATES Extreme Texas weather is a leading cause of home insurance claims in the state, which increases annual premiums for all homeowners.
Governor Abbott will lower the cost of home insurance by establishing a $400 million Texas roof fortification program.
The program will provide up to $10,000 per participating homeowner for fortified roofs that can better withstand wind and hail damage.
A fortified roof can save homeowners up to 8% on premiums and up to nearly $16,000 in total potential savings over the life of the roof.

Energy Costs LOWER ENERGY COSTS AFFORDABLE ELECTRICITY: REAL COMPETITION, REAL SAVINGS More than five million Texans reside in areas with a single municipal power provider and cannot shop for cheaper electricity rates.
Of those five million, more than 60% are served by Austin’s and San Antonio’s electric utilities — the two largest municipally-owned utility districts in the state.
Governor Abbott’s plan will allow Texans to choose their electricity provider by opening city monopolies to retail electric competition.
In Austin and San Antonio, residential ratepayers would respectively save on average 10% and 13% on their electricity bills.
Affected small business and commercial ratepayers would save up to 20% on their electricity bills, or up to $3,000 per year.
Governor Abbott would also ban city utilities from charging customers unrelated fees and prohibit using utility profits as a city slush fund.
Public Safety LOCK UP DANGEROUS CRIMINALS EXPAND TEXAS REPEAT OFFENDER TASKFORCE 1% of the population accounts for 63% of all violent crime.
That's why Governor Abbott launched the repeat offender taskforce.
Since the task force launched last year, hundreds of violent repeat offenders and gang members have been arrested as a result.

Governor Abbott's plan calls for expanding the successful Texas DPS operation to keep our communities safe from the 1% committing the majority of crimes DENY BAIL FOR CRIMINAL ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS Dangerous illegal immigrants out on bail have been behind some of the most heinous crimes committed in Texas in recent history.
Governor Abbott's plan is simple: illegal immigrants arrested for violent felonies must be denied bail and held behind bars while awaiting trail.
PROSECUTE CRIMINALS ESTABLISH A TEXAS STATEWIDE PROSECUTOR Local prosecutors are often overwhelmed when it comes to the volume of cases coming through their office.
A statewide prosecutor will fix that.
Statewide prosecutors will provide prosecutorial support to local district attorneys.
When local DAs refuse to prosecute violent criminals, a statewide prosecutor can step in their place and ensure justice is served.
IMPEACH ROUGE DISTRICT ATTORNEYS District attorneys swear an oath to protect and defend the laws of Texas.
Yet time and time again some district attorney's refuse to uphold that oath, allowing violent criminals to walk free.
Governor Abbott's plan will strengthen accountability for district attorneys by allowing for the impeachment of DA's who fail to uphold their oath.
Higher Education TUITION DISCOUNT MAKING COLLEGE AFFORDABLE Governor Abbott is making college more affordable and helping students start their career sooner.
His plan will cut the cost of summer courses that count toward a student’s bachelor degree, helping students graduate sooner and save money along the way.

Under Governor Abbott’s plan, undergraduate students at Texas public colleges and universities will receive: $500 off tuition and fees when taking 1–5 credit hours during the summer. $1,000 off tuition and fees when taking 6 or more credit hours during the summer.
Lower-cost summer courses mean students can make faster progress toward graduation while spending less on summer tuition.
By graduating sooner, students can also save on housing and other college expenses.
THREE YEAR DEGREES GRADUATE SOONER.
START EARNING FASTER.
The cost of a college degree goes beyond tuition.

The lawsuit alleges that a section of Dodd-Frank “empowers the (U.S.) Treasury Secretary to order the liquidation of a financial company with little or no advance warning, under cover of mandatory secrecy, and without either useful statutory guidance or meaningful legislative, executive, or judicial oversight.” Texas’ move comes at the same time seven other states declared they would join the lawsuit, which was filed last June on behalf of a small Big Spring, Texas-based community bank, State National Bank of Big Spring, and two political groups.
The suit names the U.S.

Treasury, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, Federal Reserve Chairman Ben Bernanke and others as defendants, and it targets Dodd-Frank’s provision that gives regulators “new authority for the ‘orderly liquidation’ of financial institutions.” “Under this law, unelected federal bureaucrats can unilaterally liquidate financial institutions in which the state invests taxpayer dollars,” Texas Attorney General Greg Abbott said in a Feb.
13 statement.

“The State of Texas could be denied basic due process rights and taxpayers’ dollars could recklessly be put at risk.” In addition, the suit challenges Dodd-Frank’s formation of the young Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and the President Barack Obama’s appointment of Richard Cordray to the role of director at the CFPB.

added: About Meet Greg Ballard Podcast Meet Greg News & Updates Greg’s Plan Voters Guide Indiana Election Integrity Act Hands-on Clerk Training Nonpartisan Recount Commission Support Donate Get a Yard Sign Buy a Shirt Volunteer CONTRIBUTE Meet Greg Ballard Greg’s Plan Voter’s Guide Indiana Election Integrity Act Hands-on Clerk Training Nonpartisan Recount Commission News and Updates Support Donate Get a Yard Sign Buy a Shirt Volunteer Subscribe Contribute Oct 9, 2026 I’m a Republican.
Here’s why I’m voting for Greg Ballard.
I saw Indiana as a state that was going up while Illinois was going down.
I was mistaken.
Ethan Melman | Opinion Contributor I am voting for Greg Ballard for Indiana secretary of state.
I did not make this decision easily or lightly.
I have been a lifelong Republican.
When I was in high school, I knocked on doors for Republican candidates in Chicago.
In college, I worked for a Republican state senator from Illinois.
When I first started looking into Indiana politicians, figures like former Vice President Mike Pence and former Gov.
Eric Holcomb seemed to embody the good old conservative ideals that I had grown up with.

I moved to Indiana during the summer of 2024 with dreams of establishing my own law practice in Indianapolis and building a home for myself in a state that I saw as going up while Illinois was going down.
I wanted to fulfill my American dream and make a name for myself.
I went to my first Marion County GOP meetings and almost felt at home.
It was as though I had finally found a place where my Reaganesque political dreams could start to blossom and where I could consider running for office under the Republican banner.
Then I started learning about Diego Morales.
I had grown up under the shadow of a century-old political machine, where four governors, dozens of Chicago aldermen and others were federally indicted.
I thought that level of corruption would stay in Illinois.
I was unfortunately mistaken.
Morales has faced allegations of sexual misconduct , nepotism and favoritism, questionable taxpayer spending and taxpayer-funded self-promotion .
That all weighed on me as I waited for the upcoming secretary of state election.
I couldn't wait to see whom the GOP would put forward in June.
And then I got my answer: Max Engling.
I have nothing against Engling personally.
I think he's a great family man and father.
But I could not bring myself to consider voting for him.
When I listened to the first secretary of state debate on Aug.
26 while driving south toward Salem to meet with a client, I noticed something about Engling that took me aback.
He refused to condemn or even acknowledge the allegations of rampant corruption that have engulfed the secretary of state's office.
I expected Democrat Beau Bayh and Libertarian Lauri Shillings to call them out and ask for audits of the office, but Ballard's comments resonated with me.
Here I was, listening to a former Republican call out his former party and say that things had to change.
He agreed to an independent audit of the office he was running for and to investigate employees who had benefited from the alleged corruption of the current administration.
On the opposing side, I, as a Republican, wished Engling would say something to that effect.
Engling dodged the tough questions and moved on.
That was when I made my decision.
I'm a Republican voting for Ballard, the former Indianapolis mayor, because he represents something that modern Republican politics has lost: integrity.
If I had to make an analogy, when your car's check engine light is on and you smell smoke, you don't continue driving, shrug and say to yourself, "This is fine." You take it to the shop.
The secretary of state's office is a car with its check engine light on, smoking as it travels down the highway.
It needs a mechanic.
That mechanic is Ballard.
Ethan Melman is a law student at the Indiana University McKinney School of Law and a law clerk for Robert D.
Epstein & Associates.

New Law to Make Secretary of State Nonpartisan As Secretary of State, Greg Ballard will establish a hands-on election training program for county clerks and poll workers, built and taught by the people who actually know how to run elections in Indiana: experienced county clerks themselves, working alongside the SOS's own staff.

A Clerk Training Boot Camp An in-person training program for new and current clerks, run in a "sandbox" version of the statewide voter registration system — a safe practice environment where clerks can actually work through setting up an election, processing ballots, and handling problems, without touching live data.
This is a complement to the state's existing legal-update sessions, not a replacement for them — it's the hands-on, how-to-actually-do-the-job piece that's been missing.
It will be built and taught by a team of experienced, sitting and former county clerks.

Finally Funding and Implementing Poll Worker Training — the Smart Way State law already authorizes the Secretary of State office to provide standardized poll worker and county election official training.
It's never been funded or built.
The Secretary of State's office can't train every poll worker in every precinct directly — but it can equip county clerks to do it well, consistently, and with real support.
Ballard's plan does that through three steps: A standardized SOS curriculum.

The office will produce a professional training curriculum — video modules and printed materials, customized to the specific voting systems used across Indiana's counties — covering the issues that come up over and over: acceptable voter ID, provisional ballots, electioneering rules, chain-of-custody paperwork, and keeping lines moving without cutting corners.
Every county starts from the same playbook.
Train-the-trainer for Clerks.

Clerk boot camp attendees are trained not just to run elections, but to deliver poll worker curriculum locally — with the materials, timing, and talking points to run an efficient in-person session for their own poll workers.
SOS regional field staff support counties directly.
The Secretary of State's office already has staff positioned around the state.

This plan puts those existing employees to work helping county clerks plan and run local poll worker sessions — answering questions, troubleshooting, and making sure every county, especially smaller ones without the staff to build training themselves, has real support.

Consistency Across All 92 Counties Right now, Indiana effectively runs 92 different election systems, because there's no shared standard for the hands-on side of how clerks and poll workers are trained.
This plan creates a common baseline of practical knowledge and best practices so that every Hoosier's vote is handled the same rigorous way, no matter what county they live in.
Indiana needs a professional election-training system built around demonstrated competency, clear authority, practical experience, accountability, and continuous improvement.

This is what election security actually looks like: not slogans, but making sure the people running our elections — including the poll workers on the front lines every Election Day — have the training and support to do it right, every time.
It's a plan built to work, using the people and the laws already in place.
