Hoosiers deserve confidence that elections are administered fairly, professionally, and without partisan influence.
As Secretary of State, Greg will make a clear commitment: he will not endorse, donate to, or raise money for candidates whose elections his office oversees.
Many voters are surprised to learn that the Secretary of State is currently allowed to campaign for candidates whose elections they help administer.
That’s wrong.
Greg believes the person responsible for overseeing elections should act with the highest level of independence and neutrality.
He will ensure Hoosiers can trust that elections are being administered fairly, without political favoritism.
A Statewide Voter Guide for Every Hoosier Voting should be simple, clear, and accessible.

New Law to Make Secretary of State Nonpartisan Proposal would bar the state's chief election officer from endorsing, fundraising, or donating to candidates — the same standard Indiana already holds judges to The Secretary of State serves as Indiana's chief election official and chairs the State Recount Commission, which resolves disputed elections for federal, statewide, and state legislative office.

Ballard believes that an office with that much influence over the mechanics and outcomes of Indiana elections should be held to the same standard of political independence Indiana already demands of its judges.

Independent Indiana Secretary of State Candidate Greg Ballard called on the Indiana General Assembly to bar the state’s chief election officer from endorsing, fundraising for or donating to candidates once in office.
Ballard also made a personal commitment to refrain from partisan political activity while in office and challenged every other candidate in the race to make the same pledge.

Under the Indiana Code of Judicial Conduct, judges are barred from endorsing candidates, fundraising for political parties, or holding party leadership positions — restrictions designed to protect public confidence in an impartial judiciary.
Ballard's proposal would apply substantially the same restrictions to the office of Secretary of State.

The proposed legislation would prohibit a sitting Secretary of State from publicly endorsing or opposing candidates, fundraising or donating to parties and campaigns, holding party leadership positions, or serving as a featured speaker or honoree at partisan political events in Indiana.
It would preserve the Secretary of State's right to vote, register with a party, and campaign on their own behalf for their own re-election.
Complaints would be filed with the Indiana State Ethics Commission, with the ability to proceed to court if the Commission fails to act.
Ballard's campaign has released a one-page summary and FAQ detailing the proposal.

removed: About Meet Greg Ballard Podcast Meet Greg News & Updates Greg’s Plan Voters Guide Indiana Election Integrity Act Hands-on Clerk Training Nonpartisan Recount Commission Support Donate Get a Yard Sign Buy a Shirt Volunteer CONTRIBUTE Meet Greg Ballard Greg’s Plan Voter’s Guide Indiana Election Integrity Act Hands-on Clerk Training Nonpartisan Recount Commission News and Updates Support Donate Get a Yard Sign Buy a Shirt Volunteer Subscribe Contribute Jun 26, 2026 THE INDIANA CITIZEN: DENIES SPOILER ROLE: As chances of joining ballot rise, Ballard focuses on winning secretary of state race By Marilyn Odendahl The Indiana Citizen FORT WAYNE – As state Republicans were inside the Grand Wayne Convention Center in Fort Wayne on Saturday selecting their nominee for secretary of state, former Indianapolis Mayor Greg Ballard was a few miles away greeting Hoosiers at the 29 th annual BBQ RibFest.
Ballard, who is mounting an outsider campaign for Indiana secretary of state, was feeling confident about his chances in the November general election.

He needs to collect 36,943 valid signatures from Indiana registered voters by the end of June to get on the ballot as an independent and despite calling the signature requirement “onerous” and “punitive,” he believes he will clear that hurdle.
During the Republican convention, his campaign announced it had collected 52,501 signatures to get him on the ballot and by Tuesday, that number had jumped to 64,183.

His campaign is planning to make a final push for signatures by being at 12 locations around the state this Saturday and asking Hoosiers to sign the “petition of nomination” form required of independent candidates.

The signatures collected so far still have to be verified by the county clerks, but Ballard said his campaign’s internal review of the signed petitions is indicating he will meet – if not exceed – the required number.
Consequently, Ballard could become the fourth candidate to enter the secretary of state race.
When asked if he would be the spoiler in the election, Ballard erupted, “No, no, no, no.” “I’m not trying to spoil anything,” Ballard said.

“I want to go in and clean this office up and keep it in such a way that stays there for the future (as a) nonpartisan and independent office, where there’s absolutely no question how that office is going to be run.” The contest for secretary of state will likely be heated.
At their convention, Indiana Republicans sidelined current secretary of state Diego Morales and nominated Max Engling , a staff member for U.S.
Sen.
Jim Banks, R-Indiana.
Engling was a late entrant into the race for the GOP nomination, but he quickly garnered the support of elected Hoosier Republicans in state and congressional offices.
Earlier in June, Indiana Democrats rallied behind Beau Bayh and selected him as their secretary of state candidate.

Bayh has the advantage of name recognition, since his father, Evan, served as Indiana governor and a U.S. senator and his grandfather, Birch, served as speaker of the Indiana House and also as a U.S. senator.
Indiana Libertarians nominated Lauri Shillings to run for secretary of state.
She is an entrepreneur and small-business owner.
Ballard sees the November election as becoming a fight between himself, Engling and Bayh.
Ballard is distinguishing himself by highlighting the one thing he believes is his advantage over the Republican and Democratic nominees: experience.
Not only does Ballard have experience running a public administration but he also has experience surprising political pundits.
In 2007, Ballard, then a relatively unknown Republican, upset Democratic incumbent Bart Peterson in the Indianapolis mayoral race.
He outmatched an incumbent who had better name recognition and a sizable campaign war chest.
During his two terms as mayor of a city with roughly 800,000 residents, Ballard managed about 7,000 employees and oversaw a billion-dollar budget.
“I’m now the only candidate in the race that’s actually been in charge of anything.
Neither of them have been in charge of anything,” Ballard said of Engling and Bayh.
“If they want to clean house in that office, which both of them are saying, they have no experience in doing that.
I do; they don’t.” Campaign fined for late filings Ballard’s effort to get on the ballot has hit a few bumps.

In April, the campaign had to issue its first-quarter finance report in a press release, because it was unable to get the login credentials to post the documents on the Indiana Election Division’s online portal.

Days before the state GOP convention, Hamilton County Republican Party Chair Mario Massillamany called for an investigation into allegedly fraudulent signatures the Ballard campaign submitted to the Hamilton County Circuit Court Clerk.
Speaking of the problem in Hamilton County, Ballard said the alleged forgery was a single incident caused by one subcontractor paid to collect signatures.
“One guy, one time,” he said.
Also, he noted the verification system worked because the potential fraud was discovered early and the signatures were not counted in the total needed to get on the ballot.
Most recently, the campaign got fined $450 for failing to file two large donation reports by the 10-day deadline.
One donation was from an individual for $10,000 and the other was from the Hoosiers for Competitive Elections political action committee for $78,000.
In a statement, Ballard said, “We will not contest the decision.” The lapses and missteps in his campaign have exposed Ballard to questions about whether he is qualified to be secretary of state.

“Really?” Ballard responded, pointing out that the Republican party officials took two-and-a-half hours to tally a little more than 1,600 delegate votes cast at their convention in the race for the secretary of state nomination.
“People make mistakes,” Ballard continued.
“Mistakes do happen and these are very minimal mistakes in a large operation.
Things happen.
The individuals have been taken care of, everything’s been taken care of.
We admitted it all.” Eschewing party labels Ballard entered the race in March as an independent.
A week later, he announced he was launching the new Lincoln Party.
On the campaign trail, Ballard said he is not mentioning the Lincoln Party and, instead, is focused on connecting with voters as an independent.

Should he garner at least 2% of the votes cast in the November secretary of state’s race, he will then establish the Lincoln Party, he said, so future candidates will have the option of running under that label and not have to complete the arduous task independent candidates face of gathering nearly 37,000 valid signatures just to get on the ballot.
“I don’t want to go down the party route,” Ballard said, adding his polling shows more than 50% of Hoosiers want a new political party.
“We’re now trying to win this race.
This is what we’re doing.
We’re going to win this race.
I’m not focused on the other stuff.” Ballard said he was spurred to run as an independent because of what he sees as a discontent with the Democratic and Republican parties.
Moreover, he said, both parties “vigorously” tried to talk him out of launching an independent bid.
Ballard believes if he had not entered the race, polling would have shown Morales could have defeated Bayh in a two-way contest, so Engling would never have sought the GOP nomination.
Despite his outsider status, Ballard is confident that should he top the field in November, he will be able to work with Republican Gov.
Mike Braun and the Republican and Democratic legislators in the Indiana General Assembly.
However, Ballard is pushing back on efforts to close the state’s primary elections, which could put him at odds with GOP lawmakers.
The Republican Party is embracing closed primaries and Engling has said that ending the open primary system will be one of his top priorities if elected secretary of state.
“I’m hoping that everybody gets a sense of what’s best for the citizens and not best for the parties, which is worrying me right now,” Ballard said.

“I think both parties look like they’re looking out for themselves and not too many people are looking out for the citizens, so that has to change.” Dwight Adams, an editor and writer based in Indianapolis, edited this article.

He is a former content editor, copy editor and digital producer at The Indianapolis Star and IndyStar.com, and worked as a planner for other newspapers, including the Louisville Courier Journal This originally appeared in The Indiana Citizen .

title.after: Halpin 2022 F&F Packet

added: Friend, As a State Representative, it has been an honor to work with my neighbors to improve the place that we proudly call home.
This year, I am running for State Senate for the opportunity to continue serving our community.
I want to continue the good work we have done together, but I cannot do it without your support.
One quick, easy and effective way you can help is to participate in our “Friends and Family Program.” Please read the short letter below.
We’d like to send it to your friends and family on your behalf.

All you have to do is approve the letter by signing your name in the box below, and then list the names and addresses of friends and family who live in the District, which includes most of Rock Island County, parts of Henry, Knox, McDonough, Mercer and Warren Counties.
Visit HalpinForIllinois.com to see the full map.
It’s that easy for you to get involved in our campaign and play an important role in our success!
This personal contact is crucial, and I am confident your family and friends will read the letter when it arrives because it comes from someone they know and trust - you!
Thank you for participating in the Friends and Family Program!
In the next few days, one of my volunteers will be calling you.
I appreciate your support and efforts.

If you have any questions, feel free to contact me at FriendsofMikeHalpin@gmail.com Sincerely, Mike Halpin State Senate | 36th District Step 1 - Read the following letter: I hope this letter finds you well.
I wanted to take a moment to write to you about a friend of mine, Mike Halpin, who I know personally and will be voting for in this year’s general election on November 8, 2022.
As a former aide to Congressman Lane Evans, Mike Halpin will continue Lane’s legacy to protect workers, veterans and our seniors.
Illinoisans are hard workers and they deserve to have someone in the State Senate who will work as hard for them as they work for our communities.
We need Mike Halpin in Springfield because of his common sense approach.
He will put families in western Illinois first and will stand up to the career politicians in Chicago who forget about us.
Mike Halpin has a strong voice, a great work ethic and understands the issues that matter.
That’s why I am supporting him in this election.

If you need more information on Mike Halpin or would like information on absentee voting, early voting, need a ride to the polls or need help locating your polling place, email him at FriendsofMikeHalpin@gmail.com or visit his website at HalpinForIllinois.com.
Step 2 - Sign your name in the box.
Step 3 - Name friends, family and neighbors.
List the full names and place of residence of your friends, family and neighbors who you think live in State Senate District 36.
We will verify they live within district boundaries.
The more names you provide, the better our chance of success.
Names will not be used for any other purpose.
If you need more space, write names on the back!
First & Last Name Place of Residence (or address if you know it.) First & Last Name Place of Residence (or address if you know it.) Step 4 - Complete Your Contact Details Below and Return Your Form!

Name:_________________________________ Address:______________________________________ Phone: _________________________________ Your Email: ____________________________________ Other support you can offer Mike: ____ I would like to place a sign in my yard. ____ I am willing to volunteer during the campaign (we will contact you for details.) Here’s what we’ll do: Please return pages 3 & 4 (your signature, list and contact info) to 218 18th St, Rock Island, IL 61201 or 261 N.

Broad St, Ste 23, Galesburg IL 61401 or scan and email to FriendsofMikeHalpin@gmail.com by Friday, August 1, 2022. (the sooner, the better!) We’ll create a letter from you to go out to the names you have provided.
We take care of everything—printing, postage, and mailing.
You don’t have to do anything else (other than vote!) As always, we truly appreciate your support and thank you for your time!

Raised on the island of North Haven, she’s led at every level—serving as Maine’s Speaker of the House, running a small business, chairing her local school board, and directing the Governor’s Office of Policy Innovation and the Future.
From expanding access to health care and affordable housing to leading Maine’s climate work, Hannah brings people together and delivers real results for Maine families.

Today, Maine faces urgent challenges: a housing crisis, climate change, rising costs, and attacks on our rights and democracy.
Hannah is stepping up to fight back and build a stronger, fairer future for all Mainers.
As a mom raising two kids in rural Maine and a lifelong public servant, she knows what’s at stake.
With bold leadership and a deep love for this state, Hannah is ready to deliver solutions that put Maine people first.
#TeamPingree Take Action Today Maine people are already stepping up to build this grassroots campaign, pitching in however they can, early and with heart.
This work is powered by you, and together we are laying the groundwork to win.
Join us, and be part of building a bright future for our great state.

removed: Skip to content Meet Hannah Issues Affordability Education Economic Opportunity Health Care Housing Climate & Energy Accomplishments Endorsements News Volunteer Store Vote Meet Hannah Issues Affordability Education Economic Opportunity Health Care Housing Climate & Energy Accomplishments Endorsements News Volunteer Store Vote Facebook X-twitter Instagram Youtube Tiktok Donate July 21, 2026 Hannah Pingree Campaign Announces $# Million Raised, Sets New Fundraising Record Heading Into General Election MAINE — The Hannah Pingree for Governor campaign announced today that it has raised more than $3 million dollars since entering the race, including over $900,000 during this truncated 42-day fundraising period.
The campaign again has set a new record for the most funds any Democrat has raised in a Maine gubernatorial race during this reporting period and has $921,000 cash on hand as of today.

The announcement comes as Hannah just returned from a 3-day swing in Aroostook County, connecting with voters at grassroots events and touring small businesses and farms across the region in Presque Isle, Fort Fairfield and Mars Hill.
“Mainers deserve a governor who actually shows up, in every county, including the most rural,” said Hannah Pingree.
“I’ve been traveling this state since day one, and what I hear over and over is that people can’t afford housing, can’t afford health care, and they’re tired of waiting on Washington to fix it.
That’s what I’m focused on.

This kind of support, from every corner of Maine, tells me people are ready for a governor who will actually deliver, and I’m going to keep earning it all the way to November.” Since launching her campaign, Hannah has received support from all 16 counties and nearly 300 Maine towns, thousands of contributions reflecting the campaign’s statewide reach and growing support as Hannah continues to meet with workers, families, small business owners, and community leaders across Maine.
“Hannah’s momentum is clear,” said Emily Cain, Campaign Treasurer.
“Our campaign has more money, more donors, and more support in every county than Bobby Charles and Rick Bennett combined.
Hannah’s strength shows up in the polling, too.
Our opponents have no real statewide operation or base of support.
Voters from all sides are backing Hannah because they know she can govern and they believe she can win.

Right now the Republicans can’t say either.” Hannah Pingree’s campaign for governor has had record breaking fundraising, innovative policy announcements, packed events and Town Halls across Maine, countless endorsements and 400 event campaing stops and counting— alongside two public polls showing her with a commanding lead heading into November.

These milestones highlighted the growing excitement behind her candidacy and her vision to make Maine more affordable, expand opportunities for families, and deliver results that strengthen communities across the state.
A full campaign finance report will be filed with the Maine Ethics Commission by today, July 21st.
For more information on Hannah Pingree’s campaign, visit www.hannahforgovernor.com .

The agency’s weekly fuel survey found the statewide average price of heating oil hit $5.77 per gallon on September 14 — a 74% jump from a year earlier — with kerosene averaging $6.57 per gallon.
Filling a standard 275-gallon tank now costs nearly $675 more than it did last year.
WATCH THE VIDEO HERE STATEMENT FROM HANNAH PINGREE: “Maine is the most heating oil reliant state in the country and we know our homes are often old and leaky.
With heating oil nearly $6 a gallon on average, many Mainers are worried about how they’ll afford to stay warm this winter.
“I am urging Congress and the Trump Administration to double Maine’s LIHEAP allocation to meet this unprecedented need.
Doubling our LIHEAP funding will ensure our programs can keep pace.
“As governor, I’ll also seek to provide additional urgent relief so folks can stay safe and warm in their homes this winter with energy relief support.

I’ll also fight to lower energy costs, and do more to help Mainers tighten up their houses with weatherization programs and investments in efficient technologies like heat pumps to help save money and keep people warm in their homes.
“Providing relief this winter will be urgent and with this war continuing to push prices, the state and federal government needs to step up.
Mainers never give up on their neighbors and they show up by supporting wood banks and fuel funds.

As governor, I will do the same.” ABOUT THE CAMPAIGN With a little over a month until the general election, Hannah has secured her status as the undeniable front-runner, fueled by strong grassroots support, a strong bipartisan coalition, record-breaking fundraising, high volunteer engagement, and a growing list of endorsements from elected officials, health care experts, fisherman, housing leaders and community advocates across Maine.

This guest column, written by Eloise Melcher, w as originally published in Central Maine.
When I turned 30, suddenly all of my friends were talking about buying houses.
Or, more specifically, how hard it is to buy a house.
Looking at houses on Zillow in one’s spare time is no longer a fun game; it’s just depressing.
So many house prices have skyrocketed since 2020.
Due to Maine’s housing prices, I see myself sticking to renting for a good long while.
That’s not to say, of course, that renting is necessarily easier.
Rents in Portland rival those in Boston.
And outside of Portland, we don’t find much relief either.
But at least when my dishwasher breaks, I’ll have someone to call.
Hard to save for that down payment, though.
Thankfully, we have someone running for governor who knows Maine is facing a very serious housing crisis.
Hannah Pingree’s housing plan will invest in housing, stop out-of-state corporations from driving up rents and cut the red tape that slows development.
Hannah’s smart, clear and comprehensive housing plan gives me hope for Maine’s future.
Eloise Melcher Portland Spread The Word Let's Go!

Bill Bridgeo, w as originally published in the Portland Press Herald.
I am in full support of Hannah Pingree for governor of Maine.

I’ve known and admired Hannah for many years; I believe that she has the right combination of principled leadership skills, compassion, creativity and energy to enable our great state to realize its full potential over the next four and, hopefully, eight years.

As someone whose career included managing two Maine cities over a span of 30 years (first Calais and then 23 years in Augusta), I very much appreciate Hannah’s contributions as a legislator (including her time as speaker of the House) and more recently her leadership role in the Mills administration.

Her work championing, establishing and then leading the Office of Policy Innovation and the Future coordinated state agency efforts and important resources for Maine’s nearly 500 municipalities and 16 counties — something the prior administration had shortsightedly done away with when it abolished the State Planning Office.
Hannah is a native Mainer who’s done an admirable job of balancing the roles of spouse, mother, community leader and prominent public official.
She’s warm, genuine and wicked smart.
I hope folks will join me in voting for her on Nov.
Rep.
Bill Bridgeo Augusta Spread The Word Let's Go!

During her years in public service, Hannah has partnered with Tribal leaders on economic opportunity, infrastructure, climate resilience, and public health.
As governor, she will build a strong government-to-government relationship to continue taking action on these issues.
More pictures and video available upon request Hannah supports full tribal sovereignty and will work with the Tribal Nations and the Legislature to pass legislation in her first 100 days in office.
She believes the Wabanaki Nations deserve the same rights and opportunities as every other federally recognized tribe.
“Sovereignty is not a favor from the state.
It is overdue.
Restoring it means Tribal Nations will have the same rights and autonomy as every other federally recognized Tribe.
It is an issue of fairness.
Getting this done will be a top priority for me,” said Hannah.
Statements of Support from Wabanaki Chiefs Chief Sheila McCormack, Mi’kmaq Nation: “Hannah Pingree has my full support to be the next Governor of Maine.

She has demonstrated a consistent commitment to working together with Tribal governments and has the experience and temperament to deliver on her campaign promise of Tribal Sovereignty within her first 100 days in office.” Chief William Nicholas, Passamaquoddy Tribe at Indian Township: “I’m proud to endorse Hannah Pingree for Governor of Maine.
She is a leader who listens first and works alongside people to get things done.

She has shown that she values real partnership, and I believe she will bring that same collaborative spirit to the governor’s office.” Chief Kirk Francis, Penobscot Nation: “Hannah is a proven leader with deep roots in Maine.
As Speaker of the House and as a community leader, she has a reputation for listening, bringing people together, and honoring her word.
I’m so pleased to support her for Governor.” Chief Clarissa Sabattis, Houlton Band of Maliseets: “Hannah Pingree does not back down when it matters for Maine families.

She is tough, she is fair, and she sees a future where tribal nations and the State of Maine thrive side by side.” Hannah released her third ad this week, “ Time Out ”, and has secured her place as the front-runner in the general election, fueled by strong grassroots support, a strong bipartisan coalition, record-breaking fundraising, high volunteer engagement, and a growing list of endorsements from elected officials, health care experts, fisherman, housing leaders and community advocates across Maine.
Hannah also earned strong reviews for her debate performances.
Eight public polls have shown her with a commanding lead as early voting begins and heading into November.

I’m running for re-election because Minnesota families deserve a government that lives within its means and puts taxpayers first.
With the rising cost of groceries, gasoline and energy, I’m fighting for permanent tax relief, responsible spending, and policies that help you keep more of your hard-earned money.
I’m Bobbie Harder, and I approve this message.

So am I.
I’m State Representative Bobbie Harder, proudly serving District 17B.
Last year, I supported Minnesota’s largest spending reduction.
This year, I supported plans to cut taxes by nearly four billion dollars.
My goal is simple: eliminate wasteful spending, cut your taxes, and put taxpayers first.
Vote to re-elect Bobbie Harder for State Representative.
I’m Bobbie Harder, and I approve this message. ​ ​ Bobbie Harder - Fraud Prevention Hi, I’m State Representative Bobbie Harder, proudly serving District 17B.

But there’s more work to do.
I’ll continue fighting to strengthen oversight, hold fraudsters accountable and protect your hard-earned money.
I’m Bobbie Harder, and I approve this message. ​ Bobbie Harder - Minnesota Families Tired of watching Minnesota waste your tax dollars?
So am I.
I’m State Representative Bobbie Harder, serving District 17B.
I’m fighting for permanent tax relief, responsible government spending, and to help Minnesota families keep more of their hard-earned money.
And we must fight fraud.
Billions of taxpayer dollars have been lost, and while we strengthened fraud prevention and accountability last session, there’s more work to do.
Minnesota families work hard for their money.
Government should too.
I’m Bobbie Harder, and I approve this message.

Are you in Senate District 32?
Michael Hettig FOR Georgia State Senate District 32 Attorney.
Advocate.
Democrat.
I am an attorney, advocate, and proud resident of Woodstock, Georgia.
This community's strong schools, thriving neighborhoods, and bright future are the perfect foundation for a hopeful, growing family.
But over time, hope has turned into concern as the political climate has shifted and our neighbors’ voices have gone unheard.
I grew tired of only being able to offer sympathy and empty platitudes like “it’s going to be okay.” I decided to take action.
I want more than “okay” for Cherokee and Cobb County.
I want a future that’s exciting and full of opportunity.
Donate Here!
About Me: Let’s Chat rEAD MORE POSITIONS HERE Affordable healthcare is a common-sense necessity.

Fully expanding affordable healthcare access is a critical step to keeping our rural hospitals open, lowering insurance premiums, and ensuring that a single medic al emergency doesn't lead to financial ruin for working families.
Education We must prioritize public education.
Our schools are the foundation of our future economy.
I will advocate for funding that reflects modern classroom needs.
This means competitive teacher salaries and robust vocational training, so every student, regardless of zip code, is prepared for a fulfilling career and life.
The Economy Healthcare priorities Our economy must work for working people.
Georgia’s strength isn’t built on massive corporations; it’s built on our infrastructure, our small businesses, and our workers.
I will work to shift the focus toward policies that lower everyday costs and prioritize investments in the people who actually drive our state economy, not out-of-state corporations.
As a candidate who does not accept any corporate PAC money, every dollar helps make this campaign possible. dONATE! hOW CAN i JOIN THE CAMPAIGN?
Canvassing, postcard parties, and more!
There are so many opportunities to help Michael get the word out.
VOLUNTEER!
Here are some places you can join Michael in reaching out to voters! aTTEND!

added: Skip navigation menu About Troy Endorsements Priorities News Volunteer Events Vote DONATE About Troy Endorsements Priorities News Volunteer Events Vote DONATE VOTING INFORMATION & RESOURCES MAKE A PLAN TO VOTE FOR TROY Election Day November 3 Polling places open on Tuesday, November 3 between 6:00 AM and 10:00 AM, and close at 8:00 pm.
Anyone in line by 8:00 PM on Election Day can register and vote.
Find your polling place here.
Early In-Person Voting Starts on October 5 You can vote early in-person at your municipal clerk's office between Monday, October 5 and Thursday, October 29.
Check your municipal clerk's office hours for In-Person Absentee Voting availability.
Mail-in Voting Request by October 29 To vote by mail, your absentee ballot request must be received by the close of business on Thursday, October 29.
Voters can request absentee ballots online here.
Check if you're registered to vote Register to vote Request a mail ballot Early voting locations IWILLVOTE.COM MAINE.GOV/VOTE To reach the campaign, email info@jacksonformaine.com .
For press inquiries, email press@jacksonformaine.com .
If you'd like to contribute by check, checks can be made out to Troy Jackson for Maine and mailed to: P.O.

Texas deserves another choice even if the parties and the press refuse to make room for one.
Our commitment is to all Texans who are determined to be a part of building something new.
This revolution will be powered by people, service, accountability, creative collaborations, unity, and speaking truth to power on all sides of the aisle.
Here’s how to write-in Jade Simmons for the Nov.
3rd election (or during the early voting period Oct.19th-30th): Important: If you’re not already, get registered to vote today.

We pursued ballot access through Texas’s intentionally extreme independent petition process because Texans deserve more than two party-approved options.
That process revealed what many voters already feel: the system is not designed to welcome independent voices.
So we are taking the next step.
Jade Simmons is running as a registered write-in candidate for U.S.
Senate.

Jade Simmons will be a registered write-in candidate with the Secretary of State’s office.

PRESS RELEASE Jake Johnson Wins KEYC Debate With a Clear Plan to Lower Costs in Southern Minnesota PRESS RELEASE Congressman Brad Finstad is running a TV ad with a fake photo of Jake Johnson Oct 10 2026 PRESS RELEASE Brad Finstad took $23,000 linked to the CCP.
Jake is calling on him to give it back.
WINONA, MN — Earlier this week, Rep.

Brad Finstad introduced a bill that he claims will go after technology risks from the Chinese Communist Party, warning about tech companies “closely affiliated with communist China.” Today, for the first time, Jake Johnson is pointing out that Finstad took money from a registered lobbyist for a Chinese data center company.
Jake is calling on Finstad to return that check and to return the additional $22,500 he has taken from a Chinese state-owned corporation.
“Brad Finstad received money from a lobbyist for a Chinese data center company just 13 days after he voted to speed up the construction of data centers,” said Jake Johnson .
“Now he wants us to believe he’s the one who will protect us from Chinese tech?

Folks in southern Minnesota are already worried about data centers driving up their electric bills and China buying up our farmland, and they sure didn’t expect their congressman to be taking $23,000 linked to the Chinese Communist Party.
Brad should give the money back.
I’ll stand up to China, not sell out to it.” Photo courtesy of Jake Johnson for Congress.
Media use permitted with attribution.
The check.
On Dec.
31, 2025, Finstad’s campaign took $500 from Van D.
Hipp Jr., a registered lobbyist for Bitdeer Technologies Group.
Hipp’s firm reported lobbying the Commerce and State departments for Bitdeer on “cryptocurrency mining and onshoring manufacturing for advanced semiconductors.” The timing.
The check came 13 days after Finstad voted for the SPEED Act, which speeds up federal permitting for data centers.
The CCP ties.
The Texas Standard featured Bitdeer in its reporting on Chinese-owned crypto mines and the national security and power grid concerns they raise.
Bitdeer was founded by Jihan Wu, who a New York Times reporter described to the Texas Standard as “born in China, raised in China,” and who co-founded Bitmain, the Chinese bitcoin mining-chip giant.
Bitdeer was spun off from Bitmain in 2021 in a likely effort to shield it from scrutiny from the U.S.
Commerce Department and U.S. national security investigations, and Wu has since moved to Singapore, where Bitdeer lists its headquarters.
The power bill.
Bitdeer runs data centers and bitcoin mines.
Its Texas site alone uses about as much electricity as 300,000 homes, according to the Texas Standard .
The security risk.
Finstad’s bill is about “cyber espionage risks” from Chinese tech.

Bitmain, the company Bitdeer was spun off from, has been the subject of a Department of Homeland Security investigation into whether its machines could be used for espionage or to sabotage the power grid.
The Commerce Department blacklisted a Bitmain affiliate for “acting at the behest of Beijing.” Not the first time.

Finstad has also taken $22,500 from the PAC of Syngenta, which is owned by a Chinese state-owned company that the Pentagon lists as a “Chinese military company.” Syngenta owns hundreds of acres of farmland in Goodhue County.

Finstad has voted against stopping Chinese companies from buying more farmland, and has also voted to shield pesticide companies including Syngenta for being held liable if their products harm farmers and community members.
REMINDER: Finstad took over $40,000 from data center and utility companies and voted to give over $80 billion in tax breaks to the companies building data centers.

The doctored photo replaces Beth Benike – a 10-year U.S.
Army veteran and the 2025 Minnesota Small Business Owner of the Year – with Tim Walz.
Now, the Finstad campaign is blasting this image out on the airwaves, despite being fabricated.

“My own congressman wouldn’t even talk to me in my time of deepest need that he was directly impacting and continuing to make worse, and now he’s using a photo taken at my warehouse and took me out of it?,” said Beth Benike in a comment to HuffPost .
“Can you make someone feel any less significant?” “Brad Finstad is fabricating fake photos because he can’t defend his record,” said Nik Marda, spokesperson for Jake Johnson .

“He’s trying to trick people, but the voters of southern Minnesota won’t be distracted from Finstad’s votes to raise prices, continue the Iran War, and give tax breaks to data center companies.” Finstad’s campaign did not deny that the photo was altered.

Instead, his spokesperson in a statement to KSTP said that his campaign has “not violated any laws.” Minnesota state law bans the use of deepfakes to influence an election , and that law covers any photograph or electronic image “so realistic that a reasonable person would believe it depicts speech or conduct of an individual who did not in fact engage in such speech or conduct.” This is part of a broader pattern of conduct.
Finstad’s first TV ad falsely claimed Jake would raise taxes on tips, overtime, and Social Security.
Jake supports ending taxes on all three.

When the next Finstad ad drops, feel free to reference this press release: Jake does not support taxpayer-funded healthcare for people who are in the United States illegally, and Jake supports full funding for our police departments, Veterans’ programs, Social Security, and Medicare.

This image of Johnson giving Walz a thumbs up never happened.

It’s a combination of one half of a photo of Johnson with a local business owner, but the business owner’s image is replaced by a picture of Walz.” “State law says a deepfake can be any video or photograph that is so realistic a reasonable person would believe the speech or conduct happened.

Brad Finstad Runs Attack Ad That Erases Critical Voter From Photo “Minnesota small business owner Beth Benike was watching the Netflix show “Bridgerton” on Monday night when she noticed a familiar image in a political ad that aired during a commercial break: the exact shot of Democratic congressional nominee Jake Johnson from a photo she’d been in with him last year.” “Except in this attack ad from Johnson’s opponent, Republican Rep.
Brad Finstad, Benike wasn’t in the photo anymore.
In her place, in what appeared to be an AI-generated image , was Democratic Gov.
Tim Walz.” “After being named Minnesota’s Small Business Person of the Year in March 2025, Benike was making news days later talking about struggling because of Trump’s tariffs.
She reached out to Finstad several times for help, but said he didn’t offer any.
When she twice tried to meet with him in Washington, D.C., he declined.

She met Johnson in April, when he heard her story and asked if he could come to her warehouse to learn more about tariffs.” “That’s where they ended up in a photo together, and why Benike quickly recognized Johnson’s image in Finstad’s campaign ad.

She said she remembers that day “really clearly,” including what Johnson was wearing and where they were standing in her warehouse.” “I was like, ‘You’ve got to be kidding me,’” Benike told HuffPost, with a weak laugh.

“My own congressman wouldn’t even talk to me in my time of deepest need that he was directly impacting and continuing to make worse, and now he’s using a photo taken at my warehouse and took me out of it?
Can you make someone feel any less significant?” “What a poor decision,” said Benike.
“You’d better believe I’m going to be sharing this with the people that have been following my story....

Days Hours Minutes Seconds Testimonials What People Say Most of the “stuff” we struggle with in our political discourse is nonsense, which will fade away with the passage of time.
What will stand the test of time is the primary purpose and focus of Rev.
Gailliard’s campaign: common sense policy helping the average citizen earn a living wage, have access to health care and safe effective public schools, among other things.
All else falls short of what should always be the standard : “ Until All Thrive!”.
Robert Evans “My wife and I are natives of Nash County who have spent our lives in the Tarheel State.
Since we made Nash County our retirement home, we have witnessed the politics of division leaving more citizens behind.
We have also made a new friend in James Gailliard and have observed his untiring efforts to promote unity and well-being among our neighbors.
James embodies the old values of honesty and integrity.
We know that when he returns to the North Carolina legislature as our senator he will help create the positive change we need so that everyone will have the opportunity to thrive.
As unaffiliated voters, neither Democrat nor Republican, we stand with James Gailliard.” Chuck Taylor “As Senate Minority Leader, I’m thrilled to endorse Pastor Gailliard for N.C.
Senate.

As a trusted community figure and proven leader in the legislature, Pastor Gailliard knows firsthand the issues facing District 11 and how best to serve the people of Nash, Franklin, and Vance Counties.

I’m confident that he will lead with integrity, and I look forward to working with him to ensure all North Carolinians have access to the opportunities they need to thrive.” Sydney Batch James Gailliard possesses the character, commitment and intellect necessary to serve the people in the North Carolina Senate.
James understands the legislative process and will fight for those who have been left behind regardless of race or party affiliation.
He knows when to fight; and he knows when to compromise.
I urge my friends to vote for James Gailliard for State Senate.
G.K.
Butterfield Since his arrival to Nash County, James Gailliard has been my brother and friend, a visionary who reads the signs of the times and responds with wisdom.

Gailliard For over 25 years, Pastor James D.
Gailliard has answered the call to shepherd and serve—first as the organizing Senior Pastor of Word Tabernacle Church in Rocky Mount, and then as your voice in the North Carolina General Assembly.

His journey from planting a 14-person congregation to building one of America's 100 fastest-growing churches mirrors his commitment to turning vision into reality for working families across our district.
James D.
Gailliard This isn’t about politics.
It’s about people.
James D.

Gailliard Political Leader Pastoral Leadership That Transforms Communities As Senior Pastor of Word Tabernacle Church, Pastor Gailliard has shepherded a ministry that now impacts thousands of families across 35 North Carolina counties and reaches internationally.
Under his leadership, the church transformed a former 110,000 sq. ft.
Home Depot into a thriving community hub—the largest building re-use project of its kind in North Carolina.
This represents more than renovation; it’s community reclamation at its finest.
Historic Legislative Leadership Pastor Gailliard made history as the first person of color elected to represent North Carolina House District 25, serving two terms with distinction.
His legislative work focused on the issues that matter most to working families: criminal justice reform, educational equity, and economic opportunity.

He brought both pastoral wisdom and policy expertise to Raleigh, serving on critical commissions including the Task Force for Racial Equity in Criminal Justice and the DRIVE Task Force for educational inclusion.

Commissioner of MyFutureNC Community Impact Beyond the Pulpit His commitment to systemic change extends through multiple leadership roles: Commissioner of MyFutureNC, co-developing North Carolina’s statewide educational attainment goals.
Founder and Chairman of The REACH Center, Inc.
Trustee of Elizabeth City State University.
Principal of Impact James D.
Gailliard A Voice for Our Times As an inductee of the Morehouse College Board of Preachers and sought-after speaker, Pastor Gailliard brings prophetic clarity to today's challenges.
His work has been featured in Facts & Trends, Church Executive, and Business North Carolina.
Husband, father, grandfather, and servant-leader—James D.
Gailliard continues to lead with the same compassion, conviction, and courage that built a thriving church and delivered results in the legislature.
Because when all may thrive, our communities are stronger.
Recognition for Service Pastor Gailliard’s lifelong dedication has earned him the Algernon Sydney Sullivan Award and the President Joseph R.
Biden, Jr.
Lifetime Achievement Award.
He’s a Fellow of the NC Institute of Political Leadership and former Chairman of the Board for the NC Legislative Black Caucus Foundation.

The district’s leadership has the opportunity to advocate for the needs of working families, small businesses, and underserved communities across the region.
Policy Positions Areas of concern Policy Positions Key priorities for District 11 include expanding workforce training, closing the digital divide, and advancing criminal justice reform.
The platform champions equitable healthcare, strong public schools, housing stability, and food security through initiatives like Homes and Hope and Abundant Life Nutrition.

Donate Now Blog By James Gailliard December 11, 2024 0 Comments In times of crisis, we often find ourselves at a crossroads, facing challenges that seem insurmountable.
Yet, it is precisely in these moments that we are called to rise, to act, and to transform our circumstances.
Today, we stand at such a juncture – a political, moral, and spiritual inflection point that demands our attention and action.
The prophet Joel spoke of a time when God would pour out His Spirit on all flesh, when young and old alike would prophesy and see visions.

This ancient prophecy, echoed by Peter on the day of Pentecost, reminds us that in moments of great upheaval, God is at work, empowering His people to speak truth to power and to envision a new reality.
We find ourselves in a moment where democracy is under siege, where health disparities widen, and where the very institutions meant to protect us seem to falter.
It’s a time when Black landowners face displacement, when environmental injustice threatens our communities, and when systemic inequalities persist.
But make no mistake – this is not a new crisis.
It is the latest iteration of an old pattern, one that our ancestors warned us about and fought against.
In the face of such challenges, we need not a new idea, but an old standard – the ancient paths of righteousness and justice.

We are called to be both biblically grounded and politically urgent, recognizing that the issues we face are not isolated but interconnected strands of oppression threatening to unravel the fabric of our society.
Yet, in this crisis lies opportunity.
As Queen Esther was told, “Who knows if you have come to the kingdom for such a time as this?” We too are here for such a time as this.
We are called to chart a course not away from the storm, but through it – guided by the North Star of justice, steered by the rudder of faith, and powered by the wind of the Spirit.
History reminds us that crisis is often the cradle of calling.
From the Exodus to the Empty Tomb, God has always done His best work in the worst of times.
When Pharaoh’s grip seemed unbreakable, God raised up Moses.
When Jericho’s walls loomed impenetrable, God brought them down with a shout.
When Goliath threatened to destroy David, God turned a sling into a sword.
And when they nailed Jesus to a cross and sealed Him in a tomb, God rolled the stone away.
As we navigate these turbulent waters, we must recognize that the systems we’re up against are not accidental but intentional architectures of oppression.
Like skilled navigators, we must identify the rocks and shoals of injustice that threaten to wreck our common life.
But we cannot allow discouragement to dry up our will.
The enemy of our movement is not just racism – it’s resignation.
We are called to participate in the process, protect the polls, prioritize public health, preserve the planet, pursue penal reform, and promote prosperity.
These are not just political objectives; they are moral imperatives rooted in biblical principles.

Proverbs 31:8-9 commands us to “Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves; ensure justice for those being crushed.” This means protecting voting rights, challenging unjust systems, and confronting corrupted power – just as Esther did before the king, and as Jesus did when He overturned the tables in the temple.

Luke 4:18 reminds us that we are anointed to “heal the brokenhearted” and “proclaim liberty to the captives.” This calls us to address health disparities, tackle environmental injustice, and reform a penal system that disproportionately affects communities of color.
We must embody the spirit of the Great Physician, healing not just with prayers, but with policies.
Amos 5:24 urges us to “let justice roll down like waters.” How can justice flow if our rivers are poisoned?
Environmental justice is biblical justice, a sacred responsibility given to us since the Garden of Eden.
In all these efforts, we must remember that we serve a God who specializes in the impossible.
The same power that raised Jesus from the dead is alive in us.
When we feel weary, we must recall the words of Langston Hughes: “I tire so of hearing people say, Let things take their course.
Tomorrow is another day.
I cannot live on tomorrow’s bread.” We are called to rise today, to act today, to love today.
As we face these challenges, let us draw strength from our rich heritage of resilience and faith.
If Rosa could sit, if Martin could march, if Fannie Lou could testify, if Jesus could die and rise again – then surely, we can stand.
We will not bow to unjust policies, shrink in the face of opposition, or stay silent in the chambers of power.
We will speak.
We will vote.
We will build.
We will believe.
This is our moment.
This is our mandate.
This is our ministry.
We stand at the threshold of a new chapter in our collective story.
The problems we face are vast, but we serve a God who split the sea, stopped the sun, made manna fall from heaven, and turned water into wine.
If God can part seas and raise the dead, surely He can raise up a generation of justice warriors.
Surely, He can part the red tape of policy and make a way where there seems to be no way.
As we move forward, let us do so with the conviction that justice will roll, hope will rise, and freedom will ring.
Let us remember that the blood still works, the cross still saves, the tomb is still empty, and the kingdom is still coming.
In the face of crisis, we are called to conquest – not through force or domination, but through faith, love, and unwavering commitment to justice.
This is the moment we’ve been waiting for, the movement we’ve been praying for, the miracle we’ve been preparing for.
Let us rise to the occasion, knowing that with God, all things are possible.
Our ancestors walked this road before us, and now it’s our turn to carry the torch forward.

Donate Now In The News By James Gailliard July 18, 2025 0 Comments About This News This article is based on a full feature published by WRAL News on July 11, 2025.

Read the original story here: Why NC Democrats think 2026 midterms will run through Rocky Mount – WRAL News Rocky Mount, NC – July 11, 2025 – WRAL reports that Democrat James Gailliard , Rocky Mount pastor and former state representative, has officially announced his campaign for the 2026 North Carolina State Senate seat now held by Republican Sen.
Lisa Stone Barnes .
The story highlights that Gailliard’s bid comes at a pivotal moment, as North Carolina Democrats attempt to dismantle the GOP’s veto-proof majority in the Senate.
Barnes’ current district—encompassing Nash, Franklin, and Vance counties—is now viewed as one of the state’s most competitive legislative battlegrounds.
A Race With Statewide Stakes Political insiders on both sides acknowledge this is among fewer than six winnable Senate races statewide—and perhaps the marquee 2026 matchup.
Analysts note that a Democratic flip here would force GOP lawmakers and Gov.
Josh Stein to collaborate more on the budget and legislative priorities.

A Pastor With a Purpose Gailliard, who leads Word Tabernacle Church and served two House terms before an electoral loss in 2022, says he aims to elevate issues of economic inequality while tailoring his message to resonate with rural voters.

“A message that works in Durham is not going to work in rural eastern North Carolina,” Gailliard emphasized, underscoring the importance of reaching working families and farmers in small-town settings.
Rallying the Party Behind Gailliard The campaign launch drew statewide Democratic leaders—including Senate Minority Leader Sydney Batch and Supreme Court Justice Anita Earls—alongside top N.C.
Democratic Party strategists.
Batch declared this contest “the #1 competitive, pick-up Senate seat” needed to break the Senate supermajority, pledging campaign investments north of $3 million.
Why It Matters This race is not just local—it’s a potential turning point in North Carolina politics.
Gailliard’s campaign raises fundamental questions about economic justice, representation of rural voices, and the balance of power in Raleigh.
With registered Democrats making up the largest voting bloc in the district but recent trends favoring Republicans, Gailliard’s candidacy offers a fresh and disciplined challenge to the status quo.

Join Us 01.
Criminal Justice Advance the “Restoration and Reconciliation Act” building on recent NC criminal justice reforms (SB 300).
Digital Access & Broadband Champion the “Digital Dignity Act” ensuring every household has access to affordable high-speed internet by 2030.
Economics & Workforce Create the “Second Chance Workforce Initiative” combining faith-based mentorship with skills training.
Healthcare Access & Maternal Health Protect and expand Medicaid expansion that has already enrolled 650,000 North Carolinians.
Educational Attainment Support legislation ensuring full constitutional funding for public schools while maintaining quality school choice options.
Housing & Community Development Create the “Homes and Hope Initiative” providing down payment assistance.
Food & Nutrition Establish the “Abundant Life Nutrition Program” combining policy advocacy with community-based solutions.
James D.
Gailliard Why I am Running I’m running for the North Carolina Senate because our communities deserve more than survival—they deserve to thrive.
As a father, pastor, and former legislator, I’ve seen firsthand what happens when people are overlooked by Raleigh and underserved by systems meant to protect them.
My life’s work—whether in the pulpit or at the policy table—has been to lift voices, build bridges, and fight for justice.
During my time in the General Assembly, I helped pass bipartisan legislation on education, healthcare, criminal justice reform, and economic development.
Now I’m ready to finish what we started.
I believe our faith should fuel public good.
Our churches, schools, and neighborhoods should be places of opportunity.

And every child—whether in Franklin, Nash, or Vance County—should grow up with access to quality education, good healthcare, and a safe place to live Accessible – Regular town halls in all three counties Accountable – Public reports on every vote Active – Present in communities, not just Raleigh Authentic – The same person in office as in the pulpit About James Support our candidate A Different Kind of Leadership Too often, politics divides us into camps, reduces complex issues to sound bites, and forgets the human faces behind policies.
I offer something different.

Healthcare as a human right.
Education that unlocks potential.
Justice that heals communities.
Infrastructure that connects us all.
Food security for every household.
Housing that families can afford.
I Will Be: Accessible – Regular town halls in all three counties.
Accountable – Public reports on every vote.
Active – Present in communities, not just Raleigh.
Authentic – The same person in office as in the pulpit.

Introduction Thank you for visiting the official website of James D.
Gailliard .
We respect your privacy and are committed to protecting any personal data you provide.
This Privacy Policy outlines how we collect, use, store, and protect your information when you visit or interact with this website.
By using this website, you consent to the practices described herein.
Data Collected Data Storage Location We operate servers located in the United States.
Any data you provide through this website is processed and stored in accordance with applicable privacy regulations.
Contact Forms and Newsletter Signups When you fill out a contact form or subscribe to our newsletter, we collect your name, email address, and any other information you provide voluntarily.
This data is used solely for the purposes of communication and outreach related to James D.
Gailliard’s public activities.
Website Analytics We use third-party services such as Google Analytics to understand how users interact with our website.
This involves collecting anonymized data such as pages visited, browser type, and general location (based on IP address).
No personally identifiable information is stored.
Comments (if enabled) If the website allows users to leave comments, we may collect the comment, name, email address, and IP address to help with spam detection and moderation.
Use of Your Personal Information We may use the information we collect to: Respond to inquiries or messages you send via our contact form.
Send email updates or newsletters (only if you opt in).
Improve website performance and user experience.
Ensure the security and integrity of the website.
Comply with legal obligations if necessary.
Embedded Content from Other Websites Articles or pages on this site may include embedded content (e.g., videos from YouTube, tweets, etc.).
Embedded content behaves exactly as if the visitor has visited the originating website.
These websites may collect data, use cookies, and monitor your interaction with the embedded content if you are logged in to their platform.

We currently use or may use services such as: YouTube – Video embedding Facebook – Page feeds or post previews Twitter/X – Embedded tweets Please refer to each platform’s own privacy policy for details.
Cookies You can disable cookies through your browser settings at any time.
Who Has Access to Your Data Your personal information is only accessible to the website administrator and authorized personnel responsible for managing site content and communications.
Third-Party Access We do not sell or share your data with third parties for marketing purposes.
However, some data may be shared with trusted third-party services solely to operate the website efficiently (e.g., email delivery services, analytics platforms, or hosting providers).
Data Retention We retain your personal data only for as long as necessary to fulfill the purpose for which it was collected.
For example, email inquiries are kept as long as needed for correspondence.
If you’ve signed up for a newsletter, you can unsubscribe at any time and your data will be deleted upon request.
Security Measures We use SSL (Secure Sockets Layer) technology to protect data transmissions between your browser and our website.
Regular maintenance, updates, and monitoring help ensure the security and reliability of the site.
Your Rights If you are a resident of the European Union or a region with similar data rights, you have the right to: Access, correct, or delete your personal data.
Request a copy of the data we hold about you.
Withdraw consent for communication or data processing.
To exercise these rights, please contact us using the details provided at the end of this policy.
Links to External Sites This website may contain links to third-party websites.
We are not responsible for the privacy practices or content of those websites.
Please review their privacy policies before submitting any personal data.
Legal Disclosure We may disclose your information if required to do so by law or in response to valid legal processes.
We will make reasonable efforts to notify you if such disclosure is requested unless prohibited by law.
Contact Us If you have any questions or concerns about this Privacy Policy or your data, please contact: James D.

Donate Now Blog By James Gailliard July 9, 2025 0 Comments In our fast-paced world of instant gratification and “get rich quick” schemes, it’s easy to lose sight of the profound value of hard work.

Yet, as we delve into the very foundations of human existence, we find that work is not just a means to earn money – it’s a divine tool for personal growth, relationship readiness, and community contribution.
Let’s journey back to the beginning, to the Garden of Eden.

In Genesis 2:15, we find a powerful truth: “The Lord God took the man and put him in the Garden of Eden to work it and take care of it.” This verse reveals God’s intention for humanity from the start.
Before introducing relationships or any other aspect of adult life, God established work as the primary building block for human development.
Why is this significant?
Because work is not something we do after becoming adults; it’s what makes us adults.
It cultivates our character, commitment to excellence, and ability to contribute to our community.
These three pillars form the foundation of a fulfilling and purposeful life.
Cultivating Character When we engage in consistent, purposeful work, we develop essential traits that shape our character.
Patience, consistency, selflessness, long-term thinking, and problem-solving skills are all honed through our daily tasks.
Consider the nurse working a 12-hour shift, learning stamina and selflessness that will later help in caring for a crying baby.
Or the teacher managing 35 students, building patience and multitasking abilities that will prove invaluable in various life situations.
These character traits don’t magically appear when we need them in our personal lives or relationships.
They are cultivated through the discipline of showing up, day after day, to fulfill our responsibilities.
This is why God established work before introducing Eve to Adam – He wanted to ensure Adam had developed the character necessary for a successful partnership.
Commitment to Excellence Work not only shapes our character but also instills in us a commitment to excellence.
When we consistently apply ourselves to our tasks, we naturally develop a desire to do things well and to make a meaningful impact.
This commitment to excellence translates directly into our relationships and other areas of life.
Think about the skills we develop through work: communication, conflict resolution, shared responsibility, and teamwork.
These are the very same skills needed for successful relationships, whether in marriage, friendship, or community involvement.
By learning to excel in our work, we’re preparing ourselves for excellence in all areas of life.
It’s worth noting that Jesus himself modeled this principle.
He didn’t begin his ministry until he was 30 years old, having spent years working as a carpenter.
During that time, he cultivated patience through repetitive tasks, developed precision through measuring and cutting wood, and built problem-solving and customer service skills.
All of these prepared him for his ultimate calling.
Contributing to Community Finally, our work ethic directly impacts our ability to contribute to our community.
When we approach our jobs with diligence and excellence, we’re not just benefiting ourselves – we’re adding value to the lives of those around us.
Conversely, when we neglect our responsibilities or refuse to work, others must carry our load.
This principle extends beyond paid employment.
It applies to our roles in our families, churches, and broader communities.

As the saying goes, “Takers make terrible partners.” Whether in a marriage, a friendship, or a community organization, those who consistently contribute are the ones who build strong, thriving relationships and communities.
Reflecting on Work in Our Lives As we consider these truths, it’s important to examine our own attitudes toward work.
Are we viewing our daily tasks as mere obstacles to our goals, or are we recognizing them as pathways to personal growth and relationship readiness?
Are we seeking to become the kind of person a quality partner would want to marry, or are we simply hoping to find the perfect person?
Are we building the character that will qualify us for future opportunities, or are we just waiting for the perfect job to fall into our laps?
The reality is, our daily work is not separate from our spiritual life, our family life, or our relationship goals.
It’s an integral part of God’s process for building responsible adulthood.
By embracing this truth, we position ourselves for growth, success, and fulfillment in all areas of life.

Practical Steps Forward If you find yourself struggling with work ethic or feeling unfulfilled in your current role, consider these steps: Reframe your perspective: Instead of viewing work as a necessary evil, see it as an opportunity for personal growth and character development.
Set small, achievable goals: Focus on excelling in your current tasks, no matter how mundane they may seem.
Seek opportunities to learn: Every job has lessons to teach.
Be intentional about identifying and applying these lessons to your personal and professional life.
Contribute beyond your job description: Look for ways to add value to your workplace, family, or community beyond what’s expected of you.
Cultivate a spirit of service: Approach your work with the mindset of serving others, rather than just earning a paycheck.
Remember, it’s not about finding the perfect job or relationship.
It’s about becoming the kind of person who is ready for the opportunities and relationships God has in store for you.
By embracing a strong work ethic, you’re not just building a career – you’re building a life of purpose, excellence, and meaningful contribution.
As we go forward, let’s challenge ourselves to approach our work – whatever it may be – with renewed vigor and purpose.
For in doing so, we’re not just earning a living; we’re living out God’s design for our growth, our relationships, and our impact on the world around us.
The harvest of a life well-lived begins with the hustle of daily faithfulness.
Are you ready to embrace the challenge?

Donate Now Blog By James Gailliard December 11, 2024 0 Comments In a world where the term “woke” has become both a rallying cry and a point of contention, it’s time we reclaim its true spiritual meaning.
Being woke isn’t about political correctness or divisive ideology—it’s about being awake to injustice, open to the suffering of others, and conscious of how power and systems affect the vulnerable.
In essence, it’s about following in the footsteps of Jesus, who was acutely aware of religious hypocrisy, economic exploitation, and political oppression.
The problem facing many today isn’t being too woke—it’s being too fake.
Fake faith sleeps through injustice, accumulates wealth while preaching about a poor savior, and serves political power while claiming to worship the Prince of Peace.
It’s this in authenticity that’s driving people away from the church, not an awakened consciousness to the world’s problems.
Young people aren’t leaving the church because it’s too woke; they’re leaving because they’re too real for fake faith.
They crave authenticity, relationships, and a community that doesn’t just talk about love but actually practices it.
They’re seeking a faith that doesn’t shy away from difficult questions or discourage intellectual curiosity.
So what does a “woke” church—a church truly awake to God’s calling—look like?
We can find a blueprint in Acts 2:42-47, which paints a picture of the early church that was vibrant, engaged, and transformative.
Cultivating Real Relationships The early believers “devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer” (Acts 2:42).
This wasn’t a sporadic enthusiasm or a casual commitment—it was a radical life reorientation.
They didn’t just show up once a week for an hour; they were constantly engaged in learning, growing, and supporting one another.
Real faith demands more than just looking better on the outside.
It’s not about learning to sin in better clothes or figuring out how to hide our flaws more effectively.
It’s about genuine transformation from the inside out.
It’s about committing to collective learning and growth, challenging ourselves and each other to become more like Christ every day.
Combating Economic Exploitation “They sold property and possessions to give to anyone who had need” (Acts 2:45).
The early church recognized that true faith couldn’t coexist with economic inequality within their community.
They took radical steps to ensure that everyone’s needs were met, sharing resources sacrificially and voluntarily.
This stands in stark contrast to both prosperity theology, which often focuses on individual wealth accumulation, and forms of Christianity that ignore social justice issues.
The early church understood that spirituality and social action are inseparable—the same God who saves souls cares deeply about systems and structures that affect people’s lives.
When we give to support our faith communities, we become agents fighting against economic exploitation.
We demonstrate that Christianity is about shared prosperity, not individual accumulation.
And crucially, this giving and support should come without strings attached—we serve and give because it’s right, not because we expect something in return.
Championing Authentic Witness “Every day they continued to meet together in the temple courts.
They broke bread in their homes and ate together with glad and sincere hearts, praising God and enjoying the favor of all the people” (Acts 2:46-47).
One of the most powerful witnesses to the truth of our faith is authentic joy.
The early believers didn’t just endure their faith—they lived it out with gladness and generosity of spirit.
This joy wasn’t dependent on circumstances; it was a deep-seated contentment and excitement about what God was doing in and through them.
In a world full of cynicism and despair, nothing stands out more than someone who maintains their joy even when things are difficult.

When we can praise God in the midst of a funeral, when we can maintain our faith in the face of a difficult diagnosis, when we can still lift our hands in worship after losing a job—that’s when people take notice.
That’s when they start to wonder about the source of our strength and peace.
This joy isn’t about plastering on a fake smile or denying the reality of our pain.
It’s about recognizing that our ultimate source of joy is God Himself, not our circumstances.
When God is the wellspring of our joy, no person or situation can take it away from us.
The Challenge Before Us As we reflect on these characteristics of a truly “woke” faith, we’re faced with a challenge.
Are we cultivating real, deep relationships within our faith communities?
Are we actively working to combat economic exploitation and injustice?
Are we living out our faith with such authentic joy that others can’t help but take notice?
It’s time to move beyond fake faith—beyond performative Christianity that looks good on the outside but lacks depth and authenticity.
It’s time to wake up to the real, transformative power of the gospel.
It’s time to be too woke to be fake.
This journey isn’t easy.
It requires us to be vulnerable, to challenge our own assumptions, and to step out of our comfort zones.
It means being willing to have difficult conversations, to examine our own biases and blind spots, and to actively work for justice and equality.
But the reward is immeasurable.
When we embrace this kind of awakened faith, we don’t just change ourselves—we begin to change the world around us.
We become living testimonies to the power of God’s love and grace.
We create communities where people can find healing, hope, and belonging.
So let’s wake up.
Let’s commit ourselves to real relationships, to combating injustice, and to living out our faith with authentic joy.

Let’s be the kind of believers that make others say, “I want the God you have.” In doing so, we’ll not only transform our own lives but also offer a compelling witness to a world desperately in need of authentic, transformative faith.

Gailliard Support our candidate Why I am Running James D.
Gailliard Leadership you can always trust I’m running for the North Carolina Senate because our communities deserve more than survival—they deserve to thrive.
As a father, pastor, and former legislator, I’ve seen firsthand what happens when people are overlooked by Raleigh and underserved by systems meant to protect them.
My life’s work—whether in the pulpit or at the policy table—has been to lift voices, build bridges, and fight for justice.
During my time in the General Assembly, I helped pass bipartisan legislation on education, healthcare, criminal justice reform, and economic development.
Now I’m ready to finish what we started.
I believe our faith should fuel public good.
Our churches, schools, and neighborhoods should be places of opportunity.
And every child—whether in Franklin, Nash, or Vance County—should grow up with access to quality education, good healthcare, and a safe place to live.
About James Our district stands at a crossroads Why District 11 and why now, you ask?

Economic Crossroads Because our district stands at an Economic Crossroads – Manufacturing jobs disappearing while new opportunities remain out of reach; Young families unable to afford homes in communities where they grew up; Seniors choosing between medication and meals; Rural communities feeling left behind by economic growth.

But, we are also at a Social Crossroads – Achievement gaps that perpetuate generational poverty; Health disparities that cut lives short; Criminal justice systems that punish poverty; Digital divides that exclude rural families.
And let’s not forget, there is a Moral Crossroads Will we choose policies that divide or those that unite?
Will we invest in all our children or just some?
Will we extend second chances or perpetuate cycles?

My Commitment to You When elected I will fight for: Economic opportunity for every family; Healthcare as a human right; Education that unlocks potential; Justice that heals communities; Infrastructure that connects us all; Food security for every household; Housing that families can afford.
While I am fighting, I will never forget where I came from, never put party over people, and never accept the status quo as good enough.
Too often, politics divides us into camps, reduces complex issues to sound bites, and forgets the human faces behind policies.
I offer something different.
For me, this isn’t about politics.
It’s about people..
It’s time to put community back at the center of policy.
My experience as a nonprofit executive has shown me how to bridge differences and build coalitions.
My years in the General Assembly taught me how to navigate complex policy challenges and find common ground.
But it’s my calling as a pastor that drives my commitment to justice, mercy, and walking humbly with our God.

Building a District Where Everyone Thrives Our district needs representation that reflects our diversity – speaking to the concerns of young families struggling with student debt and housing costs, working parents balancing multiple jobs, seniors worried about healthcare and prescription drug costs, and communities seeking both justice and reconciliation.

As someone who has walked alongside people through their darkest moments and celebrated their greatest triumphs, I understand that effective leadership requires both prophetic vision and practical wisdom.

I’m running because the challenges we face – from the digital divide isolating rural communities to the healthcare disparities affecting our most vulnerable residents – require more than partisan politics.
They require the kind of transformative leadership that sees beyond political talking points to the human dignity of every person in our district.
That’s why I’m running.
