added: Menu About Accomplishments Endorsements News Media Get Involved store Facebook Twitter Instagram Youtube Donate Vote Lauren Boebert’s Record for Colorado Lauren Boebert answers to Colorado, not Washington.

Since taking office, she has become one of the most effective legislators in Congress and worked to deliver clean water, better roads and real results for the families, farmers and small towns of Colorado’s 4th District.

Read Lauren's Legislative Victories › By the Numbers $11.75 million signed into law for 13 water projects in Colorado’s 4th District $3 million signed into law for road projects in Colorado’s 4th District 75 legislative and funding provisions signed into law 8 bills and 78 amendments passed the U.S.

House 270+ mobile office hours, held in every county in the district Delivering for Colorado’s 4th District $14.75 Million for Local Water and Roads Signed into law · February 2026 Lauren secured $11.75 million for 13 water projects across the district.
That includes clean, reliable water for Castle Rock, Wiggins, Severance, Lamar, Louviers, Ovid, Kiowa, Brush and Walsh.

She got an additional $3 million for road improvements on the Heartland Expressway (SH 71), Highway 85 and in Windsor. $15 Million+ More for Our Towns Passed committee · June 2026 Lauren is fighting for 16 more local projects, including water and sewer upgrades in Kit Carson, Bristol, Holly, Merino, Nunn, Eaton, Simla, Ault and Burlington; the Republican River Compact pipeline in Yuma County; and road improvements in Highlands Ranch, Castle Pines and Sedalia.
Finishing the Arkansas Valley Conduit About 50,000 people in Southeast Colorado are still waiting on clean drinking water.

Lauren’s Finish the Arkansas Valley Conduit Act passed both the House and the Senate, and she secured the conduit’s language in the Water Resources Development Act, which passed the House in September 2026.
She won’t stop until it’s done.

Keeping South Platte Water in Colorado Nebraska wants to build the Perkins County Canal through Sedgwick County to take South Platte water, and has threatened eminent domain against Colorado landowners.
Lauren is fighting Senate language that would force federal approval of the canal.

Hometown ZIP Codes Passed the House · July 2025 Lauren’s bill, backed by both parties, gives Severance, Castle Pines, Highlands Ranch, Lone Tree and dozens of other communities their own ZIP codes, so residents get the right mail, the right services and the right tax rates.
It passed the House 278-121.

Standing Up for Farmers and Ranchers A Seat at the Farm Bill Table Passed the House · April 2026 Lauren voted to pass the Farm Bill and was named a Farm Bill conferee, where she’s pushing her CREP Improvement Act and local meat processing, grazing access and a ban on Chinese Communist Party ownership of American farmland.
Millet Recognized as a Specialty Crop Passed the House · June 2026 Lauren won specialty crop status for millet, opening new resources for Eastern Plains growers.

Restoring Eastern Plains Rangeland Passed the House · June 2026 $850,000 to treat about 8,900 acres of cheatgrass-infested rangeland in Cheyenne, Kit Carson, Lincoln, Washington and Yuma counties. $10 Million From Bureaucracy to Rural Colorado Passed the House · June 2026 Five Boebert amendments moved $10 million out of back-office spending and into the Farm Service Agency, rural development, rural utilities, conservation and anti-fraud oversight.
Protecting Ranchers Signed into law $3 million to compensate ranchers for livestock killed by wolves, relief for livestock haulers from burdensome regulations, and a block on listing the sage-grouse.
Rural Jobs and Hydropower Expansion Act Passed committee · May 2026 Co-led with Democratic Rep.
Adam Gray, this bill expands hydropower at federal water facilities to create rural jobs and lower energy costs.
It passed committee with support from both parties.
More Water and Land Wins Western Water Accelerated Revenue Repayment Act lets farmers and towns pay off federal water project debt early.
(Passed committee) Trust the Science Act removes the gray wolf from the endangered species list.
(Passed the House) Pet and Livestock Protection Act (Passed committee) CREP Improvement Act, with Rep.
Gabe Evans (Introduced) Serving Our Veterans and Military Veterans Laws Signed into law Expanded travel benefits for rural veterans and permanent veterans’ dental coverage (H.R.

5293) In-state tuition for surviving families using the GI Bill (McHugh Tuition Fairness for Survivors Act) A cost-of-living increase for veterans’ benefits $10 Million More for Veterans Passed the House · May 2026 Five Boebert amendments redirected about $10 million to veterans and their programs.
All five passed with support from both parties.

Strengthening Colorado’s Military Passed the House · August 2026 Four Boebert amendments to the defense bill strengthen the Colorado Air National Guard, protect military bases from drone threats, counter Chinese Communist Party influence on college campuses and bar the military from buying vehicles made with forced labor.
Veterans’ Mental Health Access Act Introduced · October 2026 Veterans in crisis would get inpatient mental health care within 24 hours, and the VA would have to publish its wait times.

Protecting Your Privacy Standing Up to Her Own Party on Surveillance Vote cast · June 2026 When party leaders tried to extend warrantless government spying without new protections, Lauren was one of 19 Republicans who voted no.
The government should need a warrant to search Americans’ data.

Surveillance Accountability Act Introduced · April 2026 Lauren introduced a bill to: require warrants before the government searches Americans’ data stop license plate cameras like Flock from tracking your every move ban warrantless facial recognition in public places, including schools and churches stop federal agencies from buying your location data to get around the warrant requirement Jobs and Energy Pueblo Jobs Act Signed into law · December 2023 Lauren’s Pueblo Jobs Act became law in the national defense bill, paving the way for 1,000+ Colorado jobs as the Pueblo Depot closes.

Cutting Red Tape on American Energy Passed the House of Representatives American Energy Act: extends drilling permits from two to four years 90-Day Review Act: speeds up permitting for major infrastructure Restoring American Energy Dominance Act: repeals a costly BLM rule on Colorado energy producers Colorado Energy Prosperity Act: stops the BLM from locking up 1.6 million acres of Colorado land Keeping Space Command in Colorado Lauren has fought to keep the U.S.
Space Command headquarters, and the jobs that come with it, in Colorado.

removed: Menu About Accomplishments Endorsements News Media Get Involved store Facebook Twitter Instagram Youtube Donate Vote Accomplishments During her short tenure, Congresswoman Lauren Boebert has been one of the most effective legislators in Congress.
She has passed significant legislation into law including the Pueblo Jobs Act and 75 legislative appropriations initiatives.
The Congresswoman has also passed 7 bills, 78 amendments, and 202 legislative appropriations initiatives through the House.
10 of her Community Project Funding requests that were signed into law secured over $20 million for important water and infrastructure projects in Colorado.

Read Lauren's Legislative Victories › Closing the Border & Stopping the Invasion Authored and Introduced the Build the Wall and Deport Them All Act to end “catch and release,” finish building the wall, prohibit funding for sanctuary cities, restore the “Remain in Mexico” policy, and expedite the removal of illegal aliens.
Authored and passed an important appropriations amendment to prohibit funds from going to sanctuary cities.
Authored and Introduced the No Amnesty Act to nullify and remove funding for Biden’s unconstitutional amnesty executive actions.
Cosponsored and Voted in favor of the strongest border security bill ever passed by the House.
Authored and Introduced the Fentanyl Is A WMD Act to help law enforcement agencies crack down on drug traffickers and more aggressively combat fentanyl distributors.
Secured $703 million into law for counter-narcotics support, including an additional $50 million for programs to counter illicit fentanyl and synthetic opioids.
Secured $306 million into law for the national guard counter-drug program.
Passed an amendment through the House that redirected funding to CBP fentanyl detection at Border Patrol Checkpoints to prevent fentanyl from entering America.
Passed an amendment through the House that redirected funding to Counter Narcotics Support to enhance DoD’s role in countering the flow of illicit fentanyl and synthetic opioids.
I voted for and passed legislation to impeach DHS Secretary Mayorkas for orchestrating the worst border crisis in American history.

I was the first Republican in 24 years to successfully initiate impeachment proceedings against a President by passing legislation on the House floor to hold Joe Biden accountable for his dereliction of duty at the Southern Border.

H.R.6547: Colorado Energy Prosperity Act The Colorado Energy Prosperity Act passed the House as part of the Interior Appropriations Bill and prohibits the Bureau of Land Management from locking up 1.6 million acres of land in Colorado from responsible oil and gas production.
The BLM’s 1.6-million-acre land grab is another blatant overreach designed to dismantle the fossil fuel industry, increase gas prices, and force a green transition.
Promises Made, Promises Kept - Read More HR1067: American Energy Act Congresswoman Boebert’s American Energy Act successfully passed through the House as part of HR1.

The bill extends the length of drilling permits from two to four years, which allows energy producers on the Western Slope and beyond to focus more on producing energy and spend less time adhering to bureaucratic requirements.

Energy - Read More HR2366: 90-Day Review Act Also part of HR1 which was successfully passed by the House, the 90-Day Review Act decreases the amount of time that someone or an organization can file for a judicial review of a permit or major infrastructure project from 150 days to 90 days.
This would be a huge boost to getting major infrastructure projects moving instead of being bogged down by the threat of litigation from bad actors.

Promises Made, Promises Kept - Read More HR2746: Pueblo Jobs Act The Pueblo Jobs Act is a critical piece of legislation for the Colorado economy that will create over 1,000 new jobs following the closing of the Pueblo Chemical Depot.
This legislation prevents billions of dollars of infrastructure from being torn down and bulldozed and allows it to be repurposed for local economic development.
This important legislation was signed into law as part of the National Defense Authorization Act in December of 2023.

Promises Made, Promises Kept - Read More HR2746: Trust The Science Act In response to decisions that kept grey wolves listed as an endangered species by the Biden Administration, Congresswoman Boebert partnered with Rep.
Tom Tiffany of Wisconsin to introduce the Trust The Science Act and delist the grey wolf as an endangered species.
This would get the federal government out of the way of states taking action to allow ranchers and farmers to protect their livestock from being killed by grey wolves.
This legislation was supported by a multitude of ranching and farming advocacy groups, including the Colorado Farm Bureau and the Colorado Livestock Association.

While this bill would not immediately produce a fix to the problem in Colorado due to Proposition 114 and the state’s listing of the grey wolf, it has raised awareness of the issue and would remove the federal government as a roadblock to progress.
This legislation passed the House both as a standalone bill and also as a provision included in the Interior Appropriations Bill.

Local Issues - Read More HR2997: CONVEY Act Congresswoman Boebert worked directly with local stakeholders in Mesa County to craft this piece of legislation, which would allow the County to purchase 31 acres of BLM land at fair-market value in Clifton that could be used for economic development.
After years of the County unsuccessfully trying to acquire the land, Congresswoman Boebert stepped up to produce a legislative solution to the problem.
This bill passed the full House of Representatives as standalone legislation.

Local Issues - Read More HR3675: Western Water Accelerated Revenue Repayment Act The WWARR Act allows water users who currently have infrastructure debts or leases with the federal government to pay off their amount due ahead of schedule.
This not only allows these users to get out from under the bureaucracy and red tape of the government, but brings in more federal revenue at a quicker rate.

The bill provides stability to water users and was supported by a wide coalition of stakeholders including the Colorado Water Congress and the Family Farm Alliance, which led to its passage through the House Natural Resources Committee in July.

Energy - Read More HR4596: “Endangered Fish” Bill This piece of legislation, which has a bipartisan companion bill in the Senate sponsored by Senator John Hickenlooper, would protect four species of threatened and endangered fish as well as preventing 2,500 water and power users, with 1,200 in Colorado, from being subject to burdensome government regulations after the current programs expire in September 2024.
The bill has a broad coalition of support from local stakeholders and passed through the House Natural Resources Committee unanimously.

Local Issues (Water/Forestry) - Read More HR6009: Restoring America’s Energy Dominance (RAED) Act In response to another harmful BLM rule that would put more undue regulations on oil & gas producers in the 3rd District, Congresswoman Boebert introduced the RAED Act to repeal this Biden Administration policy.
This legislation passed the House as a standalone bill.

added: Menu About Accomplishments Endorsements News Media Get Involved store Facebook Twitter Instagram Youtube Donate Vote ← back to all news Drones Are Bringing The Surveillance State To Your Front Door 9.23.2026 - Op-Ed Congresswoman Boebert’s op-ed was originally published in the Daily Caller .
At the moment, the United States government has no official public count of how many drones law enforcement agencies own and fly in the U.S.
There is no list from the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), the Department of Justice (DOJ), or any state agency accessible to the public.
Various industry estimates put police drone programs in the thousands — one recently cited as high as about 6,000 .
Congress should not have to take its numbers from corporate executives on quarterly earnings calls about how many drones are already circling overhead and surveilling the American people.
The Department of Transportation, FAA, DOJ, and the Office of Justice Programs should put the fleets on the books and brief the House and Senate.

Until recently, most drones sold to police departments were made in China, raising significant concerns about Chinese government access and influence — either directly from China or through American companies that marked them up and profited.
Congress has spent years trying to stop the Chinese drone invasion of our police departments.
Those efforts were necessary.
They are not finished.
Even if new sales slow, fleets of Chinese drones remain deployed across the nation.
And there are still continued efforts to keep Chinese components, software, and supply chains in the fleet.
Not one piece of hardware or software from the People’s Republic of China belongs on a police or federal drone in the United States, or in any piece of related equipment for that matter.
Not the chip, camera, battery, flight controller, app, firmware, or cloud login.
Grant funding, FAA registration, and operational approval should not be granted to aircraft or ground systems that contain Chinese hardware or software.
American first responders deserve American supply chains.
That is already the direction of federal law, and it ought to be enforced without loopholes.

Section 848 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2020 barred the Department of Defense from operating or contracting for covered foreign unmanned aircraft systems and critical components.
The American Security Drone Act of 2023 was enacted as part of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024.

The order on funding Unmanned Aircraft Systems says no Office of Justice Programs funds may go to unmanned aircraft systems manufactured or assembled by a covered foreign entity, with only limited exceptions.
Members of Congress should not have to guess how many drones are flying overhead.

Congress must investigate and coordinate with executive agencies to determine the facts: how many unmanned aircraft federal agencies and state, local, tribal, and territorial law enforcement agencies already fly; fleet size by agency; their missions and payloads; and under what rules, if any, they operate.
That is the level of transparency we need for government-used drones.
Existing fleets should be registered within 30 days of operational deployment so we can put the brakes on unfettered overhead surveillance.
Federal tax dollars should go to real emergencies — search and rescue, wrecks, officer safety, and a barricaded suspect — not ever-present aerial patrol above American homes.
Those dollars already flow through the Office of Justice Programs, the Community Oriented Policing Services Office, Byrne Justice Assistance Grants, among others.
Unmanned aerial systems are an explicit priority for Fiscal Year 2026 Community Oriented Policing Services Community Policing Development.
“Drone as first responder” is not a substitute for a warrant.
Persistent neighborhood surveillance is a general warrant from the sky, and a microphone on a drone is an intercept.
Listening should require the same legal process as a Title III wiretap under 18 U.S.C. §§ 2510–2523 , or the state equivalent — no fishing expeditions, audit logs, and short retention.
Weaponized drones bought with Department of Justice grant money are already banned.
That ban should apply to all related funding streams unless Congress authorizes otherwise.
No guns.
No launchers.
No explosives.
An officer with a badge and a lawful use-of-force policy is accountable.
Flying weapons over Main Street is not how we support first responders.
We need to provide sunlight on a situation that is moving quickly, so Americans have more visibility.
The current rules, if they even exist, are shrouded in mystery, spread across executive and local agencies.
That has to end.
We must protect the Fourth Amendment, tax dollars, and local departments from signing complex contracts that bring in potentially dangerous foreign components and software.
As I always say, I stand with law enforcement.
I stand even more firmly with the Constitution.
We can give first responders the tools they need without surrendering the right of free Americans to live unmonitored lives.
Calling out license plate readers while ignoring the drones misses a large part of the problem.
Protecting individual privacy is essential if freedom is to mean anything for the next generation.

added: Menu About Accomplishments Endorsements News Media Get Involved store Facebook Twitter Instagram Youtube Donate Vote ← back to all news Fighting for every Colorado rural hospital on the eastern plains 9.11.2026 - Op-Ed Congresswoman Boebert’s op-ed was originally published in Colorado Politics .

After touring Melissa Memorial Hospital in Holyoke and Wray Community District Hospital — two of more than a dozen rural hospitals in my district — I was again reminded why I fight for them in Washington.
The doctors, nurses and staff on the eastern plains keep care close to home.
In rural Colorado, a hospital is more than a building.
It is emergency care, maternity services, good jobs and the backbone of a town.
When one is affected negatively, families drive farther, often on poorly managed roads.
Local economies suffer.
And the most vulnerable pay the highest price.
As November approaches, it’s hard not to be reminded that for the past decade Democrats and socialists have blamed President Donald Trump for everything.
Regarding Republicans and rural hospitals, do not believe the well-funded ActBlue Chinese propaganda machine.
In Colorado, Gov.
Jared Polis and Democrat leaders have spent two years cutting healthcare while running sanctuary policies that make fraud and crime harder to stop.
These healthcare cuts are happening because of mismanagement and a lack of focus on citizens here in Colorado.
Since 2025, about $79 million of a $252 million midyear cut package came from Medicaid .

Polis halted a planned 1.6% provider-rate increase — taking $38 million from hospitals, rolling back dental rates, cutting family caregiver pay, delaying extra payments to small and rural providers, tightening prior authorization and cutting pediatric behavioral therapy rates.

In 2026, despite the Colorado Rural Health Center warning that even a 2% cut is devastating with the state’s rural hospitals already in the red, the Democrats in Denver passed a budget that cut most Medicaid rates another 2%, taking $95 million from hospitals and scaled back other services, including adult dental caps and family caregiver hours.
So, when Democrats talk about cuts, they happened here in Denver.
Those are state choices, not slogans.
Sanctuary rules that block cooperation with federal immigration enforcement make it easier for illegal presence.
They also benefit fraud, identity theft, cartels and repeat offenders who drain dollars that should go to hospitals, nurses and families who play by the rules.

Republicans are doing the opposite: getting crime and fraud out of government programs, enforcing the law and sending resources back to the people who need them — farmers, ranchers, seniors, children and rural frontier hospitals on the eastern plains.
Secure communities and honest books protect care close to home.
Cutting fraud, waste and abuse puts real money into rural care.
I worked with my colleagues for years — long before President Trump’s reelection — to plan what became the One Big Beautiful Bill so we would have a plan ready to go.
That bill, also known as the Working Families Tax Cuts law, created the Rural Health Transformation Program — $50 billion over five years, $10 billion a year from fiscal year 2026 through 2030 .
Colorado’s first-year award is about $200.1 million .

This funding of almost $160 million in the first year goes out as competitive grants to rural providers for new or innovative work: Expand telehealth and technology — $44 million Recruit and keep rural doctors, nurses and staff — $23.4 million Support rural hospitals, clinics, EMS and other providers, including hospital mini-grants and EMS coordination — $48.9 million Fund new and alternative care models — $40 million Improve chronic-disease prevention and rural care — $4.8 million I have advocated and been in the corner of rural hospitals for years.
Just last Congress, I fought for the bipartisan Rural Hospital Technical Assistance Program Act (H.R.
4713) to authorize USDA’s rural-hospital technical-assistance program in statute.
Recently I voted yes on the Improving Care in Rural America Reauthorization Act (H.R.
2493) , which passed the House in April 2026.
That bill would extend HRSA rural outreach, network and small-provider grants through FY 2030 at about $80 million a year.
I’m working with the Senate for it to become law.
I am an original cosponsor of the bipartisan Rural Hospital Revitalization Act of 2026 (H.R.
9005) , with Republicans and Democrats in the House and a Senate companion from Sens.
Jerry Moran and Michael Bennet.
That bill would offer interest-free USDA Community Facilities loans of up to 10 years so rural hospitals can build or renovate and put the savings into care and staff.

I will continue to be a voice for common-sense budgeting, flexibility for telehealth closer to home, fairer Medicare and Medicaid payments and an end to one-size-fits-all rules that ignore rural medicine.
Socialism is not the answer, and no Coloradan should have to choose between their health and a long drive to the nearest open hospital.

added: Menu About Accomplishments Endorsements News Media Get Involved store Facebook Twitter Instagram Youtube Donate Vote ← back to all news Funding water projects ensures Colorado’s future 10.8.2026 - Op-Ed Congresswoman Boebert’s op-ed was originally published in The Denver Gazette .
Whiskey is for drinking, and water is for fighting.
That old Colorado line is still true.
Water decides whether a farm stays in the family, whether a small town can fight a fire and whether our kids have a reason to stay.
I will always fight for it.
In the 4th District, that fight is not theoretical.
Families in the southeast still drink groundwater that can carry radium and uranium.
Towns on the Eastern Plains are one well failure away from a boil order.
Farmers on the South Platte are watching interstate fights decide how much water is left for the next generation.
Cities along the Front Range are trying to get off nonrenewable groundwater before the wells run down.
None of that gets fixed with a press release.
It gets fixed with storage, pipes, treatment plants and a spine in Washington.
Southeastern Colorado has been waiting on this water since the project was authorized.
About 39 communities and roughly 50,000 people in Bent, Crowley, Kiowa, Otero, Prowers and Pueblo counties were promised clean, reliable water from Pueblo Reservoir.
Many of those families still drink groundwater that can carry radium and uranium.
A town should not have to fail a health standard while a project that was already approved sits unfinished.
That is why the conduit still matters.
It is not a luxury.
It is the difference between safe drinking water and water that fails a health standard.
I have supported finishing it, and I will keep fighting until Southeastern Colorado gets the water it was promised.
I have worked to have the Finish the Arkansas Valley Conduit language pass the House of Representatives twice in the last three months, and I will get it across the finish line.
While that larger fight continues, I have delivered funding that is already on the books.
Thirteen of my community project requests were signed into law, including $11.75 million for water projects across the district.

That money is going to real work: a pipeline from Plum Creek to Rueter-Hess Reservoir so Castle Rock can store renewable water instead of mining groundwater; a regional treatment plant at Cobb Lake for Severance, Windsor, Eaton and neighbors in Weld County; consolidation of the Prairie View Ranch system near Wiggins so families do not lose drinking water and fire protection; a new wastewater plant in Lamar; well redundancy in Kiowa; reverse-osmosis treatment in Brush; and system upgrades in Ovid, Louviers and Walsh.
These are not headlines.
They are pipes in the ground.
I am also opposing the Perkins County Canal.
Nebraska wants to revive a century-old claim, cut a canal through Sedgwick County and take South Platte water that Colorado farms and towns depend on.
It has sued Colorado in the U.S.
Supreme Court and has threatened eminent domain against Colorado landowners who refused to sell.
That is the wrong way to settle a compact.
Colorado is meeting its obligations on the South Platte.
Nebraska does not get to seize Colorado land or dry up irrigated acres in Sedgwick, Logan and Washington counties to build up a project that is a bad bet for both states.
Language in the Senate-drafted Water Resources Development Act has been quietly moving forward that would force the Army Corps of Engineers to approve a permit so that this canal can move forward.
Colorado, the number one rule is to protect our water.
The fear is that talking about it will complicate the Supreme Court case.
Here is the truth.
If that Senate language moves forward and the Corps is pushed to sign off, the Supreme Court won’t matter.
The permit becomes the project.
Nebraska gets to dig while Colorado is still arguing the law.
I will not trade away Sedgwick County in a permitting deadline written for another state.
The principle is simple.
Colorado water should stay under Colorado control.
We store it.
We clean it.
We deliver it to the people who have the right to use it.
We do not give it away in a backroom deal, and we do not let another state dig a canal through our farms because a 1923 compact is suddenly convenient.
I will keep funding the projects rural towns can actually build, push to finish the Arkansas Valley Conduit, and keep opposing the Perkins County Canal in the Senate WRDA bill.
Water is how Colorado works.
I am never giving it up.
Lauren Boebert represents Colorado’s 4th District in Congress and serves on the House Committee on Natural Resources and the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.

added: Menu About Accomplishments Endorsements News Media Get Involved store Facebook Twitter Instagram Youtube Donate Vote ← back to all news Newsletter: Important Updates from Team Boebert 10.19.2023 I’d like to issue a friendly reminder - we run out of funding for the government once again in 26 days.
I will not sit back and watch a complete betrayal of the GOP base with this “plan” that’s being discussed.
I ran because I was sick and tired of politicians coming up here and cutting deals and releasing “holier than thou” statements about why we just had to accept it.
Just remember that there is far more that unites the Republican Party than divides us.
It’s time to get on with finishing these appropriations bills.
We’re here to work for the people.
Let’s act like it.
The country is counting on us!
We’re not letting the Speaker debate distract us – there’s plenty of work to be done, and rest assured that we are on it.
In fact, here’s a recap of some of my recent work, as well as a few campaign updates.

Take a look! -﻿ Lauren Fighting Back Against the IRS Lauren submitted a public comment this week to the IRS demanding that they not tax the refunds that Coloradans get under the Taxpayer’s Bill of Rights.
These payments are REFUNDS.
They shouldn’t be included in an individual’s federal gross income and, therefore, shouldn’t be taxable.
Lauren will always fight for Colorado taxpayers!
North Pueblo Train Derailment Earlier this week, a train derailment tragically took the life of a truck driver just outside of Pueblo on an I-25 overpass.
While there were no other serious injuries, the loss of life was deeply saddening and a full investigation of what took place is underway.

Lauren has been engaged with stakeholders like the NTSB, CDOT, BNSF Railway, and others from Sunday evening onwards to make sure that a full accounting of what went wrong is revealed and that clear steps can be taken to make sure this does not happen again.
School Board Election Advocacy Lauren is using her voice and impressive reach to remind Republicans of the importance of voting in local school board elections this November.

Ballots for school board races across the 3rd District are being mailed out this week and Lauren needs you to join her in voting for conservative leaders who will support parental rights and put our children’s education ahead of promoting woke ideology.
If you don’t know who your conservative candidates are, visit the Colorado GOP website and contact your local county GOP organization to learn who is standing up for conservative values.

Ouray County Lincoln Day Dinner Lauren was the headline speaker at the Ouray County GOP Lincoln Day Dinner where she discussed the latest events in D.C. and how she’s continuing to produce results for the 3rd District.
The event was the first Lincoln Day Dinner organized by Ouray County in six years.
Lauren gave a clear update on what’s happening in Congress regarding her fight to cut spending and the latest machinations on selecting a new Speaker of the House.
Delta County Lincoln Day Dinner Lauren made the trip to Hotchkiss to speak at the Delta County GOP Lincoln Day Dinner in front of over 100 proud Republicans.

She discussed the current fight in Congress over electing a new Speaker of the House and gave a great update on the seven bills she’s gotten passed out of House committees that focus on the local issues most impacting 3rd District families.

Aspen Adam Gets Called Out in Daily Sentinel Aspen Adam Frisch got called out in the Letters to the Editor section of the Daily Sentinel for his recent op-ed on the BLM “conservation rule.” His piece was eerily similar to statements and press releases that Lauren has put out of the previous five months, as she co-sponsored HR3397 to rescind the rule back in May while Frisch failed to take a position on it until this month.
The move by BLM would be damaging to ranchers, farmers, and the entire rural Colorado community as it would lock up lands from public use.
It would have a serious negative impact on grazing, livestock, recreational use, and energy production.

They’re already coming at her with everything they’ve got.
Please make an online donation today and help us prepare for the fight ahead!

added: Menu About Accomplishments Endorsements News Media Get Involved store Facebook Twitter Instagram Youtube Donate Vote ← back to all news Newsletter: Important Updates from Team Boebert 9.8.2023 WATCH: Lauren Discusses Water on KRDO 13 Water continues to be a top priority for Lauren, who got the WWARR Act passed through the House Natural Resources Committee to allow water users to get out from the red tape and bureaucracy of the federal government ahead of schedule.
Lauren is also pushing the bipartisan “Fish Bill” as the prime sponsor in the House, which would protect four endangered species of fish and 1,200 different water projects and users in the state.
Protecting this critical resource ensures prosperity for our ranchers, farmers, and entire 3rd District community for generations to come!

Visiting La Plata County Lauren maintained an aggressive travel schedule through the 3rd District during the August recess, holding meetings with county commissioners and other leaders to discuss the issues facing their community.

Lauren was able to secure $1.5 million in funding for a stoplight in Bayfield, a direct infrastructure improvement that will benefit the residents of La Plata County and improve their quality of life.
Ending Biden’s Work From Home Policies In her role on the House Oversight Committee, Lauren is taking action to hold federal bureaucrats accountable and make sure they show up to work.

Despite the pandemic being declared over for months, many federal agencies are still allowing their employees to telework despite there being no evidence of elevated work performance and a significant lack of transparency over the amount of employees teleworking.
Lauren believes that if your tax dollars are going to pay the salaries of bureaucrats, the least they can do is actually show up to work.
Delta County Independent LTE: “Boebert: The Best Candidate” Lauren is getting noticed for her willingness to engage with voters at major community events like the Deltarado Days parade.

This letter to the Delta County Independent talks about issues like fentanyl and protecting our freedom of speech, and how Lauren is taking immediate action and introducing thoughtful pieces of legislation to protect the rights of 3rd District residents.

PHOTOS: Lunch with Mesa County Republican Men’s Club Lauren made a trip to Mesa County to visit with the Mesa County Republican Men’s Club and catch up with our Mesa County Commissioners in Grand Junction.
Lauren loved catching up with so many great 3rd District residents!

Changing the Rules in Congress During her remarks at the Mesa County Republican Men’s Club, Lauren tied together her principled stand in January to change the rules of Congress and how that fight directly led to substantive results for the people of the 3rd District.

For example, with the reform of the earmark Lauren won as part of the Speaker nomination process, she was able to bring nearly $20 million in water and infrastructure project investment for specific 3rd District projects.
That doesn’t happen without her standing up to the D.C. establishment and getting results back in January.
PHOTOS: First Responders Appreciation BBQ Lauren was honored to spend time with true heroes and their families at the First Responders Appreciation BBQ.
Their dedication and selflessness are awe-inspiring.
Lauren was grateful for the chance to express her appreciation for their service!
Check Out This Awesome Moment!
Lauren has seen a lot of things on the campaign trail, but this was a first for her: this 2A-supporting mama asked Lauren to sign the slide for her Sig Sauer P238!
She’s raising her son right, too!
Support Lauren’s Fearless Conservative Movement As you know, the Radical Left is very easily triggered by Lauren.
They’re already coming at her with everything they’ve got.
Please make an online donation today and help us prepare for the fight ahead!

added: Menu About Accomplishments Endorsements News Media Get Involved store Facebook Twitter Instagram Youtube Donate Vote ← back to all news Republicans kept their promise: America’s border is secure again 9.18.2026 - Op-Ed Congresswoman Boebert’s op-ed was originally published in The Hill .
For four years under the Biden administration, Americans watched our southern border collapse.
Record numbers of illegal crossings poured into the country.
Cartels flourished.
Fentanyl flooded our communities.
Criminal illegal immigrants, including members of the violent Tren de Aragua gang, embedded themselves in my home state of Colorado and across the United States.
The previous administration’s open-border policies were a choice.
That chaos ended when President Trump returned to office and Republicans in Congress kept the promise we made to the American people.
At the start of the 119th Congress, I voted for the Laken Riley Act , which requires the detention of illegal immigrants charged with theft, burglary or similar crimes.

Named after the young woman murdered by an illegal immigrant who should never have been free to walk our streets, this law is a straightforward step to protect American communities from preventable violence.
Since January 2025, the results have been dramatic and undeniable.
Daily encounters at the southwest border have plummeted by roughly 95 percent , falling from more than 5,000 per day under the Biden administration to about 250.
For months at a time — now more than a year straight — zero illegal immigrants have been released into the U.S.
Apprehensions are at historic lows, including the lowest fiscal-year Border Patrol total since 1970 .
Deterrence is working again because the policies changed.
A secure border also protects American health care.
Cartel fentanyl, emergency-room costs, and benefit fraud drain hospitals and taxpayers.
Stopping that at the border keeps care available for veterans, seniors, and families who play by the rules.

I authored the Fentanyl is a WMD Act to treat cartel poison as a mass-casualty threat; I passed a bipartisan House amendment requiring the Department of Homeland Security to report how many illegal aliens are deported for assaulting law enforcement; and I introduced legislation to stop federal health insurance dollars from covering people here illegally .
When fentanyl, fraud, and uncompensated emergency care flood rural hospitals, nurses and families on the Eastern Plains pay the price.
A secure border stops that poison before it reaches our neighborhoods.
It ends the deadly trek that cartels sell to migrants, and it removes criminals who never should have been here.
That is not a slogan.
It is the difference between families whose loved ones come home at night and those who never do.
Securing the border does more than keep Americans safer.
It also slashes the fraud and waste that exploded when millions of illegal immigrants were funneled into public systems.
When the border is closed and interior enforcement is real, taxpayer dollars stop being siphoned off by illegal claims, emergency costs and benefit abuse.
That money can go where it belongs: to American citizens who actually need it — veterans, seniors, working families, schools, and health care for people who play by the rules.
Republicans did what they promised: the One Big Beautiful Bill Act , set aside $46.5 billion for border barriers and technology .
Steel is going in the ground for primary and secondary walls, Rio Grande water barriers, sensors, and roads are going up from California to Texas.
Dozens of miles are finished; hundreds more are under construction.
When Democrats once again shut down the government and attempted to defund Customs and Border Protection and ICE — and reopen the border — I voted for the Secure America Act .

This legislation provides multi-year mandatory funding for Border Patrol and ICE through the end of Trump’s term, delivering roughly $70 billion to hire, train, equip, and retain the agents and officers who enforce our laws.

It strengthens interior enforcement, expands detention capacity, supports removals, and ensures these critical agencies are fully funded without being held hostage by the defund the police crowd during annual appropriations deliberations.
I support expansion of the 287(g) program , which lets federal and local police identify and remove criminal illegal immigrants.
More cooperation is needed to protect communities from violent offenders and drug traffickers who entered under the previous administration’s policies.
Some will never admit it, but a secure border works.
Crime is down, fewer gang members are on the streets, and states like Colorado can put more money into education and health care for American citizens instead of cleaning up open-border chaos.
Ignore the socialist propaganda and paid protests.
More than a year of zero releases proves we are safer.
Voters demanded an end to catch-and-release and the removal of criminal aliens.
Republicans delivered.
America is safer, and American tax dollars are better protected.
Now Congress must finish the work by codifying Trump’s executive orders into statute.
Future administrations should not be able to flip a switch and reopen the border.
I will continue fighting to ensure these gains are permanent.

title.after: Surveillance On Every Corner Is Not Freedom | Lauren Boebert

added: Menu About Accomplishments Endorsements News Media Get Involved store Facebook Twitter Instagram Youtube Donate Vote ← back to all news Surveillance On Every Corner Is Not Freedom 9.1.2026 - Op-Ed Congresswoman Boebert’s op-ed was originally published in the Daily Caller .

As we near the 25th anniversary of September 11, 2001, I write in defense of freedom not as a politician seeking applause, but as a Coloradan, a mother, a grandmother, and a fierce defender of the liberties that define this nation.
Fixed license plate reader cameras are quietly turning American streets into zones of constant monitoring.
These systems continuously scan and record vehicle plates, logging time, location, and travel patterns.

In community after community, this infrastructure has often expanded without explicit statutory authorization, clear democratic limits, or the individualized suspicion that a warrant typically requires.
It is simply happening.
The result is a growing database of everyday movements — where people work, worship, shop, and take their children — compiled without the consent of the governed.
Since September 11, 2001, Americans have been asked repeatedly to trade pieces of liberty for promises of security.
The Patriot Act and related measures expanded government surveillance powers in ways earlier generations would have rejected.
Many of those steps were advanced with the best of intentions.
The justification was almost always the same: “If you’re innocent, you have nothing to worry about.” That phrase has become the soft rationalization for hard erosions of privacy.
It shifts the burden onto citizens to prove they deserve freedom rather than requiring government to justify intrusion.
The Constitution does not work that way.
Automatic license plate readers take this logic further.
Fixed camera networks treat the general public as a pool of potential data points.
Patterns of daily life are recorded and retained, sometimes for months or years.
When citizens or lawmakers raise concerns, the pushback is frequently emotional rather than constitutional.
Questioning these systems is framed as a failure to support police.
Let me be clear: no one backs the blue more than I do.
I have stood with officers, defended their ability to do their jobs, and rejected the reckless rhetoric that endangered both law enforcement and the communities they protect.
Supporting the men and women who wear the badge does not require surrendering the Bill of Rights.
My mission is freedom.
Cameras on every street corner tracking free citizens is not freedom.
It is the opposite.
The problem deepens when the data leaves legitimate policing.
Information is often shared widely , retained far longer than necessary, and in some cases made available to government agencies through commercial data vendors.
When the movements of millions of Americans become a commodity that enriches a few while the many are cataloged, we have moved from public safety into the monetization of liberty itself.
Ordinary people become the product.
That is a manipulation of freedom, not its protection.
We need look no further than Hong Kong for a cautionary example.
During the major 2019–2020 pro-democracy protests, authorities extensively used surveillance technology.
Protesters smashed cameras, covered lenses with paint or plastic, used umbrellas and lasers to block them, and tore down “smart” lampposts out of fear they could be used to surveil protesters.
Hong Kong police had access to AI facial-recognition tools, and the crackdown that followed accelerated the expansion of camera networks under mainland China’s high-tech surveillance model.
Americans should not wait until similar systems are fully entrenched here before demanding accountability.
Companies such as Flock Safety have rightly drawn public attention for their widespread deployment of these systems, yet they are far from alone.
Many vendors manufacture and sell this technology, and the problem is bigger than any single firm.

To fix the situation, we must restrict the federal grant funding that can be used to purchase these camera networks, tighten our laws to require warrants, limit data retention, ban the commercial sale of the information, and educate the public about how their everyday liberties are being put at risk.
This is not a partisan issue, and it should never be treated as one.
I am not arguing against useful technology in legitimate investigations.
Targeted, warrant-based use of license plate data can help solve crimes and protect the public.

What must be rejected is the quiet acceptance of fixed, always-on camera networks that treat every driver as a potential subject whose movements must be logged “just in case.” That approach inverts the proper relationship between citizen and state.
It assumes government may collect first and justify later — an assumption foreign to the Fourth Amendment.
I stand with law enforcement.
I stand even more firmly with the Constitution.
Continuous tracking of free Americans without warrant and without democratic consent fails that test.
We can protect public safety without surrendering the right to live unmonitored lives.
That balance is not only possible — it is essential if liberty is to mean anything for the next generation.

added: Menu About Accomplishments Endorsements News Media Get Involved store Facebook Twitter Instagram Youtube Donate Vote ← back to all news The Journal: House committee votes to reauthorize Boebert fish recovery bill 9.23.2023 On Sept.
20, the House Committee on Natural Resources voted to approve U.S.
Rep.
Lauren Boebert’s bipartisan bill to protect endangered fish and aid 1,200 Colorado water and power users.

The Upper Colorado and San Juan River Basins Endangered Fish Recovery Programs Reauthorization Act, HR 4596, would reauthorize the Upper Colorado and San Juan Recovery Programs to protect four threatened and endangered native fish species until 2031.
The Upper Colorado and San Juan Recovery Programs began in 1988 to fully recover four federally listed endangered fish species – Colorado pikeminnow, bonytail, razorback sucker and the humpback chub.
During this time, significant water and power-use restrictions were threatened.
As part of the Colorado River Storage Project, the recovery programs bring water from Aspinall Unit, Navajo and Flaming Gorge reservoirs.
Together they store 6.5 million acre-feet of water.

Local communities, water users, environmental groups, Tribes, energy users and states have worked together to recover the four threatened and endangered fish species while sustaining water and power facility development and operations in the Upper Colorado River and the San Juan River Basins over the past three decades.

Lauren explained this is why we are seeing the growing divide between the rich and the poor, noting that it is unacceptable that the wealthy pay a far less percentage of tax than the average worker.
She added that raising the income cap on paying into Social Security will restore its solvency.
Steven Jacob also joined the conversation.

added: NOV 2025 SENATOR NELSON’S NEWSLETTER Property Tax Update It’s on Everyone’s Mind Property taxes are an ongoing topic of discussion.
Most say they are too high and unpredictable, and I agree!
The Comprehensive Property Tax Taskforce, convened by the legislature after the 2025 session, continues to meet, and many ideas are being discussed.
There is still much to develop and consider on this complex subject.
However, you can be certain of three things from me.
First, I will not support new taxes or the shifting of taxes.
Instead, Pierre needs to cut spending.
Second, Introducing a tax to “reduce” property taxes is not an option.
Over time, the tax reduction will rise again, along with the new tax, resulting in taxpayers paying double.
Third, I cannot support any ideas that give Pierre complete control over our counties and/or schools' funding.
Pierre is not doing an exemplary job with money now; how would they be any different with additional funds from local entities?
The task force's next and final meeting is on October 22, 2025, in Pierre.
My fellow District 18 legislator, Rep.
Julie Auch, serves on this committee.
Our state needs to shift from expensive spending to smart investing.
Our priority should be getting youth back on track early, before they end up in adult prisons, which cost YOU about $35,000 a year per inmate.
Two areas I’m particularly interested in are diversion and mentoring programs.
Both show tremendous success.
I’m working towards a collaborative effort in Pierre this winter to pass legislation that will help reduce pressure on our schools and provide meaningful support for struggling youth.
Interim Committee Success The Community Support Providers (CSPs) Interim Committee held its final meeting.
CSPs assist individuals with developmental disabilities lead productive, fulfilling lives.
Locally, we have two CSPs: Ability Building Services (ABS) in Yankton and Southeast South Dakota Activity Center (Sesdac) in Vermillion.
Sen Lauren Nelson & Rep Julie Auch at the 2025 Yankton Achievement Days Juvenile Justice and Schools I received an email from a South Dakota superintendent.
He said, “Our school leaders are feeling that they are the only real discipline for the justice system at times.” He is not alone in this thinking.

After talking with many school administrators this summer, the juvenile justice system needs immediate attention and reform to improve support for our schools. www.LaurenNelsonforSenate.com Paid for by LaurenNeslonforSenate.com For years, the Department of Developmental Disabilities (DDD) has consistently failed to provide timely and appropriate oversight of CSPs.

This has resulted in taxpayer waste and, more importantly, has left many vulnerable South Dakotans without proper programming, which prevents them from successfully living and working in their communities.
In our final report, the committee proposed cost-saving measures and approved a draft bill to establish a legislative oversight committee.
This group will monitor and evaluate the DDD's activities to ensure accountability and implementation of our recommendations.
As District 18 Senator, I will routinely check with local providers for their feedback on the DDD's current activities.
It was my honor to serve on this committee.

I met many outstanding support providers, administrators, and caregivers across the state. www.LaurenNelsonforSenate.com Governor Rhoden Calls Special Session for Prison On September 23rd, the governor called legislators from both Houses for a special session.
Our task was to decide the fate of the new $650M prison, the same prison proposed at $825M during the 2025 legislative session, but halted by the House.
OCT/NOV 2025 The Enclosed Self-Addressed Envelope The 2026 election is approaching, and once again, I’m counting on the support of District 18.
In the Senate, we were one vote short of blocking this project.
Despite intense pressure, I stood with ten senators (⅔ is required for spending bills) and voted ‘no’.
Your contributions of $25, $50, or $100 made the difference last time—and they will again.
With your help, I’ll continue to be a voice in Pierre that puts you first.
My opposition was threefold.
Please consider using the enclosed envelope to contribute.
First, only one CMAR (Contract Manager At Risk) bid was accepted when state law requires three.
Second, $145M is still needed for this project, and upwards of $50M additional annual dollars will be necessary once it’s built for maintenance.
How can we “find” and “absorb” this into a very tight budget?
Finally, the Department of Corrections is in chaos.
Giving them $650M without demonstrating improvement or ensuring changes in policies and procedures shows the state's irresponsible handling of your money.
Highlights from 2025 legislative session A vote “no” did not kick the can down the road or jeopardize public safety.
Instead, it was wise and prudent, balancing fiscal responsibility and public safety by taking time to hire a new secretary, gather more bids, and begin the clean-up of the DOC.
Passed HB 1052 - prohibit the exercise of eminent domain for a pipeline that carries carbon oxide.
This bill followed the referred law RL 21.
A statewide effort, “No on RL 21” was successful on the Nov 5, 2024 ballot. -Thank you, Lauren.
Stopped SB 177 - provide a sales and use tax refund for goods and services related to data center operations.
This bill would have given a $20 million sales tax refund on a $500 million data center project built by an out of state corporation.
Stopped HR 1261 - provide the board of commissioners with authority over certain intracounty land uses and construction projects.
(Intra-county = townships) Mark Your Calendars 2025 Tabor Czech Days Parade in Tabor, SD Summer Parade Time I enjoyed participating in the lively parades during summer festivities and homecomings.
It was wonderful to see how the citizens of Gayville, Wakonda, Irene, Menno, Viborg, and Yankton warmly welcomed everyone and enthusiastically shared in the celebrations.

My last parade is Mount Marty’s Homecoming on Saturday, October 25th. www.LaurenNelsonforSenate.com Paid for by LaurenNeslonforSenate.com The annual Yankton County Lincoln Day Dinner will be held on Saturday, November 1st, in Gayville at the Community Center.
The social starts at 5:30 p.m., with the dinner and program following at 6:30 p.m.
For tickets, Contact Laura Kotalik at (605) 7603717.
Keep Informed Receive a daily update and weekly newsletter via email during the 2026 Legislative Session.
Scan the QR code or email lauren.nelson@sdlegislature.gov.
You can also follow me on Facebook at: Lauren Nelson for Senate—District 18.

Every one of them represents the future of Illinois, and every one deserves the opportunity to build a life filled with hope, purpose, and possibility.400

removed: Home About Issues Endorsements News Volunteer Signs Vote Shop Donate Donate News CAIT CONLEY CHICKENS OUT OF BOTH NATIONAL DEBATES, HIDES UNTIL SEPTEMBER 28 August 14, 2026 After telling a national cable audience that Mike Lawler was “scared” to face her, and that she would “kick [Lawler’s] ass”, Conley ducked Meet the Press and State of the Union, and stalled for 52 days to agree to just two debates, fewer than this district got in 2024 and none before September 28.
Lawler has accepted four and is ready for all six.
The candidates’ first forum is on Wednesday morning in Poughkeepsie and is open to the press.

Pearl River, NY — August 14, 2026… After telling a national cable audience that Mike Lawler was “scared” to face her , and that she would “kick [Lawler’s] ass”, Conley ducked Meet the Press and State of the Union, refused CBS2, and stalled for 52 days before agreeing to just two debates, fewer than this district got in 2024 and none before September 28 – after early voter are already being cast.
Lawler has accepted four and is ready for all six.
The candidates’ first forum of the cycle is on Wednesday morning in Poughkeepsie and is open to the press.
Lawler challenged Conley to six televised debates on June 23 , the night her primary was called.
He renewed the challenge in a letter on July 7 and proposed holding the first debate that month .

He r epeated it on NBC’s Meet the Press NOW on July 10, and five days later publicly called on her to stop stalling and accept the six debates plus the Dutchess County Regional Chamber of Commerce candidate forum .
On August 11, he accepted four debates : Meet the Press with Kristen Welker, State of the Union with Dana Bash, News 12 with Tara Rosenblum, and Pix11 with Dan Mannarino.
Conley’s answer took 52 days and rejected two of them.
Under her schedule, the first debate of this race comes 97 days after Mike Lawler first asked for one.
Lawler accepted both debates Conley named before she even considered them.
The two she killed are the two with the biggest audiences.

The National Republican Congressional Committee r eported this week that her campaign’s explanation for turning down the networks is that she “doesn’t want to do network debates. ” Two years ago, voters in this district got three televised debates.
News 12 hosted Lawler and Mondaire Jones , CBS News New York held a debate between them , and PIX11 hosted the final debate .
Conley’s schedule keeps News 12 and PIX11 and drops CBS2.

Under her plan, NY-17 voters will have fewer debates in 2026 than in 2024, in a race the entire country is watching – and 1 of only 3 where a Republican won a district also won by Kamala Harris in 2024.
“Cait Conley went on national television in June and told the country Mike Lawler was scared to face her.
Shortly thereafter, NBC and CNN offered her a national stage with Mike Lawler, and she chickened out of both,” said Lawler for Congress spokesman Ciro Riccardi.
“If Mike Lawler is the one who’s ‘scared,’ why did Cait Conley just run away from two of the debates on the table?

We know the answer: It’s because Conley hasn’t lived in this district, doesn’t pay taxes or own a home here, and is embarrassingly unprepared to talk about the issue facing the hard working families, seniors, and small business owners who do.” Conley’s statement leans on “multiple forums between now and Election Day.” The first one is five days away.

On Wednesday morning, August 19, the Dutchess County Regional Chamber of Commerce hosts the general election’s first candidate forum at the DoubleTree by Hilton in Poughkeepsie, and it is open to the press.

title.before: LAW ENFORCEMENT FOR LAWLER: ELEVEN POLICE UNIONS ENDORSE CONGRESSMAN MIKE LAWLER FOR REELECTION - Mike Lawler for Congress

removed: Home About Issues Endorsements News Volunteer Signs Vote Shop Donate Donate News LAW ENFORCEMENT FOR LAWLER: ELEVEN POLICE UNIONS ENDORSE CONGRESSMAN MIKE LAWLER FOR REELECTION August 17, 2026 Presidents and officers representing law enforcement across the Hudson Valley, New York City, and New York State stood with Lawler in Rockland County to formally announce their support .

Haverstraw, NY — August 17, 2026… Congressman Mike Lawler (NY-17) was joined Monday morning in Rockland County by presidents and leaders of police unions from across the Hudson Valley, New York City, and New York State, as eleven law enforcement organizations announced their endorsement of his campaign for reelection, representing over 80,000 law enforcement officers statewide, including: Rockland County PBA – President Sean O’Connor Police Conference of New York – President Mike O’Mara Port Authority PBA – President Frank Conti, First Vice President Michael Mollahan, and Financial Secretary Brian Ahern Port Authority Sergeants Benevolent Association – Second Vice President Andrew Caruso Haverstraw PBA – First Vice President Michael Lupo and Sergeant Pete Connolly Carmel PBA – President Vincent Serio Carmel LBA – President Mike Bodo Westchester County Correction Superior Officers Association – President Peter DiChiara New York State Supreme Court Officers Association – President Patrick Cullen Sergeants Benevolent Association of New York City – Treasurer Ed Geary New York State Fraternal Order of Police – Zone One Vice President Enrique Pabon “I grew up here in Rockland County.
I know what it means to live in a community where the police are part of the neighborhood, where they coach the teams, know the families, and show up for people on the worst day of their lives.

These are the men and women who run toward danger when everyone else runs away, and they are the reason Rockland, Putnam, Westchester, and Dutchess counties remain among the safest places in America to live and raise a family.
That happens because of the people standing behind me,” said Congressman Mike Lawler .
“On behalf of the Rockland County PBA, it is my honor to offer our full support and endorsement of your campaign to Congress in New York’s 17th District.
We proudly give Congressman Lawler our endorsement, not because of the party he represents, but because of what he has done for police officers, both in office and in his professional life.
When it comes to policing and public safety, our decisions are not driven by party affiliation.
They are based on the individual, their record, and their commitment to those who serve and protect Rockland County,” said Rockland County PBA President Sean O’Connor.

“The Police Conference of New York represents police officers from the tip of Long Island to Buffalo and up to the Canadian border, including New York City, and at our May meeting we unanimously endorsed Mike Lawler in his reelection campaign for Congress.
We’ve known Mike since he was an Assemblyman.
He spoke up for us, he called out hypocrisy, and he used common sense.
I’m also a constituent, and I appreciate that he puts my family before felons.

He always, always, always stands with our police officers, and we will do anything in our power to help him get back into Congress to represent not only the members of his district, but police officers statewide,” said Police Conference of New York President Mike O’Mara .

The endorsements come eight days before cooperation agreements between a dozen New York law enforcement agencies and federal immigration authorities are set to be torn up under Albany’s new sanctuary law.

“Cait Conley just accepted the endorsement of the Working Families Party, the party that has called for defunding the police and abolishing ICE, and she said she was ‘excited’ to be working alongside them.

Meanwhile, Albany Democrats passed the so-called Local Cops, Local Crimes Act, which bars local police from cooperating with federal immigration authorities and threatens to strip state law enforcement funding from any department that refuses to comply.
On August 25, cooperation agreements at a dozen law enforcement agencies across ten counties will be torn up under that law,” continued Lawler.
“I have a simple question for Cait Conley: will you call on Albany to repeal its sanctuary law, yes or no?
The men and women on this stage deserve an answer, and so does every family in this district.” “This election is a choice.
You can stand with the people who protect our communities, or you can stand with a party that wants to defund them.
I made my choice a long time ago, and I will never apologize for backing the blue,” concluded Lawler .

“ABSOLUTELY NOTHING” October 8, 2026 It should come as no surprise that Cait Conley, who pays no property taxes in the 17th Congressional District, would believe “nothing” is the right move on SALT.

Cait’s tax plan would massively benefit the top filers in the country with unlimited SALT while crushing middle- and working-class Hudson Valley families with a halved standard deduction, taxes on tips and overtime, and a child tax credit cut in half.

Suffern, NY — October 8, 2026 — Democratic nominee Cait Conley got a harsh education on the issue that hits Hudson Valley homeowners hardest at Wednesday’s Spring Valley NAACP Candidate Forum at Rockland Community College.

After telling the audience the best thing Congress could have done for New Yorkers’ taxes was nothing, she was met with laughter and a fact-check from Congressman Mike Lawler, who walked Cait through what doing nothing would have cost families in this district.
Conley tried to cut in at the end with a false claim about this year’s tax refunds that drew laughter from the room.

Watch the exchange here “The best thing that Congress could have done for New Yorkers was absolutely nothing and just letting it go away,” Conley said , referring to the $10,000 cap on the state and local tax (SALT) deduction.
Letting the cap fully expire would have disproportionately benefitted the absolute top tax brackets, including the billionaires Cait Conley claims she doesn’t support.
“Unfortunately, my opponent doesn’t really understand this, in part because she doesn’t pay taxes here,” Lawler responded .
“The fact is that if we did what you want and what you’re advocating for, to let the tax bill expire, it would have been a $4 trillion tax increase on the American people.
Every family in this district would have paid $5,000 more.
Why?
Because the standard deduction would have been cut in half, the child tax credit would have been rolled back.
All of the rates would have gone up.” The 2017 tax law’s individual cuts were set to expire at the end of 2025.
Had Congress let them lapse, the standard deduction would have been cut roughly in half, and the child tax credit would have dropped from $2,000 to $1,000 per child.
“The reason I negotiated the deal the way we did was to make sure that taxes didn’t go up.
I stood up to the president.
I stood up to my own party.
There were only five of us out of 220 that wanted to get this done,” Lawler said .
“We delivered the single largest tax cut in the entire bill, raising it from $10,000 to $40,000.

Ninety percent of my constituents were able to fully deduct their state and local taxes, and in the Hudson Valley, over a $4,000 tax refund in your pocket this past April.” Conley interrupted him : “And that would have also happened if you did nothing.” “No, it wouldn’t,” Lawler replied , as the room laughed at Conley’s pathetic response.
The SALT fight in the Hudson Valley comes down to property taxes.
Homeowners in Rockland and Westchester counties pay some of the highest property taxes in the country, and they use the SALT deduction to write those taxes off their federal returns.
Many of these are due to unfunded mandates passed down by Kathy Hochul and Albany Democrats, who support Cait Conley to the hilt.
Cait Conley doesn’t understand this because she owns no property in the district and pays no property taxes.
The only house on the financial disclosure she filed with the Clerk of the House in May is in Lee County, North Carolina, where she collected between $15,001 and $50,000 in rent last year.
“Cait Conley told voters at Rockland Community College that the best thing Washington could have done about their taxes was absolutely nothing.
Then she told them the bigger refund they got this spring would have come anyway, and they laughed, because they know she’s lying,” said Lawler for Congress spokesman Ciro Riccardi .
“Mike Lawler stood up to his own party to quadruple the SALT cap so Hudson Valley families could deduct the property taxes they pay.

Cait Conley doesn’t own property here, doesn’t pay a dime in property taxes here, and has no idea what it’s like to pay New York’s crushing property taxes – all thanks to Cait’s best friend, Kathy Hochul.” “Cait Conley can continue to claim she knows best on taxes, but it’s clear when she’s asked this question in the future, she should take her own advice and say nothing,” concluded Riccardi .

“At least that would save her the embarrassment of rooms full of Hudson Valley voters laughing in her face.” ### Home About Issues Endorsements News Volunteer Signs Vote Shop Donate Donate Lawler for Congress PO Box 137 Chappaqua, NY 10514 [email protected] (845) 213-3253 Lawler HQ 118 Maple Ave, Back Door New City, NY 10956 Hours: 9 AM - 5 PM Shrub Oak 948 E Main St Shrub Oak, NY 10588 Hours: 9 AM - 5 PM Carmel 16 Fair St Carmel, NY 10512 Hours: 9 AM - 5 PM Hawthorne 373 Elwood Ave Hawthorne, NY 10532 Hours: 9 AM - 5 PM Paid for by Lawler for Congress, Inc.

DOES CAIT CONLEY SUPPORT UNDOING THEM AND GIVING BENEFITS TO ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS?
October 9, 2026 In “My Dad,” Congressman Lawler talks about losing his father to cancer and the reforms he voted for to keep Medicaid there for the families who depend on it.
New limits on federal Medicaid for non-citizens took effect October 1, preventing abuse of the system by those in the country illegally.
Does Cait Conley support President Biden’s position on the matter, which covered 90% of expenses for illegal immigrants?

Pearl River, NY — October 9, 2026 — Lawler for Congress today released “My Dad,” a 30-second ad in which Congressman Mike Lawler (NY-17) talks about his family’s battle with cancer and his work to protect Medicaid from fraud and abuse so other families have the resources they need in their own health battles.
Lawler opens with images of him and his father.
“When my dad was dying of cancer, Social Security kept my parents afloat,” Lawler says .

“So I know firsthand how health care costs can bankrupt a family.” That, he says, is why he strengthened Medicaid for the people who need it most and stopped “illegal immigrants and other scam artists from ripping off the system.” He closes on his dad: “I’m Mike Lawler, and I approve this message, and so would my dad.” Watch “My Dad” here Federal Medicaid now covers only U.S. citizens and green card holders .

Illegal immigrants were still receiving benefits as the federal government, thanks to President Biden’s policies, was still paying 90 percent of the cost of emergency Medicaid in expansion states like New York for people who would have qualified except for their immigration status, the same higher rate it pays for citizens in the expansion population.
That federal share is now capped at each state’s regular matching rate , 50 percent in New York.
The Congressional Budget Office estimated the change will save taxpayers $28 billion over ten years.
The law also goes after people who game the program from the inside.

In July 2025, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services reported that, in 2024, an average of 1.2 million people per month were potentially enrolled in Medicaid or CHIP in two or more states, and 1.6 million were potentially enrolled in both Medicaid and a subsidized Affordable Care Act plan.
Starting January 1 , 2027, states must verify enrollees’ addresses against reliable data and check federal death records at least every quarter for enrollees who have died.

In 2028, states must begin screening Medicaid providers against the Social Security Death Master File, and a national system to catch anyone enrolled in more than one state must be running by October 2029.
CBO estimated the duplicate enrollment provisions will save $17 billion over ten years.
Lawler has gone after Medicaid abuse in Albany, too.
In March 2025, he called for federal intervention and a Justice Department investigation into how the state awarded its contract to run the Consumer Directed Personal Assistance Program.

In June, the Justice Department sued the state Department of Health and the contractor, Public Partnerships LLC , alleging a sham bid process that let the company collect unauthorized profits funded by federal taxpayers.
“Mike Lawler lost his father to cancer, and he knows what a diagnosis like that does to a family’s finances.

Medicaid has to be there for those families, and every dollar paid for someone enrolled in two states, or for someone who has died, is a dollar that never reaches those who need it most,” said Lawler for Congress Campaign Manager Ciro Riccardi .
“Cait Conley has spent this campaign attacking the legislation that put these protections in place.
Does she want Washington to stop checking whether people are enrolled in Medicaid in two states at once?

Does she want taxpayers back on the hook for 90 percent of Medicaid expenses for illegal immigrants?” ### Home About Issues Endorsements News Volunteer Signs Vote Shop Donate Donate Lawler for Congress PO Box 137 Chappaqua, NY 10514 [email protected] (845) 213-3253 Lawler HQ 118 Maple Ave, Back Door New City, NY 10956 Hours: 9 AM - 5 PM Shrub Oak 948 E Main St Shrub Oak, NY 10588 Hours: 9 AM - 5 PM Carmel 16 Fair St Carmel, NY 10512 Hours: 9 AM - 5 PM Hawthorne 373 Elwood Ave Hawthorne, NY 10532 Hours: 9 AM - 5 PM Paid for by Lawler for Congress, Inc.

NEWS ARTICLE Democratic Nominee Leela Gray Previews Anna Paulina Luna Matchup in Battleground FL-13 Oct 9 2026 PRESS RELEASE Leela Gray on Morning Joe: “Luna is Driven By Her Vanity" Gray slams Luna’s headline-chasing, soaring costs for Florida families, and highlights concerns over the Iran war and American national security FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE: October 9, 2026 CONTACT : Sera Guerry | sera@leelagray.com St.

Petersburg, FL — This morning, retired Army Brigadier General Leela Gray, candidate for Florida’s 13th Congressional District, joined MS NOW's Morning Joe to make the case that voters across the political spectrum are ready to replace self-serving Anna Paulina Luna with serious, service-driven leadership focused on lowering costs and protecting America’s national security.
Watch the full interview here .
Gray outlined the mounting financial pressures facing Floridians, including rising insurance costs as communities continue rebuilding on the two-year anniversary of Hurricane Milton.

She pointed to the combined impact of Luna’s votes to support the Iran war, tariffs, and rising health care costs: “I actually have some numbers: at least $1,200 for families because of this reckless war of choice in Iran, at least $1,700 because of these illegal tariff taxes.
And recently, I received data showing that health care costs for many of the people right here in our district are going to go up about $5,300 per year.

“Most people don’t have an extra eight grand sitting in their pocket.” Asked about Luna’s record of chasing viral headlines while refusing to debate or hold town halls, Gray sharply criticized her opponent’s priorities: “Clearly, Luna is driven by her vanity.
That’s why she’s always chasing these headlines.
You know the type of person who comes into a room, makes a lot of noise, and does the job half ass?
“That’s Luna.

“People are tired of that.” Gray also described the growing frustration she is hearing from Republicans and Independents across FL-13 who want representatives focused on solving problems rather than attracting attention: “What I’m hearing from independents and Republicans is that they want to know they are the most important people to their representatives.
“It’s in the title: representative.
That’s the job.
“That’s what I did for 30 years serving my country.

It was always about service over self, and that’s what I’m going to deliver in November.” Addressing American national security, Gray drew on her decades of military leadership, including service at U.S.

Central Command under General James Mattis, to question the administration’s strategic planning in Iran: “I can say with high confidence that we did not prosecute this war with Iran with a clear strategic objective.
“Because if we had, we would have secured the Strait of Hormuz first and foremost.
“But let’s also be really clear…this reckless war of choice is…being led by Hegseth.
“Hegseth is an unqualified frat boy.” ### About Leela Gray Leela Gray is a third-generation veteran, retired U.S.
Army Brigadier General, attorney, small business leader, and mother running for Congress in Florida's 13th Congressional District.
The first in her family to attend college, Leela worked her way through school and served more than 30 years in uniform, including two combat deployments and a peacekeeping mission.
She retired in 2018 as Deputy Commanding General of the U.S.
Army Central and subsequently advised U.S.
Army Cyber Command on modernizing national cyber policy.
After retiring from the military, Leela served on non-profit and private sector advisory boards, and earned her law degree to help veterans access healthcare and other critical benefits.
Leela and her husband, Tony, have lived in the Tampa Bay area for more than 20 years and are proud parents of their adult daughter.
Learn more at leelagray.com .

added: Property Tax Local property taxes have nearly doubled in the last decade.
Leaders in Topeka point to local governments and public schools as the culprit.
Truth is Topeka has just as much fault.

There have been at least 8 separate ways that the legislature has take previously provided funds away from localities, leaving them to pass the shortfall on to homeowners – just so they can keep cutting income tax, which disproportionately benefit the folks that don’t need it.
We must also strengthen the Homestead Refund for our Seniors who’s limited retirement security keeps getting chipped away at by raising property taxes and other expenses.
Income Tax Our legislature has put us on a path to flat tax, where the richest receive millions and the impact for most of us wont even cover the increases to our health insurance premiums.
Legislators passed Senate Bill 269 then overrode Gov.
Data Centers When the federal agency tasked with environmental protections number one priority is more data centers, we can no longer expect that agency to have the publics best interest at heart.
Kansas must enact a moratorium on this resource intensive industry until proper regulations are developed in our state.

We must repeal the 20 year sales tax exemption, or at a minimum change it to a local option where it is up to the local governments to decide if they will forgo the massive revenue these projects would create.
Flock and ALPR regulations or bans need serious consideration.
