It’s an economic crisis. ​ We must invest in affordable, accessible, and workforce-connected housing that helps our region grow stronger from the ground up. ​ As your next State Senator, I'll fight to: ​ Create affordable housing by expanding rural housing tax credits, state-local developer partnerships, and using vacant or underused properties for housing. ​ Reform zoning laws and support adaptive reuse to make it easier to convert old buildings, second-story downtowns, and surplus land into housing.
Standing Strong for Michigan's Public Schools Every child in Michigan deserves a world-class education, no matter their zip code, family income, or ability.
As your State Senator for the 32nd District, I will fight to keep public education truly public – because my kids’ futures depend on it.

That means fully funding our neighborhood schools, not funneling taxpayer dollars into private and for-profit schools. ​ As your next State Senator, I'll fight to: ​ Fund teachers, not tax breaks, to ensure educators have the pay, tools, and classroom support they need to teach effectively.
Provide every child with what they need to succeed, including free school lunches so no student learns on an empty stomach.
Guarantee free, high-quality preschool for all Michigan children, laying the foundation for lifelong success.
Invest in rural school transportation, so every student, no matter how far they live from their school, can get to class safely and on time. ​ Let’s put our children first.
Let’s keep public education public, and support all families working to give their children the best possible start.

Supporting the LGBTQIA+ Community: Promoting Equality Despite significant progress, the LGBTQIA+ community continues to face systemic challenges that hinder their access to essential rights, resources, and opportunities.
Discrimination, stigma, and lack of representation can lead to adverse outcomes in health, employment, and overall well-being.

Everyone deserves to live authentically and without fear of judgment or discrimination. ​ As your next State Senator, I'll fight to: ​ Advocate for Non-Discrimination Policies: Push for laws that protect LGBTQIA+ individuals in employment, housing, and public accommodations. ​ ​ Increase Access to Healthcare: Support initiatives that ensure all LGBTQIA+ individuals receive comprehensive healthcare, including mental health services. ​ Enhance Mental Health Resources: Provide funding and access to mental health services tailored to the unique needs of the LGBTQIA+ community. ​ Combat Homelessness: Support targeted programs to address and prevent homelessness among LGBTQIA+ youth and adults. ​​ ​ ​ ​ When we invest in inclusion and understanding, we create a world where everyone can thrive, live authentically, and contribute positively to our communities.

Strengthening Native American Communities: Promoting Well-Being and Opportunity Native American communities continue to face significant challenges stemming from historical injustices and ongoing systemic inequalities.
Despite rich cultural heritage and contributions to society, many Native Americans experience disparities in health, education, and economic opportunities.

It is essential to recognize and address these issues to support the well-being and empowerment of Native peoples. ​ As your next State Senator, I'll fight to: ​ Advocate for Tribal Sovereignty: Support policies that respect and uphold the rights of tribal nations to govern themselves and manage their resources. ​ Increase Access to Healthcare: Push for improved funding and access to healthcare services for Native American communities, including mental health and substance abuse treatment. ​ Support Education Initiatives: Invest in educational programs that respect and incorporate Native culture, language, and history into curricula. ​ Promote Economic Development: Encourage investment in sustainable economic opportunities for Native communities, including support for tribal businesses. ​ Protect Land Rights: Advocate for the preservation and protection of Native lands and natural resources, recognizing their cultural significance. ​ Supporting Native American communities is vital for fostering justice, equity, and dignity.
By investing in their rights and heritage, we contribute to a more inclusive society where all voices are heard and respected.

title.after: Ask Me Anything | Rob Epstein for Georgia

added: Platform ▼ Healthcare Access For the People Economic Growth Education Environment Housing Affordability About Endorsements Get Involved Contribute Español Ask Me Anything (AMA) Curious about my campaign or values?
Here you'll find answers to the questions I hear most from neighbors like you.
If you don’t see what you’re looking for, please reach out—your voice is always welcome.
Who are you?
I'm a retired software leader seeking to redefine my purpose through public service, guided by my Christian faith—which emphasizes love, compassion, and service to others.
As a Lego enthusiast and father of two amazing sons, Blake (21) and Bryce (18), family is at the heart of everything I do.
For 20 years, I lived in Woodstock, where my wife and I raised our family until she passed away in May of 2025 after a four-year battle with bile duct cancer.
In August of 2025, I moved to the River Green community in Canton to be closer to my sons and begin a new chapter of my life.
Why did you decide to run?

I decided to run for the Georgia House of Representatives because I care deeply about the people of House District 23—our neighborhoods in Canton, River Green, Bridgemill, and the surrounding Cherokee County communities.

Living here, I see firsthand the challenges and opportunities facing our families, from the need for better access to Northside Hospital Cherokee and quality healthcare, to supporting our local schools like Knox Elementary and Cherokee High.
My Christian faith guides me to serve others and work for fairness, compassion, and opportunity for everyone.

I want to help strengthen our local economy so small businesses in downtown Canton and throughout the district can thrive, and make sure our democracy truly reflects the voices of the people—not just the powerful few.
What issues matter most to you?
The issues that matter most to me are the ones that touch people’s everyday lives right here in House District 23: Canton, River Green, Bridgemill, and our surrounding Cherokee County communities.
I care deeply about making healthcare more accessible and affordable, so families in neighborhoods like Great Sky and Laurel Canyon never have to choose between getting well and paying their bills.

I want to expand economic opportunity so every Georgian, whether you’re running a small business in downtown Canton or working in our local schools like Teasley Middle and Canton Elementary, has a fair shot at success.
And I believe we must strengthen our democracy to ensure government works for the many, not just the well-connected few.
At the heart of it all, I want to help build a Georgia where every person in our district and state has the chance to live with dignity, hope, and opportunity.
How will you stay in touch?
Staying in touch starts with being accessible and listening.
I plan to hold regular town halls in Canton, River Green, Bridgemill, and other neighborhoods across House District 23.

I’ll meet with community groups like the River Green HOA, Bridgemill Civic Association, and local school PTAs, and keep open lines of communication through social media, email updates, and neighborhood visits.

I want my neighbors to feel comfortable reaching out anytime with an idea, concern, or question, whether you’re a parent at Knox Elementary, a small business owner in downtown Canton, or hitting up Publix outside in Laurel Canyon.
Serving well means staying connected, showing up, listening, and being responsive to the people who trust me to represent them.
What shapes your leadership style?
My leadership style is shaped by my faith, my family, and my belief in listening before leading.
I’ve learned that good leadership means serving others with humility, building trust through honesty, and always keeping people first.
I try to approach every decision with compassion and common sense, bringing people together instead of dividing them.
My goal is to lead in a way that reflects the values I live by—faith, fairness, and a genuine desire to make life better for everyone in our community.

Georgia’s economy is strong in many areas, but too many families and small businesses are being left behind.
Wages have not kept up with the cost of living, and rural communities often lack the investment and infrastructure needed to thrive.
Small businesses face barriers to growth, and economic opportunity is not shared equally across our state.
Where Can We Go?
We can build a Georgia where every community—urban and rural—has the tools to prosper.
By supporting local entrepreneurs, investing in infrastructure, and fostering innovation, we can create good jobs, grow our middle class, and ensure prosperity is within reach for all Georgians.
How Do We Get There?

added: Skip to content Join Team Rob Home About News Labor Endorsements Get Involved Vote Shop Donate Instagram Facebook X YouTube DONATE Congressman Rob Bresnahan Earns Endorsement of Hazleton City Firefighters IAFF Local 507 October 9, 2026 Pittston, PA — The Rob Bresnahan for Congress campaign today announced the endorsement of the Hazleton City Firefighters, International Association of Fire Fighters (IAFF) Local 507, in Congressman Rob Bresnahan’s reelection bid in Pennsylvania’s 8th Congressional District.
In its endorsement letter, Local 507 pointed to Bresnahan’s continued support for the firefighters serving the City of Hazleton, including his efforts to help address a critical staffing shortage.

The union specifically highlighted Bresnahan’s recent visit to its firehouse, where he met directly with members to hear their concerns, as well as his advocacy surrounding the department’s recent federal grant applications.

“Your willingness to advocate on behalf of our Local, including your support surrounding our recent federal grant applications, demonstrates your commitment to addressing the public safety needs of the communities you represent and the firefighters who serve them,” wrote IAFF Local 507 President Shawn McArdle in the union’s endorsement letter.
The full endorsement letter can be read HERE .
“When someone calls 911, they expect help to be there.

The men and women of the Hazleton City Fire Department put their lives on the line every day to answer those calls, and they deserve the staffing, equipment, and resources necessary to do their jobs safely,” said Congressman Rob Bresnahan .
“I’ve had the opportunity to sit down with these firefighters, hear their concerns firsthand, and work alongside them to address their needs.

I’m honored to have their endorsement, and I’ll continue fighting for the men and women who keep our communities safe.” The Hazleton City Firefighters IAFF Local 507 joins a large and growing coalition of unions and labor organizations supporting Congressman Bresnahan’s reelection, representing building and construction trades, transportation and maritime workers, federal and public added: Skip to main Become a Sustaining Donor Donate now Volunteer Donate Return to all news NEW ADS: Rob Sand Launches Ads Featuring Support from a “Tax-Hating Republican” and Warnings from a Cancer Survivor For Immediate Release Contact: press@robsand.com Rob Sand for Iowa 10/9/2026 DES MOINES, IA – Today, nominee for governor Rob Sand released two new campaign ads as part of a six-figure ad buy across all platforms in the state – TV, digital, and streaming.
The first ad, titled “ One Reason ,” features Wayne from O’Brien County, a self-described “tax-hating Republican” that has never voted for a Democrat for governor – until now.
Wayne is supporting Rob because he knows he supports low taxes for everyday Iowans as they face a crisis of costs and that he’ll hold corrupt politicians accountable – regardless of party.
The second ad, titled “ Down the Road ,” focuses on Laurie, a cancer survivor from Earlville.
In the ad, Laurie highlights Zach Lahn’s support for cuts that endanger rural Iowa hospitals and his efforts to strip health care away from everyday people.
Laurie warns that Zach Lahn won’t have to live with the consequences of his actions because he can just fly back to Kansas to avoid them.
WATCH: View a full transcript of the ad below: Wayne: “I’m a Republican for one big reason, and that’s taxes.
I hate paying taxes, and that’s why I’m voting for Rob Sand.
Rob wants low taxes, accountability, and jail time for tax thieves.
I know that there’s corruption on both sides.
Rob Sand isn’t afraid to go after either party to keep them from reaching into our pockets even more.
Rob’s done such a great job that he’s actually pissed off both parties, so he’s gotta be doing something right.
I have never voted Democrat for governor, but I am this time.
This tax-hating Republican loves Rob Sand.” WATCH: View a full transcript of the ad below: Laurie: “After I was diagnosed with cancer, I actually felt blessed.
People came out of the woodwork, offering to drive me for treatment.
But Zach Lahn supports the cuts that put our local hospitals at risk.
I guess when you can fly everywhere, you don’t worry about having a hospital down the road.
And Lahn tried to take away health insurance from people like me who have jobs and have children and families.
It’s just not right.
Zach Lahn won’t be living with the consequences, because he doesn’t even live here.” ### Become a Sustaining Donor of our campaign We need your help to ensure we have the resources to win.

title.after: Rob Sand Hits the Ground Running in October to Kick Off “Iowa for All” Tour

added: Skip to main Become a Sustaining Donor Donate now Volunteer Donate Return to all news Rob Sand Hits the Ground Running in October to Kick Off “Iowa for All” Tour For Immediate Release Contact: press@robsand.com Rob Sand for Iowa 10/9/2026 DES MOINES, IA – After wrapping up his second 100 Town Hall Tour of the campaign and ninth annual tour as a public servant, nominee for governor Rob Sand isn’t slowing down.
He’s continuing to show up in communities across Iowa, listening to voters, hearing about the challenges they’re facing, and talking about his plans to make Iowa work better for everyone.

Since wrapping up the tour, Rob has launched his “Iowa For All” tour, starting out with a visit with residents at a senior living facility, touring economic development projects in Adams County, grabbing a morning coffee in Davenport with voters to talk about Iowa’s toughest challenges, touring and joining a roundtable discussion at a Coralville food pantry, talking with students at Grinnell College, and firing up a standing-room-only crowd in Indianola.

From small-town Main Streets to college campuses, Rob is continuing to meet Iowans where they are, bringing people together around the issues that matter most, and making the case for an Iowa that’s not redder or bluer, but better and truer.

See more about Rob’s time on the road below: On Monday, October 5, Rob toured Corning with members of the Adams County Economic Development Corporation to learn more about local economic development efforts and discuss how his “Opportunities for All” plan will support small businesses, strengthen small-town Main Streets, and create more opportunities for rural Iowa communities as governor.

On Wednesday, October 7th, Rob Sand met with students and community members at Grinnell College to discuss how our broken two-party system keeps us divided, and the importance of coming together to focus on the issues that matter most to Iowans.

WATCH: KCAU: Rob Sand speaks with voters in central Iowa READ: Quad City Times: After debate, Rob Sand takes questions at Davenport coffee shop “I know that if I win, I’m going to be working with that same Republican Legislature that passed the reforms, and so me running around and just hollering that we’re going to go back, that’d be me being dishonest with you,” Sand said.

“Maybe you feel that we should, but I won’t stand up and tell you a thing that I don’t think is realistic.” Juan Kamacho of Bettendorf asked Sand about his position on income limits for the Education Savings Accounts, the state program that provides state funding for families’ private school expenses.
Sand has said he supports income caps on Education Savings Accounts so that taxpayers aren’t paying for the wealthiest families in Iowa to attend private school.
“It just doesn’t make sense to be giving it to the wealthiest folks in the state, especially when we’ve got that budget deficit,” Sand said.

“And for the folks that are already in it, I think at the end of the day, the idea would be we’re going to be going back to a level where, when we say, ‘Oh, we’re putting the limit here,’ they might say shoot or darn, but it’s not going to change their lives because they’re still making enough money that it’s not a struggle for them to afford it.” Washington Examiner: Democratic governor nominee Rob Sand bashes Trump over Iowa’s food stamps problems Sand held a roundtable discussion at the Coralville Community Food Pantry and discussed with local charitable leaders how the federal SNAP changes have affected local communities, particularly in rural Iowa.
Sand criticized the Republican House members and senators representing Iowa in Washington for voting in support of SNAP cuts in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act in the first place.
“If we had a better system, we would probably have people who actually worked to stop those cuts before they started because they would understand that their job was representing Iowans,” Sand said.
Sand chided Gov.

Kim Reynolds (R-IA) for turning down roughly $30 million in federal assistance to provide summertime subsidized or free lunches for children in Iowa who receive state assistance during the school year.
“When we have a chance to bring federal money into the state of Iowa to do something that’s just a fundamentally good thing, we’re going to take every opportunity that we can to do that,” Sand said.

Indianola Independent Advocate: Sand makes final push in Indianola During the main event, before about 200 spectators, Sand pushed back on the amount of time Lahn spends in Kansas, where some of his children live.
“This is a big job and you have to be in Iowa to do it,” said Sand.
“We can laugh about this, but here’s where the laughter stops.
Imagine being governor of a state you’re only in half the time.
Who’s going to suffer for that?” Sand said Iowans are “sick and tired of a political system designed to get politicians re-elected instead of solving the problems that we face.
That’s what we want to do if we win this race.” “It’s not in the bag,” he said.
“We know we can win, but we have work to do.
I don’t want to get to Nov.
3 and say, ‘Shoot, I should have done another afternoon knocking doors.
I should have called a few more friends.
Once we hit Nov.
3, we’re done.
This is over.
We either won and we have a new direction for the state of Iowa, or we haven’t.
You are a part of that.” Sand encouraged people do everything from door knocking to phone calling to posting their support on social media.
The event drew in both longtime Democrats, and newcomers to the party.
“We were going to vote for him anyway,” said Andy Massoth of Indianola, who said he was an independent, but couldn’t vote for Republicans he is seeing on the ballot.
“It’s not about party, it’s about issues and getting things done.
I hope he can pull it off and do what he’s saying.” ### Become a Sustaining Donor of our campaign We need your help to ensure we have the resources to win.

title.after: Keeping Our Roadways Safe – Representative Roger Goodman (D) Washington State Legislature

added: Skip to content Home Meet Roger Legislative Accomplishments Justice Reform Photo Gallery Media Awards Endorsements Contact Roger Endorse Roger Volunteer Donate Menu Home Meet Roger Legislative Accomplishments Justice Reform Photo Gallery Media Awards Endorsements Contact Roger Endorse Roger Volunteer Donate Home Meet Roger Legislative Accomplishments Justice Reform Photo Gallery News Awards Endorsements Menu Home Meet Roger Legislative Accomplishments Justice Reform Photo Gallery News Awards Endorsements Volunteer Contact Donate Mailing List Menu Volunteer Contact Donate Mailing List Keeping Our Roadways Safe Roger is the Chair of the House Public Safety Committee and also as a senior member of the House Judiciary Committee.
He has worked successfully to enhance public safety.
Roger is especially distinguished for his work to reduce drunk driving and domestic violence, which are the greatest sources of harm in our society.
He has passed more than a dozen pieces of major legislation to address these chronic problems and his work in this area has earned him national acclaim.
Even with tougher punishments and ad campaigns, drunk drivers continue to plague our roads.
People need to know that when you drive drunk and put lives at risk, it will not be tolerated.
Strong sentences aren’t the only answer; we need new solutions to make our roads safer and to save more lives.

For several years, Roger Goodman has worked closely with the Washington State Patrol, Mothers Against Drunk Driving, judges and prosecutors to come up with innovative ways to hold drunk drivers accountable.

He has passed a dozen bills in this area, and the Washington State Traffic Safety Commission has reported that his legislation has resulted in a 44 percent decline in alcohol-related deaths and serious injuries on Washington’s roads in the last seven years, making Washington the model for the nation.
Roger’s legislation has aimed at known drunk drivers, installing breathalyzers, or what are called “ignition interlock devices” in DUI offenders’ cars.
If the driver has been drinking, the car won’t start and can’t get on the road.
The DUI offenders must pay for the device themselves, sparing the taxpayers any expense.
Eighty percent of drivers with a suspended license drive anyway.
By installing the alcohol-detection devices, we allow them to get a special driver’s license, so they can continue to drive to work or school.
These are known drunk drivers and we’ve been able to make sure they’re driving sober, saving several hundreds of lives in the process.

Roger’s DUI and road safety bills enacted into law include: HB 2700 (Chapter 203, Laws of 2016), a significant reform of DUI laws, expanding alcohol monitoring, ignition interlock requirements, vehicular homicide penalties and license suspensions.
HB 2314 (Chapter 213, Laws of 2016, enacted as companion SB 6160), criminalizing the manufacture, sale and installation of counterfeit and defective automobile safety airbags.
HB 2728 (Chapter 100, Laws of 2014, enacted as amendment to SB 6413), holding repeat DUI offenders in jail after arrest, punishing the tampering with ignition interlock devices, et al.

HB 1482 (Chapter 35, Laws of 2013, enacted as companion SB 5912), a major reform of DUI laws strengthening the felony DUI law, ignition interlock requirements, DUI courts, alcohol monitoring and treatment programs, among many other provisions.
HB 2443 (Chapter 183, Laws of 2012), another significant update to the ignition interlock program, including a major expansion of Washington State Patrol’s enforcement capability.
HB 2302 (Chapter 42, Laws of 2012), a child endangerment statute requested by the Washington State Patrol, increasing penalties for driving drunk with children in the vehicle.
HB 1789 (Chapter 293, Laws of 2011), another major expansion of the ignition interlock program and further toughening of other DUI penalties.

HB 1017 (Chapter 167, Laws of 2011, enacted as companion SB 5000), requiring a mandatory 12-hour impound of DUI offenders’ cars, preventing drunk drivers from retrieving their vehicles while they are still drunk.
HB 2742 (Chapter 269, Laws of 2010), a major bill expanding the ignition interlock program and toughening other DUI penalties.
HB 2466 (Chapter 268, Laws of 2010), a bill requested by the Washington State Patrol to ensure the reliability of ignition interlock technologies.
HB 1732 (enacted in the 2009 Transportation Budget), securing a revolving fund, financed by DUI offenders, to pay for the ignition interlock devices of indigent DUI offenders.
HB 3254 (Chapter 282, Laws of 2008), a landmark measure, holding DUI offenders accountable through the establishment of the new Ignition Interlock License program.
HB 2130 (Chapter 474, Laws of 2007), strengthening the felony DUI law by properly accounting for prior DUI offenses.

added: 0 Skip to Content MEET MIKE NEWS HOUSING PLAN HEALTHCARE PLAN FAMILY OF SERVICE HOW TO VOTE VOLUNTEER CONTACT MERCH DONATE VIA BITPAY DONATE Open Menu Close Menu MEET MIKE NEWS HOUSING PLAN HEALTHCARE PLAN FAMILY OF SERVICE HOW TO VOTE VOLUNTEER CONTACT MERCH DONATE VIA BITPAY DONATE Open Menu Close Menu MEET MIKE NEWS HOUSING PLAN HEALTHCARE PLAN FAMILY OF SERVICE HOW TO VOTE VOLUNTEER CONTACT MERCH DONATE VIA BITPAY DONATE MIKE ROGERS ON FOX & FRIENDS: ABDUL EL-SAYED IS LIKE A GLITCHY AI CHATBOT Oct 9 Written By Hinson Peed DETROIT, MI – Army veteran, former FBI street agent, former House Intelligence Chair, and candidate for U.S.
Senate Mike Rogers today joined Fox News’ Fox & Friends to call out Conman Abdul El-Sayed’s pitiful debate performance.
WATCH THE FULL INTERVIEW HERE .
On Conman Abdul El-Sayed: “I thought this was really important.
We exposed him for who he really is.
I mean, this guy has been the ultimate conman. [He] can’t answer questions on Medicare for All, refuses to tell you that you’ll lose your private health insurance.
Think of Iran.
He couldn't answer the question on a country that has attempted terrorist attacks in the United States.
Oh, and by the way, has blood of U.S. soldiers on its hands.
I mean, this guy is absolutely dangerous.
And I think what we were able to do is show he says one thing, does another thing, and wants to present the one set of facts when the real facts just don't match it up.

Which to me is a conman.” On Abdul’s Refusal to Condemn the IRCG: “[The IRCG is] the equivalent of the biggest state sponsor [of terrorism] in the world, with blood on their hands from just about every country in the Middle East and beyond, including U.S. soldiers.
He can't answer the question: Who the good guy is and who the bad guy is?
If you can't answer that question, you have no business walking into the United States Senate.
This guy could not get a security clearance.
Why would we vote somebody into the Senate who couldn't get a security clearance if he needed one?
To me, that was the moment that we exposed who exactly he is.

He's dangerous, extreme, and if he can't figure out that the Americans and our allies are the good guys, and people like the IRGC and the Iranians are the bad guys, I worry about the future of the country.” On Conman Abdul Campaigning with Obama: “[Abdul] lost the Detroit vote by 67%.
His opponent got into the city of Detroit.
That's a huge number, and we have been making inroads into the black community in Detroit.
You know, the Democrats walked by the city of Detroit #ago, and they just stopped looking.
They just came to collect votes.
So we've made huge inroads with the black vote in the city and other Democrats around the southeast, and so they're hemorrhaging.
If you can't consolidate the black vote, that's why they brought in Barack Obama.
The problem is, he's been saying how terrible Barack Obama was.
I think this is going to backfire.
Even people we're talking to down in the city are saying, ‘Hey, this guy hated Barack Obama.
He hates blacks.
There's no way in heck I can vote for this guy.’ And that is the environment he has created in the city of Detroit.” On Conman Abdul’s Green New Deal Policies: “This is like a glitchy AI chatbot.
All he just repeats the same thing.
Well, your gas prices are high.
Your gas prices are high.
Your gas price.
He has no answer, no solution.
He believes in 100% renewables within 10 years.
What that would do to people's costs for their homes, their utilities.
By the way, auto workers.
I don't know if you noticed, we build cars in Michigan — kind of shocking — gas cars.
You might want to take a tour of the state.” Learn more about Conman Abdul El-Sayed’s lies, corruption, and extremism at StopAbdul.com .

SENATE Sep 16 Written By Hinson Peed DETROIT, MI – The Detroit News today endorsed Mike Rogers to represent Michigan in the U.S.
Senate.
They cited his extensive experience as an Army officer, FBI special agent, and former U.S.
House Intel Chair, calling him “the prototype of a United States Senator.” They go on to say, “He is mature, trustworthy and more than prepared.

Rogers’ experience, clear-thinking, and temperament, are bound to quickly vault him into the Senate’s leadership ranks.” The Detroit News also called out Conman Abdul El-Sayed’s extreme views and alarming record saying, “He has worked so hard covering his tracks leading up to this Senate race that it's impossible to know who he really is or where he would stand in the Senate.” They raised further concern with his deleted tweets; campaigning with Hasan Piker, who said “America deserved 9/11;” and animosity toward the Jewish community.
“Mike is grateful for the support as we continue the fight to fix our broken education system, lower housing costs, and bring back manufacturing jobs.
Michiganders deserve solutions, not slogans — and that’s exactly what Mike will bring to the U.S.
Senate.
We have a state to save.” – Alyssa Brouillet, Communications Director SUPPORT KEEPS STACKING This endorsement builds on support from the following: President Trump U.S.

Senators John Thune, Tim Scott , Bernie Moreno, John Barrasso , Roger Wicker, Tom Cotton, Steve Daines, Cynthia Lummis Congresswoman Lisa McClain , Congressman Bergman, and Congressman Walberg 20 local leaders in Macomb County State Representatives Greg Alexander , Joe Aragona , Brian BeGole , Matthew Bierlein , Karl Bohnak, William Bruck , Cam Cavitt , Jay DeBoyer, Nancy DeBoer, Steve Frisbie , Jamie Greene , Phil Green , Mike Harris , Mike Hoadley , Nancy Jenkins-Arno , Tim Kelly , Tom Kuhn , Tom Kunse , Matt Maddock , Greg Markkanen , David Martin , Luke Meerman , Mike Mueller , Jerry Neyer , Joseph Pavlov , Bryan Posthumus, Dave Prestin , Ron Robinson , Kathy Schmaltz , Bill G.
Schuette , Brad Slagh , Donni Steele , Alicia St.

Germaine , Jamie Thompson , Mark Tisdel , Curt VanderWall , Pauline Wendzel , Jason Woolford , Douglas Wozniak State Senators Joe Bellino , Kevin Daley , John Damoose , Roger Hauck , Michele Hoitenga , Ed McBroom , Aric Nesbitt , Rick Outman , Lana Theis Sheriffs Dan Abbott, Doug Chapman , Mike Murphy , Pat Whiteford , Scott Hodshire The Police Officers Association of Michigan (POAM) , “Auto Workers for Trump,” Associated Builders and Contractors , Southeast Michigan Chamber of Commerce , Sentinel Action Fund , AgriPAC , and College Republicans of America .
Learn more about Mike Rogers and his plan to get to work for Michigan at RogersForSenate.com .

added: Skip to content Donate to become a founding member of our campaign now Home Meet Roy Get Involved Make Stuff Cost Less Lowering the Cost of Food & Groceries Making Health Care Affordable Lowering Energy & Utility Costs Making Child Care Affordable Lowering Housing Costs FAQ Store Home Meet Roy Get Involved Make Stuff Cost Less Lowering the Cost of Food & Groceries Making Health Care Affordable Lowering Energy & Utility Costs Making Child Care Affordable Lowering Housing Costs FAQ Store Facebook Instagram X-twitter Tiktok Threads Flickr Donate Roy Cooper for North Carolina ICYMI: Roy Cooper Continues “Make Stuff Cost Less” Tour in Winston-Salem October 9, 2026 Roy Cooper: “I am running to make stuff cost less and will work with anyone in Washington to deliver for North Carolina families.” RALEIGH – Yesterday, Roy Cooper continued his “Make Stuff Cost Less” tour, holding an event in Winston-Salem to discuss how he will work in the U.S.
Senate to make life more affordable for North Carolina families.
WFMY: Roy Cooper Encourages North Carolinians to Vote During “Make Stuff Cost Less” Event in Winston-Salem Roy Cooper: “I’m encouraging people to make sure you go out and vote.
Vote all the way up and down the ballot.

This is not a race to sit out because there is too much at stake .” Winston-Salem Journal: Leading in polls, Roy Cooper tells supporters Senate race is far from over Richard Craver Cooper relied on his characteristic homespun humor mixed with his economic and healthcare campaign priorities, and how they represent the opposite of Whatley’s agenda.
Cooper said he chose to run for the U.S.

Senate to be part “of fixing what’s wrong in Washington.” “As hardworking families in Winston-Salem and around the state pay more at the gas pump and on their energy bills, Washington, D.C., insider Michael Whatley profits off his oil and utility stocks,” Cooper said.

Cooper said he plans to bring “North Carolina commonsense” to Congress and welcomes the opportunity to work with Republican counterparts in what would be the final two years of the second Trump administration.
“I am running to make stuff cost less and will work with anyone in Washington to deliver for North Carolina families.” “This is not a ballot to sit out,” Cooper said.
“There’s too much at stake.” WXII: Roy Cooper Continues “Make Stuff Cost Less” Tour in Winston-Salem Reporter: “Today, Democratic candidate for U.S.

Senate Roy Cooper was in Winston-Salem as part of his “Make Stuff Cost Less” tour, his focus on this campaign, as the name suggests, is to make life more affordable for families in North Carolina.” Roy Cooper: “We’ve seen a lot of times where Democrats have been ahead in October polling, only to lose in November.” Elon News Network: Roy Cooper discusses rising costs, key priorities at “Make Stuff Cost Less” event Miles Hayford Cooper discussed his recent conversations with supporters and the issues they are facing.
He said many people are facing rising costs and are now struggling to buy a home.
At the event, Cooper advocated for public education and criticized federal cuts to the Department of Education.

Some of Cooper’s biggest points of emphasis included his desire to roll back tariffs, end the war in Iran and restore healthcare subsidies. “[Michael Whatley] has worked to pass legislation that allows them to raise prices and raise rates,” Cooper said in his speech.
“As he cheers on the war in Iran, the oil stock goes up.
And guess what?
He still owns the stock.

So that’s money out of people’s pockets and into his.” “I’ve had a Republican legislature for eight years when I was governor, and yes, we disagreed on things, and yes, I vetoed legislation, but we worked together in many ways,” Cooper told Elon News Network.
“I think I got some receipts that I can bring to Washington to show that you can achieve consensus, and that’s what people want.

People just want government to work.” WFDD: Democratic Senate nominee Roy Cooper visits Winston-Salem Rachel Moody “I’m talking with people who are in the middle class and who are barely hanging on,” Cooper said.
“They need someone who will represent them, not the billionaires, not the big corporations that are already doing okay.

Represent everyday people who are being left behind by this broken, chaotic Washington.” For Cooper, bringing prices down includes ending the war in Iran, which has raised the cost of gas and fertilizer.

added: Skip to content Donate to become a founding member of our campaign now Home Meet Roy Get Involved Make Stuff Cost Less Lowering the Cost of Food & Groceries Making Health Care Affordable Lowering Energy & Utility Costs Making Child Care Affordable Lowering Housing Costs FAQ Store Home Meet Roy Get Involved Make Stuff Cost Less Lowering the Cost of Food & Groceries Making Health Care Affordable Lowering Energy & Utility Costs Making Child Care Affordable Lowering Housing Costs FAQ Store Facebook Instagram X-twitter Tiktok Threads Flickr Donate Roy Cooper for North Carolina NEW TV AD: Eastern North Carolina Sheriff Who Led Investigation Into Convicted Child Sex Predator Harvey Lee West Denounces Michael Whatley For Appointing West October 9, 2026 RALEIGH – Today, Cooper for North Carolina released a new TV ad, “Led” where former Beaufort County Sheriff Alan Jordan – the man who led the investigation into Harvey Lee West – denounces Michael Whatley for knowingly putting a convicted child sex predator in a senior leadership position with access with kids.

“Harvey Lee West was a convicted child sex predator who spent six years in prison for his crimes and yet, Michael Whatley knowingly championed him and gave West a top political role with access to children,” said Cooper for North Carolina Campaign Manager Jeff Allen .
“Whatley is out for himself and will stop at nothing to benefit himself.

Roy Cooper is the only candidate in this race who has put violent criminals, rapists and child sex offenders behind bars and kept them there.” On the campaign trail, Whatley continues to embrace predators, campaigning with a convicted child rapist , members of a cult accused of sexually abusing children and at a church that protected a child sex abuser.
The ad will run on broadcast television, streaming and digital platforms statewide as part of a seven-figure buy.
Read a transcript of “Led” below.
Roy Cooper: I’m Roy Cooper and I approve this message.
Former Beaufort County Sheriff Alan Jordan: I was the sheriff in Beaufort County for 16 years.
I led the investigation into Harvey Lee West.
He spent six years in prison for sexually abusing kids.
He’s a monster, but Michael Whatley – he put him in a senior leadership role anyway, even though he knew he was a convicted sex offender.
Whatley even let West attend events with little kids.
I put predators like Harvey Lee West in jail.
Michael Whatley put one on his team.

Michael Whatley has a disturbing pattern of campaigning with and elevating child sex predators, including: Appointing Harvey West, who spent six years in prison for sexually abusing three minors to NCGOP leadership.
Campaigning with Daimon King, a registered lifetime sex offender who spent years in prison on two separate occasions for child sex crimes, including rape and incest.
Attributing his rise in politics to the Rutherford County GOP, which has been “taken over” by the Word of Faith Fellowship – a cult that has been accused of physically and sexually abusing children.
Campaigning at Victory Baptist Church, which reportedly covered up for and protected an employee who was indicted for sexually abusing children for over a decade.

CruzNYC All Articles Search Reimagining Local Education Plans for the Future: Bold Education Plan Improvements Ruben Cruz Sep 15 3 min read Education shapes our future.
It molds the minds that will build our communities, drive our economy, and protect our values.
But the way we plan education at the local level?
It’s stuck in the past.
It’s time to shake things up.
I’m here to tell you why reimagining local education plans is not just necessary - it’s urgent.
And I’ll show you how we can make bold education plan improvements that truly serve our community’s needs.
Why We Need Education Plan Improvements Now We can’t afford to wait.
Our schools face challenges that demand immediate action.
Overcrowded classrooms, outdated curricula, and a lack of resources are just the tip of the iceberg.
Students deserve better.
Teachers deserve support.
Our community deserves a plan that reflects today’s realities and tomorrow’s possibilities.
I’ve seen firsthand how rigid, one-size-fits-all education plans fail to address local needs.
We need plans that are flexible, inclusive, and forward-thinking.
Plans that embrace technology, foster creativity, and prepare students for a rapidly changing world.
Here’s what education plan improvements should focus on: Personalized learning: Tailoring education to individual student strengths and challenges.
Community involvement: Engaging parents, local businesses, and organizations in shaping education.
Career readiness: Integrating skills training and real-world experiences.
Equity and access: Ensuring all students have the resources they need to succeed.
These aren’t just ideas.
They’re essential steps to build a stronger, smarter community.
Ruben Cruz working with students on the QCAN network What are the current education reforms?
You might wonder, what’s already changing?
Several reforms are underway, but many fall short of addressing local realities.
Statewide mandates often overlook the unique challenges and opportunities in our district.
For example, standardized testing remains a heavy focus, sometimes at the expense of creativity and critical thinking.
Some districts have started incorporating technology and project-based learning.
Others have expanded after-school programs and mental health support.
These are positive moves, but they need to be part of a larger, cohesive strategy.
We need reforms that: Break down bureaucratic barriers.
Empower local educators to innovate.
Prioritize student well-being alongside academic achievement.
Foster partnerships with local businesses to create internship and apprenticeship opportunities.
Without these, reforms risk being superficial fixes rather than transformative change.
How to Implement Effective Local Education Plan Improvements Change starts with a clear vision and community buy-in.
Here’s how I believe we can implement effective education plan improvements: Conduct a thorough needs assessment.
Gather data from students, parents, teachers, and local businesses.
Understand what’s working and what’s not.
Set measurable goals.
Define what success looks like in terms of graduation rates, skill acquisition, and student engagement.
Develop flexible curricula.
Incorporate STEM, arts, and vocational training tailored to local economic needs.
Invest in teacher training.
Equip educators with tools and methods to deliver personalized, engaging lessons.
Leverage technology wisely.
Use digital tools to enhance learning, not replace human connection.
Create accountability structures.
Regularly review progress and adjust plans based on feedback and outcomes.
This approach ensures that education plans are not static documents but living frameworks that evolve with our community.
The Role of Community and Local Businesses in Education Education doesn’t happen in isolation.
It thrives when the entire community is involved.
Local businesses, in particular, have a critical role to play.
They can offer internships, mentorships, and real-world learning experiences that textbooks simply can’t provide.
Imagine a local tech company partnering with schools to teach coding.
Or a small business owner mentoring students on entrepreneurship.
These connections make education relevant and exciting.
They also build a pipeline of skilled workers ready to contribute to our local economy.
I’m committed to fostering these partnerships.
Together, we can create a vibrant ecosystem where education and economic development go hand in hand.
Bracelet Gift to Ruben Cruz Moving Forward: A Call to Action for Our Community We stand at a crossroads.
The choices we make about education today will echo for generations.
I urge you to join me in demanding bold, meaningful local education plan reform.
We need plans that reflect our values, address our challenges, and unlock our potential.
This is not just about policy.
It’s about people.
It’s about giving every child the chance to succeed.
It’s about building a community where education fuels opportunity and growth.
Together, we can reimagine education for the future.
Together, we can make education plan improvements that matter.
Let’s get to work.

Yet, our local schools face challenges that demand urgent action.

CruzNYC All Articles Search Rethinking Housing Policies for Local Impact: Affordable Housing Strategies That Work Ruben Cruz #ago 4 min read Housing is more than just shelter.
It’s the foundation of our communities, the backbone of local economies, and the key to stability for families and small businesses alike.
Yet, too many residents in New York State Assembly District 38 face skyrocketing rents, limited options, and policies that don’t serve their needs.
It’s time to rethink housing policies with a sharp focus on affordable housing strategies that create real, lasting local impact.
I’m here to break down what needs to change, why it matters, and how we can push for reforms that protect our neighborhoods and empower our people.
Why Affordable Housing Strategies Must Be Local and Practical Affordable housing isn’t a one-size-fits-all issue.
What works in one city or district might fail in another.
That’s why I believe in tailoring solutions to the unique challenges and opportunities right here in District 38.
We need strategies that: Address the real cost of living for families and small businesses.
Encourage development without displacement .
Support economic growth by keeping workers close to jobs.
Protect residents from predatory landlords and unfair practices .
For example, zoning reforms that allow for more mixed-use developments can create vibrant neighborhoods where people live, work, and shop without long commutes.
Incentives for developers to build affordable units alongside market-rate housing can increase supply without sacrificing quality.
We also need to invest in preserving existing affordable housing stock.
Too often, older buildings are lost to luxury conversions or neglect.
Local policies should prioritize rehabilitation and maintenance grants to keep these homes safe and affordable.
Eye-level view of a mixed-use residential building with retail shops on the ground floor Key Affordable Housing Strategies That Can Transform District 38 Let’s get specific.
Here are some affordable housing strategies that can make a difference right now: Inclusionary Zoning Require new developments to include a percentage of affordable units.
This spreads affordable housing throughout the district and prevents economic segregation.
Community Land Trusts Support nonprofit ownership of land to keep housing affordable permanently.
This model removes land from the speculative market and stabilizes neighborhoods.
Rent Control and Tenant Protections Strengthen laws that limit rent hikes and protect tenants from eviction without cause.
Stability in housing means stability in life.
Streamlined Permitting for Affordable Projects Cut red tape for developers who commit to affordable housing.
Faster approvals mean quicker construction and more homes.
Public-Private Partnerships Leverage government resources with private investment to fund affordable housing projects.
Collaboration can unlock new funding and expertise.
Small Business Support in Housing Areas Integrate commercial spaces for local businesses in housing developments.
This keeps the local economy thriving and accessible.
These strategies are not theoretical.
Cities across the country have seen success by implementing them.
We can adapt these proven methods to fit the needs of our district.
What is in the housing bill that just passed?
Recently, a new housing bill passed that aims to address some of these challenges.
It includes provisions for increased funding for affordable housing projects, stronger tenant protections, and incentives for developers to build mixed-income communities.
However, the bill also leaves room for improvement.
It doesn’t fully address the need for community land trusts or provide enough support for small businesses affected by housing changes.
It’s a step forward, but not the finish line.
We must push for amendments and local policies that fill these gaps.
The fight for affordable housing is ongoing, and every voice counts.

High angle view of a community meeting discussing housing policies How Local Housing Policy Reform Can Drive Real Change I want to emphasize the power of local housing policy reform in shaping our future.
Statewide or federal policies often miss the nuances of our district’s needs.
Local reform allows us to: Engage directly with residents and businesses to understand their challenges.
Create flexible policies that respond quickly to market changes.
Hold developers and landlords accountable to community standards.
Build partnerships with local organizations that know the neighborhood best.
By focusing on local solutions, we can ensure that affordable housing strategies are not just words on paper but actions that improve lives.
What Residents and Small Businesses Can Do Now Change doesn’t happen without action.
Here’s how residents and small businesses in District 38 can get involved: Attend local council meetings and voice your concerns about housing.
Support candidates and policies that prioritize affordable housing.
Join or form community land trusts or housing advocacy groups.
Report predatory landlord practices to local authorities.
Collaborate with neighbors to push for zoning reforms that benefit everyone.
Your participation is crucial.
Together, we can hold policymakers accountable and ensure that housing policies reflect the needs of our community.
Building a Future Where Everyone Has a Place to Call Home Affordable housing is not just a policy issue.
It’s a moral imperative.
It’s about dignity, opportunity, and fairness.
When we rethink housing policies with urgency and clarity, we create neighborhoods where families thrive, businesses grow, and communities flourish.
I’m committed to fighting for these changes in New York State Assembly District 38.
But I can’t do it alone.
We need your voice, your energy, and your vision.
Let’s build a future where affordable housing is a reality, not a dream.
Where every resident has a safe, stable place to call home.
Where our local economy is strong because our people are supported.
The time to act is now.
Together, we can make it happen. www.rubencruz.nyc Recent Posts See All Transforming Local Education: Essential Education Reform Strategies Education shapes our future.
It molds the minds of tomorrow’s leaders, workers, and citizens.
Yet, our local schools face challenges that demand urgent action.

AI Autonomous Weapons: ARE WE ALREADY TOO LATE?
AI Autonomous Weapons: The Race to Stop Machines from Deciding Who Lives and Dies Artificial intelligence is transforming warfare at a frightening pace.
Autonomous weapons capable of identifying, tracking, and attacking targets with decreasing human involvement are no longer just science fiction.

This documentary examines the urgent international effort to establish a legally binding treaty restricting or prohibiting autonomous weapons systems before their development and deployment outpace meaningful human control.
But the danger extends far beyond conventional warfare.
What happens when these technologies spread to terrorist organizations, drug cartels, criminal networks, or wealthy individuals capable of financing private armies of autonomous machines?
Imagine a future in which a single individual could command hundreds of thousands—or even a million—AI-powered drones.
The documentary raises this extraordinary possibility, illustrating how artificial intelligence could concentrate unprecedented destructive power in the hands of very few people.
We may already be dangerously behind in establishing the safeguards needed to prevent catastrophic misuse.
The question is no longer simply what artificial intelligence can do.
It is what humanity will allow it to do—and whether we can establish enforceable international limits before these weapons become impossible to control.
Watch this documentary and consider what is at stake for humanity, international security, and future generations.

A political party?

PAY ATTENTION — Are We Failing Our Children?
A New Gaia Knights Song About Childhood, Technology, Education, and Our Responsibility to the Next Generation “Everybody wants their attention.
Who's paying attention to them?” What happens when we raise an entire generation in a world designed to compete for every second of their attention?

PAY ATTENTION , the latest song from Gaia Knights, asks a difficult but essential question: Are our children failing to meet society's expectations, or are we failing to provide the environment they need to thrive?
Through a powerful musical narrative, the song follows the everyday experiences of children, parents, and teachers struggling to connect in an increasingly distracted world.
A young child tries to get a parent's attention.
A tired teacher struggles to reach students.
An exhausted mother hands her child a tablet for a moment of peace.
A teenager scrolls late into the night, caught in an endless stream of digital stimulation.
These are not stories about bad children, bad parents, or bad teachers.
They are stories about a society that has allowed technology, economic pressures, and the demands of modern life to reshape childhood.
Childhood Is Practice for Being Human One of the song's central messages is that childhood is not simply preparation for tests, grades, or future employment.
Childhood is when we learn to cooperate, disagree, negotiate, imagine, create, fail, recover, and understand one another.
These essential human experiences cannot always be replaced by a screen.

Yet children are increasingly growing up surrounded by digital systems designed to capture their attention, while opportunities for unstructured play, meaningful relationships, and personal discovery compete for time.
A Call for Adult Responsibility PAY ATTENTION challenges the tendency to blame children for behaviors that may be influenced by the environment adults have created.
It asks parents, educators, technology companies, policymakers, and society as a whole to reconsider our priorities.
We need to support families, give parents more time with their children, strengthen education, and take seriously the effects of digital technology on childhood development.
The goal is not to reject technology.
It is to ensure that technology serves humanity—especially our children—rather than allowing human development to become secondary to commercial interests.
Music With a Message Created and produced by Rob Rush [Ruszkowski] , Independent write-in candidate for the U.S.
House of Representatives in Georgia's 14th Congressional District, PAY ATTENTION is part of the Gaia Knights music project: Songs for a Brighter Tomorrow .
Gaia Knights uses music to explore the challenges facing humanity and encourage people to imagine a better future.
The message of PAY ATTENTION is simple but urgent: “The children aren't failing us.
We're failing the children.” Our children deserve more than criticism.
They deserve our time, attention, understanding, and commitment to building a better world.
Watch the complete PAY ATTENTION music video below.
If the song resonates with you, please visit YouTube to LIKE the video, leave a COMMENT, SUBSCRIBE to Gaia Knights, and SHARE the song with others.
Because the future of our children is the future of us all.

PAY ATTENTION — Protecting Our Children A Powerful New Gaia Knights Song About Childhood, Social Media, Screen Addiction, and Our Responsibility to Protect the Next Generation.
Everybody wants their attention.
Who's paying attention to them?
We are raising an entire generation in a world where technology companies compete for every moment of their attention.
Children are surrounded by smartphones, social media, addictive algorithms, endless scrolling, and digital entertainment designed to keep them engaged for as long as possible.
Meanwhile, parents are exhausted, teachers are overwhelmed, and children are increasingly expected to navigate a digital environment that even adults struggle to control.
And when children have difficulty concentrating, listening, learning, or connecting with others, we often blame them.
But who created the environment they're growing up in?
My new Gaia Knights song, PAY ATTENTION , explores this question through the everyday experiences of children, parents, and teachers.

It tells the story of a child trying to get a parent's attention, a student struggling in the classroom, an exhausted mother handing her child a tablet, and the powerful digital systems constantly calling young people back to their screens.
But the song is about something much bigger than technology.
It's about the childhood experiences we're losing—and the human connections we need to restore.

“Childhood is practice for being human.” Children need time to play, imagine, explore, make friends, resolve disagreements, experience disappointment, and learn how to interact with the world around them.
These are essential parts of growing up.

Why I Support Stronger Protections for Children As part of my Protecting the Children policy platform, I support prohibiting social media access for children under 16, establishing healthier screen-time boundaries, and creating phone-free learning environments in our K–12 schools.
These proposals are not about rejecting technology or denying its benefits.

They're about recognizing that children deserve special protections during critical years of development—and that companies profiting from capturing their attention should not be allowed to determine the conditions of childhood.
Parents and teachers cannot solve these problems alone.
We need policies that support families, protect children, and place their long-term well-being ahead of corporate profits.
We must also recognize the pressures on working parents and the importance of giving families more time together.
The responsibility belongs to all of us.
Listen to the Full Song: PAY ATTENTION I invite you to watch this complete Gaia Knights music video and consider the questions it raises.
The song isn't intended to blame children, parents, or teachers.
It's a call for all of us to recognize what is happening and take responsibility for creating a healthier future.
“The children aren't failing us.

We're failing the children.” If this song speaks to you, please LIKE the video on YouTube, leave a COMMENT, and SHARE it with parents, grandparents, teachers, and others who care about the future of our children.
Because protecting childhood isn't just about limiting screen time.
It's about giving children back the time, attention, relationships, and experiences they need to become healthy, capable, compassionate human beings.
PAY ATTENTION — Created and produced by Rob Rush [Ruszkowski] for Gaia Knights: Songs for a Brighter Tomorrow.
People Over Parties.

added: Skip to content Skip to sidebar Skip to footer Menu Close Home About Ask David Virtual Rally Volunteer Events Close Home About Ask David Virtual Rally Volunteer Events Youtube Instagram Get in Touch Home About Ask David Virtual Rally Volunteer Events Money Wins October 9, 2026 We have all heard it all of our lives, “Money Wins Elections.” I have always said, “As long as Money Wins, we will get what we have always had.” People keep asking where the money is.
They ask it like the answer is supposed to embarrass me.
It does not.
I filed the #RussIsForUS third-quarter report with the FEC today.
When it posts, you will see that I brought in just over $19,000 this year.
I do not have a million dollars of my own to drop into the campaign and call it a “movement.” The RNC took money from my constituents and gave it to candidates in other states instead of me.
The NRCC did not send money, and refuses to respond to me.
I received no money from Big Industry nor Big Pharma.
No other politician nor organization elevated me, funded me, nor sent me out to read a script.
Funding from those people means I have no hooks in me and can represent you (#US) completely and without reservation.
What I did receive was the overwhelming support of Oregon District 6 Republican voters in the 2026 primary.
That is the part the establishment talking heads never understand.
They treat a small donation number as a failure.
As stated in the heading of this post, “As long as money decides who gets elected, we will get what we have always had.” This is how we (#US) break that cycle.
It is also how I stay out of the kind of trouble that follows the money.
Large totals create large problems.
The truth is, people who have big money in their election coffers generally didn’t get it from you.
When did you last contribute to a congressional candidate?
For the average citizen, the answer is “never.” I never did, except now to my own camapaign committee.
That is true for most people in Oregon’s 6th Congressional District.
That is who I represent.
Andrea Salinas is the other model.
This cycle she has taken $656,650 through ActBlue, 2,280 of her 5,200 individual donations.
You can look at the filings yourself: FEC receipts, Andrea Salinas for Oregon .
ActBlue is not a neighbor handing her twenty dollars at a picnic.
It is a national (international?) machine, and that machine is currently under investigation.

Three House committees just reported that ActBlue failed to stop illegal foreign contributions, and last week they summoned ActBlue’s attorney over the contradiction in its own story: House report , Fox News, September 28 .
So where is my campaign money?
It is not in a committee account with strings that tie me and my Congressional Votes back to the donors.
It is still in your pocket, serving you…Like I will.
I am a candidate with no owner except those who elected him.
That is worth infinitely more to you than the candidate bought and paid for by the political machine.
This is your opportunity to break the cycle.
Vote for Russ.

They're Waiting Until You've Voted Republicans already admitted they'll redraw our maps.
The only question is when.
Saira Draper October 09, 2026 Republicans have a plan for our maps after Election Day.
Here's what it is, and how your vote can stop it.

Click to view my Instagram reel on the most important reason to vote for Keisha Lance Bottoms Georgia Republicans plan to redraw our political maps right after the November election, in a lame-duck session while Governor Kemp is still in office to sign them.
They backed off in June because redrawing was politically risky right before an election, not for the reasons they gave.
The best way to fight back is to elect Keisha Lance Bottoms governor –her veto would give us the leverage to force fair maps, and to flip seats in the legislature.
In this Edition of the Draper Paper Their plan: a lame-duck map grab Why the governor's veto is our best leverage Watch and share: my new video You're invited!

Support Tanya Miller for Attorney General Their plan: a lame-duck map grab It's an open secret that Republicans plan to call a special session after the midterms to draw new electoral maps for Congress, and the Georgia State House and Senate.
They laughed about it during the special session in June, after their plans to redraw the maps then were put on hold by Republican party leaders.
Let's back up.
On April 29 , the Supreme Court issued its decision in Louisiana v.
Callais , gutting what was left of the Voting Rights Act.
That law was the guardrail stopping Georgia Republicans from drawing rigged maps that silence minority voters.
Overnight, the Voting Rights Act was gone.
Within weeks of the Callais decision, Governor Kemp called a special session and put redistricting on the agenda.
He asked lawmakers to redraw Georgia's congressional maps and their own legislative districts and to pass those maps right away.( AP via PBS ).

Then, on June 17 , hours before the special session began, House Speaker Jon Burns stood before a packed Capitol atrium and announced that the House would not take up redistricting during that special session.
Check out our Guide to Georgia Legislative Procedure and Redistricting Terms here.

Speaker Jon Burns’ broken promise Although Republican leaders claimed they delayed redrawing political boundaries to allow for public input and court reviews, that excuse was just a political trick to avoid voter backlash before the midterm election.
Instead of holding hearings, they are running out the clock to push through partisan maps in a “surprise” post-election session.
Speaker of the House Jon Burns, R-Newington, speaks during a special legislative session at the state capitol, Wednesday, June 17, 2026, in Atlanta.
(AP Photo/Mike Stewart) Standing before a large crowd of angry Georgians, Speaker Burns laid out his reasons for not redrawing the maps in June ( watch the press conference ).

He said when the House learned redistricting was one of the governor’s priorities for the June special session, "we knew it was not the right path forward for our state at this time ." Notice those last three words.
Not never.
Just not now.

He said redistricting should be done "the Georgia way — responsibly, transparently, and with ample opportunity for public input." He promised "joint reapportionment meetings to hear from voters in every corner of the state," in "a fair and bipartisan environment." He also stated that the state’s decision to drop redistricting plans was driven by a commitment to a "thoughtful, fact-driven process" rather than "partisan gain.” And he pointed to the courts.

With several cases pending over Georgia's maps, he said Republicans "look forward to receiving additional judicial opinions to assist in our future map drawing efforts." He made this point in his letter to Governor Kemp that morning.
Senate President Pro Tem Larry Walker III, standing beside him, was even more candid.
He said the Callais decision "left no doubt that we would need to draw new maps.

The question was when." He said the Senate wanted "to allow the judicial process to further develop in other states" while "receiving additional public input before considering any changes to our maps." But those weren't the Republicans' real reasons for delaying redistricting.
Before the special session, Republicans polled redistricting, and it polled poorly.

Behind closed doors, Republican lawmakers worried that a redraw diminishing Georgians' ability to elect the politicians of their choosing would spark a backlash, leading to even bigger Democratic wins in the midterms.
With their own members on the ballot in November, House and Senate Republican leaders rejected their own governor's call.
It wasn't a moral decision.
It was a political one.
How do we know these reasons were a pretext?
Compare each one to what has happened since.
"Ample opportunity for public input." Not one of the promised joint reapportionment meetings has been held.
Not in a single corner of the state.
In September, the Speaker's office told the AJC that none were even scheduled.
And Walker, who promised "additional public input" in June, told the AJC he had not committed to the joint hearings at all.
"Additional judicial opinions." The federal district court is now in the process of reviewing Georgia's maps , but no decision has been issued yet.
If Republicans redraw the maps in a lame-duck session before those opinions come down, the pending litigation excuse was never real.
"Not to rush through it." A lame-duck session called weeks after Election Day, with no hearings held and the courts still deciding, is the very definition of rushing it.
"Not the right path forward … at this time." Republicans never said they wouldn't redraw.
Walker said it himself: "The question was when." The answer: after the voters are done voting in the midterms.
If Republicans truly cared about transparency and public input, they had all summer and fall to hold hearings.
Instead, they are running out the clock until a lame-duck session, when voters will have no chance to weigh in and no election left to hold them accountable.

So much for "not partisan gain." As I told the AJC last month : "If Keisha Lance Bottoms wins, they're going to push this through, and I think any promises of halting for pending litigation or transparency will be out the window." What Happens Next Instead of facing voters before the midterms, Republicans plan to rush a partisan redistricting map through a lame-duck session later this year while Governor Kemp is still in office to sign it, locking in legislative republican majorities for a generation before a new governor can take office.
When I wrote to you in April , I laid out two paths Republicans could take.

One of those paths was to redraw the maps in a special session this year, too late to affect the midterms, but early enough to avoid a veto from a Democratic governor or a fight with a Democratic House or Senate.
That is exactly the path they've chosen.
Here's how it will work.
Wait until the votes are counted in November.

If Democrats make significant gains in the State Legislature or win the Governor and other statewide races, call legislators back to the Capitol in a lame-duck session, in November or December, and draw the rigged maps they refused to draw in June while Governor Kemp is still in office to sign them.
Politically, Georgia is a 50/50 state.
We've proven that in election after election.
But with rigged maps, Georgia Republicans could lock in their majorities for a generation, no matter how Georgians vote.

And make no mistake about what that would mean: The same one-party rule that has controlled our state for more than two decades, without real checks and balances, that has given us sky-high costs and unchecked data centers popping up in our backyards while our power bills keep going up will remain in power.
Rigged maps would make that the permanent state of affairs, no matter how you vote.
Why the governor's veto is our best leverage If you elect Keisha Lance Bottoms as governor, every single thing Republicans want for the next four years has to get past her veto.
Their budget priorities.
Their tax bills.
Their pet projects.
All of it.
So if Kemp signs the maps before she takes office, why does it matter who wins the governor's race?
Because a map isn't permanent.
The legislature can redraw maps any year it chooses, and a Democratic governor can make sure it chooses to.
Democratic candidate for governor Keisha Lance Bottoms speaks at a joint campaign rally with U.S.
Sen.
Jon Ossoff at the Tabernacle in Atlanta on May 31, 2026.
(Source: Arvin Temkar/AJC) And Georgia's governor holds more cards than most.
The governor sets the revenue estimate that caps the entire state budget and can strike individual spending items with a line-item veto.
Republicans do not have the two-thirds majorities in both chambers they would need to override her.
That's leverage.
And Governor Bottoms can use it to force Republicans back to the table on fair maps.
Without a Democratic governor, those rigged maps stand for a generation.
With her as governor, we have a fighting chance.
The same goes for the legislature.
Flipping the Georgia House or Senate would give us a second check on one-party rule and a seat at the table when maps are drawn.
That's why it matters that you vote all the way down your ballot.
Watch and share: my new video I made a short video explaining all of this in about a minute.
Almost nobody is talking about this issue, and that's exactly what Republicans are counting on.
Please watch it, share it with every Georgian you know, and follow me on Instagram for more.

added: Saltar al contenido principal Saira Draper for State Senate District 44 for SD44 Acerca de Conoce a Saira Apoyos Distrito 44 Participa Participa Trabaja con Saira Toca puertas Noticias y eventos Obtén ayuda Únete a la campaña Donar Accesibilidad Tamaño del texto ES English Español Tiếng Việt ← All News Posted: October 9, 2026 at 11:07 AM EDT A Guide to Georgia Legislative Procedure and Redistricting Terms Articles Breaking down the essential terms governing district mapmaking, voting rights, and statehouse procedures in Georgia.
Georgia's General Assembly, also known as the "Gold Dome," has its own vocabulary to describe legislative processes.
Here's a guide tos ome of the common terms, along with some additional helpful information.
Mapmaking and Voting Rights Redistricting: The process of redrawing the boundaries of congressional and state legislative districts in Georgia.
This process determines which voters are grouped together to elect each representative.

Gerrymandering: The practice of drawing district lines specifically to give one political party an unfair advantage, enabling it to win more legislative seats relative to its overall share of the vote.
Voting Rights Act: The 1965 federal civil rights law enacted to protect minority voters from discrimination, including prohibiting electoral maps that dilute their voting power.
Louisiana v.
Callais : An April 2026 Supreme Court decision that gutted the remaining protections under the Voting Rights Act against discriminatory redistricting maps.
Legislative Sessions and Authority Special Session: A meeting of the Georgia legislature called by the governor outside the standard January-to-April regular session.

A special session is strictly limited to the topics specified by the governor on the agenda, known as "the call." Lame-Duck Session: A legislative session held after an election but before newly elected officials take office.
During this period, outgoing officials can act on legislation without facing immediate accountability from voters.
Veto Override: The constitutional mechanism by which the Georgia General Assembly passes a bill into law over a governor's veto.
To successfully override a veto, a two-thirds vote is required in both the Georgia House of Representatives and the State Senate.

added: Skip to main content Saira Draper for State Senate District 44 for SD44 About Meet Saira Endorsements District 44 Get Involved Get Involved Work with Saira Canvass News + Events Get Help Join the Campaign Donate Accessibility Text size EN English Español Tiếng Việt ← All News Posted: October 9, 2026 at 2:46 PM EDT They're Waiting Until You've Voted By Saira Draper Draper Paper Republicans already admitted they'll redraw our maps.
