And, it requires a willingness to tell the truth about what is happening in plain sight. Langston Hughes once wrote: “O, yes, I say it plain, America never was America to me, And yet I swear this oath—America will be!” That tension — between what this country has been and what it has the capacity to become — is part of the unfolding American story. Georgia has always stood at the center of the struggle for representation, voice, and democracy. And once again, we are being reminded that fair representation does not defend itself. People, pay attention. Ask questions. Speak up. And know that I’ll be fighting for fair representation and our voting rights under the Gold Dome. Because the map is never neutral. And it is never just a map.

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t39.30808-6/704367010_1373870971232245_9093196896951057183_n.jpg|3 votes cast today — including my first-time voter. ❤️ Watching my kids step into their civic responsibility will never grow old. A reminder that democracy is not abstract. It is personal. It is generational. And it only works when we participate. Georgia, there is less than 1 hour left to vote in today’s primary election. If you are still in line by 7 PM, stay in line. Your voice matters. Your vote matters.

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t39.30808-6/724598292_1396864692266206_7491307811334795185_n.jpg|Hey Georgia! Hey Fulton County! It’s Election Day and it’s your last chance to vote in these runoff elections. I got my peach sticker! 🍑 Go get yours. And while you’re at it, let’s keep our democracy strong by making our voices heard.

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t39.30808-6/725440018_1397686355517373_6996259346694652865_n.jpg|BREAKING NEWS: Back at the Capitol for special session and here’s a first update. Republicans have announced that they will NOT be redrawing maps during this special session. There’s no question that every call, every rally, everyone who has showed up on these days leading to the start of session and here at the Capitol today have made it clear that disenfranchising black and brown voters is not what the people of our state want. And it's not what we will tolerate. Today, the people won. BUT we must continue to keep the pressure up so maps remain off the table. Round 2: November. Eyes wide open!

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t39.30808-6/727864803_1399445155341493_4782010524670662717_n.jpg|Juneteenth reminds us that freedom is not just a moment in history but a responsibility we carry forward.

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t39.30808-6/728664217_1401602785125730_5328628331734526883_n.jpg|Back at the Capitol and in committee meetings early this Monday morning. One of the most important pieces of legislation passed and signed into law this year is the Georgia Early Literacy Act of 2026, which will place literacy coaches in K-3 schools across our state. As a member of the Senate Education & Youth Committee, I can’t overstate how important the work we’ve done on literacy over the last three years has been. Today, only about 30% of Georgia third graders are reading at grade level. We can do better than that. And we will. Because when a child learns to read, they gain the foundation to learn, grow, and succeed in every subject that follows. Every child deserves that chance.

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t39.30808-6/729069127_1402389708380371_4739887556392488066_n.jpg|More explanation on why I voted NO on these tax bills which swaps property tax relief for a new sales tax.

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t39.30808-6/729414176_1401118195174189_8642219699021418361_n.jpg|Today, I’m grateful for the fathers, grandfathers, stepfathers, mentors, and father figures who show up with love, wisdom, patience, and strength. The ones who guide, encourage, protect, and help shape who we become. To those celebrating, remembering, missing someone, or carrying on their legacy—wishing you peace, love, and meaningful moments today. Happy Father’s Day.

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.71878-15/689393031_2181606912587624_3218313443040261390_n.jpg|The cost of living is hitting families harder than ever. Groceries are through the roof, health insurance premiums keep rising, and too many people across District 39 and all of Georgia are being forced to choose between basic necessities. I see it, I hear it, and I’m committed to speaking up for the people who feel overlooked and unheard. We deserve leadership that fights for affordable healthcare, lower everyday costs, and real solutions that help working families thrive — not just survive. I will continue using my voice to advocate for our communities, our seniors, our parents, our small business owners, and every Georgian working hard to make ends meet. #District39 #Georgia #CommunityFirst #AffordableHealthcare #CostOfLiving

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.71878-15/705451056_1048815681139964_3171737461591848021_n.jpg|Too many hardworking Georgia families are doing everything right and still finding it difficult to keep up with rising costs. That’s why affordability remains one of my top priorities. From conversations at the Capitol to ongoing work with colleagues across state government, I remain focused on solutions that help families afford housing, access quality healthcare, support their children, and build financial stability for the future. Public service is about improving everyday life for the people we represent. I’ll continue fighting for policies that put working families first and ensure every Georgian has the opportunity to thrive—not just get by. Thank you for allowing me to be your voice under the Gold Dome. Together, we will keep moving Georgia forward. #SonyaSays #Sonya4Ga

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.71878-15/788966064_2297828984378140_4486292939109961078_n.jpg|Whew… I blinked and my middle is off to college. Somehow, all those years of growing, learning, laughing, pushing boundaries, and finding his way brought us here. Move-in. Convocation. A few last hugs. And then the moment you realize it’s time to let him go make this next chapter his own. But not before shedding a few tears…okay, maybe more than a few. There’s so much I could say, but mostly I just want him to know how proud we are of the young man he has become—and how excited we are for all that is ahead of him. Go learn. Go explore. Go make some new friends. Take some chances. Make some mistakes. Call home. Definitely call your mom. 😏 And most of all, enjoy becoming more and more of who you are. The world is waiting for you. And we’ll always be just one call away. ❤️

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.71878-15/814800512_1419565056772601_1237319889168188743_n.jpg|A look back at the @ga_blackcaucus and @gacoalitionofblackchambers BlackPrint Prosperity Convening!⁠ ⁠ On day two, I had the opportunity to lead a great conversation with @boodieforga, @sandra.l.williams3, and Rep. Al Williams on infrastructure and what it takes to build lasting economic prosperity.⁠ ⁠ I started the conversation with a simple premise: infrastructure is about more than roads and bridges. It’s the physical, digital, financial, educational and institutional systems that make prosperity possible.⁠ ⁠ But opportunity alone doesn’t create prosperity. The real test is whether people can participate, advance and build something from it—and whether our communities are stronger because of it.⁠ ⁠ That’s the work ahead. From rural Georgia to our urban centers and everywhere in between, we have to keep asking what we need to put in place so that more people, businesses and communities can thrive.⁠ ⁠ And the conversation doesn’t stop with the convening. I’m looking forward to continuing it—with more voices at the table and more ideas we can turn into action as we work toward a more prosperous Georgia.⁠ ⁠ #Sonya4Ga #BlackPrint #EconomicProsperity #GaInfrastructure

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/683483692_18105941546312458_6041532980430484482_n.jpg|For weeks now, I’ve been feeling a mix of emotions leading up to my son’s high school graduation. Pride. Gratitude. Nostalgia. Excitement. And if I’m being perfectly honest… a little (sometimes a lot of) sadness too. This is my middle child, my second son, so this is not my first time watching one of my children graduate from high school. And somehow, that makes the passage of time feel even more real. You would think the second time around makes it easier…but in many ways, you become even more aware of how quickly childhood gives way to adulthood. I mean one moment you are packing lunches, fussing about missing assignments and messy rooms, and helping with homework. Then suddenly, you are watching them prepare to step into adulthood with their own voice, their own dreams, and their own path ahead. I am so incredibly proud of the young man my son has become — thoughtful, resilient, kind, curious, and grounded in the values that matter most. This past weekend was about his accomplishment but it was also about possibility, About one chapter closing and another beginning as he heads off to college — a journey that will bring new lessons, new growth, and new opportunities just waiting to be discovered. To Nathaniel: never lose sight of who you are. Carry your integrity with you. Treat people well. Stay open to learning. And know that no matter how big this world gets, there will always be a place where you are loved, supported, and cheered on unconditionally. What a gift it is to be your mother. 🎓❤️

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/696261565_18105000680312458_79262261711059663_n.jpg|To all of the amazing mothers across Georgia — Happy Mother’s Day! 💐 Today, we celebrate the strength, love, sacrifice, and wisdom that great mothers bring to our families, communities, and future generations every single day. Your impact is truly immeasurable, and Georgia is stronger because of you. Thank you for all that you do and all that you are. Wishing you a beautiful day filled with the love you so deeply deserve. ❤️ Tag a Mother! #HappyMothersDay #GeorgiaMoms #MothersDay #CelebrateMothers #GeorgiaFamilies

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/696266575_18105584096312458_4169641146848533924_n.jpg|I don’t operate from excuses, I operate from execution. I’ve never been the one to say “we don’t have the votes” and stop there. I do the work anyway — building relationships, finding common ground, and pushing ideas forward until they become results. That’s what leadership requires. So imagine what I can do with even more trust, more opportunity, and a stronger mandate to lead. Imagine what’s possible when I’m fully empowered to govern and deliver for the people I serve. I’m ready to do the work — not someday, but now. #sonya4ga #SonyaSays

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/702982607_18105969650312458_7704255354311971770_n.jpg|Tomorrow is Election Day, and your voice matters more than ever. As your State Senator, I want to encourage every eligible voter to make a plan, know your polling location, and understand your rights before heading to the polls. In Georgia - a place with so much to offer and a history of setting powerful examples for the rest of the country - we can and must do better. I am committed to finding real solutions to the problems we face. Thank you for trusting me to be your voice under the Gold Dome! Voters can use several forms of acceptable ID, including a Georgia driver’s license, state ID card, U.S. passport, military ID, tribal ID, or voter identification card. Don’t let confusion or misinformation stop you from participating in our democracy! Voting is more than a right — it’s a responsibility and an opportunity to shape the future of our communities, our families, and the next generation. Educate yourself, encourage someone else to vote, and make your voice heard tomorrow. 🗳️🇺🇸 #Vote #GeorgiaVotes #UseYourVoice #Democracy #Sonya4GA

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/703633314_18106194053312458_4116125814918551635_n.jpg|Thank you, District 39. The work continues— I am focused, committed, and rooted in the needs of our community!!! ✔️🩵 #SonyaSays #Sonya4Ga #ThankYou #Community #District39

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/708088294_18107057414312458_5967760545517148167_n.jpg|May has been nothing short of eventful — filled with conversations, community, advocacy, and action. But through every meeting, event, and challenge, one thing remains the same: my dedication to serving my state. Being your senator is a responsibility I never take lightly, and I’m committed to continuing the work that moves our communities forward every single day. Thank you for trusting me to lead, listen, and fight for what matters most. #SonyaSays

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/714871101_18108118709312458_5629928560102886075_n.heic|The last couple of days have given me a chance to reflect on something I’ve come to appreciate throughout my time in public service: Georgia’s success is built through partnership. I’m here at the Georgia Chamber’s Spring Meeting, where I’m honored to have been recognized as Senate Legislator of the Year. The issues facing Georgia families and the issues facing Georgia businesses are often more connected than we think. A strong workforce, affordable housing, access to healthcare, reliable infrastructure, and economic opportunity matter to both. We may not always agree on every policy solution, but we do share a common interest in making and keeping Georgia strong. I’m grateful for the opportunity to work alongside business leaders, community partners, and colleagues across the state to help create a Georgia where both people and businesses can thrive. Economic growth and quality of life are not competing priorities—they rise and fall together.

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/733271341_18111611996312458_6878008467114591255_n.jpg|The measure of leadership isn’t what we build for ourselves — it’s what we leave behind for others. The institutions we lead belong to the American people, and our responsibility is to strengthen them and leave them better than we found them. As we celebrate America’s 250th anniversary, that reminder has never felt more urgent. From the Kennedy Center to our classrooms to the halls of Congress — we are in a moment that will test whether our leaders remember they are stewards, not owners. I wrote more about this for Common Dreams this week. Link in bio. 🔗 Today, let’s celebrate how far we’ve come, honor those who’ve expanded freedom and opportunity, and commit ourselves to doing the same. Happy Independence Day. Here’s to continuing the work of building a more perfect union. Better days are ahead. #July4th #Independence250 #BetterDaysAhead #SonyaHalpern #gapol

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/779002152_18117113351312458_4440478631369301382_n.jpg|Last Tuesday, I toured Fulton County’s Emergency Management facility with representatives, lobbyists, and leaders working to keep Fulton strong. 💙 As Chair of the Fulton County Senate Delegation, I helped organize this visit to see firsthand how our Emergency Management and Service teams like 911 work and how they prepare for unexpected disasters like earthquakes and infrastructure failures for example. Thank you to the Fulton Emergency Service and Emergency Management teams for protecting us behind the scenes. I’ll keep showing up to support the work that keeps us safe. #FultonStrong #CommunityFocused#Thankful #Sonya4Ga

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/780520381_18117495725312458_5924328307879087969_n.jpg|You're Invited! Join us next Thursday, August 26th, at 6:00-7:30 p.m. for the 2026 Southwestern Athletic Conference (SWAC) Commissioners Reception at the Commerce Club. This unique event will open the door for the community to connect with SWAC leaders across eleven colleges and various corporations. I encourage everyone to attend this night of culture, celebration, and unforgettable SWAC energy! I hope to see you all there.

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/782511189_18117604865312458_1646928453014674285_n.jpg|Atlanta's small businesses and artists are the backbone of this city's economy. Last week I got to stand with @byronamos and @councilmanlewis at the 13th Annual Biz Savvy Artist Competition to celebrate the work and impact of our local entrepreneurs and creatives. As an entrepreneur who's also worked alongside art organizations before I ran for office, this work matters to me. Thank you @bizsavvyartist for building community and creating real opportunity for Atlanta businesses.

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/786492803_18118004366312458_4131569903522336952_n.jpg|Happy 84th birthday to my beautiful mom! There are some people whose influence on your life is so deep, it’s hard to put into words. My mom is one of those people for me. She has taught me so much about strength, grace, family, faith, and showing up for the people you love. And the older I get, the more I understand just how much of who I am began with what I saw in her. Mom, I’m so grateful for your love, your example, and for the blessing of celebrating another trip around the sun with you. 84 looks pretty fabulous on you. I ❤️ you!

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/795068462_18119363774312458_263542338700642106_n.jpg|@atlutd has officially launched its 25th soccer field! The GA 100 project, apart of the Atlanta United Community Fund , is an initiative committed to making soccer more accessible to the communities who need it most by building 100 new soccer pitches across Georgia. This one is especially meaningful to me. As the State Senator representing this community and a proud board member of the YMCA of Metro Atlanta, I couldn’t think of a better home for this new pitch than the Andrew & Walter Young Family YMCA. The Y has spent generations creating places where young people can learn, play, grow, and discover what they’re capable of. And now, this field gives them one more place to do exactly that. The measure of what we build isn’t just what it means today. It’s what it makes possible for the next generation. Thank you to the Atlanta United community and everyone who helped make this happen. I can’t wait to see the soccer stars — and the leaders — who get their start right here. ⚽

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/815866632_18121228088312458_5546285040295885050_n.jpg|Georgia Voter Registration Made Easy: What You Need To Know and How To Vote Safely! This guide covers Georgia’s voter registration process, different ways to register, checking your registration status, helping others through the process, and protecting your personal information from unverified sources. Save this guide, share it with your family and friends, and pass it along to your neighbors! Help keep our community informed, and ensure that we are prepared to vote in November. 🗳️ #Sonya4GA #VoterEngagement #StayInformed

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/838219126_18123406094312458_3168602444421833367_n.jpg|November 3rd’s Midterm elections are fastly approaching. That means we’re in the final stretch of voter registration. Today is the last day to register for your voice to be heard in Georgia’s Midterm Elections! Not registered yet? Theres still time, Verify your registration today by visiting https://mvp.sos.ga.gov/s/. #VoterRegistration #GeorgiaVotes #MidtermElections #YourVoteMatters

alt://scontent-den2-1.cdninstagram.com/v/t51.82787-15/838715048_18123539342312458_2783950269080230588_n.jpg|Atlanta is moving forward, and @Glydways is proud to be part of the conversation about the future of public transportation in our city! 🚝 Last week, Atlanta’s Community Improvement Districts hosted an Automatic Transit Network demonstration, offering community leaders and partners an inside look at what’s possible. As @andreforatlanta often says, “Atlanta is a group project.” This gathering was a great example of that spirit in action, bringing people together, sharing ideas, and working collectively to move our community forward. The new track will span half a mile around the Georgia International Convention Center, with three convenient stations designed to help connect people to where they need to go. The future of transportation is being shaped together, and we’re excited to be part of Atlanta’s journey. 🍑

title.after: WOODSON BRADLEY FAILED TO VOTE FOR IRYNA’S LAW, AND NOW SHE’S LYING ABOUT IT

added: top of page ABOUT PLATFORM VOLUNTEER PRESS RELEASES EVENTS DONATE All Posts Search WOODSON BRADLEY FAILED TO VOTE FOR IRYNA’S LAW, AND NOW SHE’S LYING ABOUT IT #ago 4 min read CHARLOTTE, N.C. – Stacie McGinn, Republican nominee for Senate District 42, responds to her opponent Woodson Bradley’s lies to the Charlotte Observer as to why she missed the final vote on Iryna’s Law.
In the article, Senator Bradley claims, “I was ready to vote for the bill the morning it came on to the floor at 10 a.m.
I had an excused absence to leave at 4 p.m. to attend Iryna’s Vigil, but voting was postponed and I was unable to stay any longer.
If I had had the opportunity to vote for Iryna’s Law, I would have done so.

I was elected to make judgments, not blindly follow party positions.” Bradley shared this same false narrative with the local lodge of the Fraternal Order of Police when she sought (and ultimately received) their endorsement.

She told the FOP: "I left at 4pm to get back to Charlotte and participated in the somber evening memorial event." Woodson Bradley is lying as to her whereabouts during the final vote on Iryna’s Law First, at 10 a.m., the day of the vote, the bill was still making its way through the Judiciary and Rules committees, according to Senate records .
The bill was never expected to come to the floor until the afternoon, and the vote on the first amendment did not occur until 4:36pm.

Second, the only “vigil” we are aware of that was being held that evening in Charlotte was a vigil to mark the one-month anniversary of Iryna’s death sponsored by the Mecklenburg County Republican Party at 8pm .
Bradley did not attend that vigil.

The Republican Party leadership did not see her, and she does not appear on any televised coverage of the event. ﻿﻿ Third, it would have been a physical impossibility for Bradley to have made it back to Charlotte in time for the vigil, because she was voting on amendments up until 6:13pm .
The day after the vote, Bradley took to social media to complain about the Berger substitute amendment.

See Bradley’s Facebook Post on September 23rd : “Iryna’s Law Hi-Jacked to bring back hanging and fire squad to NC.” Bradley is lying when she says she would have voted for Iryna’s Law The Senate Democratic Caucus sent Governor Stein a letter urging him to veto Iryna’s Law.

The Assembly – a reputable news source that covers political events in Raleigh – published an early version of this letter (presumably leaked by a member of the Senate Democratic Caucus) that includes a line for Bradley’s signature .
The final letter sent to Governor Stein was sent with a cover letter from Sen.
Sydney Batch, NC Senate Democratic Leader.

Senator Batch notes the letter is being sent “On behalf of the North Carolina Senate Democratic Caucus…” She continues, “…our Caucus stands in opposition to this bill…because we believe the bill as passed is deeply flawed, constitutionally questionable and unlikely to make our communities safer.” While Woodson Bradley’s name does not appear on the final veto request, she was, and is, a member of the Senate Democratic Caucus.

Even taking as true her claims she “broke from her Caucus” on sending the letter to Governor Stein, her Facebook rant against the Berger amendment the day after the vote, noted above, and the fact she walked out before the final vote was taken – not to attend a vigil, but in defiance – make it clear Bradley opposed Iryna’s Law, and had no intention of voting for it.
Not a single Democratic Senator voted in favor of Iryna’s Law.
Are we really expected to believe Woodson Bradley was prepared to be the ONLY Democratic Senator to stand up and support it?
Far from showing her leadership, she took the coward’s way out: taking an excused absence; using a made-up excuse and walking out before the final vote was taken.
Bradley’s pattern of attempting to rewrite history to explain away decisions she later regrets is beneath the dignity of a sitting state Senator.
This latest fabrication regarding her failure to vote for Iryna’s law is not the first time Bradley has tried to rewrite history.

Her continuously changing explanations regarding her involvement in a notorious pyramid scheme, for example, and her failure to simply take responsibility for this mistake, recently described by two journalists [ Andrew Dunn , WFAE ], shows a decided lack of character.
The lies she is now telling to explain her ill-advised decision to walk-out on the final vote on Iryna’s Law compounds questions being raised regarding this freshman Senator’s honesty and integrity.

According to Stacie McGinn, Republican Nominee for NC Senate District 42, “Recent chaos and alleged dishonesty within our CMS school board has made it abundantly clear to voters in Mecklenburg County that we must elect representatives with proven character, honesty and integrity.
Senator Woodson Bradley has been lying to the public about her role as a ringleader in a major pyramid scheme that scammed nearly 20,000 North Carolinians out of their hard-earned savings.
Now she’s lying about her failure to vote on the most consequential anti-crime legislation in decades.

This pattern of dishonesty makes her unfit to serve in the North Carolina Senate.” Recent Posts See All NEW AD: Stacie McGinn Calls Out Woodson Bradley's Rewriting of History Around Her Involvement in an Illegal Pyramid Scheme Stacie McGinn Slams Woodson Bradley for Missing Final Vote on “Iryna’s Law” in Second Digital Ad Stacie McGinn Highlights Education in her First Digital Ad ABOUT PLATFORM VOLUNTEER PRESS RELEASES EVENTS PRIVACY POLICY TERMS & CONDITIONS DONATE Stay Connected.

added: Skip to content Home About Events Updates Facebook Instagram Donate Johnny Austin Thompson for Florida House Privacy Policy Effective date and last updated: October 8, 2026 Johnny Austin Thompson for Florida House (the “Campaign,” “we,” “us,” or “our”) respects your privacy.

This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, disclose, and protect personal information through standwithjohnny.com, our campaign forms, our email and text messaging programs, and related campaign activities that refer to this policy.
Our text messaging program is voluntary.
We do not sell personal information or disclose it to other organizations for their own marketing, fundraising, or promotional use.
Additional protections for mobile information and text messaging consent appear in Section 4.

1 Information we collect Information you provide: We collect information you choose to give us when you sign up for updates, volunteer, register for an event, complete a survey or petition, make a contribution, or communicate with us.
Depending on your interaction, this may include your name, email address, mailing address, telephone number, interests, volunteer availability, responses, and the content of your communications.

Contribution information: If you contribute, we may receive your contact information, contribution amount and date, transaction status, occupation, employer, and other information needed to process the contribution and comply with campaign finance requirements.
Online contributions linked from our website are processed through ActBlue.
Payment information you enter on a payment provider’s website is handled under that provider’s privacy policy.

Technical information: Our website and service providers may collect your IP address, browser and device information, referring pages, pages visited, access times, approximate location derived from your IP address, and information about your interaction with our website, emails, and message links.
Cookies and similar technologies may be used as described in Section 5.

Messaging records: When you enroll in or interact with our text program, we collect your mobile number, consent and preference records, messages you send us, and related information such as timestamps, delivery status, and opt-out requests.
Consent records may include the signup source and the disclosure presented when you enrolled.
Information from other sources: We may receive information from public records, including voter records, and from campaign service providers or people acting on our behalf.
We may combine that information with information you provide.
A number’s presence in a voter file, donor record, or another organization’s list does not establish consent to our recurring text program.

2 How we use information We use personal information to operate and improve the website; respond to questions; organize volunteers and events; process and record contributions; understand issues and activities that interest supporters; conduct lawful campaign outreach; maintain communication preferences; protect against fraud and misuse; and meet legal, accounting, and campaign finance obligations.
Where you have provided the required consent, we use your mobile number to send recurring campaign text messages about campaign news, events, volunteering, fundraising, and voting reminders.
We also use messaging records to deliver messages, respond to requests, document consent, and honor opt-outs.
We do not treat use of our website or acceptance of this Privacy Policy as consent to receive text messages.
3 When we disclose information Campaign personnel and service providers: We allow authorized campaign staff and volunteers to access information needed for their work.
We also use providers that assist with website hosting, data storage, communications, payment processing, campaign administration, analytics, security, and professional advice.
We limit access to the information needed for those functions.
Providers acting on our behalf must protect that information and may not use it for their own independent marketing or fundraising.
Required reporting and legal process: We disclose information when required by campaign finance law, a valid legal demand, or other applicable law.
Contribution reports may include a contributor’s name, address, occupation when required, and contribution amount and date.
Information filed with election authorities may become public.
We may also disclose information as reasonably necessary to investigate fraud, protect rights or safety, or respond to legal claims, subject to the additional restrictions in Section 4.
At your direction: We may disclose information when you specifically ask us to do so, such as when you authorize publication of a testimonial.
We do not interpret such a request as permission to transfer your text messaging consent.
We do not sell or rent personal information.

We do not provide supporter information to other candidates, campaigns, political parties, committees, advocacy organizations, or commercial partners for their own marketing, fundraising, or promotional use.
Section 4 controls whenever another provision could otherwise be read to permit disclosure of mobile information or text messaging consent.

4 Mobile information and text messaging privacy We will not sell, rent, trade, or disclose your mobile number, mobile messaging information, or SMS opt-in and consent records to third parties or affiliates for marketing or promotional purposes.
This restriction includes other political campaigns, candidates, parties, committees, and organizations, as well as data brokers and lead generators.
Text messaging consent is specific to this Campaign and is not transferable.
Limited processing for our program is permitted.

We may provide the information necessary to operate our text program to messaging vendors, including Twilio, and to carriers and other providers that transmit messages, maintain consent and suppression records, provide program support, or perform messaging compliance functions.
These disclosures do not authorize a recipient to market to you independently or to use your consent for another sender.
We may also disclose mobile information or consent records if legally required.
These limited operational and legally required disclosures do not permit sale of SMS lists or disclosure for another organization’s marketing, fundraising, or promotional use.
The general disclosure provisions in Section 3 do not expand these exceptions.
Messages are recurring, and message frequency varies based on campaign activity and your interactions.
Message and data rates may apply.
You can unsubscribe by replying STOP to a campaign text.
We honor other clear requests to stop as well.
After you opt out, you may receive one message confirming the opt-out; we will not resume program texts unless you provide new consent.
For help, reply HELP or call (850) 910-2629.
Consent to receive texts is not required to make a contribution or purchase, volunteer, attend an event, or otherwise support the Campaign.
We do not purchase, rent, or accept transferred SMS consent.
We keep consent and opt-out records to administer the program, respect your choices, and meet applicable recordkeeping obligations.
Additional program details appear in our SMS Terms and Conditions .
5 Cookies and similar technologies 6 Your choices and requests Text messages: Reply STOP to a campaign text to unsubscribe.
You may also contact us at (850) 910-2629 to request that we stop campaign texts.
You do not have to use particular wording when your request clearly communicates that you want the texts to stop.
Email and other outreach: Use the unsubscribe link in a campaign email or contact us to request a change in your communication preferences.
Tell us which channels you want to stop so we can apply your request accurately.
A request to stop texts will not require you to unsubscribe from unrelated communication channels.
Access, correction, and deletion: You may contact us to request access to, correction of, or deletion of personal information we maintain about you.
We may take reasonable steps to verify your identity before responding.
We will honor rights that apply under applicable law.
We may retain information needed for legal reporting, recordkeeping, fraud prevention, legal claims, and honoring an opt-out.
We cannot remove information from government records or third-party systems we do not control.
7 Retention We keep personal information for as long as reasonably needed for the purposes described in this policy, including applicable legal and campaign finance requirements.
The retention period depends on the information, its use, and legal obligations.
We retain consent evidence and limited suppression information as needed to demonstrate compliance and avoid contacting someone who has opted out.
When information is no longer needed, we delete it or make it no longer identifiable, subject to lawful retention and routine backup processes.
8 Security We use reasonable administrative, technical, and organizational safeguards to protect personal information against unauthorized access, use, alteration, and disclosure.
Access is limited according to campaign responsibilities and service needs.
No website, storage system, or transmission method is completely secure.
Please do not send payment card details, Social Security numbers, or other sensitive information through ordinary email or text messages.
9 Children Our website is intended for a general audience and is not directed to children under 13.
We do not knowingly collect personal information online from children under 13.
If you believe a child under 13 has provided personal information to us, contact us so we can investigate and take appropriate action.
Our recurring text messaging program is limited to people who are at least 18 years old.
10 Other websites and services Our website may link to ActBlue, social media platforms, and other third-party websites or services.
This policy governs information handled by the Campaign.
A third party’s own privacy policy governs information it collects directly.
Please review that policy before providing information on its service.
Choosing to interact with another organization does not transfer your consent to receive texts from the Campaign.
11 Changes to this policy We may update this policy to reflect changes in our practices or legal obligations.
We will post the revised policy with an updated date and provide any additional notice required by law.
A policy update does not by itself give us new text messaging consent, authorize a new sender, or override a prior opt-out.
We will obtain additional consent when required before making a change that requires it.

added: Skip to content Home About Events Updates Facebook Instagram Donate Johnny Austin Thompson for Florida House SMS Terms and Conditions Effective date and last updated: October 8, 2026 These SMS Terms and Conditions govern the voluntary recurring text messaging program offered by Johnny Austin Thompson for Florida House (the “Campaign,” “we,” “us,” or “our”).
Please review these terms before enrolling.

1 Program description Subscribers may receive SMS and MMS messages about Johnny Austin Thompson’s campaign for Florida House District 2, including campaign updates, event announcements, volunteer opportunities, fundraising requests, and voting reminders.
We may use automated technology to send messages.
Messages may include links to campaign resources or contribution pages.
2 Enrollment and consent You enroll by entering your mobile number in a campaign signup form and submitting the form after reviewing the text messaging disclosure presented with it.
By doing so, you authorize the Campaign to send the recurring texts described in that disclosure to the number you provide.
You must be at least 18 and the subscriber or authorized user of that number.
Text messaging consent is optional and is not a condition of any purchase, contribution, volunteer activity, event attendance, or other campaign participation.
Providing a telephone number for another purpose, making a contribution, or accepting general website terms does not enroll you in recurring campaign texts.
Your consent applies only to this Campaign and the subjects disclosed when you enroll.
3 Frequency and charges Message frequency varies with campaign activity and your interactions.
Message and data rates may apply to messages you receive and send, according to your wireless plan.
The Campaign does not charge a separate subscription fee for the text program.
Contact your wireless provider with questions about your plan or charges.
4 How to stop messages Reply STOP to a campaign text at any time to unsubscribe.
We also honor other clear requests to stop, including requests made by calling (850) 910-2629.
After you opt out, you may receive one confirmation text.
We will stop further program messages unless you provide new consent to re-enroll.
You can re-enroll through the campaign’s text signup form.
If your number changes or you are no longer authorized to use it, please unsubscribe or contact us so we can update our records.
5 Help and support Reply HELP to a campaign text for assistance, or call (850) 910-2629.
The HELP function provides program support information; it does not withdraw your consent.
Use STOP or make another clear opt-out request to unsubscribe.
6 Delivery and carrier availability The program is available to compatible U.S. mobile numbers on participating wireless networks.
Availability and delivery depend on your device, carrier, and network conditions.
Delivery is not guaranteed.
Wireless carriers are not liable for delayed or undelivered messages.
If you need official information about voting deadlines, eligibility, or polling locations, consult the appropriate election authority.
7 Privacy We use mobile numbers and messaging records to administer this program, deliver texts, assist subscribers, document consent, and honor opt-outs.
We do not sell or rent SMS subscriber data or provide it to affiliates or third parties for their marketing, fundraising, or promotional use.
Messaging providers may process the information needed to operate our program, and legally required disclosures may occur, as explained in our Privacy Policy .
8 Program changes We may change or end the program and may update these terms.
Updated terms will be posted with a revised date, and we will give additional notice when required.
Changes will not enroll you in a different sender’s program, revive a withdrawn consent, or expand your consent to new message subjects without any additional consent that is required.

Back To Top Taxation Being smarter about taxes is not just saying we’ll cut taxes, it is about an honest and transparent conversation about where our tax dollars will be spent.

It is also widely accepted that some form of taxation must exist to pay for goods and services that are enjoyed by the public at large and which contribute to their safety and security in their homes and communities.

Our country’s founding and continued existence is filled with examples of citizens largely fighting against excessive taxation either on a personal or community level or resentment against segments of the populace that are not paying their share of taxes .
Ohio's example is clear; tax cuts initiated by Republicans regularly over the years to the wealthy has Ohio using more and more Fed dollars to balance its books than ever before.
During the same time, Republican administrations have siphoned away local tax revenue forcing local governments to raise more levies to cover costs.

Ohio needs to have a truly equitable form of taxation that ensures everyone is paying their share who are capable and obligated to do so, and to reduce the state's reliance on federal funds to balance its books.

New Mexico RECA Resource Guide $100,000 one-time payment for individuals affected by radiation exposure.
Deadline to file: Dec 31, 2027 Congresswoman Leger Fernandez introduced the RECA Amendments Act in 2021.
She led the U.S.

House of Representatives effort to expand RECA to cover New Mexico downwinders and post '71 uranium miners alongside Senator Ben Ray Lujan, the New Mexico congressional delegation, and New Mexico advocates.
What is RECA?
The RECA Program provides a one-time payment of $100,000 to individuals affected by radiation exposure from the Trinity and other nuclear tests.
RECA compensation is now available to New Mexico downwinders and post '71 uranium workers.
How to Apply Application Deadline: Dec 31, 2027 All claims must be filed by this date.
Visit justice.gov/civil/reca for the latest information.
Option 1: Apply Online Visit www.justice.gov/civil/reca to access the online application.

Option 2: Apply by Mail Fill out the relevant application form Gather original or certified copies of supporting documents such as: Proof of residence, employment, or onsite participation during a qualifying period Medical records documenting your diagnosis of a compensable disease Identification documentation as described on the claim form Mail everything to the address provided in the application form ​ Important Tips: Keep copies of all submitted materials for your records Include your return address Consider using Certified Mail for tracking Who is Eligible to Apply in New Mexico?
Note: The one-year period does not have to be consecutive; cumulative months across the qualifying periods count.

Downwinders Keep copies of all submitted materials for your records Include your return address Consider using Certified Mail for tracking Presence Requirements: Must have been present in New Mexico for one year between Sep 24, 1944, and Nov 6, 1962 OR For the entirety of Jun 30, 1962 to Jul 31, 1962 Note: The one year period does not have to be consecutive; cumulative months across the qualifying periods count.

Qualifying Diseases: Leukemia (other than chronic lymphocytic leukemia) Multiple myeloma Lymphomas (other than Hodgkin's disease) Primary cancers of the: thyroid, male or female breast, esophagus, stomach, pharynx, small intestine, pancreas, bile ducts, gallbladder, salivary gland, urinary bladder, brain, colon, ovary, liver (except if cirrhosis or Hepatitis B is indicated), or lung 2.

Uranium Workers Employment Requirements: Must have been employed as a uranium miner, uranium miller, core driller, in the transport of uranium or vanadium-uranium ore, or involved in remediation efforts at a uranium mine or mill in New Mexico Must have been employed for at least one year or 40 working level months between Jan 1, 1942 and Dec 1, 1990 Qualifying Diseases: Lung cancer Pulmonary fibrosis / fibrosis of the lung Silicosis Pneumoconiosis Cor pulmonale related to fibrosis of the lung Renal cancer Any other chronic renal disease including nephritis and kidney tubal tissue injury Additional Benefit: Qualified uranium workers may also qualify for DOE's Energy Employees Occupational Illness Compensation Program Act (EEOICPA), which provides an additional $50,000 payment and medical benefits.

Onsite Participants Presence Requirements: Must have been present onsite above or within a government installation during the atmospheric detonation of a nuclear device before Jan 1, 1963 including at the Trinity Test Qualifying Diseases: Leukemia (other than chronic lymphocytic leukemia) Multiple myeloma Lymphomas (other than Hodgkin's disease) Primary cancers of the: thyroid, male or female breast, esophagus, stomach, pharynx, small intestine, pancreas, bile ducts, gall bladder, salivary gland, urinary bladder, brain, colon, ovary, liver (except if cirrhosis or Hepatitis B is indicated), or lung 4.
Survivors If an eligible individual dies, their survivor may apply for compensation on their behalf.

Survivors are considered in the following order: Living spouse Children Parents Grandchildren Grandparents Free Resources to Help Apply Important Note: Rather than submitting medical records to prove that you had a qualifying cancer, you may check the box on the application form to authorize DOJ to contact the New Mexico Tumor Registry on your behalf.
The Tumor Registry has records for New Mexicans diagnosed with cancer after 1973.
If you were diagnosed between 1966 and 1973, the Tumor Registry has only partial records.
Remember: There is NO FEE to apply for RECA and there are FREE resources available to help file claims.
University of New Mexico RESEP Program Provides free assistance in filling out applications and conducts free health screenings.

As Governor, I will always value and support community leaders who put people first and work to create real, lasting change.
This campaign has never been about political insiders, big money, or powerful connections.
It has always been about the people of Arizona.
Every mile traveled, every conversation, every event, and every challenge has been fueled by one purpose—to serve you.
I am the definition of a grassroots candidate because this movement belongs to everyday Arizonans.
Thank you for believing in a different path forward.
Together, we are proving that integrity, hard work, and the voices of the people still matter.
Arizona, thank you for standing with me.
Let’s keep building this movement—together.
The next 12 weeks will be filled with travel across our great state, conversations with Arizonans, listening, learning, and staying focused on what matters most—you, Arizona.
I am excited for the road ahead and grateful for the opportunity to experience this campaign alongside the people I am asking to serve.
I want to hear your stories, understand the challenges facing your communities, and talk about real solutions for Arizona’s future.
Thank you, Arizona, for giving me this incredible opportunity.
I am ready for the miles, the conversations, the work, and the full experience of this journey.
Let’s make these next 12 weeks count.

Videos Arizona Community - Glendale Daily Hustle - Glendale community Scottsdale Community Scottsdale Coffee & Smiles Phoenix Community Scottsdale AZ Voters Phoenix Car Dealership Fun Phoenix Shoutout Honda Phoenix - Bringing Real People Back Phoenix - Small Business Phoenix - Non Profit Phoenix - AZ Is Worth Change THIS I S WHAT GRASSROOTS LOOKS LIKE I’m not going to lie—I am incredibly excited and feeling so blessed as I drive across Arizona putting up our campaign signs.
Angela is out there doing the same thing.
This is grassroots.
Grassroots is running with very little funding but an incredible amount of passion.
It’s loading signs into your own vehicle, driving across Arizona, meeting people face-to-face, putting in the miles, and doing the work yourself because you believe Arizona deserves another choice.
We don’t have a massive political machine behind us.
We don’t have special interests carrying this campaign.
We have grit, determination, and people who believe ordinary Arizonans should have a voice.
Being a true grassroots candidate isn’t easy—and that’s exactly why this matters.
This is what democracy is supposed to look like: normal, everyday people having the courage to step forward, run for office, and fight to represent their communities.
We already proved it can be done by winning an election.
Now we’re taking that fight across Arizona.
Not Left.
Not Right.
Only Forward.

Videos Real Grassroots Candidate PodCast: Move the Needle - Chandler Chandler Coffee & Talk Phoenix in Arizona I Cannot Be Bought AZ Leaders Need to NOT be Bought Phoenix - Where You Are Glendale - Community & Spirit Real Grassroots in Flagstaff 🇺🇸 Today I’m in Flagstaff spending the day where I believe a Governor belongs—with the community and the people.

And apparently, I decided today was the day to wear my cute shoes. 😂 Usually I’m smart enough to wear the comfy ones, but cute shoes aren’t stopping me from putting in a 10-hour day talking with Arizonans, listening to their concerns, and hearing what they want for the future of our state.
I still have hours to go, and I’m excited to be here!
Flagstaff is beautiful today, the people have been wonderful, and this is exactly what our campaign is about.
Arizona, this is REAL grassroots.
It’s not about the shoes.
It’s about showing up for PEOPLE.
Not Left.
Not Right.
Only Forward.
Videos Flagstaff - Grassroots Candidate Community in Flagstaff RAIN OR SHINE, I’M SHOWING UP — TERI ANN HOURIHAN FOR AZ GOVERNOR 🇺🇸🌵 I’m in Prescott campaigning today, and it is absolutely pouring.
Right now, I’m sitting on the cement under the small overhang of a building, waiting for the rain to let up so I can get back out there and keep going.
This is what commitment looks like to me.
I’m not running for power, glory, a political career, or special interests.
I’m out here every day working my ass off because I genuinely want a better tomorrow for ALL of us.
I see the problems Arizona families are facing.
I see what is happening in our communities, our healthcare system, our schools, our prisons, our economy, and our government—and I refuse to simply sit back and complain about it.
So, yes, I’ll sit on the cement in the pouring rain and wait.
And when it stops, I’ll get back up and keep campaigning.
Because this isn’t a joke to me.
This is my home.
This is our future.

And I am serious about doing everything I can to make it better. 🇺🇸♥️🌵 Videos Prescott Rain or Shine Community Shines in Prescott Love the people in Prescott Animals in Prescott Teacher Interview in Prescott Campaign like a Butterfly Snake Charlie in Prescott Prescott Moments Prescott Animals & Families I Love Kingman! 🇺🇸🌵 I literally love Kingman!
I haven’t been here in several years, and I was genuinely touched by the strong sense of community, warmth, and kindness I experienced throughout my visit.
Kingman has that special small-town community feel while still offering so much to the people who live here.
The people are welcoming, the local businesses are proud of their community, and you can feel the connections people have with one another.
As Governor, I want Arizona’s rural and smaller communities to know they will never be forgotten or treated as an afterthought.
Every community matters, and I want to make sure people across our state have a Governor who shows up, listens, and understands what their communities need to thrive.
Thank you to every person, community member, and local business that welcomed me.
I’m already excited to come back — see you again in about four weeks, Kingman!

Videos Community in Kingman Angel Manor & Kingman Kingman Friendships and Community Kingman Excitement & Time Last day in Kingman Small Business in Kingman Kingman - Listening to the People Wickenburg Experience Kingman I am Here Fire Dpt in Kingman Mohave County Animal Shelter Kittens & Friendship Kingman Cowboys Kingman Story of Hope On the Road for Arizona: Pinal County, Kearny & Phoenix Today, I’m headed to Pinal County for a ribbon-cutting event celebrating employment and economic opportunity, followed by stops throughout the county—including Kearny, Arizona.
Kearny is facing a serious water crisis, and I want every resident to know: I see you, I hear you, and I support you.
As Governor, protecting Arizona’s water and the safety of our communities will be a priority.
I will work to ensure communities like Kearny have access to safe, reliable water and that their concerns are not ignored.
I’ll finish the day around 6 PM near 27th Avenue and Indian School Road, where I’ve been invited to speak and spend time with a local group.
Follow along as I continue traveling across our state and campaigning to help save Arizona.
For me, this truly is a God story.
Every day, I’m on a mission to serve, listen, and fight to make Arizona the best it can be for every person who calls our state home.

Videos Arizona Pinal County Campaign Pinal on the Road Superior Arizona Dream Wickenburg Arizona I Love Sedona! 🇺🇸🌵 Heading to Sedona & Connecting with Arizona I’m headed out to Sedona today, and I’m excited to spend time in the community, meet more Arizonans, and hear your stories.
Running for Governor means showing up.
I’m going to be everywhere I can across Arizona—listening, connecting, learning about what matters in each community, and making sure people know their voices matter.
This campaign is about the people of Arizona.
I look forward to meeting you where you are and earning the opportunity to serve you as your next Governor.
Thank you for welcoming me into your communities.
Sedona, I’m excited to see you today!

They are one of the most important opportunities voters have to hear directly from the people asking to earn their vote.
Arizonans deserve candidates who are willing to answer tough questions, explain their positions, and engage in open, honest discussion.
I showed up for Arizona.
My opponent did not for the Primary election.
Now in the General Election Katie Hobbs is choosing to decline, her Lieutenant Governor Giles also declining while myself and Biggs will debate 10/06/2026 at 6pm.
And if the Green candidate Risa Lombardo is not kicked out of there race before then due to alleged fraud in the clean elections then she will too.
When candidates refuse to debate, voters lose the opportunity to hear where they stand on the issues that affect their daily lives.
Public service requires accountability, and debates are one of the best ways to demonstrate it.
I am incredibly grateful for the opportunity to run for Governor of Arizona.
Every day, I am thankful for the chance to meet people across our state, listen to their concerns, and share my vision for a better Arizona.
It still feels surreal that I have this opportunity.

If I earn the privilege of serving as your Governor, I will work every day to make meaningful changes that strengthen our state, protect our communities, and ensure Arizona's government serves all of its people.
Arizona deserves leaders who show up.
Stop Blending In.
Think Independent.
Vote Independent.
Nearly one-third of Arizona’s registered voters are Independent or unaffiliated.
But being independent is bigger than what is written next to your name on your voter registration.
You can be a registered Republican or Democrat and still think independently.
You can step outside party expectations, reject the pressure to automatically vote for your party’s candidate, and choose the person you believe will best serve Arizona.
I challenge Arizona voters to stop blending into the two-party system simply because that is what we have always been told to do.
You do not owe any political party your vote.
Your vote belongs to you.
If you believe Arizona needs something different, then have the courage to vote differently.
Republicans, Democrats, Independents, No Labels voters and unaffiliated voters can come together and choose people over party.
We cannot keep demanding change while automatically returning our votes to the same two-party system.
Independents—and independent-minded voters from every party—have the power to change Arizona politics.
Stop blending in.
Think for yourself.
Vote for the person, not the party.
Rise with me, Arizona.
Let’s lead the nation in change.

Practical Healthcare Solutions for Arizona As both a healthcare provider and business owner, I understand the challenges families face when insurance premiums, deductibles, and out-of-pocket costs continue to rise faster than wages.
I also understand the pressures placed on employers who want to provide quality healthcare benefits for their employees but struggle with escalating costs.
My administration will pursue innovative solutions that increase affordability and expand access to care.

This includes developing employer rebate and incentive programs that help businesses provide healthcare coverage to their workforce, increasing transparency in healthcare pricing, and strengthening oversight to ensure insurance companies are not engaging in unfair pricing practices that drive up costs for consumers.

I will also work to create additional healthcare options for Arizonans by encouraging competition, supporting independent healthcare providers, expanding access to preventive and mental health services, and reducing unnecessary administrative barriers that increase costs without improving patient care.
Healthcare should be affordable, accessible, and focused on patients—not bureaucracy.
Arizona can lead the nation in creating a healthcare system that supports families, employers, providers, and taxpayers while delivering better outcomes for everyone.

As Governor, I will fight for practical, fiscally responsible solutions that lower costs, expand choices, and make healthcare more affordable for every Arizona family Fighting for Affordable Housing and Lower Costs Teri Ann Hourihan for AZ Governor.
Arizona’s cost of living and inflation rates remain above national targets, making it increasingly difficult for families to afford housing, groceries, transportation, and other necessities.
As Governor, I will address affordability by tackling its root causes.
Arizona’s rapid growth, combined with water shortages, drought conditions, and housing supply constraints, has driven costs higher.
By strengthening water security, improving school funding, reforming government agencies, and reducing fraud and waste, we can create long-term affordability for residents.
My administration will work to lower utility costs, reduce inflationary pressures, increase wages, and expand opportunities for Arizonans to live within their means without needing multiple jobs.

I will pursue stronger oversight of fuel pricing, expand rebate programs for teachers, first responders, public servants, farmers market vendors and shoppers, and incentivize water-efficient landscaping.

I will promote affordable housing through adaptive reuse of vacant buildings, strengthen homelessness services, explore universal childcare options, and evaluate data center tax revenues to support affordability initiatives and public education Protecting Arizona Healthcare & Respecting the Voters Arizona voters deserve a Governor who will protect access to healthcare while respecting the laws decided by the people.

Recent concerns raised by Arizona physicians focus on Andy Biggs’ record on Medicaid and abortion, including his support for federal Medicaid reductions and previous efforts to restrict abortion nationally.

As a healthcare professional, healthcare business leader, and expert who has worked directly within Arizona’s healthcare system, I understand where the system is failing patients, providers, and taxpayers.

As Governor, I will take on Arizona’s entire health-plan system, address the problems within AHCCCS, strengthen accountability, eliminate waste and fraud, protect legitimate providers, and make sure healthcare dollars actually reach the people they are intended to serve.
I am pro-life, but I also respect the will of Arizona voters.
Arizona voters established our current abortion law, and I will not seek to repeal or override what the voters decided.
My personal beliefs will not replace the voice of the people I am elected to serve.
Arizona needs a Governor who understands healthcare from the inside and is prepared to fix it—not another career politician talking about it.
I’ll Be on the Debate Stage—Will My Opponents?
Arizona deserves leaders who are willing to stand before the voters, answer tough questions, and defend their records.
The gubernatorial debate is scheduled for October 6, 2026, and I will be there, ready to discuss the issues that matter most to Arizona.
Reports indicate that Governor Katie Hobbs has declined to participate.
I believe that’s disappointing because voters deserve to hear directly from every candidate.
Leadership means showing up, being accountable, and engaging with the public—even when the questions are difficult.
This election is about giving Arizona a new direction, and I look forward to earning your vote by answering your questions and sharing my vision for our state’s future.
Teri Ann Hourihan for Arizona Governor Email Teri@teriann4azgov.org Phone/Text 520-633-1234

Did she in fact hire illegal aliens on her farm, did she falsify tax documents to conceal what she had done?” Watch the Interview Today, Senator Cotton joined The Scott Jennings Show to discuss a bombshell news report from a whistleblower and former senior employee of U.S.

We are supporting Brad Trahan due to his support for: • Affordable Choices • Fewer Unfunded Mandates • Cutting Health Insurance Taxes Brad has demonstrated an understanding of complex health insurance issues and knows that the rapidly increasing cost of health insurance is a big part of what is driving the high cost of living Minnesotans are experiencing.

Minnesotans for Affordable Health Insurance • Bob Stein, Chair Facebook: MNforAffordableHealthInsurance Twitter: @AffordableHealthMN Website: www.affordablehealthinsmn.com Email: mnforaffordablehealthins@gmail.com 24 Sep Thursday, 9:41 AM · 2026 Brad attends the Arc Minnesota- SE Region, The Region 10 Quality Council and SAM (Self-Advocates Minnesota), Forum September 22nd Brad was pleased to attend this forum, sponsored by ARC Minnesota - SE Region, The Region 10 Quality Council, SAM (Self-Advocates Minnesota, this past Tuesday.
This event focuses on issues that impact people with disabilities in our community.

Questions asked, and addressed were questions on how candidate plan to listen to self-advocates when making decisions on waiver services/supports, Transportation, Housing, and Fraud (to make sure the fraud doesn't negatively impact people who need those services) Brad’s answer to the fraud question was, in part: “Don’t allow it to happen to begin with—in the first place!” Internal controls are designed to identify and prevent fraud before it reaches the level we have witnessed.
When state employees raise concerns about potential fraud and those concerns are not adequately addressed, that demands accountability.
Brad put it this way: “When your checking account shows unusual activity, your financial institution doesn’t simply look the other way.

It will freeze the account and contact you to determine whether the activity is legitimate or whether your account has been compromised.” The federal government took similar action when concerns arose that Minnesota funds were not being used for their intended purposes.
Minnesota has a fiduciary responsibility to safeguard taxpayer dollars and ensure public funds are being used as intended.
Brad believes that responsibility must be taken seriously.
Whistleblower warnings should be investigated, internal controls should be followed, and fraud should be stopped before it happens, not after taxpayers have already lost millions of dollars.
As Brad said, “FRAUD-FRAUD-FRAUD!” It should be a top priority to protect Minnesota taxpayers and the essential services that depend on those dollars.
This is not simply a federal issue, as our Democratic friends choose to blame.
Minnesota state agencies had responsibility for administering and overseeing many of these programs, and the state’s own Legislative Auditor has found significant failures in oversight.
In the Feeding Our Future case, for example, the Legislative Auditor concluded that inadequate oversight by the Minnesota Department of Education created opportunities for fraud.
The people of Minnesota deserve accountability from those responsible for overseeing these programs, including Governor Tim Walz and state agency leadership.
Minnesotans also deserve to know where elected officials stand when serious failures occur, and whether they are willing to publicly demand accountability, stronger safeguards, and meaningful reform.
Brad's opponent has mostly been silent.

Brad's opponent has spoken publicly about fraud in a newsletter, and a few media outlets, and supported anti-fraud legislation, but we have not found one, not one public press release specifically condemning the scale of Minnesota's fraud or publicly assigning responsibility for the failures to Governor Walz and his administration, nor her party, for allowing this massive fraud to occur.
Some Democrats have called for Minnesota to look forward and avoid politicizing the issue.

But accountability requires more than simply moving forward, it requires asking how these failures happened, who was responsible for oversight, and what must change to prevent them from happening again.
Minnesotans deserve transparency and accountability from their state government.
As your elected State Representative, Brad Trahan will not hesitate to ask tough questions, hold government accountable, and call out fraud, waste, and abuse when it occurs.
As many people know, Brad is the proud father of Reece, a 26-year-old with severe autism.
For the past 23 years, Brad has been not only a dedicated parent and advocate for his son, but also a passionate self-advocate for countless individuals and families facing similar challenges.

His personal experience has given him a firsthand understanding of the importance of ensuring that people with disabilities have a strong voice, access to needed services, and the opportunity to live with dignity and support.
In 2016, Brad led an initiative for 13 years, 8 months, for Mayo Clinic to provide autism therapy, benefits for their employees' dependents, diagnosed with autism.
Just recently in 2026, Brad led initiative to expand access to specialized oral care, in hospital, under anesthesia for individuals with cognitive and intellectual disabilities.
There were only five (5) hospitals in the State of Minnesota that provided this case for adults with cognitive and intellectual disabilities, and Brad was able to add a sixth, Olmsted Medical Center.
A project he started in January 2025, and completed in June 2026.
Also, recently in late August 2026, Brad identified a gap in Mayo Clinic Insurance Policy, regarding oral anesthesia care and provider coverage.
Brad worked closely with Mayo, Medica (Plan Administrator), and MN DHS.
May0 agreed that there was a gap, and effective October 1st, they were going to add OMC as an approved Provider for this Oral anesthesia care for adults with cognitive and intellectual disabilities.
Brad achieved this task in just one-weeks time!
In 2007, Brad led an initiative to bring Project Lifesaver to Olmsted County/City of Rochester.
This technology helps those most vulnerable, if they wander away.
It helps law enforcement find those missing individuals quickly.
In 2009, Brad led efforts to raise $25,000 to help get Project Lifesaver implemented in other SE Minnesota Counties.
In 2015, Brad led efforts at the state level for “Lifesaver Technology” grant in St.
Paul, secured $80,000 for 2 years, for law enforcement to invest in this technology for the communities they serve.
Brad has not simply talked about his commitment to the disability community, he has demonstrated it through action, advocacy, and meaningful changes in legislation and insurance coverage.

8 Sep Tuesday, 4:32 PM · 2026 Brad does a Ride-Along with the Rochester Police Department September 5th On Saturday, September 5th, Brad had the opportunity to ride along with the Rochester Police Department from 7:00 p.m. until 4:00 a.m.
Brad can’t tell you enough how blessed we are to have the police officers we do in Rochester, under the leadership of Police Chief James Franklin and his Command Staff.
It was an incredible learning experience!
Throughout the evening, Rochester Police Officers were going from call to call to call.
Domestics, fights, weapons calls, people in crisis, and much more.
These men and women simply kept answering the call.
They don't always get the credit they deserve.
One moment during the night really stuck with Brad.
After responding to a serious call and getting things settled down, an RPD Sergeant noticed a 6-year-old little girl and her teddy bear nearby.
The Sergeant took the time to get police stickers for the young girl and her teddy bear.
They weren't the reason the officers were there.
But they noticed her.
And that small act made that little girl's night.
That's Rochester Police.
Friends, we need to stop talking about the seriousness of mental health in our community without coming together around serious, long-term solutions.
What I witnessed Saturday night reinforced that for me.
Our officers are responding to mental-health crises, domestics, fights, weapons calls and other difficult situations, sometimes simultaneously and just blocks apart.
And when you add drugs and alcohol to the equation, these situations can become even more challenging.
We cannot continue to band-aid mental health in our communities.
We need long-term solutions that address the underlying problems and provide law enforcement with the resources and partnerships they need.
Throughout the night, I saw Rochester Police Officers demonstrate professionalism, patience, compassion and courage.
Brad is a member of the Rochester Police Civil Service Commission, and it's important for him to get out from behind the meetings and see firsthand what is happening in our community.
It also gives Brad the opportunity to reconnect with some of the officers the Commission has helped approve for hire.

If elected to serve in the Minnesota House, Brad intends to make this an annual commitment, staying connected with the Rochester Police Department and the Olmsted County Sheriff's Office and listening directly to the men and women who serve our community.
We must make sure law enforcement has the tools, resources and support they need to do their jobs effectively and safely, both for themselves and for the people they serve.
RPD—THANK YOU.
Every one of you is truly policing from the heart.
You demonstrated courage, professionalism and compassion throughout Saturday night's shift.
And a special thank you to SGT JH and the entire RPD team for an incredible night, and, most importantly, for keeping our community safe with everything you encountered.
You’re all amazing.
Brad will always be a staunch advocate for Law Enforcement, Fire, and ALL First Responders.
Thank you for serving Rochester.

27 Aug Thursday, 10:21 AM · 2026 Brad attends Minnesota Transportation Alliance Meeting August 26th From 1:30 p.m. - 4:30 p.m.
Candidates were invited to take part in The Minnesota Transportation Alliance with regards to Transportation in Minnesota and why transportation matters.
Representatives from MNDOT, City, and the County were present as well as representatives with public transit.
I then was happy to join a six other candidates, from area races, for a few Q&A questions on Transportation.
We also toured the Rochester International Airport runway, construction project - IMPRESSIVE!
Transportation needs unified cooperation from Federal, State, County, Township, and City government.
Safety is always a priority.
We need to maintain existing infrastructure, and spend tax dollars wisely.
We also must always listen to the stakeholders using our roadways.
Transportation drives economy dollars with our roads, rail, air, and waterways.
Transportation also involves Public Transportation who transport individuals to medical appointments, and more.
And, we can't forget about the need of our rural transportation needs, especially for those that have disabilities and/or are unable to drive for a variety of reasons.
Everyone is fighting for dollars.
One area I would like to see explored (just one idea) is that current purchases of auto parts goes into the Highway User Tax, Transportation, and the "General Fund".
I don't like to see monies always going into the "General Fund" I'd like to explore the idea to put auto parts purchases ALL into Transportation to help them make up some funding.
Funding is allocated in many different ways, but also depends highly on motor vehicle registration tax (license tabs fees).
We need to explore that more.
I do not support our current license tab fee structure.
You can register a 2024 Tahoe in Wisconsin for $95, and in Minnesota for $905.
I would have liked to see more of our 2023 $18 billion surplus used for matters such as this, and imagine if we cleaned up our budget and tackle fraud!
Transportation is bi-partisan issue, but we just need to work hard to determine funding, and explore other avenues perhaps then just depending extremely high license tab fees that are out of control.
We have to be good stewards of taxpayer dollars, as well as assess what is the return on investment on each project.
But, safety is always going to be the top issue!

And, should be! https://www.postbulletin.com/news/local/minnesota-transportation-alliance-eyes-potential-funding-shortfalls 27 Aug Thursday, 10:09 AM · 2026 Brad attends forum hosted by ARRM August 26th From 12pm - 1pm, Brad took part in a forum put on by ARRM, which is a statewide association representing more than 200 residential waiver service providers for Minnesotans with disabilities.

As a Provider said today, there are options, we just need to work hard and create solutions that works for everyone.

24 Aug Monday, 10:57 AM · 2026 Brad meet with HHS Secretary RFK Jr., FEMA Director Cameron Hamilton, DOJ and Others - Announcement of Project Lifesaver National Autism Alert System August 21st A Family, a Community, and a Commitment to Protect Our Most Vulnerable For Brad, this moment is deeply personal.
Standing alongside his family—Brenden, Reece, Joanie, and Payton, and with HHS Secretary Robert F.
Kennedy Jr. during the announcement of a nationwide Autism Alert system for individuals with autism who go missing was a powerful reminder of why this work matters.
Brad has spent years advocating for programs that help protect individuals with autism and other vulnerable members of our community.
One of those efforts began right here in Rochester and Olmsted County with Project Lifesaver, a program designed to help law enforcement locate individuals who may wander or become missing.
Brad helped bring Project Lifesaver to Rochester and Olmsted County by raising $15,000 to launch the program.
He then continued that effort, raising another $25,000 to help seven additional Minnesota counties implement Project Lifesaver.
In 2015, Brad led an initiative that resulted in an $80,000 Minnesota state grant to help additional law-enforcement agencies establish Project Lifesaver programs.
Brad emphasizes that none of this happened because of one person.
“This has always been about collaboration.
So many people have stepped up and made a difference.

When it comes to protecting our most vulnerable, we have to work together and do everything we can.” Brad is especially proud of the Rochester Police Department and Olmsted County Sheriff's Office Project Lifesaver teams, whose dedication continues to make a difference for families throughout our community.
He also recognizes the continued efforts of Rochester Autism Advocacy, including its work helping families navigate the application process and identify individuals who may benefit from the program.

Brad is grateful as well for the past support of RTAAF, and for the leadership and administrative support provided by Sheriff Borchardt, Sheriff Torgerson, and Police Chief Franklin, whose belief in the program helped make this community effort possible.
For Brad and his family, this isn't simply about policy.
It's about people.
It's about families.
And it's about making sure that when a vulnerable person goes missing, every possible resource is available to help bring them home safely.

The announcement of a nationwide Autism Alert system represents an important step forward, and Brad is proud to have been part of the local effort that helped demonstrate what is possible when families, advocates, law enforcement, government, and communities work together.

5 Aug Wednesday, 11:51 AM · 2026 Brad attends Minnesota Farmfest in Morgan, MN (Redwood County) August 4th The Brad Trahan for Minnesota House District 25A campaign took me to Minnesota Farmfest in Morgan, Minnesota (Redwood County).
It was a 2½-hour drive from Rochester, and it was well worth every mile.
Farming isn't just a way of life, it's a business that depends on countless factors, many of which are completely beyond a farmer's control.
That's why it's so important that our elected leaders understand the challenges our agricultural community faces and are willing to listen.
Make no mistake: when I'm elected to represent Minnesota House District 25A, I will be a strong supporter of Minnesota farmers, farm families, and rural communities.
I don't claim to be an agriculture expert, but I have tremendous respect for the men and women who feed our state, our nation, and the world.
I will put in the time, ask questions, listen, learn, and work hard to ensure their voices are heard at the Capitol.
Spending the day at Farmfest is just one example of that commitment.
I also had the pleasure of sharing lunch with a retired judge from Redwood Falls who spent his career in child support and family law, along with his friend John, a farmer and avid polka dancer.
Thank you, gentlemen, for the great conversation and enjoyable company.
It was a highlight of the day!
