added: About Issues News Get Involved Join a Coalition Store Donate Select Page Privacy Policy Effective Date: January 28, 2022 Van Orden for Congress, which owns and operates the website www.vanordenforcongress.com (the “Site”), takes your privacy seriously.

This privacy policy is intended to inform you about the information that is collected from you when you visit the Site, how this information may be used and disclosed, how you can control the use and disclosure of this information, and how this information is protected.
If you have any questions about this privacy policy, please contact us at info@vanordenforcongress.com.
SCOPE This privacy policy applies only to the Site.
This policy does not apply to information collected through any other website or to the practices of companies that Van Orden for Congress does not control.
Please note that the Site may contain links to other websites.
For example, if you click on an advertisement on the Site and link to another website, then this privacy policy will not apply to any information collected on that website.
We are not responsible for the privacy practices of other websites, and we recommend that you read the privacy policies of each website that you visit.
WHAT INFORMATION THE SITE COLLECTS Information you provide directly to us You are not required to provide information directly to us in order to view the Site.

However, when you use certain Site functions, such as when you register for certain services, access certain content or features, or directly contact the Site, we may ask you to provide information, including: contact information, such as name, email address, postal address, phone number, and mobile number username and password information posted in community discussions and other interactive online features search queries conducted on the Site and correspondence you send to us Information automatically collected when you visit and interact with the Site When you visit and interact with the Site, certain information may be collected automatically, including: your computer’s Internet Protocol (IP) address your browser type and operating system the web pages you were visiting immediately before and after you came to the Site activities within community discussions web pages and advertisements that you view, and links that you click on, within the Site your bandwidth speed and information about the software programs that are installed on your computer aggregated data about email click-through rates and user video viewing standard server log information and information collected through HTML cookies, Flash cookies, web beacons, and similar technologies.
For more information, please see our discussion of cookies and other technologies.

Information we collect from other sources We may access information about you from third-party sources and platforms (such as social networking sites, databases, online marketing firms, and ad targeting firms), including: if you access third-party social networking services (such as Facebook Connect or Twitter) through the Site, your username and connection lists for those services; demographic data, such as age range, gender, and interests; advertisement interaction and viewing data, such as ad click-through rates and information about how many times you viewed a particular ad; and unique identifiers, including mobile device identification numbers, that can identify the physical location of such devices in accordance with applicable law.
Please note that the Site may combine the information that we collect with information we obtain from third-party sources.

HOW WE USE THE INFORMATION THAT WE COLLECT Email Communications We may use the information that we collect to send you e-mail communications, such as editorial updates, information about your account or changes to the Site, and promotional messages about our own or our marketing partners’ products and services.
If you signed up for one of our email newsletters, we also will send you the newsletter that you requested.
Mobile Communications By providing your telephone number and email, you consent to receive calls and text messages via SMS from Van Orden for Congress and Van Orden Victory Fund.
Messages may include requests for donations.
Message & data rates may apply.
Message frequency may vary.
Reply “STOP” to opt-out & “HELP” for help.
User Accounts To provide you with an open, but also civil, discussion forum, we track user involvement in our community discussions.
Request Fulfillment We may use the information that we collect to fulfill your requests for products, services, and information.

For example, we may use your contact information to respond to your customer service requests or to enable you to participate in features on the Site such as surveys, polls, sweepstakes, and message boards.

We may also provide you with information or services that we think will be of interest to you, such as sending you information to keep you informed about various campaigns, candidates, issues, events, resources, promotions, or contests.
Statistical Analysis In order to learn more about how our Site is used, we aggregate and analyze the data that we collect.
We may use this information, for example, to monitor and analyze use of the Site, to increase our Site’s functionality, and to better tailor our content and design to suit our visitors’ needs.

We may also use the information we collect to personalize and improve the Site and our users’ experiences on the Site, such as providing ads, content, or features that match your profiles or interests, and to increase the Site’s functionality and user friendliness.
Enforcement We may use the information that we collect to prevent illegal activities, to enforce the Site’s Terms and Conditions, and to otherwise protect our rights and the rights of our users.
In addition to the uses identified above, we may use the information that we collect for any other purposes disclosed to you at the time we collect the information or pursuant to your consent.
Information sharing It is our policy not to share the information we collect from you through our Site with third parties, except as described in this Policy or as otherwise disclosed on the Site.

For example, we may share information we collect as follows: We may share information we collect with vendors, consultants, and other service providers or volunteers who are engaged by or working with us and who need access to such information to carry out their work with us.
We may share aggregated information or information that does not directly identify you with third parties to help us develop content, services, and advertising that we hope you will find of interest.
We may employ third parties to perform Site-related services, including database management, maintenance services, analytics, marketing, data processing, and email and distribution.
If you choose to engage in public activities on the site, such as posting comments on community message boards, any information you submit can be read, collected, or used by others.
Please exercise caution when deciding to disclose any personal information in public activities or submissions.
We may share information we collect with candidates, organizations, groups, or causes that we believe have similar political viewpoints, principles, or objectives.

We may share information about you in connection with, or during negotiations of, any merger, reorganization, acquisition, asset sale, financing or lending transaction, or in any other situation where personal information may be disclosed or transferred as one of the assets of Van Orden for Congress.
We may use the information we collect to help connect you with other supporters, and to solicit volunteers, donations, and support for candidates, issues, and organizations that we support.

We may share information about you to investigate, prevent, or take action regarding illegal activities, suspected fraud, situations involving potential threats to the physical safety or other rights and interests of any person, violations of the Site’s Terms and Conditions, or as otherwise required by law.

We may share information about you to respond to subpoenas, search warrants, judicial proceedings, court orders, legal process, or other law enforcement measures, to establish or exercise our legal rights, or to defend against legal claims.
We may share information about you to enforce or apply this Policy, our Terms of Use, or our other policies and agreements.
SMS opt-in consent and data will not be shared with third parties.
Mobile information will not be shared with third parties/affiliates for marketing/promotional purposes.
All the above categories exclude text messaging originator opt-in data and consent; this information will not be shared with any third parties.

In addition to the scenarios identified above, we may share information about you for any other purposes disclosed to you at the time we collect the information or pursuant to your consent, including if we notify you on the Site that the information you provide will be shared in a particular manner and you provide such information.
The Mobile user information will not be shared.
Nothing herein restricts the sharing of aggregated or anonymized information, which may be shared with third parties without your consent.

Please note that third parties may independently collect data about you, including your IP address and information about the websites you visit and the links you click, through cookies, clicks on links, or other means when you visit or view ads on the Site.

Third-party services To customize your experience on the Site and to simplify the Site’s registration process, we may provide you with the opportunity to access or interact with third-party services, such as Facebook and Twitter.
When you connect to the Site through these third-party services, we may share information about you with these third-party service providers and they may share data about you with us.
When you allow us to access your data through a third-party service, we may use this data for several purposes, including: Creating relationships automatically within our system.
For example, if you connect to us via a service with a public friend list, like Twitter, we may check to see if any people you follow on Twitter are also Site members.
If we find a match, we will replicate your Twitter relationship with those members, setting them to be fans, followers, or friends on our Site.
Suggesting relationships.

For example, if you connect via a service that has a private contact list (like Google and Yahoo!), we check for people in your contacts who are Site members and suggest that you become a fan of these users.
Populating a list of potential friends to whom you can send emails.

When users share content with their friends using, for example, the forward-to-a-friend feature on the Site, we may use friend lists from third-party services to create a list of contacts to whom you may choose to send the email message.
Populating a list of potential friends to whom you can send service-specific messages.
For example, we may use friend lists from a third-party service to create a list of contacts to whom you may choose to send an invitation to view an interactive slideshow.
To enhance and personalize your experience on the Site.

When you are connected via a third-party service, we may access certain account information, such as your profile picture, what stories are popular in your network, and what your friends are saying about certain articles or blog posts, in order to enhance and personalize your experience on the Site.
In addition, if you connect to a Facebook account, your experience on the Site may be personalized.
For example, you may automatically see what stories are popular in your network, and what your friends are saying about particular stories.

We are not responsible for the actions of any service providers or other third parties, nor are we responsible for any additional information you provide directly to third parties and we encourage you to become familiar with their privacy practices before disclosing information directly to any such parties.
Other Purpose We may use the information we collect for any other purpose for which the information was collected.
We may store and process personal information in the United States and in other countries.
YOUR CHOICES Deactivating your account You can deactivate your account at any time by visiting the preferences page for your profile.
When you deactivate your account, your user profile will be disabled, but your public comments will remain on the site.
The Site has no responsibility to take down, remove, or edit any of your public activities or any submissions that are a result of your public activities.
For more information, please review our Terms and Conditions.
Opt Out You may “opt out” of receiving text messages, email updates and newsletters by following the instructions in those text messages and emails.

Please note that we may still send you other types of emails, such as emails about your use of our Site, or use information as otherwise described in this Policy, even if you opt out of receiving email updates and newsletters.

Changes to information in your account does not affect information provided to others as set forth in this policy, including in connection with petitions or donations or that are shared with like-minded candidates, organizations, groups or causes.

Cookies and other technologies When you use the Sites, some information is also automatically collected, such as your Internet Protocol (IP) address, your operating system, the browser type, the address of a referring web site, and your activity on our Sites.
We treat this information as the other information we collect if we combine it with or link it to any of the identifying information mentioned above.
Otherwise, it is used in the aggregate only.
We may also automatically collect certain information through the use of “cookies” or web beacons.
Cookies are small data files stored on your hard drive at the request of a website.
Among other things, cookies help us improve our Sites and your experience.
We may also use cookies and other technologies to provide you with personalized online display advertising tailored to your interests.
If we link cookies to any personally identifying information, we will treat this information as the other information we collect.
If you wish to block, erase, or be warned of cookies, please refer to your browser manufacturer to learn about these functions.
However, if you choose to remove or reject cookies, this could affect certain features on our Sites.
Web beacons are small, invisible graphic images that may be used on the Sites or in emails relating to the Sites to collect certain information and monitor user activity on the Sites.
We may allow others to serve advertisements on our behalf across the Internet and to provide analytics services.

These entities may use cookies, web beacons and other technologies to collect information about your use of the Services and other websites, including your IP address, web browser, pages viewed, time spent on pages, links clicked and conversion information.

This information may be used by the Site and others to, among other things, analyze and track data, determine the popularity of certain content, deliver advertising and content targeted to your interests on our Services and other websites and better understand your online activity.

For more information about Internet-based ads, or to opt out of having your web browsing information used for behavioral advertising purposes, please visit www.networkadvertising.org/managing/opt_out.asp or www.aboutads.info/choices.

Online petitions When you sign an online petition, you understand that such petition is public information and that we may make the petition, and your name, city, state, any comments, and other information you provided in connection therewith publicly available.
In addition, we may provide such petitions or compilations thereof, including your comments, name, city, and state to national, state or local leaders, or to the press.

Interactive Features You understand that when you use the Site, information you: post in your profile, blogs, forums and other interactive areas of the Site, as well as any information you share with individuals through the Site or share through social network sites, will be available to other users and, in some cases, may be publicly available.
In addition, when you sign up and create an account, certain information regarding actions you take through the Site, may available to other users and, in some cases, may be publicly available.
We recommend you be cautious about giving out personal information to others or sharing personal information in public or private online forums.
We are not responsible for the actions of any third parties with whom you share personal information.

In some cases, there may be privacy setting available regarding the information available to others, and we suggest you take time to familiarize yourself with these options and utilize these settings.
Access If you choose to share contact information with us, you may update or amend this information by contacting us at info@vanordenforcongress.com.
Confidentiality and security We have adopted commercially reasonable technical, physical, and administrative procedures to help protect information about you from loss, misuse, and alteration.

Please be aware, however, that despite our efforts, no security measures are perfect or impenetrable and no method of data transmission that can be guaranteed against any interception or other type of misuse.
We want you to feel confident using the Site, but we cannot ensure or warrant the security of any information you transmit to us.
To protect the confidentiality of personal information, you must keep your password confidential and not disclose it to any other person.

Financial Donations If you choose to make a donation to Van Orden for Congress your credit card information will be used only for this transaction through our secure online payment system.
Van Orden for Congress does not retain credit card information.
All contributions are final and cannot be rescinded, cancelled or refunded once contributed.
In addition, when you contribute, we are required to collect certain information: your name, address, employer, and occupation.
Visitors from outside the United States The Site’s offices are located in the United States.

If you visit the site from another country, please be aware that information you provide to us or that we obtain as a result of your use of the Site may be processed in and transferred to the United States and will be subject to U.S. law.

If we learn that we have collected any personal information from a child under the age of 13 without verifiable parental consent, we will delete that information from our database as quickly as possible.
If you believe that we may have collected information from a child under 13, please contact us at info@vanordenforcongress.com.
CHANGES TO THE PRIVACY POLICY We may update this privacy policy at any time to reflect changes in our practices and service offerings.

If we modify this privacy policy, we will update the “Effective Date.” We will notify you of any material changes in the way we treat the information we collect by placing a prominent notice on our site or sending a notice to the primary email address specified in your account.

added: About Issues News Get Involved Join a Coalition Store Donate Select Page Van Orden: Put “No Comment Cooke” on the Record by Grace Kim | Jul 12, 2026 LA CROSSE, WI. – Congressman Derrick Van Orden today issued a statement, challenging Democrat Rebecca Cooke to join him on a debate stage before Wisconsin voters.
The challenge comes as Van Orden raises concerns about Democratic Party insiders determining nominees rather than allowing a true primary in Wisconsin’s Third District.

You can find Van Orden’s full statement below: “With the latest political skulduggery in Wisconsin, it has become abundantly clear that rank-and-file Democrats have no choice in who their nominee will be in Wisconsin’s Third District.
Party insiders anointed Harris, Platner, Crowley, and now Cooke.
I’m done pretending this is a legitimate primary.
I’m challenging Rebecca Cooke to debate now.
Rebecca Cooke has spent six years selling an image of a struggling waitress and working-class outsider fighting for everyday Wisconsinites.
Yet behind that carefully crafted image is a longtime political fundraiser and consultant who has spent years pocketing hundreds of thousands of dollars serving coastal elites.
Today, Cooke owns two waterfront properties while portraying herself as an everywoman struggling to get by.

And despite branding herself as moderate, her public positions have flip-flopped when politically convenient and her endorsements lie with the national progressive left rather than the priorities of rural Wisconsin.
For six years, Cooke has spent dodging hard questions from the public.
If the image she’s spent years promoting is accurate, she should have no problem defending it.
If it isn’t, Wisconsin voters deserve to know before they cast their ballots.
Let’s have that conversation on a debate stage.

It’s time for ‘No Comment Cooke’ to stop dodging questions and start answering them.” DONATE Follow Follow Follow Follow Follow Mailing Address: PO Box 1836, La Crosse, WI 54602 Email: info@vanorden4congress.com Press & media inquiries: vanordenforcongresscontact@gmail.com Paid for by Van Orden for Congress Privacy Policy | Terms & Conditions

added: Donate Volunteer On the Issues Housing Eliminate barriers to missing middle housing Preserve existing affordable housing Protect renters’ rights to ensure safe and secure housing for all Incorporate transportation choice as a key piece of housing policy ​ Everyone deserves safe, secure, and affordable housing.
I primarily favor supply-side solutions that promote diverse and abundant housing stock, as well as the preservation of existing affordable units.
In general, I support loosening unhelpful regulations like restrictive zoning, parking mandates, and setback requirements, while preserving laws that are necessary for residents’ health and safety.

In my first term, I took the lead on parking reform, making Colorado one of the most advanced states in rolling back these harmful laws that prioritize storage for cars over housing for people. ​​ The state also plays a vital role in establishing balanced landlord-tenant law that gives both parties access to a fair process when resolving disputes.
I've supported legislation to require just cause for eviction, expand enforcement options for tenants living in uninhabitable conditions, and guarantee pre-trial mediation for select tenants.
I also spearheaded legislation that allows tenants to get a portable screening report when applying for leases.

Colorado renters no longer have to pay repeat fees for the same information–their own data–just to get housed. ​ I was very impressed by the eviction diversion and recovery program that was temporarily offered in our local courts, an innovative program that provided pre-trial mediation as well as immediate re-housing services for tenants experiencing eviction.
It was disappointing to see the funding for that discontinued.
An eviction can be devastating, and helping tenants avoid them wherever possible, or bounce back from one if necessary, is a wise use of our public resources.
We should secure permanent funding for services like this, and apply those principles beyond our judicial district.

Transportation Expand transportation choices so that all Coloradans can get where they need to go Support Front Range Passenger Rail (the “Colorado Connector”) and invest more in public and active transit Promote road design that puts safety first, especially for cyclists and pedestrians Make better use of taxpayer dollars by taking care of the roads we already have, and prioritizing infill over low-density sprawl ​ Whatever form of transportation you need to take, you deserve to get around safely, conveniently, and affordably.
Expanding transportation choices and using smarter road design reduces traffic congestion, improves air quality, and makes transportation more affordable for everyone.

I’ve brought more transit funding to Colorado Springs with the Zero Fare for Better Air program, and cosponsored legislation to advance Front Range Passenger Rail (now named the “Colorado Connector” or “CoCo”). ​ When a highway project near HD-16 caused the closure of Sinton Trail and cut off cycling constituents from a frequently-used path, I worked with the Colorado Department of Transportation to get the trail re-opened.

I am committed to working closely with the administration, my legislative colleagues, and our local government leaders to make sure Colorado Springs and the Pikes Peak Region see transit dollars invested here in our community. ​ The roads, trails, and sidewalks we already have need a lot of attention, and I’m glad to see the tide changing in Colorado Springs to reject low-density sprawl.
But we don’t exist in a vacuum, and communities all over Colorado owe it to each other to make better use of our shared state resources.

Environment Continue advancing Colorado’s clean energy economy Hold polluters accountable with meaningful enforcement of air quality rules Protect natural spaces and wildlife ​ Climate change is not a tomorrow problem, it is a today problem.
Droughts, heatwaves, and wildfires will continue to worsen as long as we burn fossil fuels for energy.
Our state is too beautiful, and too precious, to give our future away in exchange for short-term profit.
I’m proud that Colorado is a national leader in pursuing a just and equitable transition to all-renewable energy.

We still have a long way to go in reining in polluters like Suncor, and ensuring the successful decommission of our last coal plants, including Ray Nixon. ​ As a freshman legislator, I sponsored a nation-leading bill that set a high bar for tax credits for clean hydrogen, and will ensure that we only incentivize truly clean energy choices.
When I'm back in office, I'll keep fighting for solutions that reduce emissions and fight climate change, not reward Wall Street with even more of our money.

Healthcare Advance single-payer healthcare in the absence of Federal action Increase access to primary care by reducing administrative burden for Medicaid providers Combat suicide with stronger public health education, increased protective factors, and management of access to lethal means ​ Healthcare is a basic human need that should be covered for everyone.
I support a well-planned Colorado public option as a stepping stone to single-payer coverage.
The demand for healthcare goods and services is not like other kinds of demand in a market setting.
It is non-negotiable and often extremely time-sensitive.
You need what you need, when you need it, in order to carry on living.

Anything less than universal healthcare access fails to secure our rights to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. ​ Colorado does better than some other states on account of having embraced the Medicaid expansion under the Affordable Care Act, but we still have a lot of work to do.

The public health emergency unwind caused many eligible patients to get dropped from the rolls, and the Department of Healthcare Policy and Financing (HCPF)–the department that administers Medicaid in Colorado–has had significant internal difficulties and has gone over their budget.
Difficult decisions will be made in the 2027 legislative session, but I believe that what is most critical is to cover primary care and to at least maintain the Medicaid providers we have.

The Commission on Medicaid that has been meeting throughout the interim this year is finding many areas of improvement that are absolutely fixable – coding issues, for instance, and gaps in oversight.

There are also structural challenges that are much harder to overcome, such as Medicaid’s inability to negotiate drug prices the way a private insurer can. ​ All of this speaks to the underlying issue of healthcare in America: a patchwork of public and private insurers makes budgeting unpredictable for providers and facilities, patients struggle to pay for healthcare at precisely the moment they need it the most, and a few companies are making bank off our desperation.
We need a single-payer system as quickly as we can feasibly get to one.

Labor & Employment Make it easier to form a union by removing the second election from the Colorado Labor Peace Act Advance the rights of app-based workers and ensure that the future of work actually works for all of us Ensure living wages, safe working conditions, and a dignified work-life balance for every Coloradan ​ Working people are the true source of our nation’s prosperity.

The upward redistribution of wealth into the non-laboring investor class has dealt a terrible blow to working families, with $50 trillion moving from the bottom 90% to the top 1% over the last forty years.
We’re living in a second gilded age, and it won’t get better on its own.

Governments need to take action. ​ Attacks on organized labor have played a big hand in this, as well as corporate power in politics and government affairs, and working people are feeling the squeeze.

I also support the repeal of the confusing second election required by Colorado’s Labor Peace Act, so that workers can form a union and a collective bargaining unit with one election. ​ The way we work is also changing rapidly, with more and more work opportunities becoming remote or app-based.

In 2024, I prime sponsored a bill that will begin to rein in the worst excesses of app-based delivery and ride share companies.​ Education Protection public education against privatization Promote equitable access to opportunity and ensure a safe, inclusive learning environment for every child Respect and support education professionals so we can attract and retain great teachers ​ Every child deserves a world-class education, and teachers should be compensated and respected as the valued professionals that they are.

While we have finally paid down the budget stabilization factor, we are still frighteningly close to the bottom as a state in terms of school funding, and Colorado's unique fiscal constraints (TABOR) make it difficult to meet our educational needs.
TABOR (the “taxpayers bill of rights”) caps state spending based on inflation and population growth.

But not all costs experience the same rate of inflation, and different demographics require different public services, so that arbitrary spending cap doesn’t account for the complexity of a state budget for a population of over 6 million people. ​ School choice can be really powerful for families in need of high-quality options, especially for children with unique needs, but it is also vital that we preserve neighborhood schools, and ensure we're using public dollars for public education, not for political agendas.

Any institution that receives public education dollars, including charters, should meet public education standards, and refrain from discrimination based on identity, religion, or ability. ​ I also support revising our approach to teacher evaluations to reduce administrative burden, and focus on meaningful, long-term academic development, rather than fixating on short-term metrics that don’t acknowledge the whole child.

Civil Liberties Defend voting rights and promote more accessibility for voters Defend the right to reproductive care, including access to a safe and legal abortion Protect the safety and freedom of LGBTQIA+ Coloradans Uphold due process under the law for everyone in our state, citizen and immigrant alike ​ Self-determination is a basic human right and a core Colorado value.
It is essential that we protect our Colorado way of life against Federal overreach, especially in this dangerous time.

This means defending the will of Colorado voters in codifying the right to a safe and legal abortion, marriage equality, and equal legal protections for LGBTQ+ individuals and their families. ​ The atrocity at Club Q in November 2022, right here in HD-16, only strengthened my commitment to protect the LGBTQ+ community against politicized attacks, marginalization, and violence.​ We must stand firm in our values to protect our individual liberties, and promote safe and healthy communities for all of our neighbors. ​ We have to do more to protect Constitutional due process under the law for all–citizen and immigrant alike – and hold Federal agents accountable for abusing Coloradans’ civil rights.
This is a nation built on immigration, and that diversity makes us strong.
removed: Donate Volunteer On the Issues Housing We all need and deserve safe, secure, and affordable housing.
I primarily favor supply-side solutions that promote diverse and abundant housing supply , and the preservation of existing affordable units.
I've sponsored and co-sponsored legislation that cuts red tape to permit more missing middle housing.
The state also plays a vital role in establishing balanced landlord-tenant law that gives both parties a fair process when resolving disputes.

I've supported legislation to require just cause for eviction, guarantee pre-trial mediation for select tenants. ​ I’ve been very impressed by the Fourth Judicial District’s eviction diversion and recovery efforts, and support securing permanent funding and applying its principles beyond our district.

Transportation Transportation planning is inextricably linked to housing issues, and we must address the two in tandem.​ Expanding transportation choice is key to reducing traffic, improving air quality, and assuring safe, convenient travel for everyone.
It’s why I’ve brought more funding to Mountain Metropolitan Transit for Zero Fare during the summer, and supported legislation to improve safety for cyclists and pedestrians.

When a highway project near HD-16 caused the closure of Sinton Trail and cut off cycling constituents from a frequently used path, I worked with the Colorado Department of Transportation to get the trail re-opened. ​ With once-in-a-lifetime federal funds coming down from the bipartisan infrastructure bill, and a deal with the oil and gas industry that will put badly needed funding into transit, it is a brand new day for transportation planning in Colorado!

I am committed to working closely with the administration, my legislative colleagues, and our local government leaders to make sure Colorado Springs and the Pikes Peak Region see transit dollars invested here in our community .

Energy & Environment Climate change is not a tomorrow problem, it is a today problem , and the drought, heatwaves, and more frequent wildfires we’re experiencing demand our attention in both the short and long term.
I accept the scientific consensus on man made climate change and I’m proud that Colorado is a national leader in pursuing a just and equitable transition to all-renewable energy.

Our state is too beautiful, and too precious, to give our future away to short-term gains largely enjoyed by oil and gas investors, and that provide diminishing returns for hardworking Colorado families.
As a freshman legislator, I sponsored a nation-leading bill that set a high bar for tax credits for clean hydrogen, and will ensure that we only incentivize truly clean energy choices.
Clean energy tax credits are meant to reduce emissions and fight climate change, not to reward Wall Street with even more of our money.
Labor & Employment Working people are the true source of our nation’s prosperity.

The upward redistribution of wealth into the non-laboring investor class has dealt a terrible blow to working families, with $50 trillion moving from the bottom 90% to the top 1% over the last forty years. ​ Attacks on organized labor have played a big hand in this, as well as corporate power in politics and government affairs, and working people are feeling the squeeze.

I also support the repeal of the confusing second election required by Colorado’s Labor Peace Act in order for organizing workers to form a collective bargaining unit. ​ The way we work is also changing rapidly, with more and more work opportunities becoming remote and app-based.

In 2024, I prime sponsored one of a pair of bills that will begin to rein in the worst excesses of app-based delivery and ride share companies.​ Education Every child deserves a world-class education , and teachers should be compensated and respected as the valued professionals that they are.

While we have finally paid down the budget stabilization factor, we are still frighteningly close to the bottom as a state in terms of school funding, and Colorado's unique fiscal constraints (TABOR) make it extremely difficult to meet our current educational needs. ​ School choice can be really powerful for families in need of high-quality options, especially for children with unique needs, but it is also vital that we preserve neighborhood schools , and ensure we're using public dollars for public education , not for political agendas.

Any institution that receives public education dollars, including charters, must meet public education standards, and refrain from discrimination based on identity, religion, or ability. ​ I also support revising our approach to teacher evaluations to reduce administrative burden, and focus on meaningful, long-term academic development, rather than fixating on short-term metrics.
Civil Rights Self-determination is a basic human right and a core Colorado value.

It is essential that we protect our Colorado way of life against Federal overreach, especially in this dangerous time. ​ This means defending the will of Colorado voters in codifying the right to a safe and legal abortion , marriage equality , access to gender-affiring care , and Constitutional due process under the law for all -- citizen and immigrant alike. ​ The atrocity at Club Q in November 2022, right here in HD-16, only further galvanized my commitment to protect the LGBTQ+ community against politicized attacks, marginalization, and violence. ​ We must stand firm in our values to protect our individual liberties, and promote safe and healthy communities for all of our neighbors.

added: As a reminder, we are looking for paid canvassers to join Team Gauer: The position is flexible and part-time and pays $25 per hour.
Applicants must be comfortable knocking doors and having political conversations with neighbors, all with a smile.
Reliable transportation and a phone compatible with the MiniVAN app are requirements and while prior experience is a benefit, it is not a requirement.

removed: Home Community Priorities Bills Endorsements Photos Events Priorities Survey Contact Donate On behalf of Associated Builders and Contractors MN/ND, a statewide organization that represents more than 340 merit shop construction industry members and their 20,000+ employees, ABC MN/ND is proud to announce its endorsement of Andrew Myers for Minnesota House District 45A.
ABC endorses lawmakers and candidates who champion free market principles and who defend the merit shop philosophy in the construction industry.
This philosophy encourages competition and a free-enterprise approach to construction that is based solely on merit, regardless of labor affiliation.

We look forward to working together to pursue commonsense solutions that create the conditions for all Minnesotans to prosper and achieve their career dreams by addressing issues critical to the merit shop construction industry, including: Promoting market-based wage rates by preventing any new prevailing wage mandates or the expansion of prevailing wage laws that infringe upon local control.

Ensuring that merit shop construction contractors can continue to openly and fairly compete for public construction projects by preventing the use of union-only project labor agreement mandates on taxpayer funded projects.

Promoting an “all-of-the-above” workforce development strategy that includes both industry-driven and government-registered apprenticeship programs so workers and employers have the freedom to choose the best way to upskill and develop their workforce.
Supporting the employer-employee relationship by opposing employment mandates that impose one-size-fits all requirements.
Please do not hesitate to reach out should you have any questions.

Sincerely, Jon Boesche Director of Government Affairs Associated Builders & Contractors MN/ND Follow Follow Follow Follow Follow Prepared and Paid for by Andrew Myers for Minnesota House of Representatives District 45A | PO Box 149 Excelsior, MN 55331

removed: Home Community Priorities Bills Endorsements Photos Events Priorities Survey Contact Donate FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE Contact: Leah Courtney, Senior Media Manager, 651-293-1283, leah.courtney@nfib.org NFIB MN PAC Endorses Rep.
Andrew Myers for Re-Election Myers stands with Main Street, backs policies to help our state grow.
ST.
PAUL, MN, June 18, 2024 —The state’s leading small business political action committee, NFIB MN PAC, today endorsed Representative Andrew Myers (Tonka Bay) for re-election in House District 45A.
“Representative Andrew Myers is a proven advocate for Main Street,” said John Reynolds, NFIB Minnesota State Director.
“In his first term, Andrew put his experience as a small business owner and community leader to work for the hardworking men and women in our state.

Now more than ever, we need strong allies like Andrew Myers in the Minnesota House of Representatives.” State legislative endorsements are determined by the NFIB MN PAC Board, which is comprised of small business owners in the state.
Incumbent legislative endorsements are based on the 2023-24 NFIB MN Voting Record, which reflects how a lawmaker voted on priority issues for small business owners.
Lawmakers must have a score of 70 percent or better to qualify for endorsement.
Myers holds a 100 percent pro-small business voting record.
NFIB represents more than 10,000 small businesses in Minnesota.
The NFIB MN PAC endorsement is an important signal to voters across the state that a candidate will stand with small business.
### NFIB Minnesota PAC 380 St.

removed: Home Community Priorities Bills Endorsements Photos Events Priorities Survey Contact Donate Upper Red Lake Area Association Box 407, Waskish, MN 56685 | contact@urlaa.org | 218-556-5844 Dear Constituents of District 45A, I am writing to endorse Andrew Myers for Minnesota House Representative of District 45A.

I have had the pleasure of knowing Andrew for several years, and I can confidently say that he has the integrity and leadership experience you are looking for to tackle big problems and work for solutions in your backyard and for all Minnesotans.

As president of the Upper Red Lake Area Association, I reached out to Andrew about the growing popularity of ice fishing, overnight winter camping, and recreation on the public waters in our area, and the impact it was having on residents, often overwhelmed with the leftovers.
Together we built partnerships.

He encouraged other legislators on both sides of the aisle to recognize the potential environmental impact when tens of thousands of visitors lack the regulation, resources, and infrastructure to handle garbage and waste during extended stays on Minnesota’s frozen lakes.
In 2023, Andrew successfully Chief Authored the “Keep It Clean” Bill, finally requiring that no garbage or waste be placed on the ice of State Waters.

Andrew also knew that regulation alone was not the solution, so he again authored “Keep It Clean- Part Two”, in 2024, requiring the state to develop a grant funding system for local lake area stakeholders interested in developing clean ice strategies and infrastructure in their neighborhoods.

Andrew has pledged to continue to partner with us in this legislative effort, in 2025, so communities, not just in his constituency, but across the State of Minnesota, have the resources we need to be nice to the ice and “Keep It Clean”.
I believe it is essential to elect leaders committed to improving our communities and protecting the environment.
Representative Myers is one such leader.
He has demonstrated his commitment to public service by giving a voice to our shared cause – the protection of Minnesota’s clean waters.
Please join me in supporting Andrew Myers and re-electing him to the Minnesota House Representatives for District 45A.

Sincerely, Robyn Dwight President: Upper Red Lake Area Association Follow Follow Follow Follow Follow Prepared and Paid for by Andrew Myers for Minnesota House of Representatives District 45A | PO Box 149 Excelsior, MN 55331

They have gone above and beyond by generously offering their vehicle for decoration and bringing their positive spirit to the festivities.
We are incredibly grateful they made the long drive out to join us and take part in celebrating with the community.
Their willingness to contribute time, resources, and effort is a wonderful example of community spirit in action.
We are grateful for their enthusiasm, flexibility, and dedication to making these events a success.
Volunteers like Jane and John make a real difference, and we appreciate everything they do!

title.before: ISSUES | Chris Corry

removed: top of page HOME ISSUES ABOUT DONATE CONTACT More Use tab to navigate through the menu items.
For Families – My goal is to help you keep more of your own money, by fighting the tax-and-spend mentality in Olympia.
As a father of three, education and community safety are important to me.
We need strong local control of schools, without the disruptive state control and progressive curriculum.
I’ll work on common sense solutions to school violence, while firmly standing up for our 2nd Amendment rights.
As a licensed Foster Parent, I am a personal advocate for caring for our community members, including those with mental health or addiction battles.
For Businesses – The taxes and regulations coming out of Olympia are crushing our economy at every opportunity while treating our businesses like never ending piggy banks.
We need to tackle L&I, unemployment, and the ridiculous taxes and regulations that strangle the very drivers of our economy.
If these problems aren’t solved, businesses are going to leave Washington for friendlier states, meaning fewer jobs and less revenue to support our communities.
I want to remind Olympia that businesses are not the enemy.
Whether you are an employee or an employer, a healthy economy benefits us all.
For Central Washington – Our district deserve legislators who will represent us in Olympia.

From the Yakima Valley to the Columbia River, our district spans vast agricultural areas while also being home to higher education, manufacturing, transportation, construction and many other supportive commerce industries.
I will work tirelessly to protect the values of Central Washington.
Values like the common-sense conservative principles of upholding the Constitution, supporting lower taxes, and preserving personal accountability.
Let’s keep Central Washington strong for generations to come.
BACK TO TOP ©# Friends of Chris Corry ​ bottom of page

added: 家 认识 Danica 消息 活动 介入 接触 介入 简体中文 zh русский ru English en polski pl עברית he Español es 家 认识 Danica 消息 活动 介入 接触 介入 ★ 认识 Danica ★ 认识 Danica Hartenfels 一位不只为政治、更注重现实生活的领导者 扎根于189区 丹妮卡出生于东斯特劳兹堡，在派克县特拉华镇长大，她的家族与本地区有着深厚的渊源。她的父亲是一名海军退伍军人，在丁曼斯桥经营着一家小企业；母亲是门罗县一位受人尊敬的法律秘书，在她成长的过程中，她被灌输了勤奋、服务和社区关怀的价值观。她的家族在该地区扎根已数代——她的祖父是丁曼斯渡口一位著名的建筑商。 丹妮卡高中毕业后的第一份工作是在派克县的宾夕法尼亚州交通部担任信号员和办公室助理，同时她还一边打工一边读大学。1997年，她毕业于东斯特劳兹堡大学，获得酒店管理学位。自2004年以来，她一直定居在门罗县，并在史密斯菲尔德镇抚养孩子。 职业与创业 Danica 在酒店和旅游业拥有超过 25 年的经验，在其领域树立了领导者的声誉。她是 DB Hart 酒店咨询公司的创始人，服务的客户范围广泛，从 DDB Construction 等本地建筑商到雅高费尔蒙/莱佛士和 Lanyard Stays 等全球酒店集团。 她还是创意企业Wick It Candle Bar的老板，提供环保蜡烛、香薰和活动体验。这家公司体现了她的创业精神和对可持续发展的承诺。 社区和服务 Danica 不仅以其卓越的商业领导力而闻名，还以热衷于社区服务而闻名。她曾服务于： 国际扶轮社 ESU 校友会（副主席、高尔夫委员会联合主席、HRTM 董事会） 商会和女性商业委员会 送餐上门 家庭承诺（董事会董事） 爱心劳动篮球联盟 LPGA 高尔夫计划 她的工作赢得了诸多认可，包括“年度杰出女性”（2024年）、“小而强大的企业奖”（2024年）以及美国童子军颁发的“年度公民”称号。2025年，她再次被波科诺商会提名为“年度商业领袖”。 家庭第一 除了职业和公民事业的成就，丹妮卡最引以为豪的是她的家人。她是东斯特劳兹堡学区孩子们的母亲，也是新泽西州联合市基恩大学双项运动运动员女儿的母亲。 ★ 丹妮卡的优先事项 ★ 第189区的声音 工作家庭优先 支持儿童保育、公平工资和家庭成功。 负责任的税收使用 要求哈里斯堡实行问责制和透明度。 对小型企业的支持 减少繁文缛节并为当地企业家创造机会。 安全、强大的社区 保护社区并支持当地执法。 她为何参选 我不是职业政客。我是一名小企业主、一位母亲，也是你们的邻居。我经历过你们面临的挑战，操持家务、养育孩子、创业。我竞选州众议员，是因为我们的社区需要一个新的声音，一个支持小企业、维护社区安全、扶持工薪家庭、并确保税收得到尊重和合理使用的声音。2026年，我们可以选择能够体现我们价值观而非政治议程的领导人。我已准备好撸起袖子，为你们效力。 丹妮卡·哈滕费尔斯 丹妮卡·哈滕菲尔斯 (Danica Hartenfels) 竞选州众议员 ★ 丹妮卡·哈滕菲尔斯 (Danica Hartenfels) 竞选州众议员 ★ 丹妮卡·哈滕菲尔斯 (Danica Hartenfels) 竞选州众议员 ★ 丹妮卡·哈滕菲尔斯 (Danica Hartenfels) 竞选州众议员 ★ 丹妮卡·哈滕菲尔斯 (Danica Hartenfels) 竞选州众议员 ★ 丹妮卡·哈滕菲尔斯 (Danica Hartenfels) 竞选州众议员 ★ ★ 订阅新闻邮件 ★ 保持知情。保持参与。 获取有关 Danica 的竞选活动、活动以及如何在第 115 区做出贡献的最新动态。 联系我们 在此输入您的电子邮件 选择加入 是的，请订阅您的新闻通讯。 感谢您联系我们。我们将尽快回复您。 哎呀，发送您的消息时出错。请稍后再试。 © # Endorsements Issues Voter Guides DONATE Lets Talk Issues Lets Talk Issues Property Taxes Property Taxes What is the biggest LOCAL concern your district has that hasn’t been met by action in Harrisburg, and what would you do about them if elected? ​ On Property taxes: Homeowners, particularly seniors on fixed incomes, should not have to worry about being taxed out of homes they spent a lifetime paying for.
Where do you fall on these questions, and on how the state should fund grade-school education generally? ​ Public education is a fundamental responsibility of the Commonwealth and must come first.

Revenue Proposals Revenue Proposals There have been a number of legislative proposals that would increase revenue for the state, including marijuana legalization, a tax on digital advertisements, and the legalization/taxation of “skill games.” Which, if any, of these do you favor, and why? ​ I support legalizing and regulating adult-use marijuana and creating a legal, regulated framework for skill games.

Are there legislative measures you support to address data center concerns, such as local or statewide construction moratoriums or efforts to require more transparency/limit resource use by the centers? ​ Data centers must not raise electric rates for families, drain local water resources or overwhelm communities.
Conversely, if your party does win a trifecta, what should its top legislative priority be? ​ With divided government, I would seek bipartisan agreement on property-tax reform.

See more Videos "I'm running for Assembly to make Wisconsin the best it can be for my children and grandchildren." — Paul McGraw Wisconsin 43rd Assembly District View the district map Local Issues I oppose the 765 High Voltage Transmission Line.
As your Representative to the 43rd Assembly District I will fight against this line and fight for affordable energy where it is needed in Wisconsin.

item_pages.value: Join us for an evening of friendly competition, laughter, and brain teasers on July 25th at 5 pm at Aurelio’s Pizza in Geneva.
Gather your smartest friends and form a team to battle it out for trivia glory!

Here's what awaits: Family-friendly night of fun Rounds of challenging trivia across a variety of topics Pizza and drinks included Prizes for the top teams and most creative team name So, mark your calendars and get ready to prove you're the smartest team in Kane County!

Tickets: $25 per person (team discounts available!) Get your tickets now at VoteRicky.com or by following the link below. https://secure.actblue.com/donate/trivia12 Sponsorships include a table for a team for the event and special recognition Don't miss out on this fun and rewarding event!

This Campaign Kick-Off Fundraiser will be held at Global Brew (2100 Prairie St., Saint Charles, IL) on Monday, July 14th, from 5:00 PM to 7:00 PM.
Meet Ricky, hear his vision for our community, and help fuel his campaign to bring fresh leadership to Springfield.
Your support will make a real difference!
Ticket & Donation Details: General Admission: $50 Young Dems (under 35): $25 Sponsorship Levels: Flip ($250), Momentum ($500), Landslide ($1000), Gamechanger ($3500) Can’t attend?
You can still support the campaign by donating online at secure.actblue.com/donate/rivard65 .
Contributions can also be made payable to Friends of Richard Rivard and mailed to 1029 Ronzheimer Ave, St.
Charles, IL 60174.
Let’s build a winning campaign together—see you there!

added: Robert will stand for the parents, the seniors, the small-business owners and the church volunteers who are the real backbone of District 37. ▸ Standing for parents and parental rights ▸ Employ common sense and defend our time-honored American values in our laws and policies ▸ Protect and honor our seniors and veterans ▸ Community-first, servant leadership Questions & Answers Robert Prater on the Issues: Questions and Answers Who is Robert Prater?
Robert Prater is the Republican candidate for Florida House of Representatives, District 37, on the November 3, 2026 ballot in Seminole and Orange Counties.
He is a husband, father, and grandfather who spent more than 20 years with Orange County Public Schools as a classroom teacher, Dean of Students, and educational leader.
What office is Robert Prater running for?
Robert Prater is running for Florida State Representative in House District 37, which covers parts of Seminole and Orange Counties.
The seat is open because Representative Susan Plasencia is retiring.
When is the election?
The general election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026.
Voters in District 37 can vote by mail, vote early, or vote at their polling place on Election Day.
Where does Robert Prater stand on the cost of living?
Having raised a family on a teacher's salary, Robert Prater knows how housing costs, property insurance, tolls, and taxes are squeezing Central Florida families.
He supports expanding housing affordability, reforming property insurance, toll relief, and tax relief for working families.
Where does Robert Prater stand on public schools?
As a 20 year Orange County Public Schools educator serving families across Seminole and Orange Counties, Robert Prater believes schools need practical support rather than mandates from Tallahassee.
He supports competitive teacher pay, expanded vocational and career technical options, stronger literacy and student achievement, and educational choice for parents.
Where does Robert Prater stand on mental health and substance abuse?
Robert Prater calls mental health the crisis behind almost every other crisis, from schools to public safety to homelessness.
He supports expanding access to mental health care, substance abuse prevention, stronger family services, and coordinated crisis response.
Where does Robert Prater stand on growth and rural boundaries?
Robert Prater supports defending Orange and Seminole Counties' rural boundaries and protecting the environment.
He favors smart growth that respects the character of existing neighborhoods and infrastructure that keeps pace with development.
Where does Robert Prater stand on public safety?
Robert Prater backs law enforcement and supports full funding for firefighters and EMS.
He supports tougher penalties for fentanyl trafficking and safer schools and neighborhoods.
Where does Robert Prater stand on family and faith?
Robert Prater supports parents' rights and common sense government grounded in faith and family.
He is committed to protecting seniors and veterans and to servant leadership that puts the community first.
Who has endorsed Robert Prater?
Robert Prater is endorsed by the Florida State Fraternal Order of Police, Associated Builders and Contractors Central Florida, BusinessForce, and the Central Florida Hotel and Lodging Association.
Endorsements are listed at VoteRobPrater.com.
Stand with Robert for a Stronger District 37.

added: I believe in a stronger Tennessee, and I believe that we can get there together. my platform Healthcare - Provide health insurance coverage to more Tennesseans and support our hospitals by expanding Medicaid - Prioritize prevention and early intervention measures - ​Pass safe staffing laws to support healthcare workers and create safer and better healthcare environments ​- Hold healthcare executives accountable - Coordinated state response to addiction and the systemic issues behind it Housing - Prioritize affordable housing; utilizing builder incentive programs and working with local governments - Fight corporate influence in local housing markets - Coordinated statewide response to homelessness; providing structure, guidance, and support to local governments - End harmful policies that criminalize homelessness DCS - System-wide reform; thorough investigation and focus on improving staffing structure - Prioritize mental healthcare for children and youth - Strengthen and empower families to keep children safe and supported - Support youth aging out of foster care with resources for education, housing, employment, and mental health Criminal Justice Reform - Remove barriers to employment, housing, and healthcare for people leaving prison - Mandatory MAT and other evidence-based addiction treatment programs in all TN jails and prisons - Evidence-based policies that reduce youth incarceration Data Centers - Strict state regulations to protect people and the environment - Clear shutdown authority when facilities are in violation of regulations ​- Allow local governments to ban data centers without fear of retaliation Freedom - Ban flock cameras + all other forms of AI mass surveillance - Legalize THC ​ Where I stand on other issues ​School Vouchers Our tax revenue belongs to our public schools which are open to every child; not private schools which have the right to deny enrollment.

Charlie was a lion for America and a warrior for the truth.
It’s hard to believe it has been a year since we lost Charlie Kirk.
Charlie had a unique ability to make people feel like they were part of something bigger than themselves.
He encouraged young people to get involved, to ask hard questions, and most importantly, to never be afraid to stand up for what they believed was right.
Today, I’m thinking of Charlie, praying for Erika and their family, and remembering the passion and courage he brought to everything he did.
May we honor his memory by continuing to never back down, staying true to your convictions, and inspiring the next generation to lead with courage and purpose.
We miss you, Charlie LINK Load more View all updates on Facebook Copyright © # - VoteStumbo.com Paid for by David Stumbo for SC Attorney General P.O.

added: VON-T TAYLOR GEORGIA STATE HOUSE 127 CHANNING “Americans Make America Great” My name is Channing Von Taylor, better known as TDO (The Discriminated Officer) or Von-T “The Hope.” I am an 18-year retired U.S.
Army captain, American rapper, DJ, singer, songwriter, actor, and animal rights activist.
I attended school at every level in the state of Georgia and graduated from Columbus State University with a degree in Criminal Justice.
Like many of you, I am simply a man who wants to live comfortably and in peace.
However, I became a survivor of racial discrimination in our own community.
As the cost of living has increased, I lost most of my life’s possessions, all of my animals, and eventually the home I purchased in Columbia County in 2016.
Like many people, I was left broken and forced to “figure it out.” Those experiences are why I include others facing similar struggles in my fight today.
I have also faced overwhelming odds while pursuing my musical dreams.
I believe our current government culture has normalized bullying and too often set aside the needs of everyday people.
Together, we can send a clear message that unlawful behavior threatening our progress and our children’s future will no longer be tolerated.
I stand with the people to address affordability, support economic growth, and most importantly, protect our children.
Together, we can bring hope and balance back to Columbia County and set an example for others by showing what true American values can accomplish.

I Made the Pledge This impacts all of our ability to afford homes, pay bills, and build financial security amid statewide economic pressures that have made it a defining issue in Georgia 2026.Housing, groceries, utilities, healthcare, property taxes, and cost of living is the top of my list.
I want to push bills that tackle tax relief, housing supply increases, tenant protections, and cost-of-living measures, as I know this affects your everyday life.
Our community has faced widespread housing affordability issues, with rising rents, home prices, property taxes, and insurance premiums making homeownership almost impossible to achieve.
I want to propose to phase out or reduce property taxes on homes, incentivize denser/more affordable housing, and expand low-income housing credits and even in single-family areas.
We are working families, suburban homeowners, and decent clean people who just want to live and raise our kids in a safe environment.
We are the perfect mix of urban, suburban, and rural residents, healthcare workers, everyday contractors with the touch of our military soldiers and veterans which some stay to better our community.
Many households deal with moderate incomes not enough to live comfortably anymore, forcing us to work in unfavorable conditions or worse...turn to a life of crime just to "get by".
We can make this right!
Some of us spend >30% of income on housing and with the never-ending APR amount that can go up and rarely comes back down.
If you fall short or foreclose then you default, when that happens your credit score is affected which in turn stops you from even being able to bounce back if you tried your hardest.
Our county faces barriers to new housing development, contributing to supply shortages and higher costs.
Affordability Protecting our children from online and physical harms directly impact on our ability to raise healthy, secure kids in a rapidly changing world.
It is critically important to prioritize this matter yet again.
Our schools have families connected to public schools, military communities, and healthcare sectors like Augusta University that directly feed America with top healthcare workers.
I want to ensure our displaced children have a place to call home in the city while they find their way back into the community cycle.

This includes bills on behavioral/mental health support in schools, depression/suicide training for personnel, firearm safety, and broader protections against predators that have normalized getting away with all kinds of abuse towards our children.
Data collection centers for AI are also a major threat.
We can do more for the Department of Family and Children (DFCS) to enhance fostering care reforms, addressing child welfare agency deficits, and expanding mental health concerns.
This administration has made it clear that our children's safety is on the backburner, and it is my goal to bring them back center stage.
Protect Children Economic growth matters profoundly in the CRSA area because it drives job opportunities, supports diverse industries.
In doing this we enhance family prosperity and align with the affordability problem we face.
Which can tackle things like tax reliefs, housing, and business-friendly policies to bring Hope and Balance back to Georgia.
This keeps us thriving even amid national and global shifts.

Economic Growth Register to Vote Check your Voter’s Registration what do you care about Get involved Resources “Americans Make America Great” AMAG is “Americans Make America Great — a Movement Against Greed.” With the help of our community, we can remind the world — starting right here at home — of the greatness we already have.
America cannot “be great again,” because it is the daily actions of its people that already make it great.
This is a statement against greed.
Anyone who exploits our children, veterans, senior citizens, animals, or working people for personal gain should not hold a position of power.
We expanded AMAG overseas in 2025 to help spread positive messages around the world and to counter how we have been portrayed in the headlines.

Our efforts have included helping thousands of homeless animals in Costa Rica with Animal Love Rescue, providing school supplies to hundreds of children in the Dominican Republic, assisting people experiencing homelessness in Puerto Rico, aligning with brands across the globe that highlight genuine human values, and shining a light on cultural history from many parts of the world — bringing those experiences and lessons back to America.
There is enough opportunity for all of us to succeed, and no one should have to live through the hardships I have witnessed and experienced over the past five years.
Be ruthless in your standards, but compassionate in your decisions… and history will do the rest.
Proudly Endorsed By 402-400-1278 tdovontforoffice@gmail.com Paid for by Channing Taylor for Office VON-T TAYLOR GEORGIA STATE HOUSE 127 CHANNING

added: October 10, 2026 406-781-0741 Home Donate About Issues Gallery Events News Voting Info Social Facebook Instagram TikTok YouTube 2025 Legislative Session Home Donate About Issues Gallery Events News Voting Info Social Facebook Instagram TikTok YouTube Voting information for Cascade County Election Day is Tuesday, November 3 Mail Ballot Voters For those registered to receive a mail ballot at your home, the ballots are being mailed on Friday, October 9 .
If you have not received your ballot by Friday, October 16, you should visit the Election Office immediately to fix the situation.

Ballot Drop Box Locations The ballot drop boxes located in the foyer of the County Annex Building at 325 2nd Avenue North and in the Election Office (at that same address) will be available starting Monday, October 12th .
Mailing a Voted Ballot to Ensure Timely Delivery Remember, your ballot must be in the hands of the election officials ON NOVEMBER 3rd .
To ensure your ballot arrives in time, mail your voted ballot via USPS by Wednesday, October 28 .
After October 28, voted ballots should be hand-delivered and deposited in one of the drop box locations.
You can mail a completed voter registration form to the Election Office ( not recommended after October 2 ) or visit the Election Office to register to vote.
While Montana allows same-day voter registration, it’s not wise to wait until November 3rd .
Make a plan to register earlier than November 3rd.
On Monday, November 2nd , you can register and request a ballot on the spot until NOON .
Thereafter, plan on standing in line at Exhibition Hall on November 3rd.

The Election Office will be closed on November 3rd , but the ballot drop box in the foyer at 325 2nd Avenue North (next to the library) will be available for ballot deposits until 8:00 pm on election day.
Polls on November 3rd All election operations will be moved to Exhibition Hall at Expo Park on November 3rd from 7:00 am until 8:00 pm .

Wes Moore Launches Statewide Ad Blitz Highlighting Real Results In Maryland Moore-Miller Campaign Continues Multi-Seven-Figure Ad Buy With New TV Ads And Focus On Black Media The Moore-Miller for Maryland campaign has launched a statewide multi-seven-figure ad buy that includes two new tv ads focused on the real results he’s delivered for Maryland and direct outreach to the Black community through targeted digital, radio, and print advertisements.

“What Marylanders will see over the next month are the real results Governor Moore has delivered to grow our economy, drop violent crime to record lows, deliver relief from skyrocketing energy bills, and build the best public schools possible,” said Senior Communications Adviser Carter Elliott, IV.
“As the campaign looks to November, Gov.

Moore is keeping his foot on the gas, not taking a single vote for granted and communicating directly with Marylanders on the real results he’s delivered since taking office.” The Moore-Miller campaign just launched two new tv ads highlighting the real results Governor Moore has delivered for Maryland.
In “What I’m About” Gov.
Moore highlights the work he’s done to drop violent crime to record lows, deliver relief from skyrocketing energy bills, and build the best public schools possible.
And, in “Here We Are” , Krystal Gonzalez, a mother who tragically lost her daughter to gun violence, discusses how Gov.
Moore has worked with everyone to put record funding in local law enforcement and bring homicides in Maryland to a 40-year low.
In a new radio advertisement, “Barbershop,” Gov.
Moore discusses his commitment to public safety with a local Marylander who experienced the effects of gun violence.
He ends the ad discussing his record investments in local law enforcement and touting Maryland’s 40-year low in violent crime.
The Moore-Miller campaign is currently utilizing Black radio in the DC, Baltimore, and Salisbury media markets.
Approximately 78% of all radio dollars are being invested with Black-owned radio broadcasters, driven primarily by the Urban One (Radio One) and WHUR-FM (Howard University) in the Washington market.
The Baltimore radio investment is approximately 89% Black-owned, and Washington radio investment is approximately 80% Black-owned.
Here’s What Marylanders Are Watching And Listening: WATCH: “What I’m About” When I look at national politics today, it’s so angry and divisive.
But I got to tell you, that’s not what I’m about.
So, I don’t come from a political background.
I wasn’t born into a wealthy or a powerful family.
When I ran for governor, I saw a system that wasn’t working for many families.
So, we got right to work.
For years, crime was out of control.
Now, in Maryland, violent crime is at a 40 year low.
With utility companies making record profits while our bills keep going up.
We’re fighting back and delivering relief for every household.
And, we said that our kids deserve the best education in the country.
So, we made historic investments in our public schools.
We’ve cut the teacher vacancy rate in half and improved test scores in math and reading.
But our work isn’t done.
So, maybe in Washington, it’s about tearing people down.
But here in Maryland, we lift our people up and we leave no one behind.
WATCH:”Here We Are” Krystal Gonzalez: It’s any mother’s worst nightmare.
My daughter was killed when she was just 18 years old.
I knew my baby deserved more.
So, I started making phone calls.
I needed our leadership to know what violence has done to me and my family.
And Governor Moore didn’t just listen to me.
He heard me.
He got into office and then he tried something new.
He actually worked with everyone.
He made record investments in law enforcement and he worked with the community.
Now, homicides in Maryland are at a 40-year low.
We’ve got more work to do, but Wes Moore is doing it.
LISTEN: “Barbershop” Gov.
Moore : Hi, it’s Governor Wes Moore.
Five years ago, one of the first places I visited before announcing my campaign was the local barbershop to talk to some guys about their priorities.
And, I heard a lot about crime.
Marylander : Two of my students got shot.
It’s dealing with that stuff every single day and they demonize as if we have a choice to live the way that we live.
In this moment, like you said, it’s a systematic thing.
Gov.
Moore: I made a commitment that when I became governor that public safety would be my top priority and that’s exactly what we’ve done.
We made record investments in local law enforcement.
We worked with community leaders and provided those coming home with a second chance at life.
Now, violent crime is at a 40 year low in Maryland.
We’ve got a lot more work to do but we’re making historic progress.
Let’s keep going.
