added: But we also need to ensure the people who live here, including renters, can afford to wait until that new housing is built.
W e have made progress in recent years on issues like zoning, but still have work to do.
Another critical component of the solution is permitting reform.
Permitting delays (not permitting) alone add, by some estimates, over $50,000 to the cost of building a home in King County.
While acting in good faith, my opponent has at times reportedly led the opposition to what I believe are common-sense housing density reforms in our state.
For instance, in 2021, Rep.

Pollet made changes to a bill–intended to streamline the process for DADUs and ADUs–that would have arguably made “ it harder to build an ADU on a single-family lot, not easier .” That led groups like the AARP and environmentalists to urge that the amended bill be vetoed, which is what occurred.

With your support I will: Work with legislative colleagues, housing providers, and city leaders to reduce red tape and hurdles that slow down and raise costs for housing we need, such as by requiring pre-permitted, template housing designs to accelerate and make cheaper the kind of housing we want.
Support rent stabilization laws and just-cause eviction standards that help renters from being priced out while housing supply is built.
Help work on land tax solutions that incentivize owners to build on vacant lots, not sit on vacant lots as investments.

As your State Representative, I will: Pass a statewide ban on smartphone use in school, a common-sense issue that unites parents, educators, and students Help pass legislation to ban addictive feeds, endless scroll, and other problematic features of kids’ social media accounts, without requiring kids to provide more sensitive age-verification data to these companies Require that social media platforms permit all users to easily and intuitively choose the level of algorithmic control their apps use Work on data privacy legislation that gives all users the right to opt-out of certain kinds of data collection and to put strict timeframes on others Climate, the Environment, and Transit I am the son of an environmental lawyer, and have passionately defended the environment throughout my career.
While we’ve made great strides in certain areas, in others, we are falling further behind: Renewable energy.

While the state legislature has set aggressive targets for renewable energy and decarbonization, our state is dead last in actually adding renewable energy (e.g., wind and solar projects) to the grid over the last decade.

Because “Washington leaders paid little attention to” the nuts and bolts of delivery clean energy: transmission planning, renewable siting and permitting, interconnection, all of which are required to get clean energy to our homes.

Indeed, “ [o]f the 469 large renewable projects that applied to connect to [our region’s] grid since 2015, only one has reached approval .” A former state senator rightly called this an “ embarrassing ” mistake by our legislators, including Rep.
Pollet, who missed this issue for a decade.
That is where I have expertise, and years of experience working on transmission and clean energy issues.
Our legal wins are the reason Washington is still able to subsidize clean energy at all.
But I also worked on transmission planning issues, and understand the wholesale electricity markets and the complex interplay between federal and state authority over transmission.
I’ll bring that lacking expertise on these issues to a legislature that has missed it over the last decade.
The environment.

I’ve spent years litigating environmental issues and protecting our oceans, air, water supply, trees and national forests, Sued to prevent harmful seismic airgun testing in the Atlantic ocean, a precursor to oil drilling; Sued oil companies for failure to clean up old oil wells; Prosecuted environmental crime, including the first-ever prosecution that relied on tree DNA to prove the illegal logging of a protected species within a national forest; Advised organizations how to defeat attempts to open the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge to drilling; And represented residents against a Warren Buffett-owned utility to hold it accountable for failing to prepare for an extreme weather event that sparked multiple wildfires.

A Senior Director of Litigation at NRDC recently wrote of my campaign: “It’s a rare gift in this political moment to see someone who you unequivocally believe to be a smart, solutions-oriented, values-driven, all-around good human throw their hat in the political ring.

Will Dreher is on that (very short!) list for me.” In Olympia, I will: Fight to prevent the diversion of Climate Commitment Act funds to meet general budgetary needs Require that existing data centers be subject to stringent environmental regulation that pays for renewable energy and help impose a moratorium on new data centers, since even a 100% renewable-energy powered new data center necessarily pulls those renewables away from displacing carbon emissions elsewhere Defend wildfire resiliency funding Work with our Attorney General’s office to eliminate the scourge of plastic pollution Transit.

In Olympia, I will: Aggressively invest in expanding our light rail and regional networks, by: extending the duration of Sound Transit’s bonds and increased the cap on its debt capacity; designating state highways to accelerate construction required for light rail stations; and prioritizing the use of general-use transportation funding to invest in our regional rail network and rapid bus lines.
As a longtime bike commuter, I’ll also speed up long-awaited connections between our regional bike trail grid.
removed: But we also need, in the interim, to protect renters and homeowners who are feeling the squeeze of rising rents today.
Part of the solution is zoning reform, on which we have made progress in recent years.
But another critical component of the solution is permitting reform.
Permitting delays alone add, by some estimates, over $50,000 to the cost of building a home in King County.
And we need to ensure the people who live here can afford to wait until that new housing is built.

Instead of working productively to increase the types and affordability of housing available in our city and region, my opponent for years led the opposition to common-sense housing density reforms in our state.
The Urbanist ranked Rep.
Pollet one of the five worst state legislators in the 2021 session and in the 2022 session, and as a dishonorable mention in 2023, because of his misguided opposition on this issue.
With your support I will: Work with legislative colleagues, housing providers, and city leaders to reduce red tape and hurdles that slow down and raise costs for housing we need.
Support rent stabilization laws that help renters from being priced out while housing supply is built.

As your State Representative, I will: Pass a statewide ban on smartphone use in school, a common-sense issue that unites parents, educators, and students Help pass legislation to ban addictive feeds, endless scroll, and other problematic features of kids’ social media accounts, without requiring kids to provide more sensitive age-verification data to these companies Require that social media platforms permit all users to easily and intuitively choose the level of algorithmic control their apps use Work on data privacy legislation that gives all users the right to opt-out of certain kinds of data collection and to put strict timeframes on others Climate, the Environment, and Transit While the state legislature has set aggressive targets for renewable energy and decarbonization, it has not addressed the core reasons why our state is not on track to meet those targets.
Indeed, our state is dead last in actually connecting wind and solar projects to the grid over the last few years.
Because our legislature has neglected our electrical grid, allowing it to fall far behind peer states.

Renewable energy cannot be sited or used if it cannot be connected to the grid, and it cannot be transported to the urban centers that need it if there is insufficient transmission capacity to bring it to them.
That is where I have years of expertise.
I am the son of an environmental lawyer, and have passionately defended the environment throughout my career–and much of that work was spent on transmission and clean energy issues.
Our legal wins are the reason Washington is able to subsidize clean energy at all.

But in addition, I’ve: Sued to prevent harmful seismic airgun testing in the Atlantic ocean, a precursor to oil drilling; Sued oil companies for failure to remediate exhausted oil wells; Prosecuted environmental crime, including the first-ever prosecution that relied on tree DNA to prove the illegal logging of a protected species within a national forest; And fought alongside residents against a Warren Buffett-owned utility to hold it accountable for failing to prepare for an extreme weather event that sparked multiple wildfires.
But renewable energy is not the only environmental issue we face.

In Olympia, I will: Bring my expertise to bear on our state’s longstanding transmission and interconnection issues, which have prevented us from siting and connecting the amount of renewable energy we need and from taking full advantage of the renewable energy production we already have.

Fight to prevent diversion of Climate Commitment Act funds to meet general budgetary needs Require that existing data centers be subject to stringent environmental regulation and block or slow new data center growth Defend wildfire resiliency funding Aggressively invest in transit solutions, like expanding light rail, regional rail networks, rapid bus lines, and bike trails and lanes, in order to accelerate our use of climate-friendly transportation options.

added: Skip to content Home About Will Updates Volunteer Request a Yard Sign Donate Donate Navigation Menu Navigation Menu Home About Will Updates Volunteer Request a Yard Sign Donate Media Updated: October 9, 2026 Democrats who are likely to vote in the 2026 midterm elections in Judicial District 5 need to read: Judge Will Moynahan is the right choice for the Kentucky Court of Appeals.
He has served Kentuckians as a judge since being appointed to the seat by Gov.
Andy Beshear in April 2025.
Gov.
Beshear’s support for Judge Moynahan has been widely reported.
Judge Moynahan believes everyone deserves justice, regardless of who they are or how much money they have.

That’s why he served as a federal prosecutor for the Department of Justice under President Obama, where he went after criminals who cheated Kentuckians and corporations who colluded to inflate the cost of prescription drugs.
Judge Moynahan brings combat-tested judgment to the bench, having served 27 years in the Navy and the Navy Reserve as a naval aviator.
He has the support in this race of the Kentucky AFL-CIO, Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates, C-FAIR and VoteVets.
While Judge Will Moynahan has served and protected Kentuckians, Judge Lucy VanMeter has shown dangerous judgment that makes her the wrong choice for the Kentucky Court of Appeals.
As a trial court judge, VanMeter let a man charged with raping a teenage employee go back to his business.
Marcos Valdes was indicted on 17 counts of third-degree rape and five counts of third-degree sodomy involving a 17-year-old who worked for him.

At a hearing in July 2026 , over the objection of prosecutors and the alleged teenage victim, Judge VanMeter modified Valdes’ bond and cleared him to return to work at the same South Broadway address where he was charged with committing the assault.

Powder Hollow Brewery at Yankee Candle Village Join us for a Unity Reception in support of Lora Wondolowski for State Representative!

With election day approaching, Democrats, community leaders, supporters, and friends from across the 1st Franklin District are coming together to support Lora and her campaign for State Representative. *Co-hosted by: Governor Maura Healey, Lt.
Governor Kim Discroll, Congressman Jim McGovern, Senator Jo Comerford, Senator Paul Mark, Rep.
Homar Gomez, Rep.
Lindsay Sabadosa, Rep.
Aaron Saunders, Rep.

Susannah Whipps, Mayor Ginny DeSorgher, Bob Armstrong, Tara Brewster, Chia Collins & Michael Cohen, Jessica Corwin & Philip Silva, Marina Goldman, Tim Hilchey, Mike McCusker, and Patty Perry *Committee in formation Learn more & RSVP Pat Ryan: Vote for Lora, The People's Voice Candidates talk farming, food insecurity at forum Paul Jablon: Wondolowski Demonstrates Competence Top Issues Rural School Funding By growing and unifying the team, we can secure more funding for Western Mass.
Lora Listens, Leads, and Gets It Done Latest from the Campaign Join FCCPR for a follow-up conversation about the nine ballot questions Massachusetts voters will decide on this November!
It's a space to come together to better understand the content and wording of each question, ask questions, and learn from one another.
This free, community-focused session is about understanding what’s on the ballot, not telling people how to vote.
LAVA, 324 Main Street, Greenfield October 16 at 6 PM Everyone is welcome!
Please share with your friends, family, and community networks, and join us for an evening of thoughtful conversation ahead of Election Day.
The Hampshire-Franklin Commission on the Status of Women is seeking Regional Commissioner applicants!

The link to apply is: https://masscsw.org/apply-to-a-regional-commission/ The link to the HFCSW Web Page for more information is: https://masscsw.org/.../regional.../hampshire-franklin/ Endorse/Lawn Signs I want to hear from you!

[image]HAPPY SATURDAY![image][image]REP X YARD SIGNS![image][image]With Election Day coming up on November 3rd, we’re checking in with friends and neighbors across the Fightin’ Fifth![image][image]If you’d like a Rep X yard sign for your home or business, just send us a message with your town and let us know. We’d be happy to get one to you![image][image]Thank you for your continued support, friendship, and confidence over the years. It’s an honor to serve our communities, and I never take that responsibility for granted.[image][image]THANK YOU for being part of the GREAT FIGHTIN’ FIFTH! [image][image]God bless [image]🇺🇸😊👏🏻[image]#RepX #Fightin5th #ProudAmerican #ServiceBeforeSelf #Barnstable #Sandwich #Bourne #CapeCod #Massachusetts #MaPoli

HOUSEHOLD HAZARDOUS WASTE COLLECTION TODAY IN BARNSTABLE [image][image]Happy to stop by again this morning at the Barnstable Household Hazardous Waste Collection at the Barnstable Transfer Station in Marstons Mills, happening today from 9 AM to 12 PM.[image][image]This is a GREAT service for our residents and an important way to safely dispose of paints, chemicals, cleaners, and other materials that should NEVER go in our regular trash or down the drain.[image][image]A BIG THANK YOU to everyone who helped organize today’s collection and to all the residents doing their part to dispose of these materials safely and responsibly.[image][image]Protecting our environment, our drinking water, and the beautiful Cape Cod we all love is something we can ALL do our part to support.[image][image]GREAT JOB, TOWN OF BARNSTABLE AND BARNSTABLE COUNTY![image][image]KEEP CAPE COD CLEAN. removed.text: 25 YEARS. WE WILL NEVER FORGET.[image]AFGHANISTAN[image][image]At the end of a beautiful day here on Cape Cod, we pause and remember.[image][image]Twenty-five years ago today, the war in Afghanistan began. For 20 years, brave Americans and our allies served, sacrificed, and answered the call.[image][image]We remember those who made the ultimate sacrifice, like Nicholas. We remember those who were wounded. We remember the families who lost husbands, wives, sons and daughters.[image][image]But we also want to remember all those who came home and continue to serve.[image][image]They are all around us. They are police officers and firefighters. They are teachers, mechanics, business owners, fathers, mothers and neighbors. They continue to serve their communities and make a difference every day.[image][image]To every Afghanistan veteran: You served. You sacrificed. You made a difference. Be proud of your service, because we are forever proud of you.[image]🇺🇸🙏🏻🫡[image]#RepX #Fightin5th #ProudAmericans #Afghanistan #USA #HonorAndRespect #LivingTheDream [image]The Nicholas G. Xiarhos Memorial Fund[image]2nd Battalion 8th Marines- Front Toward Hero[image]Veterans of Foreign Wars VFW[image]Aptucxet VFW Post 5988 - New[image]Clark-Haddad Post 188 American Legion[image]Veterans of Foreign Wars Massachusetts[image]Sons of The American Legion Detachment of Mass[image]Bourne American Legion Post 230[image]The American Legion Department of Massachusetts[image]Massachusetts Executive Office of Veterans Services[image]U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs

FOR SEAN[image]What an incredible day back in Yarmouth at the K9 Sergeant Sean M. Gannon Training Center — the house that Sean built.[image][image]Today’s state-of-the-art K9 training brought together incredible police officers and some truly incredible dogs. There is so much that goes into properly training a K9 team, including teaching officers how to safely serve as decoys and teaching these dogs how to properly bite, hold and release.[image][image]These officers are committed to doing the job right, and these dogs are absolutely amazing.[image][image]Our family is proud to be in a position to help provide this training through a $5,000 grant from Big Nick’s Ride and the Nicholas G. Xiarhos Memorial Fund, in memory Nick, and in memory of the son of our good friends, Denise and Patrick Gannon.[image][image]Sean Gannon. Nick Xiarhos. Two sons. Two fallen heroes. [image][image]There is something very powerful about seeing the legacy of these young men helping protect the men and women who put their lives on the line every day.[image][image]We will always Back the Blue, and we will do everything we can to help provide our police officers and K9 teams with the training and equipment they need to do their jobs safely and effectively.[image][image]Pain to purpose. Tragedy to triumph.[image]🇺🇸💙🐕🐾🙏🏻[image]#RepX #Fightin5th #ProudAmerican #ServiceBeforeSelf #GiveBack #BackTheBlue #K9 #CapeCod #Massachusetts #MaPoli #ForSean[image]Town of Yarmouth Massachusetts[image]Yarmouth Police Foundation[image]Yarmouth Police Dept.[image]Town of Barnstable[image]Barnstable Police Department[image]Barnstable Police K9 Foundation[image]K9 PTSD Center[image]The Plymouth County Sheriff's Department[image]Falmouth Police Department[image]Veterans Collaborative[image]Riptide K-9[image]Town of Raynham Police Dept[image]Mashpee Wampanoag Police Department[image]Hingham Police[image]Medway Police Department[image]Cohasset Police Department, Cohasset MA[image]West Bridgewater Police Department[image]Sand Dollar Customs LLC[image]Rehoboth K9 Edo[image]Denise Morency Gannon[image]Frank Pacheco[image]Big Nick's Ride for the Fallen[image]The Nicholas G. added: Skip to content Menu X-twitter Threads Instagram Facebook Youtube DONATE Endorsed by Governor Andy Beshear, former Lexington mayor Jim Gray, veterans, and teachers Press Releases BREAKING: The Cook Political Report Moves KY-06 in Zach Dembo’s Direction As Momentum Surges October 9, 2026 More race raters see clear path to victory for competitive Dembo campaign Lexington, KY – Today, another national race rater, the Cook Political Report, updated their rating for Kentucky’s 6th Congressional District from “Likely Republican” to “Lean Republican,” moving the likelihood of winning in Zach Dembo’s direction.
The ratings shift comes as multiple public polls now show Zach Dembo taking a lead over opponent Ralph Alvarado.
Cook writes in part in their analysis : “Polling from both parties shows Democratic prosecutor Zach Dembo and former Republican state Sen.
Ralph Alvarado neck-and-neck — and some surveys even show Dembo in the lead.
“Bevin picked Alvarado as his running mate, and Democrats are now airing ads accusing Alvarado of being complicit when Bevin pardoned hundreds of criminals on his way out of office.
Bevin’s successor, Democratic Gov.

Andy Beshear, has performed quite well in this Lexington-based district, winning it by 20 points in 2023.” Cook’s rate change follows a series of updates from other national rate raters, citing the enthusiasm behind Zach and his competitive campaign.
The race raters also cited the lack of enthusiasm Republican voters have for Alvarado’s campaign and overall concerns with his close association with disgraced ex-Governor Matt Bevin.

Zach Dembo, former federal prosecutor and Navy veteran, released the following statement: “Our path to victory keeps getting clearer because this race is a contrast between public service and corruption.
People in Central Kentucky are tired of career politicians and know that if we want people in our government actually focused on bringing down costs, we have to send someone different to Washington.
“Political pundits are starting to realize what folks here in Central Kentucky have known for a while: this race is a toss-up.
Momentum is on our side and I will continue working to earn every vote so that we can shake up a broken Washington once we win.” ### Let's Go!
